===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single satellite downlink channel that only one drone may transmit on at a time. Incoming imagery tasks pile into a bounded work queue; drones enqueue new tasks only while the queue has room, and the ground station drains tasks one at a time. Because smoke conditions vary, the operator can reconfigure the queue capacity up or down at runtime, but never below the number of tasks already waiting. A drone grabs the downlink only when it is free and releases it when its burst finishes. The safety concern is that two drones must never be transmitting on the shared downlink simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at no reachable state do two drones hold the shared downlink channel at the same time.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Integers
VARIABLES holders, queue, cap
Init == holders = 0 /\ queue = 0 /\ cap = 2
Grab == holders = 0 /\ holders' = (holders) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Release == holders > 0 /\ holders' = holders - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, cap>>
Enqueue == queue < cap /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Drain == queue > 0 /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= queue /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, queue>>
Next == Grab \/ Release \/ Enqueue \/ Drain \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<holders, queue, cap>>
ExclusiveDownlink == holders >= 0 /\ holders <= 1 /\ queue >= 0 /\ queue <= cap
====

```cfg

NEXT Next
INVARIANT ExclusiveDownlink
```

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm writes consolidated maps to a shared store using optimistic locking with retry. Each write carries the epoch the drone believes is current; the store bumps its epoch on every accepted write, and the operator may grow the mission's epoch capacity at runtime as new drones join. A drone reads the store epoch, prepares a write, then commits only if its cached epoch still equals the store epoch, otherwise it retries with a fresh read. The count of accepted writes must always equal the store epoch, because every accepted write advances the epoch exactly once. The hazard is a stale drone committing under an old epoch and silently overwriting newer data.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of accepted writes always equals the store's current epoch, so no stale-epoch write is ever accepted.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Init == epoch = 0 /\ accepted = 0 /\ cachedOk = FALSE

Commit == cachedOk = TRUE /\ epoch < 4 /\ epoch' = (epoch) + 1 /\ accepted' = accepted + 1 /\ cachedOk' = FALSE
Stale == cachedOk = FALSE /\ cachedOk' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted>>
Next == Read \/ Commit \/ Stale
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, accepted, cachedOk>>

An elevator bank in a skyscraper routes waiting passengers through a bounded dispatch queue with backpressure: passengers move from the lobby pool into cars, and cars later discharge them at their floors, but no passenger is ever created or lost in transit. New boarding requests are admitted only while a car has spare room. One car controller can crash silently and simply stop accepting boardings, but the passengers it already holds remain accounted for. Across every step the total number of people equals those still in the lobby plus those currently riding. The safety concern is strict conservation of people.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of people in the lobby plus the count riding in cars always equals the fixed building population.

Leadership can hand off, but the fired flag persists across handoffs. The safety concern is that the irreversible unlock happens at most once.

An airport baggage router elects one leader controller to divert bags onto the sortation belt; a standby is elected on failover. Two independent baggage systems share one physical belt pool, so their leaders are drawn from a common set of controller ids, and a diversion is authorized only when it comes from the controller that is currently the leader. A stale controller that believes it is still leader must never route a bag. Every routed bag increments the count of authorized routings, which must never exceed the count of diversions the true leader performed. The hazard is a deposed controller routing bags it is no longer authorized to route.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no controller other than the current leader ever performs a bag routing.

A library book-reservation system tracks the fixed number of physical copies of a title using a compare-and-swap register on the availability count. A patron reserves a copy by atomically swapping the available count down and the reserved count up; returns swap the other way. No copy is ever created or destroyed, so available plus reserved always equals the total number of copies owned. One reservation agent can be slow but never fails, so a pending swap always eventually resolves. The register guarantees each swap either fully applies or not at all. The hazard is a bookkeeping error that creates or loses a copy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of available copies plus the number of reserved copies always equals the fixed total of copies owned.

    /\ recVal \in 0..MaxWrites
    /\ appliedWrites \in 0..MaxWrites
    /\ leader \in [Pools -> Nodes \cup {NoNode}]
    /\ alive \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ nphase \in [Nodes -> {"idle", "read"}]
    /\ readVal \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxWrites]

Init ==
    /\ recVal = 0
    /\ appliedWrites = 0
    /\ leader = [pl \in Pools |-> NoNode]
    /\ alive = [nd \in Nodes |-> TRUE]
    /\ nphase = [nd \in Nodes |-> "idle"]
    /\ readVal = [nd \in Nodes |-> 0]

Elect(pl, nd) ==
    /\ leader[pl] = NoNode
    /\ PoolOf(nd) = pl
    /\ alive[nd]
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![pl] = nd]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVal, appliedWrites, alive, nphase, readVal>>

FailLeader(pl) ==
    /\ leader[pl] # NoNode
    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![leader[pl]] = FALSE]
    /\ nphase' = [nphase EXCEPT ![leader[pl]] = "idle"]
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![pl] = NoNode]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVal, appliedWrites, readVal>>

Recover(nd) ==

    /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![nd] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVal, appliedWrites, leader, nphase, readVal>>

ReadRec(nd) ==

    /\ alive[nd]
    /\ nphase[nd] = "idle"
    /\ nphase' = [nphase EXCEPT ![nd] = "read"]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![nd] = recVal]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<recVal, appliedWrites, leader, alive>>

    /\ alive[nd]
    /\ nphase[nd] = "read"
    /\ readVal[nd] = recVal
    /\ appliedWrites < MaxWrites
    /\ recVal' = readVal[nd] + 1
    /\ appliedWrites' = appliedWrites + 1
    /\ nphase' = [nphase EXCEPT ![nd] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, readVal>>

    \/ \E pl \in Pools, nd \in Nodes : Elect(pl, nd)
    \/ \E pl \in Pools : FailLeader(pl)
    \/ \E nd \in Nodes : Recover(nd)
    \/ \E nd \in Nodes : ReadRec(nd)
    \/ \E nd \in Nodes : WriteRec(nd)

(* No update is lost: the shared record's value equals the number of        *)
(* applied writes, which can hold only if every write built on the latest.  *)
NoLostUpdates == recVal = appliedWrites

=============================================================================

(* stage, and exit. Worker processes advance cars between stages using an     *)

(* or destroyed by any of these transitions.                                  *)

\* entryQ: cars waiting to enter ; washing: cars in the wash ; done: exited
\* ver: conveyor version stamp ; staged: per-worker staged move ; crashed: dead

Kinds == {"in", "out"}   \* "in": entryQ->washing ; "out": washing->done

    /\ entryQ \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ washing \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ done \in 0..TOTAL
    /\ ver \in Nat
    /\ crashed \subseteq Workers

    /\ entryQ = TOTAL
    /\ washing = 0
    /\ done = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ staged = [w \in Workers |-> IdleMove]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* A live worker reads the version and stages a move for a stage that has a car.
StageMove(w, k) ==

    /\ staged[w].kind = "idle"
    /\ k \in Kinds

    /\ (k = "out") => washing > 0
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![w] = [kind |-> k, rver |-> ver]]

              /\ done' = done

              /\ washing > 0

    /\ ver' = ver + 1

    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)

\* inflight: set of routing messages ; load: bags per carousel
\* ver: per-carousel version stamp ; placed: carousel each bag rests on

\* version is unchanged and the carousel is below capacity.

    /\ load[m.dest] < CAP

    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![placed[b]] = @ - 1]

-------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m9p2t2 --------------------------
\* Subway signalling block system. A fixed number of movement authorities (the
\* permissions that let a train enter a track block) is distributed across the
\* blocks and is neither created nor destroyed -- authorities are only moved.
\* Two independent signalling coordinators share this single pool. Because the
\* signalling plan is periodically reconfigured, a monotone epoch is tracked;
\* each coordinator carries the epoch it last adopted, and only a coordinator on
\* the current epoch may dispatch an authority into transit or land one into a
\* block. At every moment the authorities resident in blocks plus those in
\* transit sum to the fixed total.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Coords, Blocks, Total, MaxEpoch, None

\* epoch: current reconfiguration epoch; local[c]: epoch coordinator c adopted;
\* held[b]: authorities resident in block b; moving: authorities in transit.
VARIABLES epoch, local, held, moving

vars == <<epoch, local, held, moving>>

Authorized(c) == local[c] = epoch

RECURSIVE SumHeld(_)
SumHeld(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN held[b] + SumHeld(S \ {b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ local \in [Coords -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ held \in [Blocks -> 0..Total]
    /\ moving \in 0..Total

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ local = [c \in Coords |-> 0]
    /\ held = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = CHOOSE x \in Blocks : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ moving = 0

\* Reconfigure the signalling plan: advance the epoch and adopt it locally.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![c] = epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, moving>>

\* A lagging coordinator adopts the current epoch.
Sync(c) ==
    /\ local[c] < epoch
    /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, moving>>

\* An authorised coordinator dispatches one authority from a block into transit.
Dispatch(c, b) ==
    /\ Authorized(c)
    /\ held[b] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = held[b] - 1]
    /\ moving' = moving + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, local>>

\* An authorised coordinator lands an in-transit authority into a block.
Arrive(c, b) ==
    /\ Authorized(c)
    /\ moving > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = held[b] + 1]
    /\ moving' = moving - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, local>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Coords : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E c \in Coords : Sync(c)
    \/ \E c \in Coords, b \in Blocks : Dispatch(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Coords, b \in Blocks : Arrive(c, b)

StateBound == epoch <= MaxEpoch

\* Conservation: the authorities resident in blocks plus those in transit always
\* sum to the fixed total, and no bucket is ever negative -- nothing is created
\* or destroyed, only moved.
Conservation ==
    /\ moving >= 0
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : held[b] >= 0
    /\ SumHeld(Blocks) + moving = Total

coarse lock, and a delayed job cannot grab a fine slot until it resumes. A slow

\* Print-shop job spooler with two-level (hierarchical) locking. A job must
\* first take the COARSE lock of a printer, and only then may it take a FINE
\* lock on an individual output slot. A job may be slow -- it can mark itself
\* delayed and linger holding its coarse lock -- but it is never failed; it
\* always eventually resumes.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, Slots, None

VARIABLES coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase, waiting
vars == <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase, waiting>>

Init ==
  /\ coarseOwner = [p \in Printers |-> None]
  /\ fineOwner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
  /\ jobSlot = [j \in Jobs |-> None]
  /\ jobPrinter = [j \in Jobs |-> None]
  /\ phase = [j \in Jobs |-> "idle"]
  /\ waiting = [j \in Jobs |-> FALSE]

\* Level 1: take the coarse lock of a free printer. Required before any slot.
AcquireCoarse(j, p) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "idle"
  /\ coarseOwner[p] = None
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![p] = j]
  /\ jobPrinter' = [jobPrinter EXCEPT ![j] = p]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, jobSlot, waiting>>

\* Level 2: only a job already holding a coarse lock, and not currently
\* delayed, may claim a free fine slot; the claim is recorded on both sides.
AcquireFine(j, s) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ ~waiting[j]
  /\ fineOwner[s] = None
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = j]
  /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = s]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, jobPrinter, waiting>>

\* Release the fine slot (finish printing that slot), keeping the coarse lock.
ReleaseFine(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "fine"
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![jobSlot[j]] = None]
  /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, jobPrinter, waiting>>

\* Release the coarse lock once no fine slot is held, freeing the printer.
ReleaseCoarse(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ jobSlot[j] = None
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![jobPrinter[j]] = None]
  /\ jobPrinter' = [jobPrinter EXCEPT ![j] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, jobSlot, waiting>>

\* The job is slow: it marks itself delayed while still holding its coarse lock.
SlowWait(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ ~waiting[j]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![j] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase>>

\* A slow job is not a failed job: it always eventually resumes.
Resume(j) ==
  /\ waiting[j]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![j] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase>>

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : AcquireCoarse(j, p)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(j, s)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseFine(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseCoarse(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : SlowWait(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Resume(j)

\* The slot ledger and the per-job record are mutually consistent inverses:
\* a slot's recorded owner claims exactly that slot, and a job's claimed slot
\* records exactly that job. No slot can therefore be handed to two jobs.
ConsistentSlotOwnership ==
  /\ \A s \in Slots : fineOwner[s] # None => jobSlot[fineOwner[s]] = s
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : jobSlot[j] # None => fineOwner[jobSlot[j]] = j
====

CapConstraint == capacity <= MaxCap

  /\ committedLog = {}

Propose(w) ==

  /\ w \notin record
  /\ pending' = w

attempts to enter the critical section, which succeeds only if the version stamp

the critical section by releasing the vault and bumping its version stamp. A
privileged administrator may override the protocol and forcibly evict whichever

\* A network of vending machines contends for one critical shared resource (a
\* central cash-and-stock vault) using optimistic locking with retry. A machine
\* reads the vault's version stamp, then tries to enter the critical section;
\* entry succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the read, otherwise the
\* machine retries. Leaving the critical section bumps the version. A privileged
\* administrator may override and evict the current occupant. Throughout, the
\* vault is mutually exclusive: at most one machine is ever inside it.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, None, MaxVer

VARIABLES version, owner, mode, snapshot
vars == <<version, owner, mode, snapshot>>

VerBound == version <= MaxVer

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ owner = None
  /\ mode = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]
  /\ snapshot = [m \in Machines |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: take a snapshot of the current version stamp.
ReadVersion(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "idle"
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![m] = version]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner>>

\* Optimistic commit: enter the critical section only if the version is
\* unchanged since the read and the vault is free; become the recorded owner.
EnterCS(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[m] = version
  /\ owner = None
  /\ owner' = m
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "critical"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot>>

\* Conflict detected: the version moved since the read, so abandon and retry.
Retry(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[m] # version
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, snapshot>>

\* Leave the critical section, releasing the vault and bumping its version.
LeaveCS(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "critical"
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

AdminEvict(m) ==
  /\ owner = m
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : ReadVersion(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : EnterCS(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Retry(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : LeaveCS(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : AdminEvict(m)

\* Mutual exclusion, tied to the shared owner field: a machine is inside the
\* critical section exactly when it is the vault's recorded owner. Since the
\* owner is a single value, at most one machine can be inside at any time.

\* is the op processor p is currently handling, with the version it read (exp).
NoOp == [val |-> NONE, exp |-> 0]

    /\ rec = [val |-> "init", ver |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {[ver |-> 0, val |-> "init"]}
    /\ working = [p \in Procs |-> NoOp]

\* Producers enqueue an update op; backpressure blocks enqueue when the queue is
\* full.
Enqueue(v) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QCAP
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [val |-> v])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied, working>>

\* A free processor takes the head op and snapshots the record's current version.
Take(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val = NONE
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p] = [val |-> Head(queue).val, exp |-> rec.ver]]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, applied>>

\* (no lost update); it advances the version and logs the write.
Commit(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val # NONE
    /\ working[p].exp = rec.ver
    /\ rec.ver < MAXVER
    /\ rec' = [val |-> working[p].val, ver |-> rec.ver + 1]

    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![p].exp = rec.ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, rec, applied>>

\* fails, so it stays able to commit or retry later.
Slow(p) ==
    /\ working[p].val # NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E v \in Vals : Enqueue(v)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Take(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Commit(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Retry(p)

\* write claims a version beyond the record's, and the applied write holding the
\* record's current version agrees with the record's current value.

    \A a \in applied :
        /\ a.ver <= rec.ver
        /\ (a.ver = rec.ver) => (a.val = rec.val)

    /\ lockReg = w
    /\ ledger < CAP
    /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![w] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lockReg, pending>>

Release(w) ==

    /\ lockReg = w
    /\ lockReg' = NONE
    /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, pending>>

    \/ \E r \in pending : ApplyCAS(r)

    /\ pending \subseteq [worker : Workers, exp : {NONE}]

\* critical section is the lock register's current owner. Since the register
\* names a single owner, at most one worker is ever in the critical section.

    \A w \in Workers : (pc[w] \in {"cs", "done"}) => (lockReg = w)

A subway signalling system protects a shared track region that can safely hold only a bounded number of trains at once. Admission is lock-free: a shared compare-and-swap register records the region's current occupancy. A train first reads the register, snapshotting the value it expects; it may then be slow before acting, but it never fails outright. To enter it performs a compare-and-swap that succeeds only if the register still equals its snapshot and the occupancy is below capacity, atomically incrementing the register and moving into the region. If another train changed the register in the meantime the compare-and-swap fails and the train retreats to try again. When a train leaves the region it decrements the register. SAFETY PROPERTY: the bounded track region never holds more trains than its capacity.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Trains, Cap
ASSUME Cap \in Nat

VARIABLES counter, inRegion, snap, loc
\* counter: shared CAS register holding current occupancy of the bounded track region
\* inRegion: set of trains physically inside the region
\* snap: [Trains -> Nat \cup {-1}] each train last read of counter, or "none"
\* loc: [Trains -> {"out","reading","in"}] control location of each train
vars == <<counter, inRegion, snap, loc>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ counter \in 0..Cap
  /\ inRegion \subseteq Trains
  /\ snap \in [Trains -> (0..Cap) \cup {"none"}]
  /\ loc \in [Trains -> {"out","reading","in"}]

Init ==
  /\ counter = 0
  /\ inRegion = {}
  /\ snap = [t \in Trains |-> "none"]
  /\ loc = [t \in Trains |-> "out"]

\* A train reads the occupancy register, snapshotting the expected value (it may then be slow)
Read(t) ==
  /\ loc[t] = "out"
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![t] = counter]
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![t] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, inRegion>>

\* Compare-and-swap succeeds only if the register is unchanged since the read and below capacity
CasEnter(t) ==
  /\ loc[t] = "reading"
  /\ snap[t] = counter
  /\ counter < Cap
  /\ counter' = counter + 1
  /\ inRegion' = inRegion \cup {t}
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![t] = "in"]
  /\ UNCHANGED snap

\* If another train changed the register first, the CAS fails and the train retreats
CasFail(t) ==
  /\ loc[t] = "reading"
  /\ snap[t] # counter
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![t] = "out"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, inRegion, snap>>

\* A train leaves the region and decrements the shared register
Leave(t) ==
  /\ loc[t] = "in"
  /\ counter' = counter - 1
  /\ inRegion' = inRegion \ {t}
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![t] = "out"]
  /\ UNCHANGED snap

Next == \E t \in Trains : Read(t) \/ CasEnter(t) \/ CasFail(t) \/ Leave(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The bounded track region never holds more trains than its capacity.
CapacityOK == Cardinality(inRegion) <= Cap

A print-shop job spooler serializes access to a single printer, the critical resource, using optimistic locking with retry. The printer carries a version counter that jobs read without holding any lock. A job requests the printer by snapshotting the current version and moving to a trying state; requests from different jobs may be serviced in any order (messages can be reordered). A job acquires the printer only if the version is still equal to its snapshot and the printer is currently free, at which point it becomes the owner, bumps the version, and starts printing. If the version has changed since the snapshot, another job intervened, so the job re-reads the version and retries. When the owner finishes printing it releases the printer and bumps the version again. SAFETY PROPERTY: a job is printing only when it actually holds the printer lock, so at most one job ever prints at a time.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od11m0p0t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Jobs, MaxV
ASSUME MaxV \in Nat

VARIABLES owner, version, loc, seen
\* owner: the job currently holding the printer, or "none"
\* version: printer lock version counter (wraps), read optimistically by jobs
\* loc: [Jobs -> {"idle","trying","printing"}] control state of each job
\* seen: [Jobs -> 0..MaxV] the lock version each trying job last observed
vars == <<owner, version, loc, seen>>

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxV THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
  /\ owner \in Jobs \cup {"none"}
  /\ version \in 0..MaxV
  /\ loc \in [Jobs -> {"idle","trying","printing"}]
  /\ seen \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxV]

Init ==
  /\ owner = "none"
  /\ version = 0
  /\ loc = [j \in Jobs |-> "idle"]
  /\ seen = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]

\* A job requests the printer, optimistically snapshotting the current lock version
Request(j) ==
  /\ loc[j] = "idle"
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![j] = version]
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![j] = "trying"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version>>

\* Acquire succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the snapshot and the printer is free
Acquire(j) ==
  /\ loc[j] = "trying"
  /\ seen[j] = version
  /\ owner = "none"
  /\ owner' = j
  /\ version' = Bump(version)
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![j] = "printing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED seen

\* A version mismatch means another job intervened; re-read and retry
Retry(j) ==
  /\ loc[j] = "trying"
  /\ seen[j] # version
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![j] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, version, loc>>

\* The holder finishes printing and releases the printer, bumping the version
Finish(j) ==
  /\ loc[j] = "printing"
  /\ owner = j
  /\ owner' = "none"
  /\ version' = Bump(version)
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![j] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED seen

Next == \E j \in Jobs : Request(j) \/ Acquire(j) \/ Retry(j) \/ Finish(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A job may be printing only if it actually holds the printer lock: mutual exclusion.
MutexOK == \A j \in Jobs : loc[j] = "printing" => owner = j

When the epoch advances, every machine is marked unsynced and must adopt the new epoch before it may serve normal operations. A synced machine dispenses one unit at a time and may be restocked one unit at a time, but never past the current capacity. Separately, a privileged admin override can be unlocked; while unlocked it sets any machine's stock directly, bypassing the epoch-sync requirement, but it still respects the current capacity. The override lock can be toggled on or off. SAFETY PROPERTY: no machine ever holds more units than the current epoch's capacity allows.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od13m9p4t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Machines, MaxCap, MaxEpoch
ASSUME MaxCap \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch \in Nat

VARIABLES epoch, cap, stock, synced, admin
\* epoch: current network configuration epoch
\* cap: per-machine stock capacity for the current epoch (reconfigurable)
\* stock: [Machines -> 0..MaxCap] units currently loaded in each machine
\* synced: [Machines -> BOOLEAN] whether a machine has adopted the current epoch
\* admin: TRUE when the privileged admin override is unlocked
vars == <<epoch, cap, stock, synced, admin>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap
  /\ stock \in [Machines -> 0..MaxCap]
  /\ synced \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ admin \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ cap = MaxCap
  /\ stock = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ synced = [m \in Machines |-> TRUE]
  /\ admin = FALSE

\* Reconfigure the network to a new epoch with a new per-machine cap; existing stock must fit
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E c \in 0..MaxCap :
        /\ \A m \in Machines : stock[m] <= c
        /\ cap' = c
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ synced' = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, admin>>

\* A machine adopts the current epoch before it may serve normal operations
Sync(m) ==
  /\ ~synced[m]
  /\ synced' = [synced EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, stock, admin>>

\* A synced machine dispenses one unit
Dispense(m) ==
  /\ synced[m]
  /\ stock[m] > 0
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = stock[m] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, synced, admin>>

\* A synced machine is restocked by one unit, never past the current cap
Restock(m) ==
  /\ synced[m]
  /\ stock[m] < cap
  /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = stock[m] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, synced, admin>>

\* The privileged admin override sets any machine's stock directly, bypassing epoch sync but not the cap
AdminSet(m) ==
  /\ admin
  /\ \E v \in 0..cap :
        stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![m] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, synced, admin>>

\* Toggle the admin override lock
AdminToggle ==
  /\ admin' = ~admin
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cap, stock, synced>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ AdminToggle
        \/ (\E m \in Machines : Sync(m) \/ Dispense(m) \/ Restock(m) \/ AdminSet(m))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No machine ever holds more units than the current epoch's capacity allows.
CapacityOK == \A m \in Machines : stock[m] <= cap

=============================================================================

A university course-registration system uses hierarchical locking: to enroll, a student must first take a coarse department-wide lock and only then a fine per-seat lock. A student acquires the coarse lock when it is free, and may take a fine seat lock only while holding the coarse lock, only on a seat that no other student currently locks and that has not already been irreversibly committed. Committing an enrollment is the irreversible action: it records the student as the seat's permanent owner and releases both locks. Students may be slow -- lingering while holding locks -- but never fail; a slow student may voluntarily back off, releasing its held locks without committing, and retry later. SAFETY PROPERTY: a student can hold a seat's fine lock only when that seat has not already been committed to a different student, so an enrollment for any seat happens at most once.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od8m8p5t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANTS Students, Seats

VARIABLES coarse, fine, committed, loc
\* coarse: the single department (coarse) lock holder, or "none"
\* fine: [Students -> Seats \cup {"none"}] the seat (fine) lock each student holds
\* committed: [Seats -> Students \cup {"none"}] irreversible enrollment, written once per seat
\* loc: [Students -> {"idle","coarse","fine"}] where each student is in the lock hierarchy
vars == <<coarse, fine, committed, loc>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in Students \cup {"none"}
  /\ fine \in [Students -> Seats \cup {"none"}]
  /\ committed \in [Seats -> Students \cup {"none"}]
  /\ loc \in [Students -> {"idle","coarse","fine"}]

Init ==
  /\ coarse = "none"
  /\ fine = [s \in Students |-> "none"]
  /\ committed = [seat \in Seats |-> "none"]
  /\ loc = [s \in Students |-> "idle"]

\* Acquire the coarse department lock first (hierarchy: coarse before fine)
AcquireCoarse(s) ==
  /\ loc[s] = "idle"
  /\ coarse = "none"
  /\ coarse' = s
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, committed>>

\* Acquire a fine seat lock, only while holding coarse, only on an uncommitted, unlocked seat
AcquireFine(s, seat) ==
  /\ loc[s] = "coarse"
  /\ coarse = s
  /\ committed[seat] = "none"
  /\ \A s2 \in Students : fine[s2] # seat
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = seat]
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, committed>>

\* Commit the enrollment: the irreversible seat grant, then release both locks
Commit(s) ==
  /\ loc[s] = "fine"
  /\ LET seat == fine[s] IN
        /\ committed' = [committed EXCEPT ![seat] = s]
        /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
  /\ coarse' = "none"
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]

\* A slow student may back off and release its held locks without committing, then retry later
Release(s) ==
  /\ loc[s] \in {"coarse", "fine"}
  /\ coarse' = IF coarse = s THEN "none" ELSE coarse
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED committed

Next == \E s \in Students :
           \/ AcquireCoarse(s)
           \/ (\E seat \in Seats : AcquireFine(s, seat))
           \/ Commit(s)
           \/ Release(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A student can hold a seat's fine lock only if that seat is not already irreversibly
\* committed to a different student -- this is what makes the enrollment happen at most once.
CommitOnce ==
  \A s \in Students, seat \in Seats :
     (fine[s] = seat /\ committed[seat] # "none") => committed[seat] = s

=============================================================================

An elevator bank in a skyscraper is coordinated by a set of controllers that must agree on each dispatch decision by quorum voting. A dispatch proposal is opened for voting, and each live controller may cast a single vote for it. A proposal that has collected a quorum of votes is committed and, in the same step, written durably into the shared dispatch record. The bank tolerates silent crashes: at most one controller may crash without warning, after which it casts no further votes, but the remaining controllers can still form a quorum. A proposal may also be retired and later re-opened for a fresh round of voting; committing is irreversible. SAFETY PROPERTY: every dispatch update that has been committed is always durably present in the shared record, so no committed update is ever lost.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m5p1t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANTS Controllers, Proposals, Quorum, MaxCrash
ASSUME Quorum \in Nat /\ MaxCrash \in Nat

VARIABLES proposed, votes, committed, record, crashed
\* proposed: dispatch proposals currently open for voting
\* votes: [Proposals -> SUBSET Controllers] controllers that have voted for each proposal
\* committed: proposals that reached quorum and were declared committed
\* record: proposals actually written into the shared dispatch record
\* crashed: controllers that have silently crashed (at most MaxCrash of them)
vars == <<proposed, votes, committed, record, crashed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ proposed \subseteq Proposals
  /\ votes \in [Proposals -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ committed \subseteq Proposals
  /\ record \subseteq Proposals
  /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
  /\ proposed = {}
  /\ votes = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]
  /\ committed = {}
  /\ record = {}
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Open a new dispatch proposal for voting
Propose(p) ==
  /\ p \notin proposed
  /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, committed, record, crashed>>

\* A live (non-crashed) controller casts its vote for an open proposal
Vote(c, p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ c \notin votes[p]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = votes[p] \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, committed, record, crashed>>

\* A proposal that has a quorum of votes is committed and written to the shared record together
Commit(p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ p \notin committed
  /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
  /\ committed' = committed \cup {p}
  /\ record' = record \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, crashed>>

\* A controller may crash silently; the bank tolerates at most MaxCrash such failures
Crash(c) ==
  /\ c \notin crashed
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrash
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, committed, record>>

\* A proposal may be retired and later re-opened for a fresh round of voting
Retire(p) ==
  /\ p \in proposed
  /\ proposed' = proposed \ {p}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<committed, record, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Proposals : Propose(p) \/ Commit(p) \/ Retire(p)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, p \in Proposals : Vote(c, p)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed dispatch update is durably present in the shared record: none is lost.
NoLostUpdate == committed \subseteq record

=============================================================================

VARIABLES held, grantedBy, ttl, avail
\* held: [Seats -> SUBSET Clients] the client(s) currently leasing each seat
\* grantedBy: [Seats -> Instances \cup {"none"}] which server instance granted the lease
\* ttl: [Seats -> 0..MaxTTL] remaining lease time before expiry
\* avail: shared pool of free capacity units, drawn down by either instance

TypeOK ==
  /\ held \in [Seats -> SUBSET Clients]
  /\ grantedBy \in [Seats -> Instances \cup {"none"}]
  /\ ttl \in [Seats -> 0..MaxTTL]
  /\ avail \in 0..PoolCap

Init ==
  /\ held = [s \in Seats |-> {}]
  /\ grantedBy = [s \in Seats |-> "none"]
  /\ ttl = [s \in Seats |-> 0]
  /\ avail = PoolCap

\* Either instance grants a lease on a free seat to a client, drawing one unit from the shared pool
Grant(i, s, c) ==
  /\ held[s] = {}
  /\ avail > 0
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = {c}]
  /\ grantedBy' = [grantedBy EXCEPT ![s] = i]
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = MaxTTL]
  /\ avail' = avail - 1

\* The granting instance renews an active lease, resetting its time-to-live
Renew(i, s) ==
  /\ grantedBy[s] = i
  /\ ttl[s] > 0
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = MaxTTL]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, grantedBy, avail>>

Tick(s) ==
  /\ grantedBy[s] # "none"
  /\ ttl[s] > 0
  /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![s] = ttl[s] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<held, grantedBy, avail>>

Expire(s) ==

  /\ ttl[s] = 0
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
  /\ grantedBy' = [grantedBy EXCEPT ![s] = "none"]
  /\ avail' = avail + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED ttl

  \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Seats, c \in Clients : Grant(i, s, c)
  \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Seats : Renew(i, s)
  \/ \E s \in Seats : Tick(s) \/ Expire(s)

MaxV == 2
None == "none"

    /\ allocated \in 0..Total

    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxV]

    /\ allocated = 0
    /\ ver = 0

    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]

    /\ snap[c] = ver

    /\ free > 0
    /\ free' = free - 1
    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, override>>

\* Compare-and-swap a release: only if the version is unchanged.
CommitRelease(c) ==
    /\ op[c] = "release"
    /\ snap[c] = ver
    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ allocated > 0
    /\ allocated' = allocated - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ op' = [op EXCEPT ![c] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, override>>

    /\ snap[c] # ver

    /\ free > 0

    /\ allocated' = allocated + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<op, snap, override>>

    /\ ver < MaxV
    /\ allocated > 0
    /\ allocated' = allocated - 1
    /\ free' = free + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<op, snap, override>>

    /\ ver' = 0
    /\ op' = [c \in Controllers |-> None]
    /\ snap' = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, override>>

    /\ override' = ~override
    /\ UNCHANGED <<free, allocated, ver, op, snap>>

    \/ \E c \in Controllers, o \in {"alloc", "release"} : Read(c, o)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CommitAlloc(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CommitRelease(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Fail(c)

    \/ AdminRelease
    \/ Compact
    \/ ToggleOverride

\* the total number of runway slots is invariant.

shared control network, and that network can reorder and re-present messages:

router accepts an incoming grant, taking local hold of the token, only when the
grant's round is strictly newer than anything it has seen; grants whose round is
stale (no newer than the router's remembered round) are simply discarded from
the network without effect, no matter when they arrive.

holding the token; a router releases the belt; a token holder not on the belt

  version and creates a pending request stamped with that version.

  with the live version commits it. The lock version is advanced by one, the
  request is marked done with its applied-at field set to the version it
  consumed, and the dispatch floor / bookkeeping are updated.

- Cancel(c): a controller c abandons its outstanding request (done or not).

  and all pending requests are cleared, so the system never gets stuck.

authorized controller and consumed exactly the version it was stamped with, so

Participants are the individual locks. One lock may crash silently at any time

lock because a quorum of the remaining locks can still decide.

Actions:
- Propose: when no change is pending, propose the next version (one greater than
  the current record) and clear the vote set.
- CastVote(n): a non-crashed lock n that has not yet voted votes for the pending
  change.
- Commit: once a quorum of votes is collected, append the pending version to the
  log, install it as the current record, and clear the pending proposal.
- Crash(n): a lock n crashes silently (at most one lock may be crashed at a
  time); a crashed lock casts no votes.
- Recover(n): a crashed lock n comes back online.

Because each commit installs the proposed version as the record and appends it,
the log is strictly increasing and the record always mirrors the newest commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The current record always equals the most recently committed

  bumps the sequence, so the change is built on the immediately prior record.

dispatched twice even across silent failures.

commit a request whose version still matches, reject a request whose version has

vars == <<shedTotal, committed, queue, version, dropped>>

\* Each feeder's shed weight is simply its numeric id.
Weight(f) == f

SumOf(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN Weight(x) + SumOf(S \ {x})

    /\ committed \in SUBSET Feeders
    /\ queue \in SUBSET (Feeders \X (0..(MaxVersion - 1)))
    /\ version \in 0..(MaxVersion - 1)
    /\ dropped \in SUBSET Feeders

    /\ committed = {}
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ version = 0
    /\ dropped = {}

\* version it observed. Backpressure blocks the enqueue when the queue is full.
Submit(f) ==
    /\ f \notin committed
    /\ ~ \E e \in queue : e[1] = f
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ queue' = queue \union {<<f, version>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shedTotal, committed, version, dropped>>

\* Requests may be serviced in any order. A request whose observed version still
\* matches the shared record commits its shed contribution exactly once.
Commit(e) ==
    /\ e \in queue
    /\ e[2] = version
    /\ e[1] \notin committed
    /\ shedTotal' = shedTotal + Weight(e[1])
    /\ committed' = committed \union {e[1]}
    /\ version' = (version + 1) % MaxVersion
    /\ queue' = queue \ {e}
    /\ UNCHANGED dropped

\* is discarded instead of overwriting the record; the feeder must resubmit.

    /\ e \in queue
    /\ e[2] # version
    /\ queue' = queue \ {e}
    /\ dropped' = dropped \union {e[1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shedTotal, committed, version>>

\* A dropped feeder is allowed to try again from scratch.
Resubmit(f) ==
    /\ f \in dropped
    /\ f \notin committed
    /\ dropped' = dropped \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shedTotal, committed, queue, version>>

\* is subtracted back out of the running total and the record version advances.

    /\ committed' = committed \ {f}
    /\ version' = (version + 1) % MaxVersion
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, dropped>>

    \/ \E e \in queue : Commit(e)
    \/ \E e \in queue : Reject(e)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Resubmit(f)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Restore(f)

\* the shed weights of the feeders that have committed -- no committed update is

Because several players try to grab slots at the same time, each allocation runs

if no other player already holds that lock; if the lock is already taken the
player aborts and may retry a different slot later. Once a player holds the
prepare lock it enters the commit phase and writes the authoritative allocation
record naming itself as the slot's owner. A player that has finished playing
releases its slot, clearing both the owner record and the prepare lock so the
slot can be claimed again.

The number of slots that are active is not fixed: the matchmaker resizes the pool
at runtime, changing how many slots new claims may target, though it never evicts
a player that already owns a slot.

The full set of actions is: begin a claim on an active free slot, grant the
prepare lock, abort when the lock is already held, commit the authoritative
allocation while holding the lock, release a finished slot, and reconfigure the
active-slot count.

authoritative owner record names that same player as the slot's owner, so no two

    /\ capacity \in 1..NumSlots

    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Free]

A power-grid load shedder keeps a shared shed-schedule record replicated across
regional controllers. Updates to the record are applied with a two-phase commit
so that a committed update is never lost or left half-applied at some region.

The coordinator proposes a new shed-schedule value, opening a transaction. Each
region votes to prepare it. Once every region has prepared, the transaction
commits: the authoritative record takes the new value and the protocol moves into
propagation, where each region applies the committed value into its own local
copy. When every region has applied it, the transaction settles. A prepared
transaction may instead be aborted by the coordinator, leaving the record
untouched. Finally, a privileged grid administrator can override a stuck
propagation, force-pushing the committed value into every lagging region at once
and settling the transaction immediately.

The full set of actions is: propose a new value, prepare a region, commit once all
regions have prepared, apply the committed value at a region, finish once all have
applied, abort a prepared transaction, and perform a privileged admin override of
a stuck propagation.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the protocol is settled and idle, every region's local
copy reflects the authoritative committed record, so no committed update is ever
left dropped at a region once its transaction has completed.

vars == <<master, copy, txPhase, txValue, voted>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ master \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ copy \in [Regions -> 0..MaxVal]
    /\ txPhase \in {"idle", "preparing", "committing"}
    /\ txValue \in 0..MaxVal
    /\ voted \in SUBSET Regions

Init ==
    /\ master = 0
    /\ copy = [r \in Regions |-> 0]
    /\ txPhase = "idle"
    /\ txValue = 0
    /\ voted = {}

\* The coordinator proposes a new shed-schedule value, opening a two-phase commit.
Propose(v) ==
    /\ txPhase = "idle"
    /\ txPhase' = "preparing"
    /\ txValue' = v
    /\ voted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<master, copy>>

\* A region votes to prepare the pending transaction.
Prepare(r) ==
    /\ txPhase = "preparing"
    /\ r \notin voted
    /\ voted' = voted \union {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<master, copy, txPhase, txValue>>

\* With every region prepared, the transaction commits: the authoritative record
\* takes the new value and the protocol moves to propagating it.

    /\ voted = Regions
    /\ master' = txValue
    /\ txPhase' = "committing"

    /\ copy[r] # master

    /\ \A r \in Regions : copy[r] = master

\* committed value into every lagging region at once and settling the transaction.
AdminOverride ==
    /\ txPhase = "committing"
    /\ copy' = [r \in Regions |-> master]
    /\ txPhase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<master, txValue, voted>>

    \/ \E r \in Regions : Prepare(r)
    \/ Commit

    \/ Finish
    \/ Abort
    \/ AdminOverride

\* copy reflects the authoritative committed record -- no committed update is left
\* dropped at a region once its transaction completes.

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker elects a single leader node to hand out match
assignments, with failover to a new leader when the old one is lost. Assignment
messages travel over a network that may reorder them, so the protocol tags every
message with the emitting node and the term under which it was sent, and treats a
message from a superseded leader as stale no matter how late it arrives.

A node wins a failover election under a fresh, higher term and becomes leader; any
messages still in flight from the previous leader now carry a term behind the
current one. The current leader emits match-assignment messages tagged with its
identity and the current term, and these queue up to be delivered in any order. A
pending message whose term matches the current term may be applied, in whatever
order it surfaces. A message whose term is behind the current term is stale and is
discarded rather than acted upon.

The full set of actions is: elect a new leader under a higher term, emit a
current-term message as leader, apply a pending current-term message, and drop a
stale message.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every in-flight message that claims the current term was emitted
by the current leader, so a message from a deposed leader can never masquerade as
a current-term instruction, even when it arrives out of order.

TypeOK ==

    /\ leader \in Nodes \union {NoOne}
    /\ inbox \in SUBSET Messages
    /\ applied \in 0..MaxApplied
    /\ appliedTerm \in 0..MaxTerm

    /\ leader = NoOne
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ appliedTerm = 0

\* A matchmaker node wins a failover election under a fresh, higher term and
\* becomes leader; any messages still in flight from the old leader are now stale.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, applied, appliedTerm>>

\* The current leader emits a match-assignment message tagged with its own identity
\* and the current term. Messages queue up and may be delivered in any order.

    /\ applied' = (applied + 1) % (MaxApplied + 1)

\* than acted upon, no matter how late it is delivered.

A network of vending machines reports its sales into one shared ledger. Each sale
is recorded with a two-phase commit between the machine and the ledger coordinator
so that a committed sale is never lost, even if a machine crashes silently in the
middle of the protocol.

A machine begins reporting one sale, opening a transaction. The ledger coordinator
records its yes vote for the pending sale. On commit, the sale is recorded
atomically in both the machine's own committed count and the shared ledger total,
so a committed sale never lands in only one of the two. An in-flight, uncommitted
transaction may instead be aborted, changing no committed totals. A single machine
may crash silently at a time, dropping whatever transaction it had in flight;
anything already committed is untouched. A crashed machine later recovers to idle,
its lost in-flight transaction simply gone, never having been committed.

The full set of actions is: begin reporting a sale, record the coordinator's yes
vote, commit a sale atomically into both counts, abort an in-flight transaction,
crash a single machine silently, and recover a crashed machine.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared ledger total always equals the sum of every machine's
own committed sale count, so no committed sale is ever dropped from the ledger,
not even when a machine crashes mid-protocol.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

SumFn(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumFn(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Machines -> {"idle", "preparing", "prepared", "crashed"}]
    /\ voted \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ committedCount \in [Machines -> 0..PerMax]
    /\ ledger \in 0..(Cardinality(Machines) * PerMax)

Init ==
    /\ phase = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]
    /\ voted = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ committedCount = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ ledger = 0

\* A vending machine begins reporting one sale to the shared ledger, opening a
\* two-phase commit.
MachinePrepare(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "idle"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "preparing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, committedCount, ledger>>

\* The ledger coordinator records its yes vote for the pending sale.
CoordVote(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "preparing"
    /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committedCount, ledger>>

\* Commit atomically records the sale both in the machine's own committed count and
\* in the shared ledger total, so a committed sale is never counted in only one.
Commit(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "prepared"
    /\ voted[m]
    /\ committedCount[m] < PerMax
    /\ committedCount' = [committedCount EXCEPT ![m] = committedCount[m] + 1]
    /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]

\* An in-flight (uncommitted) transaction is aborted, changing no committed totals.
Abort(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] \in {"preparing", "prepared"}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committedCount, ledger>>

\* nothing already committed is affected.
Crash(m) ==
    /\ \A x \in Machines : phase[x] # "crashed"

    /\ voted' = [voted EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committedCount, ledger>>

\* A crashed machine recovers to idle; its lost in-flight transaction is simply
\* gone, never having been committed.
Recover(m) ==
    /\ phase[m] = "crashed"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, committedCount, ledger>>

    \/ \E m \in Machines : CoordVote(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Commit(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Abort(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Crash(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Recover(m)

\* machine's own committed sale count, so no committed sale is ever dropped from
\* the ledger -- not even when a machine crashes mid-protocol.
NoLostUpdate == ledger = SumFn(committedCount, Machines)

mark a member slow, resume a slow member, award the book to a patron with a
quorum, and return the book.

    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ slow = [mb \in Members |-> FALSE]

    /\ p \notin requesting
    /\ requesting' = requesting \union {p}

\* A committee member that is responsive (not slow) grants its vote to a requester.

    /\ ~ slow[mb]
    /\ p \in requesting
    /\ granted[mb] = NoOne

    /\ requesting' = {}

    \/ \E mb \in Members : Resume(mb)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Award(p)
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Return(p)

A pharmacy prescription dispenser guards its single dispensing head with a
lock register updated by compare-and-swap, so that only one dispensing process is
ever in the critical section at once. The system tolerates one process crashing
silently, even while it holds the lock, by reclaiming a dangling lock on recovery.

A process reads the lock register, snapshotting its value. It then attempts a
compare-and-swap: if the register still reads free, matching its snapshot, it
installs itself as the holder and enters the critical section. If the register no
longer matches the snapshot or was not free, the compare-and-swap fails and the
process gives up to retry. In the critical section the process dispenses one unit,
then leaves, resetting the register to free. A single process may crash silently at
a time, even while holding the lock; on recovery, if the lock was left pointing at
the crashed process, it is freed.

The full set of actions is: read the lock register, acquire via a successful
compare-and-swap, retry after a failed compare-and-swap, dispense in the critical
section, release the lock, crash a process silently, and recover a crashed process.

SAFETY PROPERTY: any process in its critical section is exactly the one the lock
register names, so the compare-and-swap discipline lets at most one process into
the critical section at a time, even across a silent crash.

CONSTANTS Procs, MaxDisp

Free == "free"
NoRead == "no_read"

VARIABLES lock, pstate, snap, dispensed

vars == <<lock, pstate, snap, dispensed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ lock \in Procs \union {Free}
    /\ pstate \in [Procs -> {"idle", "trying", "inCS", "crashed"}]
    /\ snap \in [Procs -> Procs \union {Free, NoRead}]
    /\ dispensed \in 0..MaxDisp

Init ==
    /\ lock = Free
    /\ pstate = [p \in Procs |-> "idle"]
    /\ snap = [p \in Procs |-> NoRead]
    /\ dispensed = 0

\* A dispensing process reads the lock register, snapshotting its value.
Read(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "idle"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "trying"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![p] = lock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, dispensed>>

\* Compare-and-swap: the register still reads free (matching the snapshot), so the
\* process installs itself and enters the critical section.
CASAcquire(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "trying"
    /\ snap[p] = Free
    /\ lock = Free
    /\ lock' = p
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "inCS"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, dispensed>>

\* The compare-and-swap fails: the register no longer matches the snapshot or was
\* not free; the process gives up and will retry.
CASRetry(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "trying"
    /\ (snap[p] # Free \/ lock # snap[p])
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, snap, dispensed>>

\* In the critical section, the process dispenses one unit.
Dispense(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "inCS"
    /\ dispensed' = (dispensed + 1) % (MaxDisp + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, pstate, snap>>

\* The process leaves the critical section, resetting the lock register to free.
Release(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "inCS"
    /\ lock' = Free
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, dispensed>>

\* A single process may crash silently, even while holding the lock.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ \A x \in Procs : pstate[x] # "crashed"
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lock, snap, dispensed>>

\* Recovery of a crashed process frees the lock if it was left dangling.
Recover(p) ==
    /\ pstate[p] = "crashed"
    /\ lock' = IF lock = p THEN Free ELSE lock
    /\ pstate' = [pstate EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, dispensed>>

    \/ \E p \in Procs : CASAcquire(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : CASRetry(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Dispense(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Release(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Procs : Recover(p)

\* register names, so the compare-and-swap discipline lets at most one process into
\* the critical section at a time -- even across a silent crash.
Exclusive ==
    \A p \in Procs : (pstate[p] = "inCS") => (lock = p)

physical space.

held lease, reclaim an expired lease's reservation, and withdraw a stored unit.

never exceed the fridge capacity, so no combination of concurrent leases and
out-of-order deposit confirmations can ever overfill the fridge.

pending hold's commit is processed, it is counted only if there is genuine room
under the capacity; if there is no room by the time it is processed, the hold is

successful compare-and-swap, retry after a failed compare-and-swap, confirm a hold
under the capacity check out of order, reject a hold when full, and cancel a

    \/ \E t \in Txns, p \in Parts : VoteNo(t, p)

    \/ \E t \in Txns : Release(t)
    \/ \E t \in Txns : Recover(t)

Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Several grid controllers watch one feeder and may trip it to shed load. The

fires only if the live register is still "closed", in which case it swaps the

breaker.

and then be delayed while a faster controller trips the feeder first. When the
slow controller finally looks, its compare-and-swap cannot fire because the

controller is ever lost; each merely lags.

run, so the irreversible shed never happens twice.

Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two spooler workers append revisions to one shared spool record. Write access

a lease that names it the owner until an expiry time; only the current lease
holder, and only before its lease expires, may append a revision. The shared
record is the set of applied revision ids, which should always form a contiguous
run 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps.

Appending is a snapshot-then-write. When a worker acquires its lease it reads
the highest applied revision id into a private snapshot. To append it writes the
next id after its snapshot -- a blind increment from the snapshot -- but only if
its snapshot still equals the live highest id, so it never appends over a
revision another holder slipped in. The lease's exclusivity plus this check is
what keeps the run gap-free.

Time advances by ticks; when the clock passes a lease's expiry the lease is
gone and the record reverts to unowned, so a worker whose lease lapsed cannot
keep writing. Capacity changes at runtime: an append throughput cap toggles
between zero and one, and while it is zero no append may occur.

Actions: Acquire (an idle-lease worker takes a lease until now-plus-term and
snapshots the highest id), Tick (the clock advances), Write (the lease holder,
before expiry and with capacity, appends its snapshot-plus-one when the snapshot

Scenario: a blood-bank inventory tracker

Two clerks revise one shared inventory record that carries a version counter and

A prepared request records the version it was read against. Applying it is a
compare-and-swap: the revision commits only if the version it read still equals
the live version, in which case the live version advances by one and the record
stamps the read version as the new base. A request whose read version is stale
-- or that cannot commit because the record is already at its maximum -- is
discarded and must be prepared again. This read-check is exactly what stops one
clerk's revision from silently overwriting another's.

There is a privileged admin override: an administrator may force a queued
request to commit even without a matching read version, but the override still
stamps the base correctly as the version just superseded, so a forced revision
never corrupts the record's lineage. The override budget is finite.

queue is below capacity), Apply (a queued request whose read version still
matches the live version commits, advancing the version and stamping its read as
base), Discard (a queued request that cannot commit is dropped), and AdminApply
(the admin forces a queued request to commit, advancing the version and stamping
the superseded version as base).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the record has been revised at least once, its base
equals exactly one less than its live version, so every revision built on the
immediately preceding one and no update was lost.

Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Grid controllers revise one shared setpoint record -- an integer that only ever

until an expiry time, and only the current holder, before expiry, may revise the
setpoint.

Revising is a blind read-modify-write. On acquiring its lease the holder
snapshots the live setpoint; each revision writes back its snapshot-plus-one and
advances its snapshot in lockstep, and a revision is refused unless the snapshot
still equals the live setpoint. The system also tracks the highest setpoint ever
committed. Because the lease is exclusive, a healthy holder's snapshot stays
equal to the live value, so its blind write always moves the setpoint up to a
fresh high -- never backward over another controller's revision.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a controller may take a lease,
snapshot, and then lag while the clock advances past its expiry. Its lease then
lapses and the record reverts to unowned, so the slow controller cannot write on
a stale snapshot; a new holder re-snapshots the current value first. No
controller is lost.

snapshots the setpoint), Tick (the clock advances), Write (the holder, before
expiry and with a snapshot still equal to the live setpoint, commits its

lease), and Expire (a lapsed lease is cleared).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the live setpoint is always at least the highest value ever
committed, so no blind revision ever regressed the record over another
controller's update -- no update was lost.

AdminRevoke (the admin clears a holder and its use together).

for a still-open student, which irreversibly enrolls that student and
permanently removes them from the open pool, so they can never be enrolled

requests, but it can always speed back up, so it is only delayed.

there is none), StepDown (the leader relinquishes leadership), Allocate

into the patient tray, which counts it as dispensed. A controller that is not the current

by a non-leader back to the shelf. A controller can fail at any time; if the failed
controller was the leader, the leadership seat is vacated and a standby controller is

shelf; the pharmacist's admin override installs a chosen controller as leader.

queued job is bound for. A small group of spool servers manages it, but only one of them
holds the spooling seat at a time; the others are standbys ready to take over when the
seat holder fails. The manifest carries a revision stamp, a small wrapping counter that
advances by one every time the manifest is rewritten and rolls back to zero when it runs
past its highest value.

draft, recording the revision stamp it saw. Later it publishes the draft, which is only
allowed if it still holds the seat and the stamp it recorded is still the stamp on the
manifest; publishing advances the stamp and clears the draft. A draft that can no longer
be published -- because its holder lost the seat, or because the manifest moved on
underneath it -- is thrown away rather than applied.

A spool server may step down voluntarily, leaving the seat vacant, and a standby is then
elected into the vacant seat. Servers can also fail outright, which vacates the seat if
the failed server was holding it, and can later rejoin the group. Whenever a server takes
the seat -- by election or otherwise -- it discards any working draft it was still
carrying and starts from the manifest as it currently stands.

The shop's night manager has a privileged override: they can hand the spooling seat to
any server they name, even one that is currently marked failed and even while another
server is seated. A server installed this way also starts from a clean draft.

installs a named server in the seat with a clean draft.

ever overwrite a manifest revision its author never read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every working draft that a server takes is eventually gone from that
server, so no draft is left dangling forever without being either published or thrown
away.

board. An accepted attempt writes the team onto the room's board, advances the revision
tag, and the team scrubs in. If any of those conditions fails -- the room went out of

A bank's interbank settlement batch moves payment instructions out to the settlement rail.
Actually settling an instruction is irreversible: once the money has left, it cannot be
recalled, so an instruction must never settle twice.

Instructions arrive from the gateway and wait to be admitted into a bounded work queue.
The queue holds only a fixed number of instructions, and that bound is real backpressure:
while the queue is full nothing new is admitted, and even an instruction a settlement
worker wants to hand back has to wait for room. Admission also only happens while the
settlement window is open; the window is opened and closed through the day.

Settlement workers pull instructions out of the queue in whatever order they like, since
the rail gives no ordering guarantee. A worker holds at most one instruction at a time. It
either settles it, which is the irreversible step, or hands it back into the queue if room
allows.

The gateway keeps a replay buffer of everything it has forwarded, because instructions can
arrive at the rail out of order and the gateway may need to re-emit one that appears to
have been lost. A re-emission puts the instruction back into the queue, but only when the
instruction is genuinely nowhere in the system: not already queued, not held by a worker,
and above all not already settled. Once the gateway learns an instruction has settled it
purges it from the replay buffer entirely.

and the queue has room; a worker pulls an instruction out of the queue; a worker settles
the instruction it holds; a worker hands its unsettled instruction back into the queue if
there is room; the gateway re-emits a genuinely absent instruction from its replay buffer;
the gateway purges a settled instruction from its replay buffer; the settlement window
opens; the settlement window closes.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No instruction that has already settled is ever sitting in the work queue
or held by a settlement worker, so nothing that has settled can be picked up and settled a
second time.

spraying, at which point the bay lock goes back to free.

A blood-bank inventory tracker feeds cross-match requests to the bench technicians. The
bank is licensed for a fixed number of open cross-matches at once, and that licence is the
capacity the tracker must never breach.

Requests arrive in an inbox and are admitted, in order, onto a bounded intake queue. A
request that has been admitted occupies one of the licensed slots, and it keeps occupying
that slot the whole time it is in the system: while it waits in the queue and also while a
technician has it on the bench. Admission is therefore refused -- this is the
backpressure -- whenever the queue length plus the number of requests currently on
benches has reached the licence. A technician takes the request at the head of the queue
onto its bench, works it, and completes the cross-match, which is when the slot is finally
given back.

A bench technician can crash silently, mid-request, with nothing announcing it. The
request on that technician's bench is not lost: the shift supervisor puts it back onto the
tail of the intake queue, which moves the slot from the bench back to the queue without
ever changing how many slots are in use. A crashed technician whose bench has been cleared
can be restarted.

Actions: the tracker admits an inbox request onto the tail of the intake queue when the
licence has room; a technician takes the head request of the queue onto its bench; a
technician completes the cross-match on its bench and gives the slot back; a technician
crashes silently; the supervisor puts a crashed technician's bench request back onto the
tail of the queue; a crashed technician with an empty bench is restarted.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of requests waiting on the intake queue plus the number of
technicians with a request on the bench never exceeds the bank's licensed number of open
cross-matches.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request that lands on a technician's bench eventually leaves that
bench, either completed or put back on the queue, so nothing sits on a bench forever.

A vending machine network keeps one stock record per machine, giving the counted number of
units loaded in it. Field service handhelds amend those records, and to stop two handhelds
writing over each other the network hands out leases: a handheld takes the lease on a
machine, and only the current lease holder may amend that machine's record.

Leases are not held forever. Each lease carries a countdown; the countdown ticks down on
its own, and when it reaches the end the network takes the lease back and the machine is
free for anyone to lease again. A handheld may also give a lease back voluntarily, as long
as it is not in the middle of an amendment on that machine.

Amending is a read-modify-write. Holding a lease, the handheld reads the machine's record
and keeps that reading as a working draft; later it writes the amendment, moving the
count one unit up or one unit down, and the write is accepted only if the handheld still
holds the lease, the lease has not run out, and the count it read is still the count in
the record. When a handheld is granted a lease on a machine it always starts from a fresh
reading, so any draft it was still carrying is dropped at that moment. A draft whose lease
has gone to somebody else, or lapsed, is abandoned rather than written.

A handheld can crash silently in the field: it stops reading, stops writing, and never
gives its lease back. Nothing announces this; the lease countdown simply runs out and the
network reclaims the machine. A crashed handheld that holds no lease and carries no draft
can be re-imaged and put back into service.

reading; a lease holder reads a machine's record into a working draft; a lease holder
writes an amendment moving the count one unit up or down; a handheld abandons a draft whose lease it no longer holds; a lease countdown ticks
down; a lapsed lease is reclaimed by the network; a handheld gives back a lease it is not
amending; a handheld crashes silently; a crashed, lease-free handheld is re-imaged.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any working draft whose handheld still holds the lease on the machine it
read records that machine's current count, so no amendment can ever be written on top of a
count its author never saw.

currently dosed into that bay's feed. Crews amend those ledgers, and the amendment is a

copied list back with one more chemical added.

which covers the whole conveyor, and only while holding it may it take the lock on a

back, so the coarse lock is held only long enough to pick a bay. A crew may copy a
ledger onto its clipboard only while holding that bay's lock, and it writes its clipboard
back to the same bay while still holding the lock. A crew gives up a bay lock only once
its clipboard is clear.

nothing at all -- it does not take locks, does not copy, does not write back, and does not

indistinguishable from a stopped one and is known never to have stopped, nothing ever

holds a bay lock keeps it until it comes round and releases it itself.

spell; a crew comes out of a slow spell.

never carries pulled shares across a handoff.

whichever instance that desk belongs to, or they can be put straight back into the shared
pool. An opening print that has already been struck can still be cancelled before the
open, which sends those shares back into the shared pool as well.

pad back into the shared pool; an instance cancels a share from its opening print and
returns it to the shared pool.

desks' pads, plus the shares crossed into the two instances' opening prints always add up
to the issue's total share count, so no pull, cross, return, or cancellation ever creates
or destroys a share.

patient is ever opened twice.

An air-traffic runway allocator works with a fixed set of physical progress strips. Every
strip is at any moment in exactly one of three places: racked in the strip bay, in a

out of the rack only if the register still reads exactly what it remembered; the pull
ticks the register. A read the register has already moved past is discarded and the
controller reads again. A controller holds at most one strip.

A strip in hand is either posted at a runway or racked again. Posting is only allowed at
a runway that is currently open. A strip posted at a runway comes back to the rack when
that runway's movement is complete.

Runway capacity changes through the shift: runways are closed for sweeping, inspection or
weather and are reopened afterwards. A runway may only be closed when nothing is posted at
it, so closing never strands a strip, and a closed runway can be reopened at any time.

pulls a strip from the rack and ticks the register; a controller discards a read the
register has moved past; a controller posts the strip in its hand at an open runway; a
controller racks the strip in its hand again; a completed movement returns a posted strip
to the rack; a runway with nothing posted at it is closed; a closed runway is reopened.

right runways, plus the strips in controllers' hands always add up to the shift's total
strip count, so no allocation, stale-read retry, or runway closure ever creates or loses a
strip.

hand, so no controller stands holding a strip forever.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A bank's interbank settlement batch divides its settlement window into numbered slots, and
each participating bank may be allocated one slot to push its payments through. A slot
belongs to at most one bank: two banks allocated the same slot would collide on the rail.

Allocation is protected by two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A bank first takes the
batch lock, which covers the whole window, and only while it holds the batch lock may it
take the lock on an individual slot. Unlike a hand-over-hand scheme, the batch lock is
held throughout: a bank keeps both locks until it drops them together, releasing the batch
lock and every slot lock standing in its name in one step.

Holding both the batch lock and a particular slot's lock, and having no slot allocated to
it yet, a bank may allocate that slot: the window's allocation ledger records the slot as
the bank's, and the bank records that it holds that slot. The allocation is refused if the
ledger already shows the slot as somebody's. A bank gives a slot back by clearing both the
ledger entry and its own record together.

The window's capacity changes while the batch runs: slots are added to the window when the
rail widens, and slots are withdrawn when it narrows. A slot may only be withdrawn while
it is unallocated and unlocked, so withdrawing capacity never pulls a slot out from under
a bank.

Actions: a bank takes the free batch lock; a bank holding the batch lock takes the free
lock on an active slot; a bank holding both locks allocates an unallocated active slot to
itself; a bank drops the batch lock and all of its slot locks together; a bank gives back
the slot allocated to it; a slot is added to the window; an unallocated, unlocked slot is
withdrawn from the window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a bank records that it holds a slot, the window's allocation
ledger shows that same slot as allocated to that same bank, so no slot is ever handed to
two banks at once.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A vending machine network keeps a price record for every machine. Each machine's record
carries a version number, and beside it the machine keeps an audit log: one entry per
accepted price change, recording the version that change was written on top of.

Field pricing agents amend prices through a compare-and-swap. An agent reads a machine's
version and carries that reading around. When it comes to write, the swap is accepted only
if the machine's version is still exactly what the agent read; accepting appends the read
version to the machine's audit log and ticks the machine's version by one. If the version
has moved on since the read, the swap misses and the agent throws the reading away. An
agent may also simply abandon a reading it is carrying and walk away from it.

The network operator has a privileged admin override. The operator can lock a machine,
which shuts field agents out of it entirely: while a machine is locked no agent swap is
accepted there. On a locked machine the operator can force a price straight in without
reading anything first, and that forced write is logged exactly like an agent's, recording
the version it went in on top of and ticking the version. The operator unlocks the machine
afterwards.

A machine's audit log is only so long; once it is full no further change, agent or
operator, is accepted on that machine.

Actions: an agent reads a machine's version; an agent's swap is accepted, logging the read
version and ticking the machine; an agent's swap misses because the version moved or the
machine is locked; an agent abandons the reading it carries; the operator forces a write
into a locked machine, logging and ticking it; the operator locks a machine; the operator
unlocks a machine.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every machine's audit log reads as a gapless, repeat-free run of
versions -- its first entry went in on version zero, its second on version one, and so on
-- so no accepted change was ever written on top of a version that another change had
already built on.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every version reading an agent is carrying is eventually let go of, so
no agent holds an unresolved reading forever.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

    /\ LET m == carrying[a].mc IN

       /\ version[m] = carrying[a].saw
       /\ version[m] < MaxVersion
       /\ Len(auditLog[m]) < LogLimit

share one depot. The fleets plan their own routes and know nothing of each other; the only
thing they contend for is the depot's forklifts, of which there are fewer than there are
