The depot hands out forklift leases rather than locks. A van asks for a lease, and the
depot grants one only while the number of live leases is still below the forklift count.
A lease is not open-ended: it carries a countdown that ticks down on its own. A van that
is still loading renews its lease, which puts the countdown back to full. If a countdown
runs all the way out, the lease is gone and the depot fences that van off the forklift in
the same step, whether or not the van thought it was still loading -- an expired lease
never leaves a van standing on a forklift.

A van that holds a live lease starts loading, and when it finishes it comes off the
forklift and the restock is credited to whichever fleet the van belongs to. Credited
restocks are shipped out to the machines afterwards.

forklift count; a van holding a lease starts loading on a forklift; a loading van finishes
and its restock is credited to its fleet; a lease countdown ticks down; a lease runs out,
fencing its van off the forklift; a van renews its lease; a fleet ships out a credited
restock.

on a forklift never exceeds the depot's forklift count, no matter which fleet the vans
belong to.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler shares one physical spool of fixed capacity between a
normal lane and a priority lane. The spool's occupancy is published in a single
compare-and-swap register that carries the normal lane's job count together
with a version stamp that is bumped on every successful write.

A workstation that wants to queue a job first reads the register, keeping the
count and version it saw. It then attempts a compare-and-swap: the attempt only
lands if the version it read is still the register's current version, if the
shop administrator has not seized the spooler, and if adding one more job would
still leave the normal lane plus the priority lane within the spool's total
capacity. A workstation whose read has gone stale, because the version no
longer matches, simply discards its read and starts over.

The shop administrator has a privileged override. The administrator can seize
the spooler, which blocks all compare-and-swap traffic, and can release it
again. While holding the seizure the administrator injects rush jobs directly
into the priority lane, bypassing the register protocol entirely, but the
administrator is still required to leave the two lanes together within the
spool's total capacity. The press pulls work off either lane: printing a normal
job decrements the register's count and bumps its version, and printing a rush
job decrements the priority lane.

The complete set of actions is: read the register, compare-and-swap a normal
job into the spool, discard a stale read, seize the spooler as administrator,
release the seizure, inject a rush job into the priority lane, print a normal
job, and print a rush job.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of normal jobs recorded in the register plus the
number of rush jobs in the priority lane never exceeds the spool's total
capacity, no matter how compare-and-swap retries and administrator injections
interleave.

vars == <<reg, readOf, rush, seized>>

Reads == {NoRead} \union [cnt : 0..Slack, ver : 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [cnt : 0..Slack, ver : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ readOf \in [Stations -> Reads]
    /\ rush \in 0..Slack
    /\ seized \in BOOLEAN

    /\ reg = [cnt |-> 0, ver |-> 0]
    /\ readOf = [w \in Stations |-> NoRead]

    /\ seized = FALSE

ReadRegister(w) ==

    /\ readOf[w].ver = reg.ver

A print shop job spooler decides which presses are in service using
epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The shop holds a current configuration, which is
the set of presses authorised to take work, and an epoch number that advances
every time the configuration is changed through the normal path. Each press
separately remembers the epoch it last learned. Jobs waiting for a press sit in
a pool.

A normal reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new set of authorised
presses. Any press dropped by the new configuration immediately gives up the job
it was holding, and that job goes back into the waiting pool, so a press that has
just lost its authorisation is never left running work. A press can learn the
current epoch at any time.

A press takes a job out of the pool only when it is in the current configuration
and the epoch it has learned is the current epoch; a press whose learned epoch is
behind has to catch up first. A press holding a job can finish printing it, which
frees the press. A press can also hand a job back to the pool unfinished.

The shop administrator has a privileged override with two powers. The
administrator can install a new configuration directly, without advancing the
epoch at all, and this override still drops the jobs of any press it removes from
the configuration. The administrator can also hand a waiting job straight to a
press, skipping the epoch check entirely, but only to a press that is in the
current configuration.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure normally with an epoch advance, let a
press learn the current epoch, take a job from the pool as an up-to-date
authorised press, finish printing a held job, hand a held job back to the pool,
install a configuration by administrator override without an epoch advance, and
hand a job directly to an authorised press by administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every press that is holding a job is a member of the current
configuration, so no press that reconfiguration has stripped of its authorisation
is ever left holding shop work.

down into whichever of the three places the clerk is heading for.

irreversible for the duration of the event: once its breaker has been opened, that feeder
stays open, so a feeder must never be opened twice.

proposes one feeder at a time -- and only a feeder that is neither already open nor already
held by a proposal in flight. Each participant votes on the proposal. Once every
participant has voted for it, the proposal moves to prepared: the feeder is now locked by
the in-flight transaction, though its breaker is still closed. The transaction then
commits, which opens the breaker: the feeder leaves the prepared set and joins the open
set in one step, and the coordinator goes idle. A transaction can be aborted at any point
before it commits, whether or not it reached prepared, which releases the feeder and clears
the tally.

The grid's shed budget changes while the event runs, as reserve comes and goes: the budget
is raised and lowered by the system operator. The budget is enforced at the moment of
commit -- a transaction only commits while the number of already-open feeders is below the
budget in force right then -- and the operator may only lower the budget to a level the
already-open feeders still fit within.

votes for the open proposal; a fully-voted proposal moves to prepared, locking its feeder;
a prepared transaction commits, opening the feeder's breaker while the shed budget allows;
a transaction is aborted, releasing its feeder and clearing the tally; the operator raises
the shed budget; the operator lowers the shed budget.

so no in-flight drop can ever land on a breaker that has already been opened.

A bank's interbank settlement batch is worked by two independent settlement runs -- the
domestic real-time run and the correspondent run -- which share one pool of payment

a run must take that claim before the instruction goes anywhere near its worklist. A run

it has cleared something. A run settles an instruction from its worklist into its own book,
which takes the instruction off the worklist. The claim is not given back on settlement --
a settled instruction stays claimed by the run that settled it, for good.

A run that decides not to settle an instruction it has claimed drops it: the instruction
comes off that run's worklist and its claim goes back, so the other run may take it. Only
an unsettled instruction can be dropped this way.

claims and settles nothing.

worklist, while its worklist has room; a run settles an instruction from its worklist into

run is paused; a paused run is brought back.

instruction in common, so no payment is ever settled twice.

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker keeps one ranked ladder file, and the ladder writer is
the critical resource: only one lobby host may be writing the ladder at any moment, and the
ladder records who is writing it and for which skill bracket.

Writing is protected by two levels of lock, coarse before fine. A host takes the region
lock first, which covers the whole matchmaking region, and only while holding it may it
take the lock on an individual skill bracket. The region lock is not handed back early:
the host keeps it and the bracket lock together for the whole job, and drops both at once
at the end. A host holding the region lock and a bracket lock may begin a ladder write for
that bracket if nobody else is writing; the write ends when the host is done with it. A
host only drops its locks once it is not the one writing.

Lobby hosts are slow, never failed. A host can fall into a slow spell where it takes no
locks, begins no writes, ends no writes and releases nothing, and it comes out of the spell
on its own. Nothing is ever taken from a slow host -- there is no timeout and no sweeper --
because a slow host is known to be coming back.

takes a free bracket lock; a host holding both begins a ladder write for its bracket while
the ladder is free; the writing host ends its ladder write; a host that is not writing
drops the region lock and all of its bracket locks; a host falls into a slow spell; a host
comes out of a slow spell.

holds the lock on the very bracket being written, so two hosts can never be writing the
ladder at once and no host writes a bracket it does not hold.

never left with a write in progress forever.

A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps one shared unit-count record with a version number
beside it, and it keeps the set of version numbers that amendments have already been
written on top of.

reads the record's current version and stamps the amendment with it; the queue is bounded
and applies backpressure, so while it is full no further amendment is queued, and a
technician has at most one amendment queued at a time.

arrive in whatever order the network feels like -- so the tracker does not work the queue
in order. It picks whichever queued amendment it likes and accepts it only if the version
stamped on it is still the record's current version. Accepting an amendment records that
version as written-on, moves the unit count, and ticks the record's version by one. A
queued amendment stamped with a version the record has moved past is rejected off the
queue. A technician may also simply withdraw an amendment it has queued.

the queue has room; the tracker accepts a queued amendment whose stamp is still current,
recording the version as written-on and ticking the record; the tracker rejects a queued
amendment whose stamp has been overtaken; a technician withdraws an amendment it queued.

exactly the run of versions below the record's current version, so every version from the
start up to the present was built on exactly once and no amendment was ever lost under
another.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every amendment that reaches the queue eventually leaves it, so nothing
sits queued forever unaccepted, unrejected and unwithdrawn.

ring when it is neither holding the token nor sitting at the match-start gate, so the token

Players make themselves ready in a lobby and drop out of a lobby's ready list.

the ring; the token moves to the nearest other lobby on the ring while the gate is clear;
the token-holding lobby with a ready player begins a match start; a lobby at the gate
finishes its start and empties its ready list; a player makes ready in a lobby; a player
drops out of a lobby's ready list.

the ring token and is still a member of the ring, so two lobbies can never be at the gate

is the critical resource: only one requester may have a programming session on it, and only
a requester with the session may actually be writing to the locks.

is full nothing more joins it, and a requester already holding the session or already
writing does not queue. The channel controller grants the session to a queued requester
whenever the channel is free. A requester with the session begins a write and ends it; it
may only hand the channel back once it has stopped writing.

The householder has a privileged override. Seizing the channel cuts every write dead and
frees the session in the same step, so nothing is left writing without a session, and while
the override is in force the controller grants the session to nobody. The householder
releases the override afterwards.

free channel to a queued requester while the override is not in force; a requester with the
session begins writing; a writing requester ends its write; a requester that is not writing

the session; the householder releases the override.

programming session, so two requesters can never be writing at once and nothing writes
without the session.

with a write running forever.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling block system keeps its shared record, the set of track blocks
currently locked, in a single compare-and-swap register. The register carries the
locked set together with a version number. Alongside the register the system
keeps a write history: for each version number it records who performed the write
that produced it, or records that nothing produced it yet.

Interlocking controllers ask for a block by putting a proposal on the network. A
proposal names the controller, the block it wants, and the register version the
controller read when it built the proposal. A controller may have at most one
proposal in flight, and it may ask for any block at all. The network gives no
ordering guarantee, so proposals sit in flight and are taken up in whatever order
the interlocking gets to them; a block a controller wanted may well already be
locked by the time its proposal is taken up, in which case applying the proposal
simply leaves that block locked.

Taking up a proposal is a compare-and-swap. The proposal is applied only if the
version it carries is still the register's version and the version counter has
room left; applying adds the block to the locked set, sets the register's version
to one past the version the proposal carried, and records the proposing
controller as the writer of that new version. A proposal whose version no longer
matches, or that arrives when the version counter is exhausted, is rejected and
its proposing controller is noted as having been rejected.

The interlocking itself can release a locked block. A release also writes the
register: it removes the block from the locked set, advances the version by one,
and records the interlocking as the writer of that new version.

The complete set of actions is: put a proposal for a block on the network, apply a proposal whose version still matches, reject a proposal that no
longer qualifies, and release a locked block as the interlocking.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every version number from one up to the register's current
version has a writer recorded against it, so the write history has no gap and no
accepted write has ever been overwritten by a proposal built on a version that
had already moved on.

lanes that are in service is decided by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the

bag riding inside can be delivered. A delivered bag can be recycled back to the
outside state so it can travel again.

inside the router onto the overflow spur, so the router is empty at the moment

A bank's interbank settlement batch maintains one shared record per counterparty:
the set of numbered adjustments that have been merged into that counterparty's
net position, together with a cursor giving the highest adjustment number the
position is known to have taken. Access is protected by hierarchical locks: one
coarse lock on the whole batch, and inside it a fine lock on each counterparty's
position.

A desk with no reservation outstanding takes the batch's coarse lock. Holding the
coarse lock and carrying no reservation, a desk takes the fine lock on a
counterparty whose cursor has room left and in the same step reserves that
counterparty's next adjustment number, computed as one past the cursor. The fine
lock stays held across the reservation.

Applying is the step that writes: the desk merges its reserved adjustment number
into the counterparty's applied set, moves that counterparty's cursor up to the
number just applied, and releases the fine lock. A desk may only apply while its
reserved number is still exactly one past the counterparty's cursor; if the
cursor has moved on underneath it, the reservation is stale and the desk must
abandon it instead, releasing the fine lock and writing nothing. A desk holding
the coarse lock with no reservation and no fine lock can drop the coarse lock.

The settlement administrator holds a privileged override: the administrator can
merge a counterparty's next adjustment number straight into its applied set and
move its cursor up, ignoring both the coarse lock and the fine lock entirely. This
is exactly what can leave a desk's reservation stale.

The complete set of actions is: take the batch's coarse lock, take a
counterparty's fine lock and reserve its next adjustment number, apply a
reservation that is still exactly one past the cursor, abandon a stale
reservation, drop the coarse lock, and merge a counterparty's next adjustment by
administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: for every counterparty the set of adjustment numbers merged into
its position is exactly the run of numbers from one up to its cursor, so no
adjustment below the cursor has ever been lost by one writer overwriting
another's work.

    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ batchLock' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posLock, applied, cursor, reservation>>

ReserveNext(d, p) ==
    /\ batchLock = d
    /\ posLock[p] = FreeLock
    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ cursor[p] < MaxSeq
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![p] = d]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] =
                        [party |-> p, seq |-> cursor[p] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, applied, cursor>>

ApplyReservation(d) ==
    /\ reservation[d] # NoReservation
    /\ posLock[reservation[d].party] = d
    /\ reservation[d].seq = cursor[reservation[d].party] + 1
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] =
                    applied[reservation[d].party] \union {reservation[d].seq}]
    /\ cursor' = [cursor EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = reservation[d].seq]
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = FreeLock]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] = NoReservation]
    /\ UNCHANGED batchLock

AbandonReservation(d) ==
    /\ reservation[d] # NoReservation
    /\ reservation[d].seq # cursor[reservation[d].party] + 1
    /\ posLock' = [posLock EXCEPT ![reservation[d].party] = FreeLock]
    /\ reservation' = [reservation EXCEPT ![d] = NoReservation]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, applied, cursor>>

DropBatchLock(d) ==
    /\ batchLock = d
    /\ reservation[d] = NoReservation
    /\ ~HoldsAFineLock(d)
    /\ batchLock' = FreeLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posLock, applied, cursor, reservation>>

AdminMergeNext(p) ==
    /\ cursor[p] < MaxSeq
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![p] = applied[p] \union {cursor[p] + 1}]
    /\ cursor' = [cursor EXCEPT ![p] = cursor[p] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchLock, posLock, reservation>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks : TakeBatchLock(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, p \in Parties : ReserveNext(d, p)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : ApplyReservation(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : AbandonReservation(d)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : DropBatchLock(d)
    \/ \E p \in Parties : AdminMergeNext(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AppliedSetIsExactRun == \A p \in Parties : applied[p] = 1..cursor[p]

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A warehouse robot fleet is run by two independent control instances, the north
aisle controller and the south aisle controller, which share one pool of charging
bays. The pool is published as a register holding the set of bays currently free
together with a version number, and every write to the register bumps the version
until the version counter is exhausted. Each controller keeps its own set of bays
it has been granted.

A controller with no read outstanding reads the pool register, keeping both the
free set and the version it saw. It then tries to claim one of the bays its read
showed as free. The claim is optimistic: it lands only if the version the
controller read is still the register's current version, which is what stops the
two independent controllers from both spending the same free bay out of the same
stale picture. A landed claim removes the bay from the register's free set, bumps
the version, and adds the bay to the claiming controller's granted set.

A controller discards its read and starts over when the version has moved on,
when its read showed no free bays at all, or when the version counter is
exhausted so no claim could be written; a controller that has had to start over
is noted as having retried. A controller can release one of its granted bays,
which takes the bay out of that controller's granted set and puts it back into
the register's free set with another versioned write.

The complete set of actions is: read the pool register, optimistically claim a
bay that the read showed free while the version still matches, discard a stale,
empty or unwritable read, and release a granted bay back into the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the north controller's granted bays and the south controller's
granted bays never overlap, so the two independent instances are never both
allocated the same charging bay.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a controller that has a read outstanding eventually resolves
it, either by landing a claim or by discarding the read.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

VARIABLES pool, readOf, granted, retried

vars == <<pool, readOf, granted, retried>>

Reads == {NoRead} \union [free : SUBSET Bays, version : 0..MaxVersion]

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in [free : SUBSET Bays, version : 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ readOf \in [north : Reads, south : Reads]
    /\ granted \in [north : SUBSET Bays, south : SUBSET Bays]
    /\ retried \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ pool = [free |-> Bays, version |-> 0]
    /\ readOf = [north |-> NoRead, south |-> NoRead]
    /\ granted = [north |-> {}, south |-> {}]
    /\ retried = {}

ReadPool(i) ==
    /\ readOf[i] = NoRead
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = pool]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, granted, retried>>

ClaimBay(i, b) ==
    /\ readOf[i] # NoRead
    /\ readOf[i].version = pool.version
    /\ pool.version < MaxVersion
    /\ b \in readOf[i].free
    /\ pool' = [free |-> pool.free \ {b}, version |-> pool.version + 1]
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![i] = granted[i] \union {b}]
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED retried

DiscardRead(i) ==
    /\ readOf[i] # NoRead
    /\ \/ readOf[i].version # pool.version
       \/ readOf[i].free = {}
       \/ pool.version = MaxVersion
    /\ readOf' = [readOf EXCEPT ![i] = NoRead]
    /\ retried' = retried \union {i}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, granted>>

ReleaseBay(i, b) ==

    /\ pool.version < MaxVersion
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![i] = granted[i] \ {b}]
    /\ pool' = [free |-> pool.free \union {b}, version |-> pool.version + 1]

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler tracks every sheet of paper the shop owns. Each sheet is
in exactly one of four places at any instant: in the paper store, in the tray of
whoever currently holds the store's lease, already printed, or spoiled.

Access to the store is by lease. A lease names an operator and carries a number
of ticks left to run; when no operator holds the lease, any operator can be
granted it with a full span of ticks. A tick of the shop clock runs one tick off
a lease that still has ticks left, and a lease that has run out of ticks can be
dropped, freeing the lease for the next operator.

While holding a lease that still has ticks left, an operator can draw a sheet out
of the store into its tray. A sheet in the tray can be printed, which moves it
into the printed total. A sheet in the tray can instead be returned to the store,
but only if the store's occupancy after the return would still be within the
store's current shelf capacity. A tray sheet that the store cannot take back
because it is at or over capacity is spoiled instead.

The shop's shelf capacity changes at runtime as racking is added or pulled out.
Capacity governs returns only: shrinking it never throws sheets out of the store,
it only blocks sheets from coming back.

The complete set of actions is: grant the store lease to an operator, tick a
running lease down, drop a lease that has run out, draw a sheet from the store
into the tray, print a tray sheet, return a tray sheet to the store when capacity
allows, spoil a tray sheet that capacity will not take back, and set the shelf
capacity to a new value.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the sheets in the store, the sheets in the tray, the sheets
already printed, and the sheets spoiled always sum to exactly the shop's total
sheet count, so no lease expiry or capacity change ever creates or destroys a
sheet.

NoOperator == "nooperator"

VARIABLES store, tray, printed, spoiled, lease, capacity

vars == <<store, tray, printed, spoiled, lease, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ store \in 0..TotalSheets
    /\ tray \in 0..TotalSheets
    /\ printed \in 0..TotalSheets
    /\ spoiled \in 0..TotalSheets
    /\ lease \in [holder : Operators \union {NoOperator}, ticks : 0..LeaseSpan]
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity

LeaseRunning == lease.holder # NoOperator /\ lease.ticks > 0

Init ==
    /\ store = TotalSheets
    /\ tray = 0
    /\ printed = 0
    /\ spoiled = 0
    /\ lease = [holder |-> NoOperator, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ capacity = MaxCapacity

GrantLease(o) ==
    /\ lease.holder = NoOperator
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> o, ticks |-> LeaseSpan]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, printed, spoiled, capacity>>

TickLease ==
    /\ lease.ticks > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT !.ticks = lease.ticks - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, printed, spoiled, capacity>>

DropExpiredLease ==
    /\ lease.holder # NoOperator
    /\ lease.ticks = 0
    /\ lease' = [holder |-> NoOperator, ticks |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, printed, spoiled, capacity>>

DrawSheet ==
    /\ LeaseRunning
    /\ store > 0
    /\ store' = store - 1
    /\ tray' = tray + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, spoiled, lease, capacity>>

PrintSheet ==
    /\ tray > 0
    /\ tray' = tray - 1
    /\ printed' = printed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, spoiled, lease, capacity>>

ReturnSheet ==

    /\ store + 1 <= capacity

    /\ store' = store + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, spoiled, lease, capacity>>

SpoilSheet ==

    /\ spoiled' = spoiled + 1

    \/ DropExpiredLease

    \/ PrintSheet
    \/ ReturnSheet
    \/ SpoilSheet

A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps its units in a set of refrigerators. Which
refrigerators are commissioned is decided by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the
tracker holds an epoch number and the set of commissioned refrigerators, and each
commissioned refrigerator can hold up to a per-fridge slot figure. That slot
figure itself changes at runtime as shelving is swapped in and out, so capacity
moves in two independent ways. Every unit is in exactly one place: inside some
refrigerator, held on the bench, written off, or outside the bank altogether.

A reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new commissioned set, but it
is only available when every refrigerator being decommissioned is already empty,
so units are never stranded in a fridge that has left service. The slot figure
can be set to a new value, but only when every commissioned refrigerator's
current contents would still fit inside the new figure.

A unit from outside can be accepted into a commissioned refrigerator that has a
slot free. A unit inside a refrigerator can be pulled out onto the bench. A unit
on the bench can be placed into any commissioned refrigerator with a slot free,
or can be written off. A written-off unit can be cleared back to outside the
bank.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure the commissioned set with an epoch
advance, set the per-fridge slot figure, accept an outside unit into a
commissioned refrigerator, pull a unit out of a refrigerator onto the bench,
place a bench unit into a commissioned refrigerator, write off a bench unit, and
clear a written-off unit back to outside.

its per-fridge slot figure if it is commissioned and is zero if it is not, so
neither a reconfiguration nor a change of the slot figure ever leaves a
refrigerator holding more than it is allowed to.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every unit sitting on the bench eventually leaves the bench.

Bench == "bench"
WrittenOff == "writtenoff"
Away == "away"

vars == <<epoch, commissioned, place, slotFigure>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ commissioned \subseteq Fridges
    /\ place \in [Units -> Fridges \union {Bench, WrittenOff, Away}]
    /\ slotFigure \in 0..MaxSlots

Inside(f) == Cardinality({u \in Units : place[u] = f})
AllowedIn(f) == IF f \in commissioned THEN slotFigure ELSE 0

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ commissioned = Fridges
    /\ place = [u \in Units |-> Away]
    /\ slotFigure = MaxSlots

Reconfigure(cs) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ cs # commissioned
    /\ \A f \in Fridges : f \notin cs => Inside(f) = 0
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ commissioned' = cs
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, slotFigure>>

SetSlotFigure(k) ==
    /\ k # slotFigure
    /\ \A f \in commissioned : Inside(f) <= k
    /\ slotFigure' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, place>>

AcceptUnit(u, f) ==
    /\ place[u] = Away
    /\ f \in commissioned
    /\ Inside(f) < slotFigure
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

PullToBench(u) ==
    /\ place[u] \in Fridges
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = Bench]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

PlaceFromBench(u, f) ==

    /\ f \in commissioned
    /\ Inside(f) < slotFigure
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

WriteOffUnit(u) ==

    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = WrittenOff]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

ClearWrittenOff(u) ==
    /\ place[u] = WrittenOff
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![u] = Away]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, commissioned, slotFigure>>

    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxSlots : SetSlotFigure(k)
    \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : AcceptUnit(u, f)

    \/ \E u \in Units, f \in Fridges : PlaceFromBench(u, f)
    \/ \E u \in Units : WriteOffUnit(u)
    \/ \E u \in Units : ClearWrittenOff(u)

    /\ \A u \in Units : SF_vars(WriteOffUnit(u))

FridgeWithinItsAllowance == \A f \in Fridges : Inside(f) <= AllowedIn(f)

BenchUnitEventuallyLeaves ==

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling block system divides the running lines into zones and hands
each zone to a control centre by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. The system holds
an epoch number together with the assignment, which is the set of zones given to
each control centre. Separately, the system records which zones are physically in
service; zones are taken out of service and put back at runtime as track work
comes and goes, and those changes do not touch the epoch at all.

A control centre is entitled to a zone only when that zone is both in its own
assignment and physically in service. A centre issues a movement authority naming
itself, a zone it is entitled to, and the epoch in force at that moment. An
authority whose stamped epoch is still the current epoch can be used to move a
train, which counts one movement. Any authority can be retired.

A reconfiguration advances the epoch and installs a new assignment. It leaves
authorities alone deliberately: an authority stamped with the retired epoch is
simply stale, and nothing may be done with it. Taking a zone out of service does
not advance the epoch, so it cannot rely on the epoch to invalidate anything; it
therefore revokes, in the same step, every authority for that zone that carries
the current epoch. Putting a zone back into service leaves authorities untouched.

The complete set of actions is: reconfigure the assignment with an epoch advance,
issue an authority for a zone the issuing centre is entitled to, use a
current-epoch authority to move a train, retire an authority, take a zone out of
service while revoking its current-epoch authorities, and put a zone back into
service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every authority stamped with the current epoch names a zone that
its issuing centre is entitled to right now, meaning a zone both in that centre's
assignment and physically in service, so no centre made stale by reconfiguration
or by track work can hold an authority that still passes the check for moving a
train.

TypeOK ==

    /\ assignment \in [Centres -> SUBSET Zones]
    /\ inService \subseteq Zones
    /\ authorities \subseteq Authority
    /\ movements \in 0..MaxMovements

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network issues access credits to its locks. Every credit
the household owns is in exactly one of four places at any instant: sitting in
the vault, staged in the hub's buffer, issued out to the lock devices, or burned
by an unlock that has already happened.

Moving credits is protected by hierarchical locks. There is one coarse lock on
the hub, and inside it a fine lock on each individual door device. An installer
with the hub's coarse lock can draw a credit out of the vault into the hub buffer
and can put a staged credit back into the vault. To push a staged credit out to a
particular door, the installer must additionally hold that door's fine lock,
which it can only take while it holds the hub lock. An installer can release
everything it holds, dropping the hub lock and every door lock it is holding, in
one step. A credit that has been issued out to the doors is burned when someone
actually unlocks a door.

The household administrator has a privileged override: the administrator can pull
an issued credit straight back into the vault, holding neither the hub lock nor
any door lock.

The complete set of actions is: take the hub's coarse lock, take a door's fine
lock while holding the hub lock, draw a credit from the vault into the hub
buffer, push a staged credit out to a door whose fine lock is held, burn an
issued credit on an unlock, put a staged credit back into the vault, release
every lock an installer holds, and pull an issued credit back to the vault by
administrator override.

SAFETY PROPERTY: the credits in the vault, the credits staged in the hub buffer,
the credits issued out to the doors, and the credits already burned always sum to
exactly the household's total credit count, so no lock handover or administrator
override ever creates or destroys a credit.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A bank's interbank settlement batch keeps one shared record, the batch's running
net position, and every ordinary write to it needs a quorum of the clearing banks
to vote in favour. The batch also holds a round number and, while a write is
being decided, a proposal recording the value of the record the proposer read
together with the round the proposal belongs to.

When no proposal is outstanding and rounds remain, a proposal is raised: the
round advances, the proposal records the record's present value as its base, and
the tally of votes starts empty. A bank with no vote already travelling and not
already counted can cast a vote for the outstanding proposal, stamped with the
round in force when it cast. Votes travel on a channel with no ordering
guarantee, so a cast vote sits in flight and is picked up whenever the batch gets
to it. A vote picked up while its stamped round is still the current round and a
proposal is outstanding is added to the tally; a vote whose round has moved on,
or that arrives with no proposal outstanding, is discarded.

Once the tally is a strict majority of the clearing banks, the proposal is
applied: the record takes the proposal's base plus one, and the proposal and its
tally are cleared. An outstanding proposal can also be abandoned, clearing it and
its tally without writing.

Separately, the batch runs a netting sweep that writes the record directly
without any vote at all. Because a sweep moves the record underneath anything
being decided, it advances the round and clears the outstanding proposal and its
tally in the same step. Finally, when the rounds are used up, no proposal is
outstanding and no vote is in flight, the batch closes and the next batch opens
with the round number and the record back at zero.

The complete set of actions is: raise a proposal, cast a vote for the outstanding
proposal, pick up a vote and add it to the tally, discard a vote whose round has
moved on, apply a proposal that has reached a majority, abandon an outstanding
proposal, run a netting sweep that writes the record and invalidates the
proposal, and close the batch and open the next one.

votes, the value it recorded as its base is still the record's present value, so
a proposal can never be applied on top of a write that landed after the proposal
was raised.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: a bank that has a vote in flight eventually has no vote in
flight.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler allocates spool slots to its stations. The stations sit
in a fixed ring and a single token circulates; only the station currently holding
the token may change any allocation. The spooler keeps a registry saying, for
each slot, which station it is allocated to or that it is unallocated, and each
station separately records the slot it has been assigned, or that it has none.

Which slots are in service changes at runtime as spool trays are racked in and
pulled out. The token can be passed on to the next station in the ring at any
time.

The station holding the token can allocate itself an in-service slot that the
registry shows as unallocated, provided it has no slot of its own already; the
allocation writes the station into the registry for that slot and records the
slot against the station. The station holding the token can release the slot
recorded against it, which clears the registry entry and the station's own
record.

Taking a slot out of service is not gated on the token at all, because racking
work happens whether or not the ring is turning. It removes the slot from the
in-service set and revokes any allocation on it in the same step, clearing both
the registry entry for that slot and the record held by whichever station the
registry named. Putting a slot back into service leaves the registry alone.

The complete set of actions is: pass the token to the next station in the ring,
allocate an unallocated in-service slot to the token holder, release the token
holder's slot, take a slot out of service while revoking its allocation on both
sides, and put a slot back into service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a station has a slot recorded against it, the
spooler's registry allocates that very slot to that very station, so no slot is
ever recorded against two different stations at once.

under consideration can approve it.

car to the proposing instance and clears the command and its tally. A command
whose mandate has been superseded is dropped, clearing it and its tally without
doing anything to the cars. A car owned by either instance can be released back
to the free pool.

An airport baggage router keeps one shared record: the set of routing entries
currently loaded into the sorter. The record carries a version number, and every
write to it bumps the version. Baggage handlers update it optimistically. Each
handler can have at most one update composed at a time.

Composing an update takes a full copy of the record's current contents as the
update's base, stamps it with the version the handler read, and names one routing
entry to add. Composed updates sit waiting and are picked up by the router in
whatever order it likes, with no ordering guarantee at all, so an update composed
early can easily be picked up after several later ones have already landed.

Picking up an update applies it only if the version stamped on it is still the
record's version and the version counter has room left; applying replaces the
record's contents with the update's base plus the named entry and bumps the
version. An update that cannot be applied, because the version has moved on or
the version counter is exhausted, is rejected and its handler is noted as having
had to retry. Separately, the router can drop a routing entry out of the record,
which is itself a write and so bumps the version too; every entry ever dropped
this way is noted in the router's drop log.

composed update whose version still matches, reject a composed update that cannot
be applied, and drop a routing entry out of the record while noting it in the drop log.

record's current version has a base equal to the record's present contents, so an
update can never be applied on top of a write that landed after that update was
composed.

applied to the record or rejected.

A container-ship crane yard discharges containers under a two-phase commit across

agree before a discharge happens. Discharging is the irreversible step, and each
discharge job may be discharged at most once.

job carries the set of participants that have voted yes in its current preparing
round. A job that is idle and has not already been discharged can be moved into
preparing, which starts its vote set empty. A participant that has not crashed and
has not already voted for the job in this round can vote yes.

A preparing job whose vote set covers every participant moves to committed. A
preparing job can instead be aborted whenever some participant has crashed, which
clears its votes and puts it in the aborted phase; an aborted job can be reset back
to idle so it can be tried again.

committed job that has not already been discharged, and it does three things at
once: it records the job as discharged, it clears the job's votes, and it retires
the commit decision by putting the job back into the idle phase, so nothing is left
standing in the committed phase behind a job that has already gone.

A participant can crash silently, changing nothing else, and a crashed participant
can be restarted.

yes for a preparing job, commit a preparing job whose votes cover every
participant, abort a preparing job while some participant is crashed, reset an
aborted job to idle, perform the discharge of a committed job, crash a participant
silently, and restart a crashed participant.

committed phase, so the commit decision that authorises the irreversible discharge
is never left standing where it could authorise a second one.

preparing phase.

A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps one shared record: the set of stock
adjustments that have been applied, together with a version number that every
write to the record bumps. Each adjustment needs a quorum of the bank's duty
officers to approve it, and each adjustment carries its own tally of the officers
whose votes have been counted for it.

An officer with no vote already travelling for an adjustment, and not already
counted in that adjustment's tally, can cast a vote for it. Votes travel on a
channel with no ordering guarantee, so a cast vote waits in flight and is picked
up in whatever order the tracker gets to it. Picking a vote up adds the officer to
that adjustment's tally. A vote in flight for an adjustment that has already been
approved is simply thrown away as too late.

Once an adjustment's tally is a strict majority of the duty officers and it has
not been approved yet, it is approved and applied in the same step: the adjustment
is added to the approved set and added to the record's applied set, and the record's
version is bumped.

The tracker also compacts the record from time to time. Compaction is a two-step
whole-record rewrite: first a snapshot of the record's applied set and version is
taken, and later the snapshot is written back over the record. The write-back is
only accepted while the version on the snapshot is still the record's version and
the version counter has room; a snapshot that has gone stale, or that arrives with
the version counter exhausted, is discarded instead.

add it to that adjustment's tally, throw away a vote for an already-approved
adjustment, approve and apply an adjustment that has reached a majority, take a
snapshot of the record, write a snapshot back over the record while its version
still matches, and discard a snapshot that cannot be written back.

record's applied set, so no whole-record compaction ever drops an approved
adjustment that landed after the snapshot was taken.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every vote that is in flight is eventually taken out of flight.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container-ship crane yard hands berth slots to its cranes through a bounded
work queue with backpressure. The queue holds the slots that are waiting to be
handed out, in order, and each slot separately records the crane it has been
granted to, or that it is ungranted.

A slot that is currently ungranted and not already somewhere in the queue can be
admitted onto the tail of the queue, as long as the queue is shorter than its
capacity. When the queue is already at capacity the request is refused on the spot
and the refusal is counted, which is the backpressure the yard planners see.

A crane takes the slot at the head of the queue and has it granted to it, which
removes that entry from the queue. A crane may be running slow, which stops it
taking new work off the queue; a slow crane is never out of action altogether, so
it keeps the slots already granted to it and can still give them back. Cranes move
in and out of the slow state freely. A crane can release a slot granted to it,
which marks the slot ungranted again and makes it eligible to be queued afresh.

The complete set of actions is: admit an ungranted, unqueued slot onto the tail of
the queue, refuse a request because the queue is at capacity, take the head slot
off the queue and grant it to a crane, release a slot granted to a crane, put a
crane into the slow state, and take a crane out of the slow state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no slot sitting anywhere in the request queue is already granted
to a crane, so a slot can never be handed out a second time while an earlier grant
of it still stands.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A regional blood-bank inventory tracker manages one shared pool of refrigerated storage slots. Two independent tracking instances run against that single pool. Neither instance can see the other's internal state; they interact only through the pool and through the pool's serialized commit journal, a first-in-first-out queue of reservation rounds waiting to be resolved by the participating fridge controllers under two-phase commit.

The system behaves as follows. An idle instance may Begin a reservation by choosing a storage slot that looks unowned at that moment, entering its preparing phase and appending a round record naming itself and the chosen slot to the tail of the commit journal. Only the round at the head of the journal is actively being voted on. While that head round is short of a full set of votes, the CollectVote step records one more fridge controller's yes vote for it. Alternatively RefuseHead may fire while the head round is still short of a full set of votes: a controller declines, the round is discarded from the journal, its vote tally resets and the owning instance returns to idle. Once the head round has collected a vote from every controller, it resolves in one of two ways. CommitHead applies when the pool still shows the round's slot as unowned: the pool records the round's instance as the slot's owner, that instance adds the slot to its own set of held slots, the round leaves the journal, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. AbortStaleHead applies when the pool instead shows the slot already owned, because the other instance won the race while this round was collecting votes: the round is discarded with no change to the pool, the tally resets and the instance returns to idle. Finally, an instance may Release a slot it holds, which removes the slot from its held set and marks the slot unowned in the pool in the same step.

The hazard is that both instances can have live rounds for the very same slot, since Begin only inspects the pool at the instant it fires and the pool can change while a round waits in the journal. Correctness rests entirely on the commit-time re-check and on Release updating local bookkeeping and the shared pool together.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot that the shared pool records as owned appears in the held set of the very instance the pool names as its owner.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instance that enters its preparing phase eventually returns to idle.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A county library book reservation system spreads reservation authority across branch libraries. Each physical copy of a title has a numbered hold slot, and any branch may place a patron's hold into a slot. Because branches come and go from the cooperative, the system uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a single configuration epoch counter advances every time a branch joins or leaves, and a branch may only place holds while the epoch it knows about matches the current epoch. A branch can be slow without being failed, so a branch that has fallen behind is still running and still receiving requests; it simply has an out-of-date epoch number until it catches up.

The system behaves as follows. Reserve places a hold: an active branch whose known epoch equals the current epoch may take a slot that the shared registry shows as unclaimed, writing itself into the registry for that slot and adding the slot to its own list of placed holds. Return releases a hold: a branch that has a slot in its own list, and that the registry also attributes to it, clears the registry entry and drops the slot from its list. CatchUp models the slow branch: a branch whose known epoch is behind the current epoch advances its known epoch to the current value, after which it may act again. Reconfigure removes an active branch from the cooperative: the epoch counter advances, the branch leaves the configuration, and every hold it was holding is revoked from both its own list and the shared registry in the same step. Rejoin admits a branch that is not currently in the configuration: the epoch counter advances, the branch enters the configuration, and it starts out knowing the new epoch.

The hazard is that a branch which has fallen behind, or one that has been dropped from the configuration entirely, may still try to place holds on slots it believes are free, which is exactly how the same slot ends up allocated twice. The epoch match required by Reserve, together with the revocation performed by Reconfigure, is what stands between the cooperative and a double-booked copy.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slot that a branch lists among its own placed holds is attributed to that same branch by the shared registry.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

NoBranch == "nobranch"

VARIABLES epoch, config, known, registry, placed

vars == <<epoch, config, known, registry, placed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ config \subseteq Branches
    /\ known \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ registry \in [Slots -> Branches \cup {NoBranch}]
    /\ placed \in [Branches -> SUBSET Slots]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ config = Branches
    /\ known = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ registry = [s \in Slots |-> NoBranch]
    /\ placed = [b \in Branches |-> {}]

Reserve(b, s) ==
    /\ b \in config
    /\ known[b] = epoch
    /\ registry[s] = NoBranch
    /\ registry' = [registry EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![b] = placed[b] \cup {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, known>>

Return(b, s) ==
    /\ s \in placed[b]
    /\ registry[s] = b
    /\ registry' = [registry EXCEPT ![s] = NoBranch]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![b] = placed[b] \ {s}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, known>>

CatchUp(b) ==

    /\ known' = [known EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, config, registry, placed>>

Reconfigure(b) ==

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A university course-registration system seats students into individual numbered seats of a course section. Seating is not done unilaterally: the registrar opens a registration transaction and runs a two-phase commit across the departmental approvers, and only one transaction is open at a time. A privileged administrator override exists for exceptional cases, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. Open starts a transaction: with no transaction currently open, the registrar picks a student and a seat that the seating chart shows as empty, records the pair as the open transaction and clears the approval set. Approve records one departmental approver's consent for the open transaction; an approver who has already consented cannot consent twice. Reject models an approver refusing: while a transaction is open, an approver who has not yet consented may kill it outright, which discards the transaction and clears the approval set without touching the seating chart or any roster. Commit completes the normal path: when every approver has consented and the seat is still empty on the chart, the chart records the student in that seat, the seat is added to the student's roster, the transaction closes and the approval set clears. AdminOverride is the exceptional path: while a transaction is open, the seat is still empty and override budget remains, the administrator seats the student immediately without waiting for the approvers, consuming one unit of override budget, updating chart and roster together and closing the transaction. Drop removes a seating: a student who has a seat on their roster gives it up, clearing the chart entry and the roster entry in the same step.

The hazard the design guards against is the same seat being handed to two students, which would happen if the roster and the seating chart were ever allowed to disagree — in particular if the override path updated one without the other, or if a commit landed on a seat that had already been filled.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A network of vending machines runs a promotional voucher campaign. Redeeming a voucher is irreversible: the machine drops the item and there is no way to put it back, so a voucher must be dispensed against at most once across the whole network. The fleet is coordinated by epoch-numbered reconfiguration. A single campaign epoch counter is bumped whenever headquarters changes the campaign, and each change also resets how many vouchers the campaign will honour in total, so the campaign capacity varies at runtime. A machine may only dispense while the epoch it knows matches the current campaign epoch. Alongside the authoritative record of which machine dispensed each voucher, the network keeps an append-only audit log of dispense events, each stamped with the epoch in force when it was written.

The system behaves as follows. Reconfigure bumps the campaign epoch and simultaneously sets a new campaign capacity, which may be larger or smaller than before. SyncAll is the headquarters broadcast: whenever at least one machine is behind, every machine in the fleet is brought up to the current epoch in one step. Dispense is the irreversible act: a machine whose known epoch matches the campaign epoch, faced with a voucher that the authoritative record shows as never dispensed, and with the number of already-dispensed vouchers still below the campaign capacity, records itself against that voucher and writes an audit entry naming the voucher, itself, and the current epoch. Replay covers duplicate customer requests: a machine that the record already shows as the dispenser of a voucher may write a fresh audit entry for it at the current epoch without dropping a second item. Reset models a machine rebooting and losing its campaign state, dropping its known epoch back to zero so that it is stale until the next broadcast.

The failure this design must exclude is a second, different machine dispensing against a voucher that has already been honoured, which would show up as an audit entry attributing the voucher to a machine other than the one on record.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the audit log names the very machine that the authoritative record shows as the dispenser of that entry's voucher.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine that has fallen behind the campaign epoch eventually knows the current epoch.

Alongside the record the network keeps a settlement log: one entry per accepted change, recording which record version that change was computed against and the adjustment it applied.

The system behaves as follows. Read refreshes one machine's view, setting the version it believes current to the record's actual current version. Propose opens a change round when no round is open: the proposing machine names the version it last read as the base of its change, names the adjustment it wants, and the vote set starts empty. Vote records one machine's support for the open round; no machine votes twice in a round. CommitUpdate closes the round successfully when a strict majority of machines has voted and the round's base version is still the record's current version: the version counter advances by one and a settlement log entry is written recording the base version that was superseded and the adjustment applied. AbortStaleRound closes the round unsuccessfully when a strict majority has voted but the record has moved on since the round's base was read; the round is thrown away, nothing is logged and the version counter does not move.

The danger is a lost update: a change computed against an old version quietly overwriting a change that landed in between, which would leave a gap or a duplicate in the chain of superseded versions recorded by the settlement log.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An air-traffic runway allocator hands departure slots to ground controllers using a two-level lock hierarchy: a controller must first take the single airport lock, and only then may it take the lock on an individual runway. Every aircraft in the fleet is accounted for at all times — it is either waiting in the holding stack, sitting on a runway, or already departed. Controllers can be slow without being failed: a controller may sit on the airport lock for as long as it likes, and the rest of the field simply waits.

The system behaves as follows. AcquireAirport gives a controller the airport lock when it is free, and starts that controller's session with an empty set of runways already used. AcquireRunway gives the controller holding the airport lock the lock on a free runway, provided that runway has not already been used and given back during this session. MoveToRunway takes one aircraft out of the holding stack and places it on an empty runway whose lock the controller holds. Depart sends the aircraft on a runway the controller holds on its way, emptying the runway and incrementing the departed count. ReleaseRunway gives back a runway lock the controller holds, but only when that runway is empty, and records the runway as used for the remainder of the session so it cannot be taken again before the airport lock changes hands. ReleaseAirport gives back the airport lock, and requires that the controller is holding no runway locks at all; the used-runway set is cleared for the next session.

Because an aircraft sitting on a runway has left the holding stack but has not departed, the runway occupancy is part of the accounting; a move that took an aircraft off the stack without putting it anywhere, or a departure that emptied a runway without counting the aircraft out, would break the books immediately.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The aircraft in the holding stack, the aircraft occupying runways, and the aircraft that have departed always add up to the fixed size of the fleet.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The airport lock, once taken, is always eventually given back.

    /\ used = {}

AcquireAirport(c) ==

    /\ used' = {}

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A bank's interbank settlement batch runs on a small cluster of settlement servers with leader election and failover. Only an elected leader may wire a batch, and wiring is irreversible: the funds leave and there is no unwinding the transfer. Each batch is identified by a number that is also the amount it moves. The bank tracks the total value wired so far, and the settlement window's capacity — the total value the window will allow — is recapitalised at runtime by the treasury and may be raised or lowered at any moment.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a fresh election: the term counter advances, the leadership for the new term is vacant, and the campaigning server is the sole initial member of the vote set. Vote adds a server to the vote set for the election currently under way. TakeLeadership makes a server that is in the vote set the leader, provided a strict majority of the cluster has voted and no leader has yet been established for this term. Wire is the irreversible act: with a leader established, a batch that is still pending is wired, provided the value already wired plus this batch's amount stays within the settlement window's capacity; the batch moves to the wired state and its amount is added to the running wired total. Recapitalise sets the settlement window's capacity to any new value, which may be below what has already been wired.

The books have to balance: the running wired total is the bank's authoritative statement of how much has left, and the set of batches marked wired is the authoritative statement of what left. A batch wired a second time would add its amount to the running total again without changing the set of wired batches, and the two statements would immediately disagree.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The running wired total always equals the sum of the amounts of exactly those batches marked as wired.

An airport baggage router has a number of sorting stations arranged in a ring, all writing to the same set of diverter chutes. A single token circulates around the ring and only the station holding the token may program a chute's destination; when the token moves on, every routing that station programmed is wiped, because a routing left behind by a station that no longer holds the token is a stale instruction that could send a bag to the wrong pier. A privileged duty-manager override exists that can hand the token directly to a chosen station out of ring order, and the override budget is finite.

The system behaves as follows. SetRoute lets the station holding the token program an unprogrammed chute, recording itself as the station that programmed it. ClearRoute lets the token holder unprogram a chute it programmed. RouteBag sends one waiting bag down a programmed chute that has no bag on it already, decreasing the number of bags still waiting and putting that chute into the in-transit state. DeliverBag completes a bag's journey, taking the chute out of the in-transit state. PassToken hands the token to the next station around the ring and wipes every chute programming in the same step; it may only fire when no bag is in transit, so the router never re-programmes a chute out from underneath a moving bag. AdminForce is the privileged path: the duty manager hands the token directly to any other station, spending one unit of override budget, and this also wipes every chute programming and likewise requires that nothing is in transit.

A library book reservation system is fronted by two independent reservation portals that share one pool of loanable copies. Neither portal locks the pool; they use optimistic locking with retry instead. A portal reads the pool's version number together with the count of active reservations, decides what it wants to do, and only commits if the version it read is still the pool's version — and every commit advances the version. Because the version has a finite range in this model, commits stop once it is exhausted. The whole point of the version check is that a portal which validated the shelf capacity at read time can trust that check at commit time, so the commit itself does not re-examine the capacity.

The system behaves as follows. BeginAdd starts an add on an idle portal, but only after the portal has seen that the active-reservation count is below the shelf capacity; the portal records the version it read. BeginDrop starts a drop on an idle portal, provided there is at least one active reservation, and likewise records the version it read. CommitAdd applies an add when the recorded version still matches the pool's version: the active count goes up by one and the version advances. CommitDrop applies a drop under the same version match: the active count goes down by one and the version advances. Retry handles the conflict case: a portal whose recorded version no longer matches re-reads the pool, spending one unit of its retry allowance; the re-read takes in both the current version and the current active count, so a retry is only possible while the portal's intent is still viable — an add needs the count to still be below capacity, a drop needs at least one active reservation. Abandon lets a portal whose recorded version no longer matches simply give up and go idle.

The interesting failure is both portals reading the same below-capacity count, then both committing an add: that is exactly what the version match rules out, since whichever portal commits first advances the version and forces the other into retry or abandonment.

An elevator bank in a skyscraper boards riders into one car under a strict load limit. Several floor controllers all try to board riders at once, and they coordinate through a compare-and-swap on the car's load register: a controller reads the current load, checks it against the rated capacity, and later swaps in the incremented value only if the load register still reads exactly what it read. Because the swap only succeeds when nothing has changed, the capacity check made at read time is still valid at swap time, and the swap deliberately does not re-check it. The rated capacity itself changes at runtime — building services lowers it for heavy-goods runs and raises it again afterwards — and that is done under a service mode that first invalidates every outstanding read.

Read has an idle controller take a snapshot of the current load, and requires the car not to be in service mode and the load to be below the rated capacity at that moment. CasBoard is the swap: a controller holding a snapshot that still matches the load register boards its rider, raising the load by one and going back to idle; it is blocked while the car is in service mode. CasFail is the losing side of a race: a controller whose snapshot no longer matches the load register discards it and goes back to idle. Alight takes one rider out of the car, lowering the load and advancing the alighted tally, which saturates at its maximum. EnterService puts the car into service mode and discards every controller's snapshot in the same step. SetCapacity changes the rated capacity to a new value, and may only be done while the car is in service mode and only to a value that is not below the number of riders currently in the car, since lowering the rating cannot make riders vanish. LeaveService takes the car back out of service mode so boarding can resume.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker is run by two independent matchmaking instances that draw from one shared pool of waiting players. Every player is always in exactly one of three places: waiting in the shared pool, reserved by one of the two instances for a match it is trying to form, or already playing in a formed match. Forming a match is a two-phase commit across the region shards, and the shared pool has a single commit gate, so only one match-forming round is ever in flight; the two instances contend for that gate.

The system behaves as follows. OpenRound starts a round when the gate is free: an instance takes some number of players out of the shared pool and into its own reserved count, records the round with its own name and that party size, and starts the round with an empty vote set. Vote records one region shard's agreement with the round in flight. CommitRound closes a round that every region shard has agreed to: the reserved players of the round's instance move into the playing count and the gate is released. AbortRound closes a round that a region shard refuses before voting: the round's reserved players go straight back into the shared pool, the vote set clears, and the gate is released. Disband ends matches: a number of players who are playing return to the shared pool.

Note that a player reserved by an instance is out of the pool but not yet playing, so the reservation counts are as much a part of the census as the pool itself; a commit that moved players into the playing count without drawing down the reservation, or an abort that released the gate without giving the players back, would invent or lose players outright.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A university course-registration system hands blocks of seats out to registrar nodes on leases before those seats can be turned into enrolments. Every seat in a course is always in exactly one of three states: free in the course's pool, leased to one of the registrar nodes, or enrolled to a student. Release instructions travel over a network that can reorder them freely: an instruction is put into a pool of in-flight messages and may be picked up at any later moment, in any order relative to other instructions, and possibly long after the lease it was issued under has already timed out.

The system behaves as follows. Lease moves a block of free seats into a registrar node's leased count and starts that node's lease countdown at its full value. Enrol converts some of a node's leased seats into enrolments, moving them out of the leased count and into the enrolled count. SendRelease is the node deciding to give some of its leased seats back: it puts a release instruction naming itself and a seat count into the in-flight message pool, but the seats stay leased until the instruction is actually applied. ApplyRelease picks any in-flight instruction out of the pool and applies it, moving that many seats from the named node's leased count back to the free pool; it may only fire while that node still has at least that many seats leased. DropRelease discards an in-flight instruction that the named node can no longer honour because it no longer has that many seats leased. Tick advances the clock, decrementing every lease countdown that is above zero. ExpireLeases fires when at least one node's countdown has reached zero with seats still leased, and returns all of that node's leased seats to the free pool in one step.

The reordering is what makes this delicate: an expiry can reclaim a node's seats while a release instruction for those same seats is still in flight, and applying that instruction afterwards would hand the same seats back a second time.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps the day's theatre schedule in a single shared document that exactly one node may be writing at a time. Which node has that right is decided by leader election with failover: a term counter advances with each election, a node wins a term by collecting a strict majority of votes, and if the leader goes quiet another node simply starts a new term. Nodes can be slow without being failed — a node that has not heard about the latest term is still running, still able to vote, and catches up the moment it does hear.

The system behaves as follows. Campaign starts a new election: the term counter advances, the leadership of the new term begins vacant, the campaigning node adopts the new term and becomes the sole initial voter, and any write in progress is fenced off in the same step, because the whole point of starting a term is to stop the previous leader from continuing to write. Vote is a slow node catching up: a node whose own term is behind adopts the current term and joins the vote set for it. TakeLeadership makes a node in the vote set the leader of the current term, provided it is itself up to date on the term and a strict majority of the cluster has voted, and provided the term does not already have a leader. StartWrite lets the leader of the current term, which is up to date, begin writing the schedule when nobody is writing. StopWrite ends the write in progress. StepDown lets the leader give up the leadership of the current term while nobody is writing, leaving the term without a leader until someone campaigns again.

The document is corrupted the moment two hands are on it, so the schedule may only ever be written by the node that is the current term's leader, and a leader that has been displaced by a new term must stop immediately rather than finishing what it started.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of nodes writing the schedule never contains anyone other than the current term's leader.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A write in progress is always eventually finished.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library book reservation system also handles withdrawal from circulation, and shredding a title's catalogue card is irreversible — once the card is through the shredder there is no reconstructing it. A branch may only order a shredding while it holds the lease on that title's record. Leases time out on their own, and every timeout advances that title's lease generation. Shred orders travel as notices over a network that can reorder and delay them arbitrarily, so a notice issued under one lease may only surface long after that lease has gone; every notice therefore carries the lease generation it was issued under.

The system behaves as follows. Acquire gives a branch the lease on a title whose record nobody holds. Expire times a lease out: the title's record becomes unheld and its lease generation advances. IssueOrder lets the branch holding a title's lease write itself into the record as the branch that ordered the shredding, provided no order stands already, and puts a notice naming the title, itself, and the current lease generation into the network. ReissueNotice covers a notice that appears to have been lost: while an order stands, another notice for it is put into the network stamped with the title's current lease generation. Rescind lets the holding branch call the order off while the card is still intact: the recorded order is cleared and the lease generation advances, which is what makes every notice already in flight stale. DeliverNotice is the irreversible step: a notice in the network whose lease generation still matches the title's, whose named branch still matches the recorded order, and whose card is still intact, shreds the card and leaves the network. DropStaleNotice discards a notice whose lease generation no longer matches the title's.

The scenario to exclude is a notice that was issued, then overtaken by a rescission, arriving late and shredding a card that no longer has any order behind it at all.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital operating-room scheduler keeps one shared theatre record that is updated by two-phase commit across the surgical departments. Each round of the protocol is based on the record's version at the moment the round opened, and a round only commits if that base version is still current. Acknowledgements travel over a network that reorders freely, so an acknowledgement sent for one round can arrive after a later round has already opened; every acknowledgement therefore carries the base version it was sent for, and the coordinator refuses to count one whose base does not match the round now in progress. Alongside the record the scheduler keeps an applied-marker for each version, which is set when that version is superseded by a committed round.

The system behaves as follows. BeginRound opens a round while the coordinator is idle and the record still has room to advance: the round's base is set to the record's current version and the acknowledgement set starts empty. Notice that the network is not flushed, so acknowledgements left over from earlier rounds are still out there. SendAck puts one department's acknowledgement for the round in progress onto the network, provided that department has not already acknowledged this round and does not already have an acknowledgement for it in flight. ReceiveAck takes any acknowledgement off the network in any order; it counts towards the round only if the base version it carries matches the round in progress, and is otherwise simply consumed. RefuseRound is a department declining: the round in progress is abandoned and the coordinator goes idle. Prepare moves a round whose acknowledgement set covers every department into the prepared state. CommitRound applies a prepared round: the record's version advances by one and the applied-marker for the base version is set, after which the coordinator goes idle.

An update is lost if a version is superseded without being marked, or if a version at or beyond the record's current one is marked as though it had been superseded — which is what happens when a stale acknowledgement is allowed to carry a round to commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The versions carrying an applied-marker are exactly those strictly below the record's current version.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A round that has been opened is always eventually closed.

A smart-home door lock network is managed by two independent hubs that share one pool of lock controllers; each controller answers to one hub or the other, and controllers are handed between the hubs while the house is live.
