---- MODULE W4Od8m5p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Servers, Students, MaxEpoch, MaxLimit, NoServer

\* servedBy points from the student to the server holding their session; the
\* safety property reads the server's epoch through that pointer.
VARIABLES epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit

vars == << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit >>

Current(s) == srvEpoch[s] = epoch
Backers(s) == {k \in Servers : endorse[k] = s}
Entitled(s) == Current(s) /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(s)) > Cardinality(Servers)
OpenSessions == Cardinality({st \in Students : servedBy[st] # NoServer})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ srvEpoch \in [Servers -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ endorse \in [Servers -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ servedBy \in [Students -> Servers \cup {NoServer}]
    /\ state \in [Students -> {"waiting", "enrolled", "turned"}]
    /\ limit \in 0..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ srvEpoch = [s \in Servers |-> 0]
    /\ endorse = [s \in Servers |-> NoServer]
    /\ servedBy = [st \in Students |-> NoServer]
    /\ state = [st \in Students |-> "waiting"]
    /\ limit = 1

Resync(s) ==
    /\ ~Current(s)
    /\ srvEpoch' = [srvEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, endorse, servedBy, state, limit >>

Endorse(k, s) ==
    /\ Current(k)
    /\ Current(s)
    /\ endorse[k] # s
    /\ endorse' = [endorse EXCEPT ![k] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, servedBy, state, limit >>

OpenSession(s, st) ==
    /\ Entitled(s)
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ servedBy[st] = NoServer
    /\ OpenSessions < limit
    /\ servedBy' = [servedBy EXCEPT ![st] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, state, limit >>

Enrol(st) ==
    /\ servedBy[st] # NoServer
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![st] = "enrolled"]
    /\ servedBy' = [servedBy EXCEPT ![st] = NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, limit >>

\* A student is turned away when the registry is full, and also when no server
\* is entitled to serve anyone at all -- a split endorsement is not a reason to
\* leave someone queued for ever.
TurnAway(st) ==
    /\ state[st] = "waiting"
    /\ servedBy[st] = NoServer
    /\ \/ OpenSessions >= limit
       \/ \A s \in Servers : ~Entitled(s)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![st] = "turned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, limit >>

\* Reconfiguration voids standing and drops every session, because the server
\* holding one may no longer be entitled to it.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ endorse' = [k \in Servers |-> NoServer]
    /\ servedBy' = [st \in Students |-> NoServer]
    /\ UNCHANGED << srvEpoch, state, limit >>

SetLimit(l) ==
    /\ l # limit
    /\ l >= OpenSessions
    /\ limit' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, srvEpoch, endorse, servedBy, state >>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Servers : Resync(s)
    \/ \E k \in Servers, s \in Servers : Endorse(k, s)
    \/ \E s \in Servers, st \in Students : OpenSession(s, st)
    \/ \E st \in Students : Enrol(st) \/ TurnAway(st)
    \/ \E l \in 0..MaxLimit : SetLimit(l)
    \/ Reconfigure

\* Sessions and turn-aways both flicker with the epoch and the limit, so each
\* student needs strong fairness on getting served and on being turned away.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A st \in Students :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ SF_vars(\E s \in Servers : OpenSession(s, st))
        /\ SF_vars(Enrol(st))
        /\ SF_vars(TurnAway(st))
    /\ \A s \in Servers :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Resync(s))

SessionsAreHeldByCurrentServers ==
    \A st \in Students : servedBy[st] # NoServer => srvEpoch[servedBy[st]] = epoch

EveryWaitingStudentSettles ==
    \A st \in Students : (state[st] = "waiting") ~> (state[st] \in {"enrolled", "turned"})

====

A planner holding no snapshot may read the plan, taking its stamp and a copy of the case set. A planner holding a snapshot but no chosen case may choose a case that is not already in its snapshot. A planner holding a snapshot and a chosen case may confirm it if the plan's stamp still matches what it read: the plan becomes that planner's snapshot plus the chosen case, the case joins that planner's own system's confirmation list, the stamp advances, and the snapshot and choice are cleared. A planner whose stamp no longer matches the plan retries, discarding its snapshot and its choice. A planner may drop its chosen case while keeping its snapshot, and may abandon a snapshot entirely and read again later.

SystemOf(p) == IF p \in MainSite THEN "main" ELSE "annexe"

TypeOK ==

    /\ plan \in SUBSET Cases
    /\ snapStamp \in [Planners -> (0..MaxVersion) \cup {NoStamp}]
    /\ snapSet \in [Planners -> SUBSET Cases]
    /\ choice \in [Planners -> Cases \cup {NoCase}]
    /\ confirmed \in [Systems -> SUBSET Cases]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ plan = {}
    /\ snapStamp = [p \in Planners |-> NoStamp]
    /\ snapSet = [p \in Planners |-> {}]
    /\ choice = [p \in Planners |-> NoCase]
    /\ confirmed = [k \in Systems |-> {}]

ReadPlan(p) ==
    /\ snapStamp[p] = NoStamp
    /\ snapStamp' = [snapStamp EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = plan]

    /\ snapSet' = [snapSet EXCEPT ![p] = {}]
    /\ choice' = [choice EXCEPT ![p] = NoCase]

Retry(p) ==

    /\ snapStamp[p] # version

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A clearing house opens settlement channels from its settlement nodes to each counterparty bank. A counterparty will only accept so many channels at once, and a channel that a node has begun opening but not yet completed already counts against that counterparty, because the counterparty has reserved the line for it. The service runs in numbered configurations: reconfiguration advances the epoch and every node must resynchronise before it may begin opening anything. The treasury desk holds a bounded number of privileged closures for channels that must be torn down without waiting for the node that owns them.

A node whose epoch is behind the service's may resynchronise. A node that has resynchronised, and that has no channel of its own, may begin opening a channel to a counterparty, provided that counterparty's channels already open plus those already being opened are below its limit. A node that is opening a channel may complete it. A node with an open channel may close it. The treasury desk may force any node's channel closed, whether it is open or still opening, spending one privileged closure. The service may reconfigure while it has configurations left in its schedule, which advances the epoch; channels already open or opening are not disturbed by it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every counterparty bank, the channels open to it plus the channels being opened to it never exceed that counterparty's channel limit.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

\* A half-open channel has already reserved the counterparty's line, so both
\* terms below count against that counterparty's limit.
VARIABLES epoch, nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures

vars == << epoch, nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures >>

Committed(b) ==
    Cardinality({n \in Nodes : open[n] = b})
      + Cardinality({n \in Nodes : opening[n] = b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ nodeEpoch \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ opening \in [Nodes -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ open \in [Nodes -> Banks \cup {NoBank}]
    /\ closures \in 0..MaxClosures

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ nodeEpoch = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
    /\ opening = [n \in Nodes |-> NoBank]
    /\ open = [n \in Nodes |-> NoBank]
    /\ closures = 0

Resync(n) ==
    /\ nodeEpoch[n] # epoch
    /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, opening, open, closures >>

BeginOpen(n, b) ==

    /\ opening[n] = NoBank
    /\ open[n] = NoBank
    /\ Committed(b) < ChannelLimit
    /\ opening' = [opening EXCEPT ![n] = b]

CompleteOpen(n) ==

    /\ opening' = [opening EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]
    /\ UNCHANGED << epoch, nodeEpoch, closures >>

Close(n) ==

ForceClose(n) ==

    /\ open' = [open EXCEPT ![n] = NoBank]

    /\ UNCHANGED << nodeEpoch, opening, open, closures >>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A blood bank holds product in numbered storage slots and leases a slot to an order while that order is being made up. A lease is not permanent: it carries a countdown and lapses if the order is not completed in time. Every slot carries a lease generation, and a lease handed to an order is stamped with the generation the slot had when it was granted; granting a slot advances its generation, so any older lease on it is dead paper. How many slots the bank will have out on lease at once is a runtime setting the duty manager raises and lowers as the fridge fills, never below the leases already out.

The bank may grant a slot to an order that holds none, provided the slot is held by nobody, and provided the leases already out are below the current setting: the slot's generation advances, the order's lease is stamped with that new generation, and the countdown starts full. The bank's clock may tick while at least one lease still has countdown left, running down every live lease at once. A lease whose countdown has reached zero may be reclaimed, which takes the slot back from the order. An order holding a slot may complete, releasing the slot. The duty manager may set the lease limit to any different value that is not below the leases currently out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every order holding a slot holds it under a lease stamped with that slot's current generation, so a slot handed on to a new order leaves no older holder behind.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that has been granted a slot eventually stops holding it.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Orders, StorageSlots, MaxGen, LeaseTicks, MaxLimit, NoSlot

\* Granting a slot advances its generation, so an order still pointing at a
\* slot under an older stamp is exactly what the invariant rules out.
VARIABLES heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit

vars == << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit >>

OnLease == Cardinality({o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot})

TypeOK ==
    /\ heldSlot \in [Orders -> StorageSlots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ leaseGen \in [Orders -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ slotGen \in [StorageSlots -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ ttl \in [Orders -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ limit \in 0..MaxLimit

Init ==
    /\ heldSlot = [o \in Orders |-> NoSlot]
    /\ leaseGen = [o \in Orders |-> 0]
    /\ slotGen = [s \in StorageSlots |-> 0]
    /\ ttl = [o \in Orders |-> 0]
    /\ limit = 1

Grant(o, s) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] = NoSlot
    /\ \A p \in Orders : heldSlot[p] # s
    /\ slotGen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ OnLease < limit
    /\ slotGen' = [slotGen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ leaseGen' = [leaseGen EXCEPT ![o] = slotGen[s] + 1]
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = s]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![o] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED << limit >>

\* The clock runs every live lease down together.
Tick ==
    /\ \E o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot /\ ttl[o] > 0
    /\ ttl' = [o \in Orders |->
                 IF heldSlot[o] # NoSlot /\ ttl[o] > 0 THEN ttl[o] - 1 ELSE ttl[o]]
    /\ UNCHANGED << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, limit >>

Reclaim(o) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] # NoSlot
    /\ ttl[o] = 0
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseGen, slotGen, ttl, limit >>

Complete(o) ==
    /\ heldSlot[o] # NoSlot
    /\ heldSlot' = [heldSlot EXCEPT ![o] = NoSlot]
    /\ ttl' = [ttl EXCEPT ![o] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED << leaseGen, slotGen, limit >>

SetLimit(l) ==
    /\ l # limit
    /\ l >= OnLease
    /\ limit' = l
    /\ UNCHANGED << heldSlot, leaseGen, slotGen, ttl >>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Orders, s \in StorageSlots : Grant(o, s)
    \/ \E o \in Orders : Reclaim(o) \/ Complete(o)
    \/ \E l \in 0..MaxLimit : SetLimit(l)
    \/ Tick

\* Completing is never blocked, so weak fairness per order is enough to see
\* every lease given back.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A o \in Orders :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(Complete(o))

LeasesCarryTheirSlotsGeneration ==
    \A o \in Orders : heldSlot[o] # NoSlot => leaseGen[o] = slotGen[heldSlot[o]]

EveryLeaseIsGivenBack ==
    \A o \in Orders : (heldSlot[o] # NoSlot) ~> (heldSlot[o] = NoSlot)

====

A stored unit may be issued out of the refrigerator. The estates team may set a refrigerator's capacity to any different value that is not below its stored units plus its outstanding leases.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway interlocking lets signallers set routes through the junction. Each route has a register in the interlocking that either reads free or names the signaller that set it, and signallers take routes by compare-and-swap: a signaller reads a route's register, then writes its own name in only if the register still reads what it read. Setting a route is an authorised act, and the control centre withdraws a signaller's authority when a panel is handed over or a rating lapses. Signallers are slow rather than failed: at most one at a time is off the panel, and always comes back -- and the control centre will not withdraw authority from a signaller it cannot reach, because withdrawal has to give up that signaller's routes at the same moment.

A signaller on the panel holding no outstanding read may read any route's register, remembering the route and what it saw. A signaller on the panel whose read still matches that route's register, whose read said the route was free, and who has authority, may set the route: the register takes its name and the read is cleared. A signaller whose remembered value no longer matches the register discards the read. A signaller may give up a route its name is on. The control centre may withdraw authority from a signaller it can reach, which strikes that signaller's name off every route it holds in the same movement, and may restore authority to a signaller that has none. Finally, the one signaller on the panel may step off, and the signaller who stepped off may come back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No route is ever left set in the name of a signaller whose authority has been withdrawn.

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Routes -> Signallers \cup {Free}]
    /\ readOn \in [Signallers -> Routes \cup {NoRoute}]

    /\ readOn = [s \in Signallers |-> NoRoute]
    /\ readVal = [s \in Signallers |-> NoRead]

    /\ offPanel = NoSignaller

ReadRoute(s, r) ==
    /\ s # offPanel
    /\ readOn[s] = NoRoute
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = r]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = reg[r]]

\* route is set.
SetRoute(s) ==
    /\ s # offPanel
    /\ s \notin withdrawn
    /\ readOn[s] # NoRoute
    /\ readVal[s] = Free
    /\ reg[readOn[s]] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![readOn[s]] = s]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoRoute]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << withdrawn, offPanel >>

StaleRead(s) ==
    /\ readOn[s] # NoRoute
    /\ readVal[s] # reg[readOn[s]]
    /\ readOn' = [readOn EXCEPT ![s] = NoRoute]
    /\ readVal' = [readVal EXCEPT ![s] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED << reg, withdrawn, offPanel >>

GiveUpRoute(s, r) ==

    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![r] = Free]

    \/ StepOn

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container terminal keeps one stow plan: which loading instruction occupies each bay of the ship. The plan is written only by the elected yard master, and the yard master's chair fails over to another controller when the sitting one is thought to have gone. Once an instruction is in a bay, the terminal acknowledges it back to the shipping line, and that acknowledgement is what the line plans its cargo around. Acknowledgements travel over the terminal's message fabric, which promises nothing about order, so they land in whatever order they land. The one thing the terminal must never do is clear an acknowledged instruction out from under the line without withdrawing the acknowledgement in the same movement.

A controller may back any controller it is not already backing. A controller backed by a strict majority may take the yard master's chair when the chair is empty. The sitting yard master may write an instruction that is not already in the plan into an empty bay. An instruction sitting in a bay that has not been acknowledged may be acknowledged, in any order relative to any other acknowledgement, recording the bay the line was told about. The sitting yard master may clear an acknowledged instruction out of its bay, which withdraws the acknowledgement at the same time. The chair may fail over while there are terms left in the schedule: the term advances, the chair empties, and every backing is cleared; the plan and the acknowledgements are untouched by it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every instruction the terminal has acknowledged to the shipping line is still sitting in the bay it was acknowledged for.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every instruction that has been written into a bay is eventually acknowledged to the shipping line.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

VARIABLES term, backing, chair, plan, ackedAt

vars == << term, backing, chair, plan, ackedAt >>

Backers(n) == {k \in Controllers : backing[k] = n}
Placed(u) == \E b \in Bays : plan[b] = u

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ backing \in [Controllers -> Controllers \cup {NoCtl}]
    /\ chair \in Controllers \cup {NoCtl}
    /\ plan \in [Bays -> Instructions \cup {NoInstr}]
    /\ ackedAt \in [Instructions -> Bays \cup {NoBay}]

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ backing = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ plan = [b \in Bays |-> NoInstr]
    /\ ackedAt = [u \in Instructions |-> NoBay]

Back(k, n) ==
    /\ backing[k] # n
    /\ backing' = [backing EXCEPT ![k] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, chair, plan, ackedAt >>

TakeChair(n) ==
    /\ chair = NoCtl
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(Backers(n)) > Cardinality(Controllers)
    /\ chair' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, plan, ackedAt >>

Write(u, b) ==
    /\ chair # NoCtl
    /\ plan[b] = NoInstr
    /\ ~Placed(u)
    /\ ackedAt[u] = NoBay
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![b] = u]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, ackedAt >>

Acknowledge(u, b) ==

    /\ ackedAt[u] = NoBay
    /\ ackedAt' = [ackedAt EXCEPT ![u] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED << term, backing, chair, plan >>

\* Clearing a bay withdraws the acknowledgement in the same movement; that is
\* the whole of the property.
Clear(u) ==

    /\ ackedAt[u] # NoBay

FailOver ==

    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ chair' = NoCtl
    /\ backing' = [k \in Controllers |-> NoCtl]

    \/ \E n \in Controllers : TakeChair(n)

    \/ \E u \in Instructions : Clear(u)
    \/ FailOver

\* Acknowledging does not wait on the chair, so weak fairness per instruction
\* is enough to see every placed instruction acknowledged.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A u \in Instructions :
        /\ TRUE
        /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Bays : Acknowledge(u, b))

AcknowledgedInstructionsStillSitInTheirBays ==
    \A u \in Instructions : ackedAt[u] # NoBay => plan[ackedAt[u]] = u

EveryPlacedInstructionIsAcknowledged ==
    \A u \in Instructions : Placed(u) ~> (ackedAt[u] # NoBay)

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od10m7p5t1`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling centre protects each track block with an emergency brake drop. Dropping the
brake on a block is irreversible from the software's point of view: once the shoe is released onto
the rail only a maintenance crew walking the tunnel can lift it again, so the signalling logic must
never land a second drop on a block that is already down, even when two dispatchers react to the
same hazard at once.

Each block carries a compare-and-swap guard register holding a generation number. A dispatcher who
wants to drop a block reads that block's current generation and stamps it onto a drop order, which
goes out over the trackside radio. The air interface is not ordered: orders sit on it and are picked
up in any sequence, so an order written first may well be acted on last.

The receiver acts on an order only if the generation stamped on it still equals the block's guard
register. On a match the brake drops, the block is recorded as down, and the register is bumped, so
every other order for that block already on the air is now one generation behind and can never
compare equal again. On a mismatch the receiver throws the order away and files its number on a
refused list. The radio link can also simply swallow an order without filing it anywhere.

The centre writes orders only for blocks that are still armed, and it reuses an order number only
once the previous order bearing that number has left the air interface, so two live orders never
share a number. When maintenance re-arms a dropped block they first confirm nothing for that block
is still outstanding on the air, and only then lift the shoe and roll the guard register on to its
next generation, wrapping back to zero at the top of the range.

The full set of actions is: Issue, in which the centre picks an armed block and a free order number,
reads the block's guard register and puts a stamped drop order on the air; Execute, in which the
receiver takes an order whose stamp equals the guard register, drops that block's brake, marks the
block down and bumps the register; Refuse, in which the receiver takes an order whose stamp no
longer equals the register and moves its number to the refused list; Lose, in which the air
interface swallows any outstanding order without a trace; and Rearm, in which maintenance lifts a
dropped block that has nothing outstanding on the air and rolls its guard register forward, wrapping
at the top.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drop order still sitting on the air interface for a block whose brake is
already down carries a generation different from that block's guard register, so no outstanding
order can ever land a second brake drop on an already-dropped block.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Blocks, Orders, TopGen

VARIABLES guard, dropped, air, refused

vars == <<guard, dropped, air, refused>>

\* An outstanding drop order: the block it targets, its order number, and the
\* generation the dispatcher read off that block's guard register.
Tickets == [blk: Blocks, num: Orders, gen: 0..TopGen]

Outstanding(b) == {t \in air : t.blk = b}

TypeOK ==
    /\ guard \in [Blocks -> 0..TopGen]
    /\ dropped \subseteq Blocks
    /\ air \subseteq Tickets
    /\ refused \subseteq Orders

Init ==
    /\ guard = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ dropped = {}
    /\ air = {}
    /\ refused = {}

\* The centre only writes orders for blocks that are still armed, and an order
\* number is reused only once its previous carrier has left the air interface.
Issue(b, n) ==
    /\ b \notin dropped
    /\ \A t \in air : t.num # n
    /\ air' = air \cup {[blk |-> b, num |-> n, gen |-> guard[b]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped, refused>>

\* The compare-and-swap.  Bumping the register on success is what leaves every
\* other order already in the air one generation behind.
Execute(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ t.gen = guard[t.blk]
    /\ guard' = [guard EXCEPT ![t.blk] = @ + 1]
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {t.blk}
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED refused

Refuse(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ t.gen # guard[t.blk]
    /\ refused' = refused \cup {t.num}
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped>>

Lose(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped, refused>>

\* wrapping its generation counter cannot resurrect an older order.
Rearm(b) ==
    /\ b \in dropped
    /\ Outstanding(b) = {}
    /\ dropped' = dropped \ {b}
    /\ guard' = [guard EXCEPT ![b] = IF @ = TopGen THEN 0 ELSE @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<air, refused>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks, n \in Orders : Issue(b, n)
    \/ \E t \in air : Execute(t)
    \/ \E t \in air : Refuse(t)
    \/ \E t \in air : Lose(t)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Rearm(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing still in the air for an already-dropped block can compare equal to
\* that block's register, which is why the irreversible drop cannot land twice.
StaleAfterDrop ==

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od6m2p0t4`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has one express riser that a car can be lifted into for a
non-stop run. Only one car may be up the riser at a time, and the bank has no central arbiter it
trusts: the decision is taken by two-phase commit across the floor desks that are currently staffed.

A round begins when the dispatcher proposes a car. Every staffed desk then casts one ballot. A desk
votes yes only when its own ledger shows the riser unclaimed; if its ledger already names a car, or
if the desk simply does not like the request, it votes no. When every staffed desk has voted yes the
coordinator commits: each staffed desk writes the candidate into its ledger and the car is lifted
into the riser. If any staffed desk voted no, the round aborts and nothing is written. Either way
the round ends and the dispatcher is free to propose again.

A car that has finished its run is released: it leaves the riser and every staffed desk clears its
ledger entry.

The staffing level changes at runtime. Between rounds a desk can be closed, shrinking the set of
voters the coordinator needs unanimity from, as long as at least one desk stays open. A closed desk
can reopen, again only between rounds, and when it does it resyncs its ledger from the bank so that
it comes back knowing who, if anyone, is up the riser. Desks never open or close mid-ballot, so the
voter set is fixed for the length of a round.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which the dispatcher names a candidate car and opens a
ballot; VoteYes, in which a staffed desk with an unclaimed ledger votes in favour; VoteNo, in which a
staffed desk votes against; Commit, in which unanimous yes votes write the candidate into every
staffed desk's ledger and lift it into the riser; Abort, in which a single no vote ends the round
with nothing written; Release, in which a car leaves the riser and the staffed desks clear their
ledgers; CloseDesk, in which a desk shuts between rounds while at least one other stays open; and
OpenDesk, in which a closed desk reopens between rounds and resyncs its ledger from the bank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a car is up the express riser, every staffed desk's ledger names that car,
so no second car can ever assemble the unanimous yes vote it would need to be lifted.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ballot that opens is eventually resolved, so the bank always returns to a
state in which the dispatcher can propose again.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ cand \in Slots
    /\ ballot \in [Floors -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ ledger \in [Floors -> Slots]
    /\ riser \subseteq Cars
    /\ staffed \subseteq Floors

Occupant == IF riser = {} THEN NoCar ELSE CHOOSE c \in riser : TRUE

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ cand = NoCar
    /\ ballot = [f \in Floors |-> "none"]
    /\ ledger = [f \in Floors |-> NoCar]
    /\ riser = {}
    /\ staffed = Floors

Propose(c) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ cand' = c
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ ballot' = [f \in Floors |-> "none"]

\* A staffed floor votes yes only when its own ledger shows the express riser
\* unclaimed; that local check is the whole of the exclusion argument.
VoteYes(f) ==

    /\ f \in staffed
    /\ ballot[f] = "none"
    /\ ledger[f] = NoCar
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![f] = "yes"]

VoteNo(f) ==

    /\ f \in staffed
    /\ ballot[f] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![f] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ledger, riser, staffed>>

    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A f \in staffed : ballot[f] = "yes"
    /\ ledger' = [f \in Floors |-> IF f \in staffed THEN cand ELSE ledger[f]]
    /\ riser' = riser \cup {cand}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, staffed>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E f \in staffed : ballot[f] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, ledger, riser, staffed>>

Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in riser

A stock exchange runs its opening auction across a ring of member desks. The whole session starts
with a fixed pool of share lots sitting on the first desk, and the auction only ever moves lots
around the ring; the exchange never mints a lot and never destroys one, so at any instant the lots
sitting on desks plus the lots still travelling must add up to the pool the session opened with.

The right to release lots travels with a baton that walks the ring one desk at a time. A desk may
release lots only while it is holding the baton, and it releases them by writing a consignment note
addressed to the next desk round the ring: the note carries a quantity, which is deducted from the
releasing desk's holdings at the moment the note is written. Notes carry a tag drawn from a small
pool, and a tag is reused only when no note bearing it is still in flight, so two notes on the wire
are always distinguishable.

The settlement wire does not preserve order. Notes sit on it and are picked off in whatever sequence
the settlement system gets to them, so a note written early may be credited long after one written
later. When a note is picked off normally, its quantity is credited to the desk it was addressed to.
A note can instead be torn up, in which case the quantity goes back to the desk that released it and
the tag is recorded on the torn list. Either way the quantity leaves the wire exactly as it arrived.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which the baton moves to the next desk round the ring;
Consign, in which the desk holding the baton deducts a quantity from its own holdings and puts a
freshly tagged note for the next desk onto the settlement wire; Settle, in which any note on the
wire, in any order, is credited to the desk it was addressed to and leaves the wire; and Recall, in
which any note on the wire is torn up, its quantity credited back to the desk that released it and
its tag filed on the torn list.

the settlement wire always equal the total the session opened with.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital pharmacy keeps its controlled drugs in a secure dispensing bay whose individual drawers
are separately latched. Access is hierarchical: the bay interlock is coarse and admits one
technician at a time, and only the technician who is inside the bay may take the fine interlock on a
drawer, one drawer at a time. The bay can only be given back once that technician is holding no
drawer.

Authorisation is by badge. The pharmacist-in-charge keeps a roster of technicians on shift together
with a roster epoch, and a technician may act only while they are on the roster and their badge
carries the current epoch. Turning the epoch is how the pharmacist invalidates every badge at once
at a shift change; because every badge is stale from that instant, the turn also strips the bay
interlock and every drawer latch. A technician still on the roster can re-badge to the current epoch
and carry on.

The pharmacist also has a privileged override aimed at individuals: a technician can be struck off
the roster mid-shift, and whatever they are holding is broken open on the spot rather than waiting
for them to hand it back. Somebody struck off can be reinstated later, but they return with a zeroed
badge and must re-badge before they can act again.

The full set of actions is: EnterBay, in which a currently authorised technician takes the free bay
interlock; TakeDrawer, in which the authorised technician inside the bay takes a free drawer latch
while holding no other drawer; Dispense, in which that technician hands out the medication and
latches the drawer shut again; LeaveBay, in which a technician holding no drawer gives the bay
interlock back; RotateEpoch, in which the pharmacist turns the roster epoch and the bay interlock
and every drawer latch are stripped; Rebadge, in which a rostered technician refreshes a stale badge
to the current epoch; StrikeOff, in which the pharmacist removes a technician from the roster and
breaks open whatever they are holding; and Reinstate, in which a struck-off technician is put back
on the roster with a zeroed badge.

badge stamped with the current roster epoch, so no struck-off or stale hand is ever inside a drawer.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drawer that is opened is eventually latched shut again.

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by a shared dispatch plan that says which cars serve
which floor groups. Three floor controllers each keep their own copy of the plan, and the plan
itself lives in a revision journal: revision one is the first plan ever committed, revision two the
next, and so on. The danger the bank has to rule out is a lost update, where one controller's
revision is quietly written over while another controller still believes its own copy is current.

A change is made by quorum vote. A controller puts up a bid: the new plan it wants, stamped with the
revision number of the copy it actually has in front of it. Other controllers vote on that bid, and
a controller votes for it only when the bid was derived from exactly the revision that controller
itself is holding — a bid built on an older revision than what a voter has read gets no vote from
that voter. Once a strict majority of controllers has voted for the bid, and the bid's base revision
is still the newest revision in the journal, it commits and becomes the next journal entry. A bid
can also simply be withdrawn, and only one bid is ever on the table at a time.

A controller refreshes its copy by syncing: it takes the newest journal entry and the revision
number that goes with it. Until it does, it keeps the older copy it read, and it keeps voting on the
basis of that older revision.

The chief engineer has a privileged override and can append a plan to the journal directly, with no
bid and no vote. Any bid on the table is dropped, and every controller is left holding whatever
revision it last read.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which a controller puts up a bid stamped with the revision
it currently holds; Vote, in which a controller adds its vote to a bid whose base revision matches
the one it is holding; Commit, in which a bid with a majority and a base equal to the newest journal
revision is appended to the journal; Discard, in which the bid on the table is withdrawn; Sync, in
which a controller refreshes its copy and revision number from the newest journal entry; and
Override, in which the chief engineer appends a plan to the journal directly and drops any bid.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every controller that holds a revision at all holds exactly the plan the journal
records at that revision number, so no committed plan is ever silently replaced underneath a
controller that believes it is current.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

\* every bid carries the revision number it was derived from.
Propose(c, p) ==

    /\ bid' = [base |-> seenRev[c], plan |-> p, yes |-> {}]

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An elevator bank in a skyscraper answers landing calls by a vote of its control panel rather than by
a single dispatcher. Three controllers sit on the panel and every dispatch needs a strict majority of
them behind it. The bank runs in terms: each controller carries a term stamp, and the building's
safety case says a controller whose stamp is behind the running term must not count towards any
decision, because it is reasoning from a picture of the bank that has since been replaced.

A landing call is pressed on one of the landings and stays live until it is answered. While the call
is live, controllers back it one at a time, and a controller may back it only while its stamp
matches the running term. Once a majority is behind the call and no car is already on its way, a car
is sent; when that car arrives the call clears, the car goes back to idle and the backings are torn
up.

An emergency re-election advances the term. It happens only between dispatches, never while a car is
already on its way, and every backing collected under the old term is discarded, since the
controllers that gave them are now behind. A controller that is behind is brought up to the running
term by a restamp sweep, after which it can start backing again.

The building engineer has a privileged override: a live call can be killed outright at any moment,
taking the car assignment and all the backings with it, with no vote and no waiting.

The full set of actions is: Press, in which a landing call goes live while none is outstanding;
Back, in which a controller whose stamp matches the running term adds its backing to the live call;
Dispatch, in which a car is sent once a majority backs the call and no car is already moving; Arrive,
in which the moving car reaches the landing and the call, the backings and the car assignment all
clear; Reelect, in which, with no car on its way, the term advances and all backings are torn up;
Restamp, in which every controller that is behind is brought up to the running term; and Override,
in which the building engineer kills the live call, its backings and its car assignment outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a car is on its way to a landing, the backing behind that dispatch is a
majority of the panel and every controller in it still carries the running term stamp, so no
behind-the-term controller ever props up a dispatch in progress.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every landing call that is pressed is eventually cleared, either by a car
arriving or by the engineer's override.

An airport baggage router feeds bags from the sorter into make-up chutes, one chute per departing

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od9m1p5t1`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over a ring of protection relays. When demand
outruns supply the shedder opens the feeder breaker for one grid zone. Opening a breaker is a
one-way act for the duration of the event: the latch stays open until the control room walks it
back, and opening the same zone twice under two different orders would be logged as two separate
outages and would trip the regional interlock, so it must not happen.

Authority to raise a shed order travels with a baton that walks the relay ring one hop at a time.
Only the relay holding the baton may raise an order, and it may do so only when no zone is currently
open and the target zone has no order already on the bus. The order goes out as one copy per relay,
all bearing the same order number, and the copies travel independently: the message bus does not
preserve order, so the copies are picked up in whatever sequence the relays get to them.

Whichever copy is picked up first while no zone is open actually trips the breaker: that zone goes
open and the order number on that copy is written onto the zone's trip receipt. Copies picked up
afterwards for a zone that is already open are recognised as the same order arriving late and are
thrown away rather than acted on. The control room restores a zone once no copies for it are left on
the bus, closing the breaker again and clearing its trip receipt.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which the baton moves one hop round the relay ring; Raise,
in which the baton-holding relay broadcasts one copy per relay of a freshly numbered shed order for
a zone, provided no zone is open and that zone has nothing on the bus; Trip, in which a copy picked
off the bus while no zone is open opens its zone's breaker and writes its order number onto the trip
receipt; Ignore, in which a copy for a zone that is already open is thrown away; and Restore, in
which the control room closes an open zone whose copies have all left the bus and clears its
receipt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every copy still on the bus addressed to a zone whose breaker is open carries
exactly the order number written on that zone's trip receipt, so no late copy can ever open that
breaker a second time under a different order.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a zone has been shed, the grid is eventually restored to a state with no
zone open.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Zones, Orders, NoOrder

Relays == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Nxt(r) == (r + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES baton, bus, shed, receipt

vars == <<baton, bus, shed, receipt>>

\* A shed command is broadcast as one copy per relay; the copies travel
\* independently and are picked up in any order.
Copies == [id: Orders, zone: Zones, to: Relays]

For(z) == {m \in bus : m.zone = z}

TypeOK ==
    /\ baton \in Relays
    /\ bus \subseteq Copies
    /\ shed \subseteq Zones
    /\ receipt \in [Zones -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]

Init ==
    /\ baton = 0
    /\ bus = {}
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ receipt = [z \in Zones |-> NoOrder]

PassBaton ==
    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, shed, receipt>>

\* Only the relay holding the baton may raise a shed order, and only for a zone
\* that is neither already open nor already carrying an order on the bus.
Raise(r, z, k) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ For(z) = {}
    /\ \A m \in bus : m.id # k
    /\ bus' = bus \cup {[id |-> k, zone |-> z, to |-> d] : d \in Relays}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, shed, receipt>>

\* Opening a feeder breaker is one-way for the duration of the event: the
\* copy that lands first is the one written onto the trip receipt.
Trip(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ shed' = {m.zone}
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![m.zone] = m.id]
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED baton

Ignore(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ m.zone \in shed
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, shed, receipt>>

Restore(z) ==
    /\ z \in shed
    /\ For(z) = {}
    /\ shed' = shed \ {z}
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![z] = NoOrder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, bus>>

Ignoring == \E m \in bus : Ignore(m)
Tripping == \E m \in bus : Trip(m)
Restoring == \E z \in Zones : Restore(z)

Next ==
    \/ PassBaton
    \/ \E r \in Relays, z \in Zones, k \in Orders : Raise(r, z, k)

    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Tripping) /\ WF_vars(Ignoring) /\ WF_vars(Restoring)

\* Every copy still on the bus for a zone whose breaker is open belongs to the
\* very order that opened it, so no copy can ever open that breaker a second
\* time under a different order.
NoRivalCopy ==

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od10m3p0t2`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway line is signalled by two independent control centres, a main and a standby, that were built
by different suppliers and share one pool of track blocks. A block is the critical resource: only one
centre may be working a given block at a time, because two centres setting routes over the same
stretch of track would clear conflicting movements onto it.

Each centre runs its own leader election over its cabins. A centre with no cabin in charge elects
one, and the election turns that centre's term. Turning the term drops every claim the previous
cabin was working under, because the new cabin has no idea what the old one was in the middle of.
Blocks the centre was granted are left standing in its name, but their grant stamps are now behind
the centre's term, which marks them as unfinished business rather than live work. A cabin in charge
can fail at any time, leaving its centre leaderless.

The shared pool has a single arbiter. A cabin in charge can seize a vacant block: the arbiter records
which centre now holds it and stamps the grant with that centre's running term, and the block joins
the centre's working claims. A claim is given up by handing the block back to the pool. After a
failover the new cabin can readopt a block its centre still holds by restamping the grant with the
running term and taking it into its working claims. Blocks left standing in the name of a
leaderless centre, and not being worked by it, are reaped back into the pool by the arbiter.

The full set of actions is: Elect, in which a leaderless centre puts a cabin in charge, turns its
term and drops its working claims; Fail, in which the cabin in charge of a centre drops out, leaving
that centre leaderless; Seize, in which a cabin in charge takes a vacant block from the pool, has the
grant stamped with its centre's term and starts working it; Yield, in which a centre stops working a
block and hands it back to the pool; Readopt, in which a new cabin restamps a block its centre still
holds and takes it into its working claims; and Reap, in which the arbiter returns to the pool a
block standing in the name of a leaderless centre that is not being worked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block a centre is working has been granted to that very centre by the shared
arbiter and carries a grant stamp equal to the centre's running term, so the two centres can never
both be working the same block.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Centres, Cabins, Blocks, MaxTerm, Vacant, Nobody

VARIABLES boss, term, claimed, held, stamp

vars == <<boss, term, claimed, held, stamp>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ boss \in [Centres -> Cabins \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ term \in [Centres -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ claimed \in [Centres -> SUBSET Blocks]
    /\ held \in [Blocks -> Centres \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ stamp \in [Blocks -> 0 .. MaxTerm]

Init ==
    /\ boss = [c \in Centres |-> Nobody]
    /\ term = [c \in Centres |-> 0]
    /\ claimed = [c \in Centres |-> {}]
    /\ held = [b \in Blocks |-> Vacant]
    /\ stamp = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]

\* A fresh election turns the centre's term and drops every claim the previous
\* cabin was working under; blocks it had are left standing but now stale.
Elect(c, k) ==
    /\ boss[c] = Nobody
    /\ boss' = [boss EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![c] = IF @ = MaxTerm THEN 0 ELSE @ + 1]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, stamp>>

Fail(c) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ boss' = [boss EXCEPT ![c] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, claimed, held, stamp>>

\* The pool arbiter hands a block to one centre at a time and stamps the grant
\* with the term of the centre it was granted to.
Seize(c, b) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ held[b] = Vacant
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![b] = term[c]]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term>>

Yield(c, b) ==
    /\ b \in claimed[c]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {b}]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, stamp>>

\* After a failover the new cabin may pick a block its centre still holds back
\* up, restamping it with the running term before working it.
Readopt(c, b) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ held[b] = c
    /\ stamp[b] # term[c]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![b] = term[c]]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, held>>

Reap(b) ==
    /\ held[b] # Vacant
    /\ boss[held[b]] = Nobody
    /\ b \notin claimed[held[b]]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, claimed, stamp>>

    \/ \E c \in Centres, k \in Cabins : Elect(c, k)
    \/ \E c \in Centres : Fail(c)
    \/ \E c \in Centres, b \in Blocks : Seize(c, b) \/ Yield(c, b) \/ Readopt(c, b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Reap(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A centre only ever works a block the shared arbiter has actually granted to
\* it under the term it is running, so the two centres can never both be
\* working the same block.
ClaimsAreGranted ==

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A stock exchange runs its opening auction over a small set of order books, one per security. The
session begins with a fixed number of share lots standing in one book and the auction only ever
moves lots between books; nothing is created and nothing is destroyed, so the lots standing in the
books plus whatever is in transit must always come to the session total.

Access is hierarchical. A member firm first takes the auction floor, which admits one firm at a
time, and only the firm on the floor may latch an order book, one book at a time. Moving lots is
done in two steps that never overlap: the firm lifts a parcel out of the book it has latched, which
takes those lots out of the book and puts them into the exchange's escrow, and the parcel is later
placed into a book, which takes it out of escrow and adds it there. Escrow holds at most one parcel
at a time, and a parcel in escrow is always eventually placed. Latches and the floor are given back
in the reverse order they were taken, the floor only once the firm holds no latch.

A member firm can drop off the exchange network without a word, still holding the floor and a book
latch. Nothing it holds is released by the drop itself; the exchange's sweep is what takes the floor
and the latch back, after which the firm can rejoin. A parcel already in escrow when a firm drops
out is unaffected — escrow belongs to the exchange, not to the firm, and it is placed as normal.

The full set of actions is: TakeFloor, in which a live firm takes the free auction floor; TakeBook,
in which the firm on the floor latches a book while holding no other; Lift, in which a firm takes a
parcel out of the book it has latched and into escrow, which must be empty; Place, in which the
parcel in escrow is added to a book and escrow is emptied; Unlatch, in which a firm gives a book
latch back; LeaveFloor, in which a firm holding no latch gives the floor back; Crash, in which a
firm drops off the network silently while still holding the floor and its latch; Sweep, in which the
exchange takes back the floor and latches held in a dropped firm's name; and Rejoin, in which a
dropped firm holding nothing comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots standing across all order books plus the lots sitting in escrow always
equal the total the session opened with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every parcel lifted into escrow is eventually placed into a book.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Standing(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE

    /\ latch \in [Books -> Hands]

only the surgeon holding the day book may take the latch on a theatre, one theatre at a time.

case is confirmed — the reservation counts against the session immediately, so a case can only be
pencilled in if the theatre's already-confirmed minutes leave room for it. Confirming turns the
pencilled minutes into committed minutes and gives the latch back. Rubbing the case out gives the
latch back with nothing committed. The day book is closed once the surgeon holds no theatre latch.

theatre outright, rubbing out whatever is pencilled in and freeing the latch without asking the
surgeon holding it. The director can also cut minutes back out of a theatre's committed list, which

which the surgeon holding the day book takes a free theatre latch and reserves a case's minutes

theatre's list.

longer reads free — because the other terminal got there first — the attempt is missed and the
controller lines something else up. A controller can also yield a lane it is working, which clears

The sorter runs in waves. At the end of a wave every lane register is cleared down at once, both
controllers are left working nothing, and the wave counter rolls on, wrapping at the top of its

which the wave ends, every register is cleared down, both controllers are left working nothing and

time.

point where neither controller is working any lane.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A commercial print shop runs two job spoolers that were installed years apart and never taught about
each other. Both queue work onto the same pool of presses. A press is a critical resource: two
spoolers driving the same press means two jobs interleaved on one sheet feed and a ruined run, so a
press must never be run by both at once.

Neither spooler takes a lock up front. A spooler peeks at a press, writing down the stamp the press
is showing, and then goes away and prepares the job. When it comes back it tries to claim: the claim
only goes through if the press is still unheld, its stamp has not moved since the peek, and no job
is live anywhere in the shop — there is a single ink line, so one press runs at a time. A successful
claim records the spooler as the press's holder, rolls the press stamp on, and hands the spooler a
ticket naming the press and the stamp value the claim left behind. The stamp is a small wrapping
counter that rolls back to zero at the top.

If the press was taken, or the stamp moved while the job was being prepared, or another job is live,
the attempt lapses and the spooler's retry count goes up. The retry count is capped and a spooler
settles back to zero before going round again. When a job finishes, the press is released, the stamp
rolls on once more and the ticket is given up.

The full set of actions is: Peek, in which a spooler holding neither a note nor a ticket writes down
a press's current stamp; Claim, in which the attempt goes through because the press is unheld, its
stamp is unmoved and no job is live, recording the holder, rolling the stamp and issuing a ticket;
Lapse, in which the attempt fails and the spooler's retry count goes up; Settle, in which a spooler
resets its retry count; and Finish, in which a live job ends, releasing the press, rolling its stamp
and giving up the ticket.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every spooler holding a ticket is running a press that records that very spooler as
its holder and whose stamp still reads the value the claim left behind, so two spoolers can never
both be running the same press.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a job is live on a press, the shop eventually comes back to a state
where no spooler holds a ticket.

Tickets == [press: Presses, ep: 0 .. MaxVer]

    /\ stamp \in [Presses -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ note \in [Spoolers -> Notes \cup {NoNote}]

    /\ retries \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. MaxRetry]

    /\ stamp = [p \in Presses |-> 0]
    /\ note = [s \in Spoolers |-> NoNote]
    /\ ticket = [s \in Spoolers |-> NoTicket]

\* hold anything while it prepares the job.
Peek(s, p) ==

    /\ ticket[s] = NoTicket

Claim(s) ==

    /\ stamp[note[s].press] = note[s].saw

    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![note[s].press] = s]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![note[s].press] = Roll(@)]

    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![s] = NoNote]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

    /\ \/ holder[note[s].press] # Free

    /\ retries[s] < MaxRetry
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![s] = NoNote]

    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, stamp, note, ticket>>

    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![ticket[s].press] = Free]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![ticket[s].press] = Roll(@)]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoTicket]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<note, retries>>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
Engineering work on a subway line is protected by possessions. Before a gang may stand on the
ballast in a track section, that section's possession register must have been swapped from clear to
that gang's name, and the swap rolls the register on to a new value which the gang keeps as its
token. The register is a small wrapping counter, so it rolls back to zero at the top of its range.

The safety case is about who is standing where. A gang may step onto a section only while it is
booked on duty, the section's register still names it, and the token it kept still reads the same as
the register. That last check is what makes a possession current rather than superseded: any gang
holding a token the register has since rolled past is speaking for a possession that no longer
exists, and must not be on the track. Handing a possession back is itself a swap and is subject to
the same check, so a gang whose token has been superseded cannot hand back a section it no longer
speaks for.

The signaller has a privileged override. A section can be taken back at any moment to run a train:
the register is rolled past whatever token is out there, the section goes clear, and anybody standing
in it is cleared off the ballast in the same movement.

Gangs also come and go from shift. Standing down takes a gang off duty and off the ballast at once,
though any possession still in its name is left standing until the signaller takes it back. A gang
that signs back on is on duty again but holds whatever token it had before.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which a clear section's register is swapped to an on-duty
gang's name, rolled on, and the new value kept by that gang as its token; Enter, in which an on-duty
gang whose token matches the register of a section it is named on steps onto the ballast; Leave, in
which a gang steps off the ballast; HandBack, in which an on-duty gang holding a current token and
not standing in the section clears the register and rolls it on; Revoke, in which the signaller takes
a section back, rolls the register on and clears anybody out of it; StandDown, in which a gang goes
off duty and off the ballast; and SignOn, in which a gang comes back on duty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every gang standing on the ballast is booked on duty, is named on that section's
possession register, and holds a token equal to what the register currently reads, so nobody off
duty and nobody holding a superseded possession is ever on the track.

    /\ owner \in [Sections -> Gangs \cup {Clear}]
    /\ tok \in [Gangs -> 0 .. MaxTok]

    /\ onDuty \subseteq Gangs

    /\ reg = [s \in Sections |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [s \in Sections |-> Clear]
    /\ tok = [g \in Gangs |-> 0]
    /\ onTrack = [g \in Gangs |-> NoSec]
    /\ onDuty = Gangs

\* on in one step; the gang keeps the value the swap left behind.
Grant(g, s) ==
    /\ g \in onDuty
    /\ owner[s] = Clear
    /\ onTrack[g] = NoSec
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@)]
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![g] = Roll(reg[s])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onTrack, onDuty>>

\* section register, which is what makes the possession current rather than stale.

    /\ onTrack[g] = NoSec
    /\ owner[s] = g
    /\ tok[g] = reg[s]

    /\ tok[g] = reg[s]
    /\ onTrack[g] # s

    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, onTrack, onDuty>>

    /\ onDuty' = onDuty \cup {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, owner, tok, onTrack>>

Two signal boxes, Ashfield and Blackford, were built decades apart and control adjoining stretches of
the same subway line. Neither knows the other exists in software, but both need the same handful of
crossovers, which sit in a shared pool between them. A crossover is a critical resource: two boxes
holding the same crossover means two conflicting routes over one set of blades, so no crossover may
ever be held by both boxes at once.

There is nothing between them but a register on each crossover, which reads free or carries the name
of whichever box holds it. A box works in two steps. First it lines a crossover up — picking one it
is not already holding and noting it as the target of its next attempt. Then it swaps: the write
lands only if the register still reads free at that instant, and when it lands the box's own name
goes into the register and the crossover joins the set that box is holding. If the register is no
longer free, because the other box got in first, the attempt is missed and the target is dropped.
Neither box lets an attempt hang: a lined-up crossover is always either swapped or missed.

A box drops a crossover it is holding when the route through it is no longer needed, which puts the
register back to free and returns the crossover to the shared pool.

The full set of actions is: LineAsh and LineBlack, in which the box concerned, having no attempt
outstanding, targets a crossover it is not already holding; SwapAsh and SwapBlack, in which the

register is no longer free; and DropAsh and DropBlack, in which a box gives up a crossover it holds
and the register goes back to free.

crossover held by Blackford carries Blackford's, so the two boxes can never both be holding the same
crossover.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Neither box is ever left with an attempt hanging: any crossover a box has lined up
is eventually either swapped to it or missed.

A car-wash conveyor line runs cars past a row of treatment bays that all draw from one

grant records the epoch the line was running when it was made. Water only comes on for a grant made
under the epoch the line is currently running: a grant from an earlier epoch describes a line layout
that no longer exists, and the valves stay shut for it. A bay whose grant is behind can reaffirm it
against the running epoch, provided it is still in service, and then draw as normal. Water is shut
off again when the bay is done, and the manifold is given back once the water is off. The manifold
never stays in one bay's hands for ever.

Capacity changes while the line runs. Reconfiguration puts bays into or out of service — the site
adds a wax stage in summer, drops the pre-wash when the tanker is late — and always leaves at least
one bay in service. Reconfiguring renumbers the line to the next epoch, wrapping at the top of the

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container terminal allocates yard cells to its cranes. A cell takes one crane's work at a time, so
the yard office must never allocate the same cell to two cranes.

Nothing is locked up front. A crane reads the survey number the office is showing for a cell, then
lodges a request naming the cell and the number it read. It does not hold the cell while the request
sits in the office. The office honours the request only if the survey number has not moved since the
crane read it and the cell is still unbooked; when it does, the cell is booked to that crane, the
survey number moves on, and the crane is given the new number to keep. If the number has moved, or
the cell was booked in the meantime, the request is turned down and the crane starts again. Survey
numbers are small wrapping counters that roll back to zero at the top. Only one request sits in the
office at a time, and the office never sits on one: every request lodged is eventually either
honoured or turned down.

The cranes are slow, not broken. A crane can take a long time between reading a number and lodging
its request, and the yard does not wait: the office re-surveys unbooked cells as stacks are
rearranged, which moves their numbers on and leaves a slow crane's request standing on a reading
that has gone stale. That is not a failure and needs no recovery — the request is simply turned down
and the crane reads again.

A crane vacates the cell it was given when it has finished with it, which unbooks the cell and moves
its survey number on again.

The full set of actions is: Submit, in which a crane with no cell of its own reads a cell's survey
number and lodges a request, provided the office is free; Commit, in which the office honours a
request whose number is unmoved and whose cell is unbooked, booking the cell, moving the number on
and giving the new number to the crane; Reject, in which the office turns a request down because the
number moved or the cell was taken; Resurvey, in which an unbooked cell's survey number is moved on
as the yard is rearranged; and Vacate, in which a crane gives up the cell it holds, unbooking it and
moving its number on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane that has been given a cell is recorded as that cell's booking and holds
the survey number that cell currently carries, so a cell is never allocated to two cranes at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request lodged with the yard office is eventually settled, one way or the
other.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A warehouse robot fleet feeds pallets to a strapping station. Banding a pallet cuts the strap to
length and welds it: there is no way back from it, and a pallet that goes through twice comes out
with two straps crossed over each other and has to be broken down by hand. So a pallet must be
banded once and once only.

Work reaches the bots on a bounded belt with backpressure. A pallet joins the tail of the belt only
while the belt is below its cap, and only if it is not already banded, not already somewhere on the
belt, and not already sitting in a bot's gripper — so the belt never carries the same pallet twice
and never carries one that is already done. Bots take pallets off the head of the belt one at a
time, and a bot holds at most one pallet. A bot can put its pallet back on the tail of the belt
instead of banding it, again subject to the cap.

A bot can fall behind without failing. A lagging bot still has its pallet in the gripper and is
perfectly healthy — it is simply not going to get to the strapping head any time soon, and it will
not band anything while it is behind. It catches up on its own eventually. Rather than wait, the
floor supervisor can recall the pallet from a lagging bot and put it back on the belt; the bot is
then holding nothing, so when it does catch up there is nothing for it to band.

The full set of actions is: Queue, in which a pallet that is not banded, not on the belt and not in
a gripper joins the tail of the belt while the belt is below its cap; Take, in which a bot holding
nothing lifts the pallet at the head of the belt; Band, in which a bot that is not lagging straps
the pallet it holds and lets it go; Replace, in which a bot puts the pallet it holds back on the
tail of the belt; Lag, in which a bot falls behind while still holding its pallet; CatchUp, in which
a lagging bot comes back up to speed; and Recall, in which the supervisor takes the pallet off a
lagging bot and puts it back on the belt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A pallet that has been banded is nowhere else in the system — not anywhere on the
belt and not in any bot's gripper — so it can never be presented for banding a second time.

A warehouse floor is divided into zones, and each zone has a ceiling on how many robots may be
inside it at once. The ceiling is a safety limit — too many machines in one aisle and they deadlock
against each other and block the pickers — so it must never be exceeded.

The floor plan is numbered by epoch. A robot is admitted to a zone by being issued a permit, and the
permit is stamped with the layout epoch that was running when it was issued. Only permits stamped
with the running epoch count towards a zone's ceiling: a permit from an earlier epoch describes a
floor that no longer exists and carries no weight at all. A robot leaves a zone by giving up its
permit. A robot whose permit is behind can renew it against the running epoch, but renewing
re-checks the ceiling, so it cannot walk an old permit into a zone that has since been tightened.

Capacity changes while the fleet is working. Reconfiguration rewrites the ceilings — the dock is
widened for a container, the aisle is narrowed for a pallet drop — and rolls the layout epoch on,
wrapping at the top of its range. Every permit issued before the change is behind from that moment.
The floor controller sweeps behind-the-epoch permits away in a single pass, and permits left behind
by a reconfiguration never linger indefinitely.

The full set of actions is: Admit, in which a robot with no permit is let into a zone whose current
permits are below its ceiling, and the permit is stamped with the running epoch; Exit, in which a
robot gives up its permit; Renew, in which a robot holding a behind-the-epoch permit brings it up to
the running epoch, subject to the zone's ceiling; Reconfigure, in which the ceilings are rewritten
and the layout epoch advances; and Purge, in which the floor controller clears every
behind-the-epoch permit in one pass.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No zone ever holds more robots on current-epoch permits than that zone's ceiling
allows.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Permits left behind by a reconfiguration are eventually all cleared, so the floor
never carries stale permits for ever.

    /\ issued \in [Bots -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

    /\ permit = [r \in Bots |-> NoZone]

\* permits stamped with the running epoch count towards a zone's ceiling.
Admit(r, z) ==
    /\ permit[r] = NoZone
    /\ Cardinality(Inside(z)) < ceiling[z]
    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = z]
    /\ issued' = [issued EXCEPT ![r] = layout]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling>>

Exit(r) ==

    /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![r] = NoZone]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<layout, ceiling, issued>>

\* carry an old permit into a zone that has since been tightened.

    /\ layout' = layout + 1

A hospital blood bank tracks every unit it holds. A unit is always in exactly one place — in the
cold store, on the cross-match bench waiting to go out, on the delivery van, or up on a ward — and

Units leave the cold store onto the cross-match bench, which is bounded and applies backpressure:
once the bench is at its cap nothing further is cross-matched and the units stay in the store. The
bench is worked from the front — the unit that has been waiting longest is the next one loaded onto
the van.

Consignments on the van carry tags so that two units of the same group stay distinct, and a tag is
reused only when nothing bearing it is still out. The van is not a queue: it does its rounds and
consignments are signed for by the wards in whatever order the wards get to them, so a unit loaded
first may well be signed for last. A consignment can also be diverted back to the cold store instead
of being delivered.

signed in to the wards it was routed to, so the van never stays loaded. Units that a ward does not
use come back into the cold store.

which the driver books off and everything still on the van is signed in to the wards; and Return, in
which a unit comes back from a ward into the cold store.

A stock exchange sells opening auction slots — the matching windows in which a security's opening
price is struck. Two trading desks, cash and derivatives, run their own scheduling systems and were
never wired together, but both draw slots from the same pool. A slot goes to one desk and one desk

Each allocation is agreed by two-phase commit across the parties that have to sign it off, the
clearing house and the registrar. A desk prepares a slot that is neither already allocated nor

desks can have a ballot running at once, and nothing stops them from running ballots on the same
slot — the desks cannot see each other.

That is why the slot is re-checked at commit time rather than only at prepare time. A ballot commits
only if every party voted in favour and the slot is still free and still on offer at that moment; the
allocation is then written into the register. If a party voted against, or the slot was taken or
withdrawn while the ballot was running, the round aborts with nothing written. Allocations are handed
back when the auction for that slot is done.

Slots can also be withdrawn from the pool while unallocated — a security is suspended, a listing is
pulled — and put back on offer later.

is free and on offer; Aye and Nay, in which a party casts its single vote on a desk's ballot;

allocation into the register; Abort, in which a vote against, or the slot being taken or withdrawn,

an unallocated slot is pulled from the pool; and Reoffer, in which a withdrawn slot goes back on
offer.

opening slot name the same desk — so a slot is never allocated to both desks.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A multiplayer game's matchmaker runs as two independently deployed shards, west and east, that both
write to the same shared party roster. The roster is versioned: revision one is the first edit ever
landed, revision two the next, and so on. The hazard is a lost update — one shard laying its edit
down over a revision it never read, quietly wiping what the other shard just wrote.

Each shard runs its own leader election with failover. A shard with no chief elects one, and the
election advances that shard's leadership term. A chief can fail at any moment, leaving its shard
without one until the next election. Only a shard that currently has a chief prepares edits.

A shard keeps a cached copy of the roster's revision number and refetches it from the registry when
it wants to. When its chief prepares an edit, the edit is stamped both with the revision the shard
last read and with the leadership term it was prepared under. The registry holds one proposal at a
time and never sits on it.

The registry lands an edit only if two things still hold: the edit was built on the newest revision
in the roster, and the leadership that prepared it is still the leadership in place on that shard. An
edit built on a revision that has since been superseded is refused, and so is one prepared under a
chief that has since failed and been replaced. A refused edit changes nothing and the shard starts
again. When the roster reaches the end of its revision range it is archived and the shards' cached
revisions go back to zero.

The full set of actions is: Elect, in which a shard with no chief elects one and advances its term;
Fail, in which a shard's chief drops out; Refetch, in which a shard reads the roster's current
revision into its cache; Propose, in which a shard's chief lodges an edit stamped with its cached
revision and its term; Apply, in which the registry lands an edit built on the newest revision under
the leadership still in place; Refuse, in which the registry turns an edit down because the revision
moved, the leadership changed, the shard has no chief or the roster is full; and Archive, in which a
full roster is cleared and the cached revisions are reset.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every edit in the party roster was built on the revision immediately preceding it,
so no shard's write was ever laid down over a revision it had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal lodged with the registry is eventually either landed or refused.

A stock exchange runs its opening auction from a sheet divided into segments — equities in one,
bonds in another — with individual order books inside each segment. Member firms work the sheet under
a two-level locking discipline: a firm first takes a whole segment, holding one segment at a time,
and only then may it latch individual books inside the segment it holds. A segment is given back
only once the firm holds no latch inside it.

A latch is not just an exclusion: it is a book being actively followed by the matching engine, and
the engine has a fixed number of tracks. It can follow only that many books at once, and driving it
past that number is what makes it drop updates on the books it is already following. So the number
of books latched across the whole sheet must never exceed the engine's track count, and a firm
cannot take a latch when every track is already in use, however free the book itself may be.

An order is rested in a book by the firm holding that book's latch, and rests there until it is
matched away. Matching happens on its own as the auction proceeds.

A member firm can go slow without failing. A slow firm keeps its segment and its latches — it has
not crashed, its session is up, it is simply not doing anything with them for a while — and nobody
may take them off it. Its tracks stay occupied for as long as it is slow, which is exactly why the
track count binds. A slow firm resumes on its own and carries on.

The full set of actions is: TakeSegment, in which a firm holding no segment takes a free one;
TakeBook, in which a firm latches a free book inside the segment it holds, provided a track is free;
Rest, in which a firm rests an order in a book it has latched; DropBook, in which a firm gives a book
latch back; DropSegment, in which a firm holding no latch inside a segment gives that segment back;
Match, in which a resting order is matched away; Stall, in which a firm goes slow while keeping
everything it holds; and Resume, in which a slow firm comes back up to speed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of books latched across the whole sheet never exceeds the number of
tracks the matching engine has to follow them on.

regardless of whose lease is on it: the lease is torn up and whatever robot is sitting there is

A library group runs reservations and stock control across several branches from one catalogue.
Withdrawing a title is the one act it cannot take back: the copies go to the pulper, and a title
withdrawn twice means a second branch's stock shredded on the strength of a request that was already
carried out. So a withdrawal must happen to a title once and once only.

The catalogue is numbered by epoch. A branch raises a withdrawal order for a title that has not
already gone, and the order is stamped with the catalogue epoch it was raised under. A branch raises
at most one order per title. An order is only carried out while its stamp matches the running epoch:
an order from an earlier catalogue may be pointing at a record that has since been merged or
renumbered, so it is never acted on and is purged instead. Orders can also simply be withdrawn by
the branch that raised them.

When an order is carried out, the title is pulped and every other branch's order for that same title
goes with it, so no second order can ever be presented for it.

The hold shelf has a capacity that changes while the service runs. Reservations go onto the shelf
while there is room and come off when readers collect them. Recataloguing advances the epoch and
resizes the hold shelf at the same time, never below the number of reservations already sitting on
it.

The full set of actions is: Raise, in which a branch raises a withdrawal order, stamped with the
running epoch, for a title that has not been pulped and that it has not already ordered; Pulp, in
which an order whose stamp matches the running epoch is carried out, pulping the title and clearing
every order for it; Withdraw, in which a branch takes its own order back; Purge, in which an order
stamped with an earlier epoch is cleared away unacted on; Reserve, in which a reservation goes onto
the hold shelf while there is room; Collect, in which a reader takes a reservation off the shelf; and
Recatalogue, in which the catalogue epoch advances and the hold shelf is resized, never below what
is already on it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No withdrawal order is ever left standing against a title that has already been
pulped, so the one-way act can never be carried out on the same title twice.

    /\ orders = {}

    /\ shelf = MaxShelf
