\* and is never raised against a title that has already gone.
Raise(t, b) ==
    /\ t \notin pulped
    /\ \A o \in orders : ~(o.title = t /\ o.by = b)

A car wash pulls cars along a conveyor that holds only so many at once. Two booking systems put cars
onto it — the chain's phone app and the forecourt kiosk — and they were written by different
suppliers with no link between them beyond the line counter itself. Overfilling the conveyor jams
the rails, so the number of cars on the line must never exceed what it can hold.

Neither system locks the counter. Each reads the counter along with its version number, works out
its booking off-line, and only then tries to write back. The write goes through only if the version
is still the one it read, the count it read leaves room on the line, and the version counter has not
run to the end of its range; the write then bumps the version. If the version moved while the
booking was being worked out — because the other system got in first — or the line was already full,
the attempt clashes and the system starts again from a fresh read. Neither system leaves a
half-finished booking hanging: an attempt is always either written or clashed.

Cars come off the far end of the line as they finish, which drops the count and bumps the version
too. The version counter is renumbered back to the start between sessions, and only while neither
system has a read outstanding, so a stale read can never be mistaken for a current one by the
numbering coming round again.

line count and version; CommitApp and CommitKiosk, in which the write goes through because the

because any of those checks failed; Roll, in which a car comes off the end of the line, dropping the
count and bumping the version; and Renumber, in which the version counter goes back to the start
with nothing in flight.

holding a current version number read the count that is actually on the line.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Neither booking system is ever left with an attempt hanging: every read is
eventually either written or clashed.

A smart-home door lock network pairs key fobs to locks. Pairing a fob blows a one-time slot in the
fob's secure element: the write cannot be reversed, and blowing the same fob's slot twice bricks it,
leaving the householder locked out. So a fob must be burnt once and once only.

Two hubs drive the same pool of fobs and neither was written with the other in mind: the vendor's
cloud hub and the local bridge that keeps working when the internet is down. Each hub has its own
bounded queue of pairing requests and applies backpressure — once a hub's queue is at its cap it
stops accepting requests, and the household app has to try again later.

The fob registrar is what keeps the two hubs apart. A hub takes the request at the head of its queue
and begins burning only if the fob has not already been burnt and the registrar shows it unclaimed,
and beginning claims it for that hub. If the fob is already burnt, or already claimed by the other
hub, or the hub is already part-way through a burn of its own, the request is dropped from the queue
rather than left to sit behind. When the burn completes the slot is blown for good and the claim is
released. A hub can also abandon a burn part-way through, which releases the claim with the slot
still unblown.

The full set of actions is: Accept, in which a hub takes a pairing request onto the tail of its queue
while the queue is below its cap; Begin, in which a hub starts burning the fob at the head of its
queue, having found it unburnt and unclaimed, and claims it; Skip, in which the request at the head
of a hub's queue is dropped because the fob is burnt, claimed by the other hub, or the hub is
already burning something; Burn, in which the one-time slot is blown and the claim released; and
Abandon, in which a hub gives up part-way through and releases the claim.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any hub part-way through a burn is working on a fob that has not already been burnt
and that the registrar has claimed for that same hub, so a fob's one-time slot can never be blown
twice.

An airport baggage router sends bags to make-up stands, one stand per departing flight's build. A

been taken in the meantime, or pulled out of service, the plan is bounced off the belt instead. Bags
leave stands the ordinary way when the build is loaded onto the aircraft.

pulled out of service and put back later; a bag can be hauled straight off a stand; and the belt can

closes the belt to new plans or reopens it.

A hospital pharmacy dispenses against electronic prescriptions. Each prescription carries a revision
number that rolls on every time the script is annotated or amended, and every technician carries a
policy badge that has to match the pharmacy's current policy generation. The safety case is about
who did the work and against what: nothing may be made up by a technician who has been struck off,
nor by one carrying a superseded badge, nor from a revision of the script that has since been

make the preparation up; the script stays open to amendment the whole time. Only one preparation is
on the bench at a time. Handing the medication over is what commits it: the script is annotated,
which rolls its revision on, and the bench is cleared. A technician can also simply abandon a
preparation. Nothing is ever left half-made — a preparation on the bench is always eventually either
handed over or abandoned.

Anything that would leave the bench working from a picture that has been superseded tears the draft
up in the same movement. Amending a script tears up a draft made from it. Turning the policy
generation, which invalidates every badge at once, tears up whatever is on the bench. A technician
still on the roster can re-badge to the current generation and start again.

The pharmacist has a privileged override on individuals: a technician can be struck off mid-shift,
and whatever they had on the bench goes with them. Somebody struck off can be reinstated later, but
comes back with a zeroed badge and has to re-badge before they can work.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a rostered, correctly badged technician notes a
script's revision and starts making it up on the empty bench; Dispense, in which the preparation is
handed over, the script annotated and its revision rolled on; Abandon, in which the preparation is
given up; Amend, in which a script's revision rolls on and any draft made from it is torn up;
TurnPolicy, in which the policy generation turns and the bench is cleared; Rebadge, in which a
rostered technician refreshes a stale badge; StrikeOff, in which the pharmacist removes a technician
from the roster and tears up their draft; and Reinstate, in which a struck-off technician returns
with a zeroed badge.

roster, carrying the current policy badge, and was worked up from the revision the script is still
on.

handed over or abandoned.

A regional grid sheds load by agreement between its protection relays rather than on one relay's say
so. Opening a feeder is decided by two-phase commit: a relay opens a round on a feeder that is still
closed, the relays vote, and the feeder opens once everybody eligible has voted in favour.

Eligibility is what the safety case turns on. Every relay carries a copy of the protection settings
group, and the grid publishes a running group number. A relay counts only while it is armed and its
copy matches the published group: a relay that has been disarmed is not part of the scheme at all,
and a relay still carrying a superseded settings group is reasoning from trip thresholds that have
been replaced. Neither may open a round and neither may have its vote counted.

Publishing a new settings group supersedes every relay's copy at once, so any round in flight is
torn down rather than carried across the change. A relay brings its copy up to the published group
by adopting it, and can then take part again. Feeders that have been opened are reclosed as demand
recovers.

The control room has a privileged override on both halves. A relay can be disarmed on the spot: its
vote is pulled out of the round and, if it was the relay running the round, the round is dropped
altogether. A disarmed relay can be rearmed later. The control room can also open a feeder outright,
with no round and no vote at all.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which an armed, in-group relay opens a round on a closed
feeder and clears the tally; Aye, in which an armed, in-group relay adds its vote to the round;
Commit, in which every eligible relay having voted in favour opens the feeder and closes the round;
Abort, in which the round is dropped with nothing opened; Reclose, in which an opened feeder is
closed again; Publish, in which a new settings group is issued and any round in flight is torn down;
Adopt, in which a relay brings its copy up to the published group; Disarm, in which the control room
disarms a relay, pulling its vote and dropping any round it was running; Rearm, in which a disarmed
relay is brought back into the scheme; and ForceShed, in which the control room opens a feeder
outright.

published settings group, and every vote behind it comes from such a relay, so nobody disarmed and
nobody on a superseded settings group is ever part of a shedding decision.

    /\ r \notin ayes
    /\ ayes' = ayes \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, shed>>

Commit ==
    /\ prop # NoProp
    /\ InSync \subseteq ayes
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {prop.feeder}
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed>>

Abort ==
    /\ prop # NoProp
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, shed>>

Reclose(f) ==
    /\ f \in shed
    /\ shed' = shed \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, ayes>>

\* A new settings group supersedes every relay's copy at once, so any round in
\* flight is torn down rather than carried across the change.
Publish ==
    /\ group' = IF group = MaxGroup THEN 0 ELSE group + 1
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ ayes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, armed, shed>>

Adopt(r) ==
    /\ carried[r] # group
    /\ carried' = [carried EXCEPT ![r] = group]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, armed, prop, ayes, shed>>

    /\ armed' = armed \ {r}
    /\ ayes' = ayes \ {r}

    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, shed>>

Rearm(r) ==
    /\ r \notin armed
    /\ armed' = armed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, prop, ayes, shed>>

ForceShed(f) ==
    /\ f \notin shed
    /\ shed' = shed \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<group, carried, armed, prop, ayes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Relays, f \in Feeders : Propose(r, f)
    \/ \E r \in Relays : Aye(r) \/ Adopt(r) \/ Disarm(r) \/ Rearm(r)
    \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Publish
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Reclose(f) \/ ForceShed(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A round in flight is run by a relay that is armed and on the running
\* settings group, and every aye behind it comes from such a relay, so nobody
\* disarmed and nobody on a superseded settings group is ever part of a
\* shedding decision.
RoundIsInSync ==
    prop # NoProp => (prop.by \in InSync /\ ayes \subseteq InSync)

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway line keeps a route-plan record for each junction, and the records are versioned: every
edit rolls the revision on. Two signalling cabins edit them. The hazard is a lost update — a cabin
writing an edit it worked out from a revision that has since been replaced, silently wiping what the
other cabin just wrote.

Editing is done under two levels of lock. A cabin first takes the area panel, which admits one cabin
at a time, and only then may it latch a junction, and only one junction anywhere on the line is
latched at a time. The area panel is given back once the cabin holds no latch.

Reads are deliberately not locked. A cabin can read a junction's revision number at any moment,
without holding anything, and go away and work out its edit from it. That is exactly how it can end
up holding a revision number that has moved on by the time it gets the latch. So the write is
checked: an edit only lands if the revision the cabin is holding is still the revision the record is
on. Every edit that lands records the revision it was worked out from. When a record reaches the end
of its revision range it is archived and starts again from zero.

A cabin working the area can go slow without failing. It keeps the area panel and its latch and
simply stops for a while — nobody may take them off it, because it has not failed and will come back
of its own accord. It always does come back, and no junction latch is held for ever.

The full set of actions is: TakeArea, in which a cabin that is not slow takes the free area panel;
TakeLatch, in which the cabin on the area latches a junction while no junction anywhere is latched;
Read, in which any cabin reads a junction's revision number without holding anything; Write, in
which the cabin holding a junction's latch lands an edit, provided the revision it read is still the
one the record is on, recording the revision it was worked out from; Release, in which a cabin gives
a junction latch back; DropArea, in which a cabin holding no latch gives the area panel back;
Dawdle, in which the cabin on the area goes slow while holding everything; CatchUp, in which a slow
cabin comes back up to speed; and Archive, in which an unlatched record at the end of its revision
range starts again from zero.

before it, so no cabin's edit was ever laid down over a revision it had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No junction latch is held for ever, even by a cabin that has gone slow.

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router shifts bags between holding bays. The terminal counts bags at the start of
every shift and the count has to hold: a bag that vanishes from the system is a bag on the wrong
aircraft, and a bag that appears from nowhere is a double-count that hides the first mistake. So the
bags piled in the bays plus anything the router is holding mid-move must always come to the
terminal's total.

Moves are agreed by two-phase commit between the parties that have to sign them off, the sorter
control and the apron desk. Preparing a move lifts the batch out of the source bay straight away and
puts it into the router's escrow, where it sits for the length of the round — out of the source bay
and not yet in the destination. Each party then casts one vote. If both vote in favour, and the
destination is still open, the batch is committed into the destination bay and escrow is emptied. A
vote against, or the destination being frozen while the round is running, rolls the batch back into
the bay it came from. Either way the batch leaves escrow exactly as it arrived. Only one round is
in flight at a time.

The duty manager has a privileged override. A bay can be frozen, which stops rounds being prepared
against it and rolls back any round already heading for it, and thawed again later. The manager can
also carry a batch across by hand, moving it out of one bay and into another in one step with no
round and no vote at all.

The full set of actions is: Prepare, in which a batch is lifted out of an open source bay into
escrow and a round is opened on an open destination; Aye and Nay, in which a party casts its single
vote; Commit, in which both votes in favour and an open destination put the batch into the
destination bay; Rollback, in which a vote against or a frozen destination puts the batch back where
it came from; Freeze and Thaw, in which the duty manager closes and reopens a bay; and Carry, in
which the duty manager moves a batch between bays by hand.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The bags piled across all holding bays plus the batch sitting in the router's escrow
always equal the terminal's total.

Piled(S) ==

    /\ s # d
    /\ s \notin frozen
    /\ d \notin frozen

    /\ txn.dst \notin frozen
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![txn.dst] = @ + txn.qty]
    /\ txn' = NoTxn
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, frozen>>

    /\ txn' = NoTxn

\* by hand with no round and no vote at all.
Freeze(b) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, ballot>>

Thaw(b) ==
    /\ b \in frozen
    /\ frozen' = frozen \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, txn, ballot>>

Carry(s, d, q) ==
    /\ s # d
    /\ q <= hold[s]
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![s] = @ - q, ![d] = @ + q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txn, ballot, frozen>>

    \/ \E s, d \in Bays, q \in 1 .. MaxBatch : Prepare(s, d, q) \/ Carry(s, d, q)
    \/ \E p \in Parties : Aye(p) \/ Nay(p)
    \/ Commit \/ Rollback
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Freeze(b) \/ Thaw(b)

\* Bags only ever move between a bay and the router's escrow, so the bags piled
\* in the bays plus the batch in escrow always come to the terminal's total.

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital blood bank allocates units of blood to patients. A unit goes to one patient and one
patient only, and the physical bag carries a printed label naming the patient it is reserved for.
The dangerous state is a bag carrying a live label for one patient while the register has it
allocated to somebody else — that is how the wrong blood reaches a bedside.

The register is versioned and the cross-match bench takes no locks. The bench notes the version a
unit is on and goes away to cross-match, leaving the register free to move underneath it. The
allocation only lands if the version is still the one it noted and the unit is still unallocated;
landing it bumps the unit's version and prints a fresh label carrying the patient and the new
version. If the version moved, or the unit was allocated in the meantime, the request is refused and
the bench starts again. One request is on the bench at a time and the bench never sits on it. When a
unit is transfused it goes back to unallocated and its version bumps again, which leaves whatever
label the bag is carrying behind the register.

The consultant haematologist has a privileged override and can reassign a unit in the register on the
spot, without going near the bag. The version bumps but the bag is not relabelled, so the label it is
carrying is behind the register and counts for nothing until somebody reprints it. Labels are
reprinted from the register when a bag is checked, and stripped off when a bag is boxed up. A unit
whose version has run to the end of its range, with nothing allocated and no label on the bag, has
its version recycled back to the start.

The full set of actions is: Request, in which the bench notes a unit's version and takes on a
cross-match for a patient; Allocate, in which the allocation lands because the version is unmoved and
the unit unallocated, bumping the version and printing a fresh label; Refuse, in which the request is
turned down; Transfuse, in which an allocated unit is used and goes back to unallocated with its
version bumped; Reassign, in which the haematologist reassigns a unit in the register without
relabelling the bag; Reprint, in which a bag's label is reprinted from the register; Strip, in which
a label is taken off a bag; and Recycle, in which an unallocated, unlabelled unit's version is reset.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any label whose version still matches the register names exactly the patient the
register has that unit allocated to, so no unit ever carries a live label for one patient while
allocated to another.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The cross-match bench never sits on a request: every one is eventually either
allocated or refused.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od10m4p1t5`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway line runs off a working timetable book that every signal box amends. The book is versioned:
revision one is the first amendment ever written into it, revision two the next, and so on. The
hazard is a lost update — one box's amendment written over a revision it never saw, quietly undoing
what another box just put in.

Amendments queue on a bounded list with backpressure. A box drafts an amendment against whatever
revision the book is on at that moment, and the draft carries that base revision with it. Once the
queue is at its cap no further drafts are taken, and the queue is closed altogether while the book is
frozen.

The queue is worked from the front. An amendment lands only while the book is still on the revision
it was drafted against; landing it writes the amendment in as the next revision and moves the book
on. If the book has moved in the meantime, or the book has reached the end of its revision range,
the amendment is bounced off the queue and its box has to draft again from the revision now in force.

The line controller has a privileged override and can write an amendment straight into the book,
jumping the queue entirely. Even then the amendment goes in against the revision it supersedes, so
the book's chain of revisions stays unbroken. When the book reaches the end of its range and nothing
is queued, it is reissued and starts again from revision zero.

The full set of actions is: Draft, in which a box puts an amendment on the tail of the queue against
the revision in force, while the queue is open and below its cap; Apply, in which the amendment at
the front lands because the book is still on the revision it was drafted against, becoming the next
revision; Bounce, in which the amendment at the front is thrown off because the book has moved or
run out of range; Force, in which the line controller writes an amendment straight into the book
against the revision it supersedes; Freeze, in which the controller closes or reopens the queue; and
Reissue, in which a book at the end of its range with nothing queued starts again from zero.

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library reservation system puts holds on copies and, when a copy is not returned, raises a loss
charge against the reader who had it. Raising the charge is the one act the library will not take
back: the reader's account is debited and the debit stands. Charging the same copy twice bills a
reader for one book two or three times over, so it must happen to a copy once and once only.

Holds are leases with an expiry rather than standing claims. A copy is put on hold for a reader for
a chosen number of days, provided no live hold is already on it and the expiry falls inside the
year. Holds that have run out are reaped and the copy goes back on the shelf.

A loss charge is raised at the charge desk, one at a time. It is begun only for a copy that has not
already been charged, is not waived, and is under a live hold — the hold is what says whose account
to debit. A charge in progress rests on that hold: the moment the hold lapses as the clock moves on,
or is reaped, the charge falls off the desk with it, and the desk is never left occupied. A charge
can also simply be dropped by the assistant.

The head librarian has a privileged override and can waive a copy: no charge may be begun on it, and
any charge already on the desk for it is knocked off. A waiver can be lifted later. At the year end,
with the desk clear and no holds outstanding, the clock is reset.

The full set of actions is: Reserve, in which a copy with no live hold is put on hold for a reader,
expiring inside the year; Begin, in which a charge is taken to the desk for a copy that is unwaived,
uncharged and under a live hold; Charge, in which the debit is raised and the copy recorded as
charged; Drop, in which the assistant abandons the charge on the desk; Tick, in which the clock
advances a day and a charge whose hold has just lapsed falls off the desk; Reap, in which a hold that
has run out is cleared, taking any charge on the desk for that copy with it; Waive and Unwaive, in
which the head librarian waives a copy and lifts the waiver; and NewYear, in which the clock is reset
with the desk clear and no holds outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any loss charge on the desk is for a copy that has not been charged already and
rests on a hold that is still live and names the very reader being charged, so the one-way debit can
never be raised twice on the same copy.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The charge desk is never left occupied: a charge taken to it is always eventually
raised or cleared away.

vars == <<hold, clock, charged, charging, waived>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ hold \in [Copies -> Holds \cup {Vacant}]

    /\ charged \subseteq Copies
    /\ charging \in Charges \cup {NoCharge}
    /\ waived \subseteq Copies

Init ==
    /\ hold = [c \in Copies |-> Vacant]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ charged = {}
    /\ charging = NoCharge
    /\ waived = {}

\* A hold is a lease with an expiry, not a standing claim on the copy.
Reserve(r, c, len) ==
    /\ ~Live(c)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![c] = [to |-> r, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, charged, charging, waived>>

\* Raising a loss charge is one-way: the reader's account is debited and the
\* library will not take it back, so it must happen to a copy once only.

    /\ c \notin charged
    /\ c \notin waived
    /\ Live(c)
    /\ charging' = [copy |-> c, to |-> hold[c].to]

Charge ==

    /\ charged' = charged \cup {charging.copy}
    /\ charging' = NoCharge
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, waived>>

Drop ==

    /\ charging' = NoCharge
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged, waived>>

Reap(c) ==

    /\ hold[c].until <= clock
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![c] = Vacant]
    /\ charging' = IF charging # NoCharge /\ charging.copy = c THEN NoCharge ELSE charging
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, charged, waived>>

\* being raised on it and knocks any charge already in progress off the desk.
Waive(c) ==
    /\ c \notin waived
    /\ waived' = waived \cup {c}
    /\ charging' = IF charging # NoCharge /\ charging.copy = c THEN NoCharge ELSE charging

    /\ waived' = waived \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, clock, charged, charging>>

    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ charging = NoCharge
    /\ \A c \in Copies : hold[c] = Vacant

    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, charged, charging, waived>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Readers, c \in Copies, n \in 1 .. MaxHold : Reserve(r, c, n)
    \/ \E c \in Copies : Begin(c) \/ Reap(c) \/ Waive(c) \/ Unwaive(c)
    \/ Settling \/ Tick \/ NewYear

\* A loss charge on the desk is for a copy that has not been charged already,
\* and rests on a hold that is still live and names the very reader being
\* charged, so the one-way debit can never be raised twice on one copy.

        /\ hold[charging.copy].until > clock

ChargeDeskClears == (charging # NoCharge) ~> (charging = NoCharge)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library holds reserved books for collection on hold shelves, one bay per reserved copy. A bay takes
one copy: allocating the same bay to two copies means one reader walks off with the other's
reservation, so a bay must never be allocated twice.

Shelving is worked at two levels. An assistant takes a branch desk, working one branch at a time,
and only then draws the ticket for a single empty bay in that branch — one ticket per assistant. The
ticket is what says who is allocating that bay.

Allocation itself is done in pencil first. The assistant holding a bay's ticket pencils a copy into
it, and only a copy that is not already pencilled into or sitting in any bay anywhere. Placing the
copy turns the pencilling into a shelved copy and gives the ticket back in the same movement.
Rubbing out leaves the bay empty and the ticket still held. A ticket is given back once nothing is
pencilled against it, and a branch desk is left once the assistant holds no ticket in that branch.
Readers collect their copies off the shelf, which empties the bay.

The head librarian has a privileged override and can strip a bay outright — ticket, pencilling and
copy all at once — without asking whoever was holding it. That is how a bay is recovered when an
assistant goes home mid-task.

The full set of actions is: TakeDesk, in which an assistant working no branch takes a free branch
desk; DrawTicket, in which the assistant on a branch draws the ticket for an empty bay in it, holding
no other ticket; Pencil, in which the ticket holder pencils in a copy that is nowhere else; Place, in
which the pencilled copy is shelved and the ticket given back; Rub, in which the pencilling is rubbed
out; ReturnTicket, in which a ticket with nothing pencilled against it is given back; LeaveDesk, in
which an assistant holding no ticket in a branch leaves its desk; Collect, in which a reader takes a
copy off the shelf; and Strip, in which the head librarian clears a bay's ticket, pencilling and copy
at once.

which is not already holding a copy, so a bay is never allocated to two copies at once.

\* then draws the ticket for a single empty bay in that branch.
TakeDesk(p, b) ==

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A warehouse robot fleet works a recirculating belt of totes. The floor starts with a fixed number of
totes and the robots only ever move them between the belt, their own grippers and the stacking bins;
nothing is added and nothing is lost. So the totes stacked in the bins, plus those in grippers, plus
those on the belt, must always come to the floor total — including when a robot dies in the middle of
a carry.

Only one robot works at a time, and the right to work travels with a baton that walks the fleet ring
one robot at a time. The robot holding the baton, and only that robot, may lift a tote off the belt
into its gripper, or stow the tote it is carrying into a bin. Totes are put back onto the belt from
the bins as the picking rounds come round again.

A robot can die on the spot with no word at all — no fault code, no handover — still holding the
baton and whatever was in its gripper. Nothing it holds is released by the death itself. The fleet
supervisor puts the baton back into circulation whenever it is stranded on a dead robot, and the
baton never stays stranded. A tote left in a dead robot's gripper is salvaged back onto the belt,
and a robot with an empty gripper can be revived and rejoin the ring. At least one robot is always
left running.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which a live baton holder passes it to the next robot round
the ring; Lift, in which the live baton holder takes a tote off the belt into its empty gripper;
Stow, in which the live baton holder puts the tote it carries into a bin; Recirculate, in which a
tote goes from a bin back onto the belt; Die, in which a robot stops dead while still holding the
baton and its tote, provided at least one other robot is left running; Reissue, in which the
supervisor puts a stranded baton back onto a live robot; Salvage, in which a tote is recovered from a
dead robot's gripper back onto the belt; and Revive, in which a dead robot with an empty gripper
rejoins the fleet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The totes stacked across the bins plus those held in robot grippers plus those on
the belt always equal the floor total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The baton never stays stranded on a dead robot — it is always eventually put back
onto a live one.

Bots == 0 .. FleetSize - 1
Nxt(r) == (r + 1) % FleetSize

VARIABLES bin, grip, belt, baton, alive

vars == <<bin, grip, belt, baton, alive>>

RECURSIVE Stacked(_)
Stacked(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN bin[b] + Stacked(S \ {b})

Carried == Cardinality({r \in Bots : grip[r] = 1})

TypeOK ==
    /\ bin \in [Bins -> 0 .. TotalTotes]
    /\ grip \in [Bots -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ belt \in 0 .. TotalTotes

    /\ alive \subseteq Bots

Init ==
    /\ bin = [b \in Bins |-> 0]
    /\ grip = [r \in Bots |-> 0]
    /\ belt = TotalTotes
    /\ baton = 0
    /\ alive = Bots

\* The baton walks the ring; only the live robot holding it may touch a tote.
PassBaton ==
    /\ baton \in alive
    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, alive>>

Lift(r) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 0
    /\ belt > 0
    /\ belt' = belt - 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, baton, alive>>

Stow(r, b) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ grip[r] = 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ bin' = [bin EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, baton, alive>>

Recirculate(b) ==
    /\ bin[b] > 0
    /\ bin' = [bin EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ belt' = belt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grip, baton, alive>>

\* A robot can die on the spot with no word, still holding the baton and
\* whatever was in its gripper.
Die(r) ==
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ alive \ {r} # {}
    /\ alive' = alive \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, baton>>

\* The fleet supervisor puts the baton back into circulation whenever it is
\* stranded on a dead robot.
Reissue(r) ==
    /\ baton \notin alive
    /\ r \in alive
    /\ baton' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, alive>>

Salvage(r) ==
    /\ r \notin alive
    /\ grip[r] = 1
    /\ grip' = [grip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ belt' = belt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, baton, alive>>

Revive(r) ==
    /\ r \notin alive
    /\ grip[r] = 0
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bin, grip, belt, baton>>

Reissuing == \E r \in Bots : Reissue(r)

Next ==
    \/ PassBaton
    \/ \E r \in Bots : Lift(r) \/ Die(r) \/ Salvage(r) \/ Revive(r)
    \/ \E r \in Bots, b \in Bins : Stow(r, b)
    \/ \E b \in Bins : Recirculate(b)
    \/ Reissuing

\* stacked in bins plus those in grippers plus those on the belt always come to
\* the fleet total -- a robot dying mid-carry loses nothing.

\* The baton never stays stranded on a dead robot.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library group keeps one reservation queue per title, shared across its branches. The queue record
holds how many readers are waiting and carries a revision number that rolls on every time the record
changes. The hazard is a lost update: a branch writing a change it worked out from a copy of the
record that has since been replaced, silently undoing what another branch just did.

Branches take no lock. Each keeps its own copy of the queue length together with the revision that
copy came from, and refreshes it from the record whenever it likes. When a branch wants to put a
reader on the queue or take one off, it lodges a request stamped with the revision its copy came
from. One request is on the desk at a time and the desk never sits on one.

The request lands only if the record is still on the revision the branch worked from; landing it
changes the queue length and rolls the revision on. If the revision has moved in the meantime, or
the change does not fit — nobody to take off an empty queue, no room on the shelf for another — the
request is declined and the branch refreshes and starts again.

Hold shelf capacity changes while the service runs: shelves are added for the summer reading scheme
and taken away when the building work starts. The shelf is never resized below what is already
sitting on it. When the record reaches the end of its revision range the catalogue is reissued: the
numbering restarts and every branch's copy is re-synced in the same movement, so no branch is left
holding a revision number that has come round again.

The full set of actions is: Refresh, in which a branch takes a fresh copy of the queue length and
revision; Propose, in which a branch lodges a join or leave request stamped with its copy's revision;
Accept, in which the request lands because the record is still on that revision and the change fits,
rolling the revision on; Decline, in which the request is turned down; Resize, in which the hold
shelf capacity is changed at runtime, never below what is on it; and Reissue, in which the revision
numbering restarts and every branch is re-synced.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any branch whose copy carries the revision the record is actually on is holding
exactly the queue length the record actually has, so no branch's update was ever written over one it
had not read.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The reservations desk never sits on a request: every one lodged is eventually
either accepted or declined.

    /\ rev \in 0 .. MaxRev
    /\ queued \in 0 .. MaxShelf
    /\ sawRev \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ sawLen \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxShelf]
    /\ shelf \in 1 .. MaxShelf
    /\ bid \in Bids \cup {NoBid}

    /\ rev = 0
    /\ queued = 0
    /\ sawRev = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ sawLen = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ shelf = MaxShelf
    /\ bid = NoBid

Refresh(b) ==
    /\ sawRev' = [sawRev EXCEPT ![b] = rev]
    /\ sawLen' = [sawLen EXCEPT ![b] = queued]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, queued, shelf, bid>>

\* No lock is taken: the branch works from the copy it last read and stamps
\* its request with the revision that copy came from.
Propose(b, w) ==
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ bid' = [by |-> b, base |-> sawRev[b], want |-> w]

Accept ==

    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ IF bid.want = "join" THEN queued < shelf ELSE queued > 0

    /\ n >= queued

    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ rev' = 0
    /\ sawRev' = [b \in Branches |-> 0]
    /\ sawLen' = [b \in Branches |-> queued]

A subway line shows where its trains are on a berth display: one berth per track section, each
holding one train description. Two train describer systems drive the same display — the north
describer and the south describer, procured separately and never integrated — and they share the
one pool of berths between them.

A description that is being stepped from one berth to the next is lifted off the display into the
describer's own step queue and put back down when the step completes. Every description is therefore
in exactly one place at any instant: on a berth, or in the north describer's queue, or in the
south's. The count must always come to the number of trains the line is describing; a description
that goes missing is a train nobody can see, and one that appears twice is a phantom that will stop
a real train.

The step queues are bounded and apply backpressure, and the two are not the same depth: the north
describer has the deeper queue. A describer stops lifting descriptions off the display once its own
queue is full. At the boundary between the two systems a description is handed straight from the
head of one queue to the tail of the other, subject to the receiving queue's cap; it never touches a
berth on the way across.

Either describer can be isolated for maintenance, after which it lifts nothing new, though whatever
is already in its queue still drops back onto the display or hands across. An isolated describer is
restored when the work is done.

The full set of actions is: LiftNorth and LiftSouth, in which the describer concerned takes a
description off a berth into the tail of its own queue, while it is not isolated and its queue is
below its cap; DropNorth and DropSouth, in which the description at the head of a queue is put back
onto a berth; HandNorthToSouth and HandSouthToNorth, in which the description at the head of one
queue moves to the tail of the other, subject to that queue's cap; and Isolate and Restore, in which
a describer is taken out of service and put back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The descriptions shown on berths plus those in the north describer's queue plus
those in the south describer's queue always add up to exactly the number of trains being described.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A stock exchange runs its opening auction with a fixed number of share lots. Lots sit either in the
pre-auction pot or resting in one of the order books, and the auction only moves them between the
two; nothing is created and nothing destroyed, so the lots resting across the books plus the lots
still in the pot must always come to the session total.

Member firms take no lock on a book. A firm reads the book's depth and its version number and works
its order up while the book stays open to everybody else. Posting the order only goes through if the
version is still the one the firm read, the book has depth left for the quantity, the pot still has
the lots, and the book's version counter has not run to the end of its range. Posting moves the lots
out of the pot and into the book in one step and rolls the book's version on. If any of those checks
fails, the order is missed and the firm works up a fresh one. One working order is on the desk at a
time and the desk never sits on it. Lots are pulled back out of a book into the pot as orders are
cancelled, which also rolls that book's version on.

Book depth is retuned while the auction runs — the exchange widens a book when interest builds and
narrows it when it thins — but never below what is already resting in it. A book whose version
counter has reached the end of its range is renumbered back to the start, with nothing on the desk,
so a stale read cannot be mistaken for a current one.

The full set of actions is: Read, in which a firm takes the current version and depth of a book and
puts a working order on the empty desk; Post, in which the order goes through because the version is
unmoved, the book has room, the pot has the lots and the version range is not exhausted, moving the
lots and rolling the version on; Miss, in which the order is dropped because one of those checks
failed; Pull, in which lots are taken back out of a book into the pot and the version rolls on;
Retune, in which a book's depth is changed at runtime, never below what is resting in it; and
Renumber, in which an exhausted version counter is reset with the desk clear.

pot always equal the session total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The order desk never sits on a working order: every one is eventually either
posted or missed.

    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN book[b] + Resting(S \ {b})

    /\ d # NoDraft
    /\ ver[d.bk] = d.saw
    /\ ver[d.bk] < MaxVer
    /\ book[d.bk] + d.qty <= depth[d.bk]

    /\ ver = [b \in Books |-> 0]
    /\ pot = TotalLots
    /\ depth = [b \in Books |-> MaxDepth]

\* order up while the book stays open to everybody else.

    /\ pot' = pot - draft.qty
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![draft.bk] = @ + 1]
    /\ draft' = NoDraft
    /\ UNCHANGED depth

Miss ==

    /\ ~Sound(draft)
    /\ draft' = NoDraft

    /\ ver[b] < MaxVer

    /\ pot' = pot + q
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<depth, draft>>

    /\ draft = NoDraft

    \/ \E b \in Books, n \in 1 .. MaxDepth : Retune(b, n)
    \/ \E b \in Books : Renumber(b)

An airport baggage router keeps a single routing record that says which chute each flight's bags
go down. Ground handlers edit that record without taking it out of service: a handler first reads
the record and remembers the version stamp it saw, then later submits its recomputed routing. The
submission is accepted only if the version stamp it read is still the current one, so a handler

submissions are refused outright, but the duty supervisor holds a privileged override and may push

A subway signalling system hands out movement authority for a track block only after the

so that nothing decided under the old geometry is counted. Separately, the control centre can

authorised cabin records a no; the poll commits when every cabin's standing answer is a yes; the

answers; the control centre suspends a cabin, wiping that cabin's standing answer; and the control

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
Before a stock exchange opens, incoming orders are staged in a crossing buffer until the opening
auction runs. The buffer has an advertised depth, and the exchange republishes that depth during
the pre-open window as it sees how heavy the morning is: it can add headroom, and it can take
headroom away, but it will only shrink the advertised depth down as far as the number of orders
already staged, never below.

Staging is done by matching engines, and an engine may only stage orders while it holds a live
time-limited allocation on the buffer. An allocation is taken out for a fixed number of pre-open
ticks and counts down; when it reaches zero the engine has no allocation any more and can neither
stage new orders nor keep the ones it staged, so those orders are returned to the unstaged pool and
must be staged again by an engine that does hold one. An engine stages an order only when the
buffer still has room against the currently advertised depth. When the auction crosses an order it
leaves the buffer for good.

The full set of actions is: an engine without an allocation takes one out for the full number of
ticks; an engine's allocation counts down by one tick; an engine holding a live allocation stages
an unstaged order, provided the buffer is below the advertised depth; the auction crosses a staged
order, which leaves the buffer; an engine whose allocation has run out gives back everything it
staged to the unstaged pool; the exchange advertises one more unit of depth; and the exchange
withdraws one unit of depth, which it may do only while the staged count is strictly below the
depth it is withdrawing from.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of orders staged in the crossing buffer, counted across all matching
engines together, never exceeds the depth the exchange currently advertises.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. ---- MODULE W4Od15m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Engines, Orders, MaxDepth, LeaseTicks

VARIABLES staged, unstaged, ticksLeft, depth

vars == <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft, depth>>

\* Everything currently sitting in the crossing buffer, whoever put it there.
Buffered == UNION {staged[e] : e \in Engines}

Load == Cardinality(Buffered)

TypeOK ==
    /\ staged \in [Engines -> SUBSET Orders]
    /\ unstaged \subseteq Orders
    /\ ticksLeft \in [Engines -> 0..LeaseTicks]
    /\ depth \in 0..MaxDepth

Init ==
    /\ staged = [e \in Engines |-> {}]
    /\ unstaged = Orders
    /\ ticksLeft = [e \in Engines |-> 0]
    /\ depth = 1

\* An allocation is taken out for its full run of pre-open ticks.
TakeAllocation(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] = 0
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![e] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, depth>>

CountDown(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] > 0
    /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![e] = ticksLeft[e] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, depth>>

\* Staging is refused unless the buffer is below the advertised depth.
Stage(e, o) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] > 0
    /\ o \in unstaged
    /\ Load < depth
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \cup {o}]
    /\ unstaged' = unstaged \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, depth>>

\* A crossed order leaves the buffer permanently.
Cross(e, o) ==
    /\ o \in staged[e]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = @ \ {o}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unstaged, ticksLeft, depth>>

\* Nothing survives the end of an allocation.
GiveBack(e) ==
    /\ ticksLeft[e] = 0
    /\ staged[e] # {}
    /\ unstaged' = unstaged \cup staged[e]
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![e] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, depth>>

Advertise ==
    /\ depth < MaxDepth
    /\ depth' = depth + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft>>

\* Headroom is only withdrawn while there is headroom to withdraw.
Withdraw ==
    /\ depth > 0
    /\ Load < depth
    /\ depth' = depth - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, unstaged, ticksLeft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Engines :
         \/ TakeAllocation(e) \/ CountDown(e) \/ GiveBack(e)
         \/ \E o \in Orders : Stage(e, o) \/ Cross(e, o)
    \/ Advertise \/ Withdraw

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The buffer never holds more than the exchange says it can.
BufferWithinAdvertisedDepth == Load <= depth

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router keeps a shared manifest listing which bags have been re-tagged for a
later flight. A re-tag is not written straight into the manifest: the router first runs an agreement
round with the sorter stations that touch the bag, and each station either declares itself ready or
refuses. When every station has declared ready, the re-tag is written into the manifest, and the
round is then in the written state. From there the router sends the airline its acknowledgement,
which is the point at which the airline is entitled to treat the re-tag as durable.

A write that has not yet been acknowledged may still be backed out: the router removes it from the
manifest and returns to idle, which is what happens when the round is torn down after the write but
before the airline is told. Once the acknowledgement has gone out, backing the write out is not
available. If any station refuses during the agreement round, the round is abandoned without a
write at all. The duty supervisor holds a privileged override and may push the round straight into
the written state without waiting for the stations to declare, which is used when a flight is
closing and the stations are too slow to poll.

The full set of actions is: the router opens an agreement round on some re-tag; a station
declares itself ready; a station refuses; the write lands in the manifest once every station has
declared ready; the acknowledgement goes out to the airline and the round returns to idle; the
round is abandoned when a station has refused; an unacknowledged write is backed out of the
manifest; and the duty supervisor overrides the round straight into the written state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every re-tag the airline has been sent an acknowledgement for is still present in
the shared manifest, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A round that has reached the written state never stays there indefinitely; it
eventually returns to idle.

TypeOK ==

    /\ acked \subseteq Retags
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "agreeing", "written"}
    /\ declared \in [Stations -> {"none", "ready", "refuse"}]
    /\ active \in Retags \cup {NoRetag}

AllReady == \A s \in Stations : declared[s] = "ready"

Init ==
    /\ manifest = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ declared = [s \in Stations |-> "none"]
    /\ active = NoRetag

\* The router is always free to open a fresh round on some re-tag.
OpenRound(r) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ active' = r
    /\ phase' = "agreeing"
    /\ declared' = [s \in Stations |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked>>

Declare(s, v) ==
    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ declared[s] = "none"
    /\ declared' = [declared EXCEPT ![s] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked, phase, active>>

    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ AllReady
    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "written"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, declared, active>>

    /\ manifest' = manifest \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "written"

    /\ acked' = acked \cup {active}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag

    /\ active \notin acked
    /\ manifest' = manifest \ {active}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, declared>>

    /\ phase = "agreeing"
    /\ \E s \in Stations : declared[s] = "refuse"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ active' = NoRetag
    /\ UNCHANGED <<manifest, acked, declared>>

    \/ \E r \in Retags : OpenRound(r)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Declare(s, "ready") \/ Declare(s, "refuse")

NoAcknowledgedRetagLost == acked \subseteq manifest

carrying and whichever bin it had noted stay frozen with it. The rest of the wall keeps working
around it until a technician power-cycles it, at which point it comes back empty-handed with no bin

prescription stops naming a bin.

collects from a labelled bin, wiping the label and the ticket.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A regional power grid runs a load shedder. The region carries a fixed number of megawatts of
customer demand, and every megawatt is at all times in exactly one of three places: energised on
one of the feeders, parked in the shed pool waiting to be brought back, or riding on a dispatch
order that has left the control room but has not yet been applied at the receiving feeder.

Dispatch orders travel over the grid's telemetry bus, which does not preserve order: several orders
can be outstanding at once and they may be applied in any sequence, not necessarily the sequence
they were issued in. An order names one receiving feeder and a block of megawatts. The block is
taken off its source the moment the order is issued and only appears on the receiving feeder when
the order is applied, so it is never counted in two places and never disappears in between.

Shedding and dispatching are directed by the control room's coordinator, which is one of the
feeders acting in that role. The coordinator can drop out at any moment, leaving the region with no
coordinator; any feeder can then take the role over. While there is no coordinator, no load is shed
and no dispatch order is issued, though orders already on the bus can still be applied.

The full set of actions is: a feeder takes over as coordinator when there is none; the sitting
coordinator drops out; under a coordinator, a block is shed off a feeder into the shed pool; under
a coordinator, a block is taken out of the shed pool and issued as a dispatch order onto a free
slot on the bus; an outstanding order is applied, adding its block to the receiving feeder and
freeing its slot; and a block is moved directly off one feeder onto the bus as an order addressed
to another feeder.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The megawatts energised across all feeders, plus those parked in the shed pool,
plus those riding on outstanding dispatch orders, always add up to exactly the region's fixed
demand.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the region is left without a coordinator, some feeder eventually takes
the role over.

VARIABLES energised, pool, bus, coordinator

vars == <<energised, pool, bus, coordinator>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ energised \in [Feeders -> 0..Demand]
    /\ pool \in 0..Demand
    /\ bus \in [Slots -> Order \cup {Free}]
    /\ coordinator \in Feeders \cup {NoLeader}

RECURSIVE OnFeeders(_)
OnFeeders(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN energised[f] + OnFeeders(S \ {f})

RECURSIVE OnBus(_)
OnBus(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN

    /\ bus = [s \in Slots |-> Free]

    /\ coordinator = NoLeader

    /\ coordinator' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<energised, pool, bus>>

    /\ bus[s] = Free

Apply(s) ==

    /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![bus[s].dest] = @ + bus[s].block]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![s] = Free]

    \/ \E f \in Feeders, k \in 1..MaxBlock, s \in Slots : Issue(f, k, s)

    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(TakeOverSome)

DemandConserved == OnFeeders(Feeders) + pool + OnBus(Slots) = Demand

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A car-wash site runs two conveyor lines side by side. The lines are otherwise independent, but they
share a single bank of hot-air blowers, and a car cannot enter the drying tunnel unless a blower is
free for it. The number of blowers is fixed and is the site's shared capacity.

Availability is tracked in one shared booking counter that both lines can see. There is no
reservation desk: a line that wants to send a car into the drying tunnel first reads the booking
counter and remembers the figure it read, and then, when it is ready to move the car, writes back
the figure it read plus one. That write only takes effect if the counter still holds exactly the
figure the line remembered; if the other line has booked in the meantime the counter no longer
matches, the remembered figure is thrown away, and the line reads again. A line will only attempt
the write if the figure it remembered was still below the site's capacity.

Cars queue at the entry of each line before they are booked in, and when a car comes out of the
drying tunnel the booking counter is decremented and the car leaves the site.

The full set of actions is: a car arrives and joins the entry queue of one of the lines; a line
reads the shared booking counter and remembers the figure; a line whose remembered figure is still
below capacity and still matches the counter writes back that figure plus one, which moves a queued
car into the drying tunnel; a line whose remembered figure no longer matches the counter throws it
away and will read again; and a car leaves the drying tunnel, which decrements the booking counter.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars inside the shared drying tunnel, counted across both conveyor
lines together, never exceeds the number of blowers the site has.

vars == <<counter, remembered, drying, queued>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ counter \in 0..Blowers
    /\ remembered \in [Lines -> (0..Blowers) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ drying \in [Lines -> 0..Blowers]
    /\ queued \in [Lines -> 0..EntryDepth]

RECURSIVE InTunnel(_)
InTunnel(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET l == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN drying[l] + InTunnel(S \ {l})

Init ==
    /\ counter = 0
    /\ remembered = [l \in Lines |-> NoRead]
    /\ drying = [l \in Lines |-> 0]
    /\ queued = [l \in Lines |-> 0]

Arrive(l) ==
    /\ queued[l] < EntryDepth
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, remembered, drying>>

\* The read half: the line notes the figure it saw and reserves nothing.
ReadCounter(l) ==
    /\ remembered[l] = NoRead
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = counter]

\* The write half: it takes effect only if the counter still matches.
Book(l) ==

    /\ remembered[l] = counter
    /\ remembered[l] < Blowers
    /\ queued[l] > 0
    /\ counter' = remembered[l] + 1
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = NoRead]
    /\ drying' = [drying EXCEPT ![l] = @ + 1]
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]

\* The other line got there first, so the remembered figure is worthless.
Reread(l) ==
    /\ remembered[l] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[l] # counter
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![l] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, drying, queued>>

Leave(l) ==
    /\ drying[l] > 0
    /\ counter > 0
    /\ drying' = [drying EXCEPT ![l] = @ - 1]
    /\ counter' = counter - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remembered, queued>>

Next ==

terminal that currently holds the yard-wide claim, and only if no one else already has that bay. It
draws a cart out of a bay it has claimed, and the cart goes out with that terminal.

gives up the yard-wide claim, which also drops all the bay claims it was holding; and a terminal
pushes one of its carts back into a bay.

always add up to exactly the airfield's fixed cart count.

A container-ship crane yard has several gantry cranes that all need the same single transfer lane
running under the ship's side. Only one crane may be standing in that lane at a time, because two
booms over the same lane will foul each other.

The lane is guarded by one register that either reads "free" or carries the name of a crane. A
crane that wants the lane first looks at the register; if what it saw was "free" it then attempts
the swap, writing its own name in place of "free". The swap only goes through while the register
still reads "free", so if another crane wrote its name first, the attempt is abandoned and the
crane will look again later. A crane whose name is in the register may then move into the lane, do
a bounded number of container moves, and finally pull out, which puts the register back to "free".

The yard supervisor holds a privileged override for emergencies such as a shifted load. Invoking
the override writes a chosen crane's name into the register directly, without any swap, and at the
same instant pulls every crane out of the lane, so the chosen crane starts from a clear lane.

The full set of actions is: a crane that is neither attempting nor in the lane looks at the
register; a crane that saw "free" completes the swap, writing its own name, provided the register
still reads "free"; a crane abandons its attempt because the register no longer reads "free"; the
crane whose name is in the register moves into the lane; a crane in the lane performs one container
move; a crane pulls out of the lane and sets the register back to "free"; and the supervisor
invokes the override, writing a chosen crane's name into the register and clearing the lane of
every crane.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any crane standing in the transfer lane is the crane whose name the register
currently carries, so two cranes are never in the lane together.

    /\ attempting \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ movesLeft \in [Cranes -> 0..MoveBudget]

    /\ attempting = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ movesLeft = [c \in Cranes |-> MoveBudget]

    /\ ~attempting[c]
    /\ ~inLane[c]
    /\ register = Free

    /\ register' = c
    /\ attempting' = [attempting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]

A wildfire surveillance swarm flies drones over a fire, and the airspace over the fire is carved
into sectors. Each sector has a ceiling on how many drones may be inside it at once, set by the
separation the aircraft need from each other and from the water bombers.

A drone is never simply flown into a sector. The swarm controller opens an agreement round naming
one grounded drone and one sector, and each airspace controller then either clears the round or
objects to it. The round is committed only if every controller that is still responding has cleared
it and the named sector is currently below its ceiling; committing puts that drone into that
sector. The round is dropped if a responding controller objects, or if the named sector has
meanwhile filled up to its ceiling.

An airspace controller can go silent at any moment without saying so, and once silent it neither
clears nor objects to anything. A round is not held up by a silent controller: the decision is
taken over the controllers that are still responding. A silent controller can later come back on
the air, and it comes back with no answer recorded for the round in progress.

Finally, the swarm runs an all-aircraft recall: whenever any drone is still airborne, the recall can
be called, and every airborne drone lands and returns to the ground pool.

The full set of actions is: the swarm controller opens a round on a grounded drone and a sector; a
responding controller clears the round; a responding controller objects to the round; a controller
goes silent; a silent controller comes back on the air with its answer wiped; the round commits,
putting the drone into the sector, when every responding controller has cleared it and the sector
is below its ceiling; the round is dropped when a responding controller has objected or the sector

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router has a ring of induction stations arranged around a single oversize chute.
Only one station may be feeding the chute at any moment, because the chute takes one item at a time
and two feeds would jam it.

The right to feed is carried by a single permit that circulates around the ring in a fixed order.
The permit is either sitting at one station or travelling down the link towards the next station,
never both and never nowhere. Items build up in a bounded backlog at each station. A station
holding the permit may start feeding if it has anything waiting, and while it feeds the chute
records it as the station currently on the chute. Each turn of feeding sends one waiting item down
the chute. The station stops when it chooses to, and stopping clears the chute's record at the same
moment. A station only lets the permit go on down the ring once it has stopped feeding.

Stations differ in how quickly they work, and a slow station simply has more waiting in its backlog
and takes more turns to get through it; it is never broken and it never drops the permit. Its
backlog is bounded, so it always stops eventually and always passes the permit on.

The full set of actions is: an item arrives into a station's backlog, up to the backlog bound; the
station holding the permit starts feeding, provided it has an item waiting, which records it on the
chute; a feeding station sends one waiting item down the chute; a feeding station stops, which
clears the chute's record; a station that is not feeding lets the permit go, putting it on the link
to the next station in the ring; and a permit travelling on a link arrives at the station it was
sent to.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The chute's record of which station is on it and the stations' own feeding states
always agree with each other, so exactly the station the chute names is feeding and no second
station is ever feeding alongside it.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS StationCount, BacklogBound, NoStation

Stations == 1..StationCount

\* The ring order: the permit always moves to the next station round.
NextRound(n) == IF n = StationCount THEN 1 ELSE n + 1

VARIABLES permitAt, onLink, feeding, onChute, waiting

vars == <<permitAt, onLink, feeding, onChute, waiting>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ permitAt \in Stations \cup {NoStation}
    /\ onLink \in Stations \cup {NoStation}
    /\ feeding \in [Stations -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ onChute \in Stations \cup {NoStation}
    /\ waiting \in [Stations -> 0..BacklogBound]

Init ==
    /\ permitAt = 1
    /\ onLink = NoStation
    /\ feeding = [n \in Stations |-> FALSE]
    /\ onChute = NoStation
    /\ waiting = [n \in Stations |-> 0]

Arrive(n) ==
    /\ waiting[n] < BacklogBound
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![n] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permitAt, onLink, feeding, onChute>>

\* Holding the permit is the only thing that lets a station onto the chute.
StartFeed(n) ==
    /\ permitAt = n
    /\ ~feeding[n]
    /\ waiting[n] > 0
    /\ feeding' = [feeding EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
    /\ onChute' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permitAt, onLink, waiting>>

\* A slow station simply has more to work through; its backlog is bounded.
Feed(n) ==
    /\ feeding[n]
    /\ waiting[n] > 0
    /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![n] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permitAt, onLink, feeding, onChute>>

StopFeed(n) ==

    /\ feeding' = [feeding EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
    /\ onChute' = NoStation
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permitAt, onLink, waiting>>

Release(n) ==

    /\ ~feeding[n]
    /\ permitAt' = NoStation
    /\ onLink' = NextRound(n)

Deliver ==
    /\ onLink # NoStation
    /\ permitAt' = onLink
    /\ onLink' = NoStation
    /\ UNCHANGED <<feeding, onChute, waiting>>

Next ==

A warehouse robot fleet handles pallets, and damaged pallets are destroyed in the site baler.

supervisors who are on the roster right now outnumber the rest of the roster, that is, when they
are a strict majority of it. Running the baler takes the pallet out of the warehouse, writes it
into the ledger, and closes the review. A review can also be called off, which discards the
endorsements and closes the review without baling anything. An endorsement can be withdrawn while
the review is open.

The duty roster is not fixed. Supervisors come on duty and go off duty during the shift, so the
size of the roster, and with it the number of endorsements a majority takes, changes as the shift
runs. At least one supervisor is always on duty. Endorsements from supervisors who have since gone
off duty do not count towards the majority.

review; a supervisor on the current roster endorses the open review; a supervisor withdraws an

ledger, and closing the review; the review is called off, discarding endorsements and closing it;
a supervisor comes on duty; and a supervisor goes off duty, provided at least one remains.

closes, either by the baler running or by being called off.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop spooler hands out output trays to print jobs. The trays are physical, so a tray can be
holding the output of at most one job at a time, and the shop's finishing bench works from what
each job believes it holds.

Handing over a tray takes two steps. First the spooler prepares the hand-over: it picks a job that
is not already mid-hand-over and a tray the printer currently records as free, and the printer
marks that tray down to the job. Then the spooler sends the job its confirmation, which travels on
the shop's internal message ring. The ring holds several confirmations at once and delivers them in
whatever order it likes, not the order they were sent, so a confirmation can sit on the ring while
the world moves on. When a confirmation is finally delivered, it is applied only if the printer
still records the named tray as belonging to the named job; a confirmation that has been overtaken
by events is dropped on delivery instead of being applied.

A job that has been confirmed a tray can give it back, which returns the tray to free on the
printer's record and removes it from what the job holds. A prepared hand-over can also be abandoned. Abandoning always
tears up the job's own paperwork, but it releases the tray only if that tray is still marked to
this job and this job has not meanwhile been confirmed it; otherwise the tray is left exactly as it
stands, because it now belongs to somebody else's hand-over. Separately, the printer can pull a
tray that is marked to a job but that the job has not yet been confirmed -- a tray pulled out for a
paper jam, say -- and pulling it clears the mark back to free even though a confirmation naming
that tray may still be riding the ring. That freed tray can then be marked to a different job.

The full set of actions is: the spooler prepares a hand-over of a free tray to a job that has none
in progress, marking the tray to that job on the printer's record; the spooler sends the
confirmation for a prepared hand-over onto a free place on the message ring; a confirmation is
delivered off the ring and applied only if the printer still records that tray to that job,
otherwise dropped; a job gives back a tray it holds, freeing it on the printer's record; and a
prepared hand-over is abandoned, which releases its tray only if that tray is still marked to
that job and not already confirmed to it; and the printer pulls a marked but
not-yet-confirmed tray, clearing its mark back to free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every tray that a job believes it holds is a tray the printer's record still marks
down to that job, so no tray is ever held by two jobs at once.

    /\ ring \in [RingSlots -> Confirmation \cup {Empty}]
    /\ prepared \in [Jobs -> Trays \cup {NoTray}]

    /\ holds = [j \in Jobs |-> {}]
    /\ ring = [k \in RingSlots |-> Empty]
    /\ prepared = [j \in Jobs |-> NoTray]

\* First step: the printer marks a free tray down to the job.
Prepare(j, t) ==
    /\ prepared[j] = NoTray
    /\ record[t] = FreeTray
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![t] = j]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![j] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, ring>>

Send(j, k) ==
    /\ prepared[j] # NoTray
    /\ ring[k] = Empty
    /\ ring' = [ring EXCEPT ![k] = [job |-> j, tray |-> prepared[j]]]

    /\ t \notin holds[j]
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![t] = FreeTray]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, ring, prepared>>

GiveBack(j, t) ==
    /\ t \in holds[j]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![j] = @ \ {t}]
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![t] = FreeTray]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ring, prepared>>

\* Abandoning drops the job's own paperwork; it frees the tray only if the
\* tray is still marked to this job and this job has not been confirmed it.
Abandon(j) ==

    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![j] = NoTray]

robot that needs power puts in a request and waits; it only rolls onto a bay when the fleet
coordinator admits it, and the coordinator admits a waiting robot only while there is a bay free.

One robot at a time acts as fleet coordinator. When there is no coordinator, any robot can take the
role. A sitting coordinator can name one of the others as its standby, and the role can then hand

can also simply step down, which leaves the fleet with no coordinator and no standby named until
someone takes the role again. While there is no coordinator nobody is admitted to a bay, though
robots already charging carry on.

full, and a slow robot simply needs more steps to get there; it is never broken and it never
occupies a bay indefinitely. Once a robot is full it rolls off the bay and goes back to work.

The full set of actions is: a robot takes the coordinator role when there is none; the sitting
coordinator names a standby; the role hands over to the named standby; the coordinator steps down,
clearing the standby too; a robot puts in a charging request and waits; the coordinator admits a
waiting robot onto a bay, provided a bay is free; a robot on a bay takes on one more step of
charge; and a robot that is full rolls off its bay.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of robots on charging bays never exceeds the number of bays the bank
has.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The bank never stays completely full for ever; whenever every bay is occupied, a
bay eventually frees up again.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container-ship crane yard works from a shared stowage plan. The plan is amended in numbered
revisions, and each revision is drafted against the plan as it stands once every earlier revision
has gone in. A revision that were to go into the plan while an earlier-numbered one had not would
silently lose that earlier revision's changes, because everything drafted after it assumed they
were already there.

Amendments are not made by one person. A revision number is taken up for drafting, and the berth
officers then endorse it one at a time. The draft goes into the plan only when the endorsements
standing behind it are a strict majority of the berth officers and every lower-numbered revision is
already in the plan. Going in clears the draft and its endorsements, ready for the next one. A
draft can also be withdrawn at any time, which clears it and its endorsements without changing the
plan. Revision numbers may be taken up in any order, so a draft can perfectly well be sitting there
with an earlier revision still missing; it simply cannot go in yet.

The harbourmaster holds a privileged override, which can be armed and disarmed. While it is armed
the harbourmaster can push the current draft into the plan without any endorsements at all, but
even the override will not put a revision in ahead of a lower-numbered one that is still missing.

The full set of actions is: a revision number that is not yet in the plan is taken up for drafting;
a berth officer endorses the current draft; the draft goes into the plan when a strict majority of
berth officers stand behind it and every lower revision is already in; the draft is withdrawn,
clearing it and its endorsements; the harbourmaster arms the override; the harbourmaster disarms
the override; and the harbourmaster pushes the current draft into the plan under the armed override,
still only if every lower revision is already in.

first one, so no revision is ever skipped over and no revision's changes are lost.

Majority == Cardinality(endorsed) * 2 > Cardinality(Officers)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An air-traffic tower allocates its single active runway through one slot register. The register
either reads clear or carries the standing clearance: which aircraft has the runway, which
controller issued the clearance, and which runway configuration generation was in force when it was
issued.

Not every controller at the tower is licensed to issue runway clearances; trainees sit at positions
and can do everything except have a clearance take effect. A controller who wants the runway first
reads the register and remembers whether it read clear or busy. If it read clear, the controller
sends a clearance request to the runway system, stamped with the configuration generation as it
stands at that moment. Requests travel over the tower's internal loop, which holds several requests
at once and hands them to the runway system in whatever order it likes rather than the order they
were sent, so a request can be overtaken.

When the runway system takes a request off the loop, the request takes effect only if the register
still reads clear, the controller who sent it is licensed, and the stamp on it still matches the
tower's current configuration generation. Anything else is discarded on arrival. A controller whose
read came back busy simply throws the read away.

The runway configuration can be changed, which advances the generation, sends any aircraft holding
the runway around so the register reads clear again, and invalidates every read the controllers
were holding. Separately, an aircraft that has the runway can simply vacate it, clearing the
register.

The full set of actions is: a controller reads the slot register and remembers clear or busy; a
controller whose read came back clear sends a stamped clearance request onto a free place on the
loop; a controller whose read came back busy throws that read away; the runway system takes a
request off the loop and lets it take effect only if the register still reads clear, the sender is
licensed and the stamp matches the current generation, discarding it otherwise; an aircraft vacates
the runway, clearing the register; and the tower changes runway configuration, advancing the
generation, clearing the register and invalidating every outstanding read.

by a licensed controller and carries the runway configuration generation that is currently in
force, so no unlicensed controller and no out-of-date clearance ever holds the runway.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The runway never stays held for ever; whenever the register carries a clearance,
it eventually reads clear again.
