===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital schedules operating-room time in theatre slots. The theatre board shows, for each slot,
which surgical case is in it or that it is vacant, and each case separately holds a confirmation
letter naming the slot it has been given and the roster generation the letter was written under.

Booking a case in takes two steps. The scheduler first pencils the case into a vacant slot, which
writes the case onto the theatre board and leaves the case with a pencilled slot but no
confirmation yet. The confirmation letter is written afterwards, and only if the board still shows
that slot as belonging to that case; the letter records the roster generation as it stands at that
moment. If the board no longer shows the case in its pencilled slot, the pencilling is simply
dropped instead.

The roster is reconfigured from time to time, for instance when theatres are taken out for deep
clean. A reconfiguration advances the roster generation and wipes the theatre board clean, so every
confirmation letter written under an earlier generation is out of date and no longer governs
anything. Pencillings survive a reconfiguration on paper but no longer match the board.

A case that holds a confirmation matching the board can release its slot, which vacates it on the
board and tears up the letter. The medical director holds a privileged override for emergencies and
can write a case straight onto any slot on the board, occupied or not; whichever case was in that
slot loses its confirmation letter at that moment, and the incoming case is left pencilled in,
still needing a letter of its own.

The full set of actions is: the scheduler pencils a case into a vacant slot, writing it onto the
board; the confirmation letter is written for a pencilled case, but only while the board still shows
that case in that slot, and it records the current roster generation; a pencilling whose slot no
longer shows that case on the board is dropped; a case holding a letter that matches the board
releases its slot, vacating it and tearing up the letter; the roster is reconfigured, advancing the
generation and wiping the board; and the medical director overrides, writing a case onto any slot,
tearing up the letter of whoever was there, and leaving the incoming case pencilled in.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every confirmation letter written under the roster generation currently in force
names a slot that the theatre board still shows as belonging to that case, so two cases are never
holding the same slot at once.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A skyscraper's elevator bank has one sky-lobby transfer bay that cars use to swap between the low
and high shafts. Only one car can be in the bay at a time. The bay is interlocked in two halves: a
berth at the lobby floor and the counterweight track behind it. A car is only physically in the bay
when it has been given both halves, and it is given them one at a time, the berth first and the
track second.

Handing the halves out is the job of the bank dispatcher. One car acts as dispatcher at a time; when
there is no dispatcher any running car can take the role, and the sitting dispatcher can drop the
role at any moment, which is how the bank fails over. Nothing is handed out while there is no
dispatcher. A car asks for the bay, is given the berth, is then given the track, and only then
moves into the bay. When it moves out again both halves are given back together.

A half-handed-out bay can be taken back: as long as no car is actually in the bay, the dispatcher
can revoke whatever has been handed out, returning both halves at once, which is what happens when
a car that was given the berth never comes to collect.

One car in the bank can stop dead without signalling it. A stopped car does nothing further -- it
does not take the role, does not ask for the bay, does not move in and does not move out. When a
stopped car is found holding either half of the bay, it is towed out: both halves are returned and
the car is put back to standing at its floor, though it stays stopped.

The full set of actions is: a running car takes the dispatcher role when there is none; the sitting
dispatcher drops the role; a running car asks for the bay; the dispatcher gives the berth to a car
that has asked; the dispatcher gives the track to the car that already holds the berth; a car
holding both halves moves into the bay; a car in the bay moves out, giving both halves back; the
dispatcher revokes what has been handed out while no car is in the bay; a car stops dead; and a
stopped car found holding the bay is towed out, returning both halves.

no car is ever in the bay on half an interlock and two cars are never in the bay together.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The bay never stays half handed out; whenever a car holds the berth without the
track, either it is eventually given the track as well or the berth is eventually taken back.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital's operating-room scheduler will not send a case to theatre unless the recovery unit can
take it afterwards, and the recovery unit has a fixed number of beds. A case that is sent occupies
a recovery bed until it is discharged, at which point it goes back on the waiting list and its
paperwork starts again from scratch.

Sending a case needs the theatre committee behind it. Each committee member sends its approval for
a named case as a note on the hospital's internal paging system. The paging system holds several
notes at once and delivers them in whatever order it happens to deliver them, not the order they
were sent, so a note can be delivered long after it was written. A note is only counted when it is
delivered, at which point that member's approval is recorded against that case. A member can also
take a recorded approval back off a case.

Committee members work a rota, so at any moment some of them are on call and the rest are not; at
least one is always on call. A case goes to theatre only when every member who is on call at that
moment has an approval recorded against it and the recovery unit has a free bed at that moment. Both conditions are checked at the moment the case is
sent, not when the notes were written, so approvals that were written while there were free beds do
not entitle a case to go if the unit has filled up since. Discharging a case frees its bed and
wipes the approvals recorded against it.

The full set of actions is: a committee member writes an approval note for a waiting case onto a
free place on the paging system, for a case it has not already approved; a note is delivered off the
paging system and its approval is recorded against the named case; a member takes a recorded
approval back off a case; a case with an approval recorded from every member currently on call goes to
theatre and takes a recovery bed, provided a bed is free at that moment; a case in recovery is
discharged, freeing its bed, wiping its approvals, and returning it to the waiting list; a member
comes on call; and a member goes off call, provided at least one member is left on call.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cases occupying recovery beds never exceeds the number of beds the
recovery unit has.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od0m5p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cases, Committee, Pagers, Beds, Empty

Note == [member : Committee, case : Cases]

VARIABLES place, approvals, pager, onCall

vars == <<place, approvals, pager, onCall>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ place \in [Cases -> {"waiting", "recovery"}]
    /\ approvals \in [Cases -> SUBSET Committee]
    /\ pager \in [Pagers -> Note \cup {Empty}]
    /\ onCall \subseteq Committee

Occupied == Cardinality({c \in Cases : place[c] = "recovery"})

Init ==
    /\ place = [c \in Cases |-> "waiting"]
    /\ approvals = [c \in Cases |-> {}]
    /\ pager = [p \in Pagers |-> Empty]
    /\ onCall = Committee

Write(m, c, p) ==
    /\ pager[p] = Empty
    /\ place[c] = "waiting"
    /\ m \notin approvals[c]
    /\ pager' = [pager EXCEPT ![p] = [member |-> m, case |-> c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, approvals, onCall>>

\* Notes come off the pager in any order; the approval counts only on delivery.
Deliver(p) ==
    /\ pager[p] # Empty
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![pager[p].case] = @ \cup {pager[p].member}]
    /\ pager' = [pager EXCEPT ![p] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, onCall>>

TakeBack(m, c) ==
    /\ m \in approvals[c]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {m}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, pager, onCall>>

\* Only the members currently on call have to be behind the case, and the
\* bed count is re-checked here, not when the notes were written.
SendToTheatre(c) ==
    /\ place[c] = "waiting"
    /\ onCall # {}
    /\ onCall \subseteq approvals[c]
    /\ Occupied < Beds
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![c] = "recovery"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvals, pager, onCall>>

Discharge(c) ==
    /\ place[c] = "recovery"
    /\ place' = [place EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
    /\ approvals' = [approvals EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pager, onCall>>

GoOnCall(m) ==
    /\ m \notin onCall
    /\ onCall' = onCall \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, approvals, pager>>

\* The rota always keeps at least one member on call.
GoOffCall(m) ==
    /\ m \in onCall
    /\ Cardinality(onCall) > 1
    /\ onCall' = onCall \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<place, approvals, pager>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Pagers : Deliver(p)
    \/ \E m \in Committee : GoOnCall(m) \/ GoOffCall(m)
    \/ \E c \in Cases :
         \/ SendToTheatre(c) \/ Discharge(c)
         \/ \E m \in Committee : TakeBack(m, c) \/ \E p \in Pagers : Write(m, c, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Recovery never holds more cases than it has beds.
RecoveryWithinBeds == Occupied <= Beds

====
```

Name the module `W4Od3m8p5t0`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A bank runs its interbank settlement in a nightly batch. Each payment in the batch has a settlement
number, and releasing a payment to the central bank is final: once released it cannot be recalled,
amended or released again. The night's release ledger records, in order, every payment that has
gone out.

The batch is worked by the member banks, and getting at a payment takes two holds, the coarse one
before the fine one. A member bank first takes the batch-wide hold, which only one bank has at a
time. Holding the batch, it may then take the line hold on an individual payment, which it can only
do for a payment nobody else has taken. It releases a payment only while it has that payment's line
hold, and releasing gives the line hold back.

Releases go out in strictly ascending settlement number: a payment can be released only if its
number is higher than the number of the last payment already in the ledger. This is what makes the
batch replay-safe -- working strictly upwards, the batch can never come back round to a payment it
has already sent.

A member bank can drop an individual line hold, and it can drop the batch-wide hold, which gives
back every line hold it was holding at the same time. A member bank can also fail silently: it stops
taking any part, but whatever holds it had stay in its name. The settlement operator can reclaim
the holds of a failed bank, taking back its batch-wide hold and all its line holds, and can restart
a failed bank once it is holding nothing.

The full set of actions is: a running member bank takes the batch-wide hold when it is free; the
bank holding the batch takes a free line hold on a payment; a running bank releases a payment it
has the line hold on, provided the payment's number is above the last in the ledger, which appends
it to the ledger and gives the line hold back; a bank drops one of its line holds; a bank drops the
batch-wide hold, giving back all its line holds too; a bank fails silently; the operator reclaims
all holds standing in a failed bank's name; and the operator restarts a failed bank that is holding
nothing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The settlement numbers in the release ledger are strictly ascending from first to
last, so no payment is ever released a second time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The batch-wide hold never stays in a failed bank's name for ever; whenever a
failed bank is holding it, it is eventually reclaimed.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od3m8p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Members, PaymentCount, Nobody

Payments == 1..PaymentCount

ASSUME Nobody \notin Members

VARIABLES batchHold, lineHold, ledger, failed

vars == <<batchHold, lineHold, ledger, failed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ batchHold \in Members \cup {Nobody}
    /\ lineHold \in [Payments -> Members \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ ledger \in Seq(Payments)
    /\ failed \subseteq Members

Running(b) == b \notin failed

LastOut == IF ledger = << >> THEN 0 ELSE ledger[Len(ledger)]

Holding(b) == batchHold = b \/ \E p \in Payments : lineHold[p] = b

Init ==
    /\ batchHold = Nobody
    /\ lineHold = [p \in Payments |-> Nobody]
    /\ ledger = << >>
    /\ failed = {}

TakeBatch(b) ==
    /\ Running(b)
    /\ batchHold = Nobody
    /\ batchHold' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lineHold, ledger, failed>>

\* Coarse before fine: no line hold without the batch-wide hold.
TakeLine(b, p) ==
    /\ Running(b)
    /\ batchHold = b
    /\ lineHold[p] = Nobody
    /\ lineHold' = [lineHold EXCEPT ![p] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchHold, ledger, failed>>

\* Releasing is final, and the batch only ever works upwards.
Release(b, p) ==
    /\ Running(b)
    /\ lineHold[p] = b
    /\ p > LastOut
    /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, p)
    /\ lineHold' = [lineHold EXCEPT ![p] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchHold, failed>>

DropLine(b, p) ==
    /\ lineHold[p] = b
    /\ lineHold' = [lineHold EXCEPT ![p] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchHold, ledger, failed>>

DropBatch(b) ==
    /\ batchHold = b
    /\ batchHold' = Nobody
    /\ lineHold' = [p \in Payments |-> IF lineHold[p] = b THEN Nobody ELSE lineHold[p]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, failed>>

Fail(b) ==
    /\ Running(b)
    /\ failed' = failed \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchHold, lineHold, ledger>>

\* The operator prises everything out of a failed bank's name at once.
Reclaim(b) ==
    /\ b \in failed
    /\ Holding(b)
    /\ batchHold' = IF batchHold = b THEN Nobody ELSE batchHold
    /\ lineHold' = [p \in Payments |-> IF lineHold[p] = b THEN Nobody ELSE lineHold[p]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, failed>>

Restart(b) ==
    /\ b \in failed
    /\ ~Holding(b)
    /\ failed' = failed \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batchHold, lineHold, ledger>>

ReclaimSome == \E b \in Members : Reclaim(b)

Next ==
    \/ ReclaimSome
    \/ \E b \in Members :
         \/ TakeBatch(b) \/ DropBatch(b) \/ Fail(b) \/ Restart(b)
         \/ \E p \in Payments : TakeLine(b, p) \/ Release(b, p) \/ DropLine(b, p)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ReclaimSome)

\* The ledger only ever climbs, so nothing can go out a second time.
LedgerStrictlyAscends ==
    \A i \in 1..(Len(ledger) - 1) : ledger[i] < ledger[i + 1]

StuckOnFailed == batchHold # Nobody /\ batchHold \in failed

\* A failed bank never keeps the batch to itself.
FailedHolderReclaimed == StuckOnFailed ~> ~StuckOnFailed

====
```
```cfg
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Members = {mbk1, mbk2}
    PaymentCount = 3
    Nobody = nobody

INVARIANT LedgerStrictlyAscends

PROPERTY FailedHolderReclaimed
```
PROPERTY_INVARIANT: LedgerStrictlyAscends<|return|>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop spooler moves sheets of paper around a closed loop. The shop starts the day with a
fixed count of sheets and neither buys nor throws any away during the run, so every sheet is at
every moment in exactly one of four places: in the paper store, sitting in the printer's loading
tray, already printed on the output stack, or held in escrow by a transfer that has started but not
finished.

Moving sheets from the store into the tray is done as an agreed transfer between the spooler and
the printer, and it happens in two steps. In the first step the spooler takes a batch of sheets out
of the store and holds them in escrow; they have left the store but have not reached the tray. The
printer then signals that it agrees to take the batch. In the second step the transfer completes:
the escrowed batch goes into the tray and the escrow is emptied. A transfer that has been started
can instead be backed out, which puts the escrowed batch back into the store and empties the
escrow. Only one transfer is in progress at a time.

The tray has a working depth, and the shop changes that depth during the run as jobs of different
weights come through. The depth can be raised, and it can be lowered, but it is only ever lowered
while it is strictly above the number of sheets currently in the tray. A transfer completes only if
the tray can take the whole escrowed batch within the depth as it stands at that moment.

Printing takes one sheet out of the tray and puts it on the output stack. Sheets on the output
stack are eventually collected back into the paper store.

The full set of actions is: the spooler takes a batch out of the store into escrow, when no
transfer is in progress; the printer signals that it agrees to the batch in escrow; the transfer
completes, moving the escrowed batch into the tray, provided the printer has agreed and the tray
depth can take it; the transfer is backed out, returning the escrowed batch to the store; the
printer prints one sheet from the tray onto the output stack; the tray depth is raised; the tray
depth is lowered, only while it is above the current tray contents; and one printed sheet is
collected off the output stack back into the paper store.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The sheets in the store, in the tray, on the output stack and held in escrow
always add up to exactly the fixed count the shop started with.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od11m2p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Sheets, MaxDepth, MaxBatch

VARIABLES store, tray, output, escrow, depth, agreed

vars == <<store, tray, output, escrow, depth, agreed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ store \in 0..Sheets
    /\ tray \in 0..Sheets
    /\ output \in 0..Sheets
    /\ escrow \in 0..Sheets
    /\ depth \in 0..MaxDepth
    /\ agreed \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ store = Sheets
    /\ tray = 0
    /\ output = 0
    /\ escrow = 0
    /\ depth = 1
    /\ agreed = FALSE

\* First step: the batch leaves the store but has not arrived anywhere yet.
TakeIntoEscrow(k) ==
    /\ escrow = 0
    /\ k >= 1
    /\ store >= k
    /\ store' = store - k
    /\ escrow' = k
    /\ agreed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, output, depth>>

PrinterAgrees ==
    /\ escrow > 0
    /\ ~agreed
    /\ agreed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, output, escrow, depth>>

\* Second step: the batch lands in the tray, if the depth as it stands allows.
Complete ==
    /\ escrow > 0
    /\ agreed
    /\ tray + escrow <= depth
    /\ tray' = tray + escrow
    /\ escrow' = 0
    /\ agreed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, output, depth>>

BackOut ==
    /\ escrow > 0
    /\ store' = store + escrow
    /\ escrow' = 0
    /\ agreed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, output, depth>>

Print ==
    /\ tray > 0
    /\ tray' = tray - 1
    /\ output' = output + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, escrow, depth, agreed>>

Raise ==
    /\ depth < MaxDepth
    /\ depth' = depth + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, output, escrow, agreed>>

\* The depth is only ever taken down above what the tray is already holding.
Lower ==
    /\ depth > tray
    /\ depth > 0
    /\ depth' = depth - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<store, tray, output, escrow, agreed>>

Collect ==
    /\ output > 0
    /\ output' = output - 1
    /\ store' = store + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tray, escrow, depth, agreed>>

Next ==
    \/ PrinterAgrees \/ Complete \/ BackOut \/ Print \/ Raise \/ Lower \/ Collect
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxBatch : TakeIntoEscrow(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every sheet is in exactly one of the four places, always.
SheetsConserved == store + tray + output + escrow = Sheets

====
```
```cfg
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Sheets = 3
    MaxDepth = 3
    MaxBatch = 2

INVARIANT SheetsConserved
```

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
Two airport terminals each run their own baggage router, and the two routers are otherwise
independent, but they load onto one shared transfer belt. The belt is rated by weight, not by piece
count: bags are either standard or oversize, an oversize bag counts double, and the total weight
riding the belt must stay within the belt's rating.

Neither router reserves anything on the belt in advance. A router first takes a bag off its pile
and stages it, then reads the belt to see what weight is currently on it and remembers that figure.
When it goes to load, the load only goes through if the belt still carries exactly the weight the
router remembered, and if that remembered weight plus its staged bag stays within the rating. If
another terminal has loaded or unloaded in the meantime the remembered figure no longer matches,
the router throws the reading away and reads again, up to a bounded number of retries. At any point
a router can simply put its staged bag back on the pile and start over with something else.

Bags come off the belt at the far end and are gone from the belt's weight.

The full set of actions is: a router stages a bag that is neither on the belt nor staged by the
other router; a router with a staged bag reads the current belt weight and remembers it; a router
loads its staged bag onto the belt, provided the belt still carries exactly the weight it
remembered and that weight plus the bag stays within the rating; a router whose remembered figure
no longer matches the belt throws the reading away, counting a retry; a router puts its staged bag
back on the pile, clearing its reading and its retry count; and a bag is taken off the far end of
the belt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total weight of the bags riding the shared transfer belt, counting oversize
bags double, never exceeds the belt's rating.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The two routers never both sit holding staged bags for ever; whenever both are
holding one, at least one of them eventually lets go.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od17m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Routers, Bags, Oversize, Rating, MaxRetry, NoBag, NoRead

ASSUME Oversize \subseteq Bags

Weight(b) == IF b \in Oversize THEN 2 ELSE 1

RECURSIVE Carried(_)
Carried(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN Weight(b) + Carried(S \ {b})

VARIABLES onBelt, staged, remembered, retries

vars == <<onBelt, staged, remembered, retries>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onBelt \subseteq Bags
    /\ staged \in [Routers -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]
    /\ remembered \in [Routers -> (0..Rating) \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ retries \in [Routers -> 0..MaxRetry]

Load == Carried(onBelt)

Init ==
    /\ onBelt = {}
    /\ staged = [r \in Routers |-> NoBag]
    /\ remembered = [r \in Routers |-> NoRead]
    /\ retries = [r \in Routers |-> 0]

Stage(r, b) ==
    /\ staged[r] = NoBag
    /\ b \notin onBelt
    /\ \A q \in Routers : staged[q] # b
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![r] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBelt, remembered, retries>>

\* The read reserves nothing; it only records what the belt looked like.
ReadBelt(r) ==
    /\ staged[r] # NoBag
    /\ remembered[r] = NoRead
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![r] = Load]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBelt, staged, retries>>

\* The load lands only if the belt is untouched since the read and the
\* rating still has room for the bag.
LoadOn(r) ==
    /\ staged[r] # NoBag
    /\ remembered[r] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[r] = Load
    /\ remembered[r] + Weight(staged[r]) <= Rating
    /\ onBelt' = onBelt \cup {staged[r]}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![r] = NoBag]
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![r] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

Reread(r) ==
    /\ remembered[r] # NoRead
    /\ remembered[r] # Load
    /\ retries[r] < MaxRetry
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![r] = NoRead]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBelt, staged>>

PutBack(r) ==
    /\ staged[r] # NoBag
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![r] = NoBag]
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![r] = NoRead]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED onBelt

TakeOff(b) ==
    /\ b \in onBelt
    /\ onBelt' = onBelt \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<staged, remembered, retries>>

PutBackSome == \E r \in Routers : PutBack(r)

Next ==
    \/ PutBackSome
    \/ \E b \in Bags : TakeOff(b)
    \/ \E r \in Routers :
         \/ ReadBelt(r) \/ LoadOn(r) \/ Reread(r)
         \/ \E b \in Bags : Stage(r, b)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(PutBackSome)

\* The shared belt never carries more than it is rated for.
BeltWithinRating == Load <= Rating

\* The two routers never both sit holding a staged bag for ever.
NotBothStuck ==
    (\A r \in Routers : staged[r] # NoBag) ~> (\E r \in Routers : staged[r] = NoBag)

====
```

CONSTANTS
    Routers = {rtn, rts}
    Bags = {bg1, bg2, bg3}
    Oversize = {bg3}
    Rating = 3
    MaxRetry = 1
    NoBag = nobag
    NoRead = noread

INVARIANT BeltWithinRating

PROPERTY NotBothStuck

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop has one laminator, and only one spooler node may be running it at a time. Which node
gets it is decided by whichever node is currently acting as shop scheduler. There is at most one
scheduler; when there is none, any node can take the role, and the sitting scheduler can drop the
role at any moment, which is how the shop carries on when a node goes down.

Grants of the laminator are stamped with a scheduling term. When a node takes over as scheduler and
the laminator is not actually running, the term is advanced, which makes any grant that was
outstanding but unstarted stale; a stale grant is simply taken back and the node has to ask again.
When a node takes over while the laminator is running, the term is not advanced: the incoming
scheduler adopts the job in progress rather than interrupting it.

A node asks for the laminator and joins the queue of nodes waiting. The scheduler grants the
laminator to a waiting node when nobody holds it, stamping the grant with the current term. The
holder may start the laminator only while its grant still carries the current term and the
laminator is not already running. When it finishes, the laminator stops and the grant is given up.

The shop manager holds a privileged override and can put the laminator straight onto a chosen node:
that node becomes the holder with a grant stamped at the current term and becomes the node running
the laminator, displacing whoever was running it.

The full set of actions is: a node takes the scheduler role when there is none, advancing the term
only if the laminator is not running; the sitting scheduler drops the role; a node asks for the
laminator and joins the queue; the scheduler grants the laminator to a waiting node when nobody
holds it, stamping the current term; a stale grant that has not been started is taken back; the
holder starts the laminator, provided its grant carries the current term and nothing is running;
the running node finishes, stopping the laminator and giving up the grant; and the manager
overrides, putting a chosen node onto the laminator with a current-term grant.

A wildfire surveillance swarm shares one water-drop corridor over the fire. Only one drone may be
in the corridor at a time, and a drone gets in only on the strength of the ground observers backing
it: each observer backs at most one drone at any moment, and a drone may enter the corridor only
while a strict majority of the observers are backing it.

swarm's radio holds several calls at once and applies them in whatever order it gets round to,
which need not be the order they were made. A call names one observer and one drone and, when it is
finally applied, moves that observer's backing to that drone. There is one thing a call cannot do:
it cannot move an observer's backing off a drone that is at that moment in the corridor. An
observer that is currently backing the drone in the corridor is committed to it, so a call trying
to move that backing elsewhere is discarded when it comes to be applied. For the same reason an
observer can drop its backing outright only when the drone it is backing is not in the corridor.

Drones ask for the corridor before they can enter it, and a drone leaves the corridor when its run
is finished.

The full set of actions is: an observer makes a radio call backing a named drone, placing it on a
free radio slot; a call is applied off the radio, moving that observer's backing to the named drone
unless that observer is currently backing the drone in the corridor, in which case the call is
discarded; a drone asks for the corridor; a drone that has asked enters the corridor when the
corridor is empty and a strict majority of observers are backing it; an observer drops its backing,
provided the drone it was backing is not in the corridor; and the drone in the corridor leaves it.

observers are backing that drone, which is what stops any second drone from ever being in the
corridor alongside it.

bank that isolated it.

isolated motor to service, and puts both banks back in good standing, because nothing isolated
under the old round may be left standing under the new one. A bank's permit can also be suspended
on its own, which puts back into service everything that bank had isolated; at least one bank is
always left in good standing.

can be left standing with nobody holding the machine room. The building engineer sweeps up: when
the machine room is unclaimed but motor claims are still standing, they are all cleared away.

the bank holding the machine room takes a claim on a free motor; a bank in good standing isolates a

A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into the lobby's numbered seats. The lobby keeps
a seating book saying which player is in each seat, and every player separately knows which seat it

player with no seat and a seat the book shows empty. Region servers then vote on the proposal, and

them over in whatever order it happens to, not the order they were cast. A vote counts only when it
is handed over, and only if the proposal it was cast for is still the proposal on the table; a vote
that arrives after the proposal has gone is discarded rather than being counted towards whatever is
on the table now.

named seat is still empty and the named player still unseated at that moment, the player is seated:
the book is written and the player is told its seat. Putting a player in clears the proposal and
the recorded votes. A proposal can also be withdrawn, which clears it and the recorded votes
without seating anybody. A seated player can leave, which empties its seat in the book.

empty seat; a region server casts its vote for the proposal onto a free place on the message

recorded and the seat and player are both still free, clearing the proposal and the votes; the
proposal is withdrawn, clearing it and the votes; and a seated player leaves, emptying its seat.

that seat, so no seat is ever given out to two players at once.

other but draw their stock from one shared depot, and they fill the same set of machines. Each
machine has a hopper with a fixed depth, and a hopper must never be filled past that depth or the
mechanism jams.

Restocking is authorised by the network's route controller. One route acts as controller at a time;
when there is none, either route can take the role, and the sitting controller can drop it at any
moment, which is how the network carries on when a route's handset goes down. Nothing is restocked
while there is no controller.

A route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not already filling, and then loads
product into it one unit at a time. Each unit loaded comes out of the shared depot and goes into
that machine's hopper, and a unit is only loaded if the hopper is below its depth at that moment.
The route closes the fill when it is done. Product sold out of a machine goes back to the depot as
the empties are collected, so the network's product neither appears from nowhere nor disappears.

The full set of actions is: a route takes the controller role when there is none; the sitting
controller drops the role; a route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not filling,
provided there is a controller; a route loads one unit from the depot into the machine it is
filling, provided that hopper is below its depth; a route closes its fill; and a machine vends one
unit, which returns that unit to the depot.

A multiplayer game runs two lobby shards that are otherwise independent but share one pool of match
tickets. Tickets are the thing that lets a match run, and the operator neither mints nor destroys
them during a season, so at every moment every ticket is in exactly one place: banked at the ticket
pool or at one of the two shards, committed to a match in play at one of them, or riding on the
wire with the transfer permit.

Only one site may move tickets at a time, and the right to move them is a single permit that goes
round the three sites in a fixed ring order. The permit is either sitting at a site or travelling
down the link to the next site round, never at two sites and never nowhere. The site holding the
permit may pick up a batch of its banked tickets onto the permit, and may set down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying. Picking up takes the tickets out of that site's bank the
moment it happens; they only land somewhere again when they are set down.

Also under the permit, a site may commit some of its banked tickets to matches in play, and may
return tickets from finished matches back to its bank.

The full set of actions is: the site holding the permit picks up a batch of its banked tickets onto
the permit, when the permit is carrying nothing; the site holding the permit sets down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying; the site holding the permit commits a batch of its banked
tickets to matches in play; the site holding the permit returns a batch of tickets from play to its
bank; the site holding the permit lets it go onto the link to the next site round the ring; and a
permit travelling on a link arrives at the site it was sent to.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tickets banked across the three sites, plus those committed to matches in play,
plus whatever the permit is carrying, always add up to exactly the season's fixed ticket count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No site keeps the permit for ever; whenever a site is holding it, the permit
eventually moves off that site.

    /\ carrying \in 0..Tickets
    /\ permitAt \in Sites \cup {NoSite}
    /\ onLink \in Sites \cup {NoSite}

Total(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[s] + Total(S \ {s}, f)

    /\ inPlay = [s \in Sites |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ permitAt = 1

    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ banked[s] >= k
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ carrying' = k

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router has one oversize chute whose diversion setting says where oversize items
are being sent. The setting is only ever written by whichever scanner node currently owns the
chute, and ownership is leased rather than permanent.

A lease is granted to a node when the chute is unowned, and each grant carries a fresh lease number,
one higher than the last. A lease runs for a fixed count of table ticks and counts down; the owner
can renew it while it is still running, which puts the count back to full without changing the lease
number. When the count reaches nothing the lease is over: the chute becomes unowned and its
diversion setting is wiped, because a setting with nobody behind it is not a setting anybody should
be routing to. The owner can also hand the lease back early, which does the same thing, and can
wipe the setting itself while still holding the lease.

Diversion instructions are not applied where they are written. The owner puts an instruction onto
the router's field bus, stamped with its own name and its lease number. The bus carries several
instructions at once and hands them to the chute in whatever order it gets to them, not the order
they were written, so an instruction can arrive long after the lease it was written under has run
out or been handed on. The chute applies an instruction only if the name on it is the node that
owns the chute right now, the lease number on it is the lease number running right now, and that
lease has not run out. Anything else is thrown away on arrival.

Lease numbers do not run for ever. When the numbering has reached its last value and the chute is
unowned, its setting wiped and the bus completely clear, the numbering starts again from the
beginning.

The full set of actions is: a node is granted the lease on the unowned chute, taking a fresh lease
number and a full count; the table ticks, counting the lease down and, if that exhausts it, leaving
the chute unowned with its setting wiped; the owner renews its lease back to a full count; the
owner puts a stamped instruction onto a free place on the field bus; the chute takes an instruction
off the bus and applies it only if the name, the lease number and the running lease all match,
throwing it away otherwise; the owner wipes the diversion setting; the owner hands the lease back
early, wiping the setting; and the lease numbering restarts once it has run out with nothing owned,
nothing set and the bus clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the chute carries a diversion setting, it was written by the node that
owns the chute right now, under the lease number running right now, and that lease has not run out,
so no lapsed owner and no out-of-date instruction ever governs where oversize items go.

    /\ ticks \in 0..LeaseTicks
    /\ number \in 0..LastNumber
    /\ setting \in Stamped \cup {Idle}

BusClear == \A c \in Channels : busbar[c] = Empty

Grant(n) ==

    /\ ticks' = LeaseTicks

    /\ ticks' = ticks - 1
    /\ owner' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Nobody ELSE owner
    /\ setting' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Idle ELSE setting

A pharmacy's dispenser holds controlled drugs of more than one schedule, and each schedule has its
own ceiling on how many units of it may be out on the dispensing floor at once. The ceilings are
not fixed: the responsible pharmacist raises and lowers them during the day as the licence and the
staffing allow. A ceiling is only ever lowered while it is strictly above the number of units of
that schedule currently out, so lowering never strands units outside the new ceiling.

For each schedule the dispenser keeps one counter of how many units of it are out. A technician
drawing a unit does not lock the counter. It reads the counter for the schedule it wants and
remembers both which schedule and what figure it saw. When it goes to draw, the draw only goes
through if that schedule's counter still reads exactly the figure remembered, and if that figure is
below the schedule's ceiling as it stands at that moment; the counter then goes up by one and the
technician has the unit. If another technician has drawn or returned in the meantime the counter no
longer matches the remembered figure, so the reading is thrown away and the technician reads again.

A technician carries at most one unit at a time and returns it when the dispensing is done, which
brings that schedule's counter back down by one.

remembers the schedule and the figure; a technician draws a unit, provided the counter still reads
the remembered figure and that figure is below the schedule's current ceiling; a technician whose
remembered figure no longer matches the counter throws the reading away; a technician returns the
unit it is carrying, bringing that schedule's counter down; the pharmacist raises a schedule's
ceiling; and the pharmacist lowers a schedule's ceiling, only while it is above the units of that
schedule currently out.

floor never exceeds that schedule's ceiling as it currently stands.

opening anything; and a running theatre is closed.

Backing == Cardinality({c \in Consultants : signed[c] = request /\ request # NoTheatre})

Majority == Backing * 2 > Cardinality(Consultants)

    /\ running = {}
    /\ signed = [c \in Consultants |-> NoTheatre]
    /\ request = NoTheatre

    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, signed, thinking>>

A wildfire drone swarm maintains a shared perimeter map. The fire's edge is divided into segments,
and for each segment the swarm records how far the edge has been observed to have moved. The swarm
also keeps the raw observation file: every observation the swarm has accepted, tagged with the
segment it was for and the swarm generation it was made in.

The swarm reconfigures as aircraft join and drop out, and each reconfiguration advances the swarm
generation. Observations are stamped with the generation current when they are accepted, and a
segment only accepts an observation whose generation is strictly later than every observation
already in the file for that segment, so within a segment the file's generations only ever climb.

The map does not carry every segment. It has a carrying budget -- how many segments it can hold
open at once -- and the flight director changes that budget during the incident as bandwidth
allows. The budget is only ever cut back while it is strictly above the number of segments the map
is currently carrying. Bringing a segment onto the map is only possible while the map is under its
budget, and a segment can be dropped off the map at any time. Dropping a segment does not throw
away its observations: the file keeps them, so when that segment is later brought back onto the
map, the map must pick up again from the latest generation the file already holds for it, not from
nothing.

its carrying budget, and the map picks that segment up at the latest generation the observation
file already holds for it; an observation for a segment on the map is accepted and filed, stamped
with the current swarm generation, provided that generation is later than everything already filed

reconfigures, advancing the generation; the flight director raises the carrying budget; and the
flight director cuts the carrying budget back, only while it is above the segments currently
carried.

file, the map shows exactly the latest generation the file holds for that segment, so no accepted
observation is ever lost from the map.

A vending machine network keeps one shared stock record with a line for every machine. Restock
figures are entered against a machine in two moves: the figure is first put on the slip for that
machine, and it is then posted, which is the move that changes the machine's line in the record and

region claim, which only one desk holds at a time. Holding the region claim, it may take a claim on
an individual machine, and only a desk holding both the region claim and that machine's claim may
put a figure on the slip. A desk gives a machine claim back only with that machine's slip clear,
and gives the region claim back only while it holds no machine claims at all, so the two claims can
never come apart underneath a slip that still has a figure on it.

Head office holds a privileged override and can pull the region claim back to itself without
asking. Pulling it back would strand every machine claim underneath, and any figure still sitting
on a slip would simply vanish, so the override posts every outstanding slip into the record as it
goes, clears all the slips, and releases every machine claim, leaving the region unclaimed and the
record complete.

region claim takes a claim on a free machine; a desk holding the region claim and a machine's claim
puts a restock figure on that machine's slip, when the slip is clear and the figure fits the line;
a desk holding a machine's claim posts what is on the slip, changing the record and clearing the
slip; a desk gives back a machine claim, only with its slip clear; a desk gives back the region
claim, only while holding no machine claims; and head office pulls the region claim back, posting
every outstanding slip into the record, clearing every slip and releasing every machine claim.

the region claim, so a figure waiting to be posted is never left underneath a broken chain of
claims.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network gives visitors entry through guest code slots. Each slot on the lock
can be programmed with one guest, and a guest who has been given a code knows which slot that code
belongs to. The lock's own programming and what the guests have been told are meant to agree
exactly: if a guest has a code for a slot, that slot is programmed to that guest.

The household also sets a guest allowance -- how many slots may be programmed at once -- and it
changes that allowance from day to day as visitors come and go. The allowance is only ever reduced
while it is strictly above the number of slots currently programmed, so lowering it never leaves a
programmed slot outside the allowance.

Programming is done by the network's fitters and takes two claims, coarse before fine. A fitter
first takes the hub claim, which only one fitter holds at a time. Holding it, the fitter takes a
claim on an individual slot, and only the fitter holding a slot's claim may touch that slot. It
programs an empty slot to a guest who has no code yet, provided the programmed slots are under the
allowance; it then gives that guest the code for that slot. It can also wipe a slot, which empties
the programming and, at the same moment, cancels the code the guest was given for it, because a
code outstanding on a wiped slot is exactly how two guests end up sharing one slot.

The full set of actions is: a fitter takes the hub claim when it is free; the fitter holding the hub
claim takes a claim on a free slot; the fitter holding a slot's claim programs that empty slot to a
guest with no code, provided the programmed slots are under the allowance; the fitter holding a
slot's claim gives the guest programmed into it the code for that slot; the fitter holding a slot's
claim wipes it, emptying the programming and cancelling that guest's code for it; a fitter gives
back a slot claim; a fitter gives back the hub claim; the household raises the guest allowance; and
the household lowers the guest allowance, only while it is above the slots currently programmed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every guest holding a code for a slot is the guest that slot is currently
programmed to, so a slot is never given out to two guests at once.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container-ship crane yard lands containers into numbered ground slots. A slot holds one container,
and the yard planner works through a booking queue: each booking names one waiting container and one
ground slot, and the crane works the queue from the front.

The queue is deliberately short. It has a fixed depth, and when it is full no further booking can
be made until the crane has worked one off the front; this is the yard's backpressure, and it is
what stops the planner from running miles ahead of the crane. A booking can only be made for a
container that is waiting for a slot, for a slot that is standing empty, and for a slot that no
booking already in the queue names; likewise a container already named in the queue cannot be
booked again.

Working the front booking off the queue lands that container into that slot. A container in a slot
can later be lifted out again, which empties the slot and puts the container back among those
waiting.

The yard superintendent holds a privileged override, which can be armed and disarmed. While it is
armed the superintendent can drop a waiting container straight into any slot without going through
the queue at all. Whatever was in that slot is lifted out and goes back to waiting. Because a
booking in the queue for that slot, or for the container just placed, would now be a booking on
something already taken, the override strikes those bookings out of the queue as it goes and puts
their containers back among those waiting.

The full set of actions is: the planner books a waiting container into an empty slot that no queued
booking names, provided the queue is below its depth and the container is not already booked; the
crane works the front booking off the queue, landing that container into that slot; a container is
lifted out of its slot and goes back to waiting; the superintendent arms the override; the
superintendent disarms the override; and the superintendent drops a waiting container straight into
a slot under the armed override, lifting out whatever was there and striking out any queued booking
for that slot or that container.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every booking waiting in the queue names a slot that is still standing empty and
that no other booking in the queue names, so a slot is never booked or landed into twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The booking queue never stays full for ever; whenever it is at its depth, it
eventually drops below it again.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library reservation system puts requested books out on a hold shelf. The shelf is a row of
numbered positions, and each position holds the book for one reader. A reader whose reservation has
gone through is given a slip naming the position their book is on.

The shelf's usable length is not fixed. Shelving is added and taken away as the branch reorganises,
so the number of positions actually in use changes during the day. Length is only ever taken away
from the far end, and only while the last position in use is standing empty, so a position with a
book on it is never shelved out from under its reader.

A reservation is not simply written up. The branch and the central catalogue have to agree, so the
branch puts up one proposal at a time, naming a reader who holds no slip and a position that is
within the shelf's current length and standing empty. Each party then records its agreement. The
reservation goes through only when every party has agreed and, at that moment, the position is
still within the length, still standing empty, and the reader still holds no slip; going through
puts the book on that position and hands the reader the slip. A proposal can also be dropped, which
clears the agreements and changes nothing.

When a reader collects, the position is emptied and the slip is spent.

The full set of actions is: the branch puts up a proposal naming a reader with no slip and an empty
position within the shelf's length; a party records its agreement to the proposal; the reservation
goes through once every party has agreed and the position and reader are both still free, putting
the book out and handing over the slip; the proposal is dropped, clearing the agreements; a reader
collects, emptying the position and spending the slip; shelving is added, extending the length; and
shelving is taken away from the far end, only while the last position in use is empty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slip a reader holds names a position that is still within the shelf's
current length and still has that reader's book on it, so a position is never given out to two
readers and never left holding a book outside the shelf.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

    /\ slip \in [Readers -> 0..MaxPositions]
    /\ length \in 0..MaxPositions
    /\ proposal \in Proposal \cup {NoProposal}
    /\ agreed \subseteq Parties

    /\ slip = [r \in Readers |-> 0]

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A vending machine network empties its takings into one depot safe, and the safe has a single
docking port. Only one collection van can be on the port at a time.

The port keeps a register that either reads free or carries a van's name. Vans do not queue and
nothing is reserved for them: a van looks at the register and remembers whether it read free or
busy. A van that read free then tries to write its own name in, and the write only goes through
while the register still reads free; a van that read busy simply throws the reading away and will
look again later. A van whose name is in the register may then drive onto the port, and when it has
finished it drives off, which puts the register back to free.

A van can break down silently at any point. A van that has broken down does nothing further: it
does not look, does not write, does not drive on and does not drive off. The depot's watchdog deals
with the consequences. If a broken-down van is sitting on the port, the watchdog tows it off and
puts the register back to free. Separately, if the register carries a van's name but no van is
actually on the port, the registration has gone stale -- the van that won it may have broken down
before driving on, or simply not come -- and the watchdog times the registration out, putting the
register back to free.

The full set of actions is: a running van that is off the port and holding no reading looks at the
register and remembers free or busy; a running van that read free writes its name in, provided the
register still reads free; a running van that read busy throws the reading away; the van the
register names drives onto the port; a van on the port drives off, putting the register back to
free; a van breaks down; the watchdog tows a broken-down van off the port, putting the register
back to free; and the watchdog times out a registration that no van has driven on against.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any van on the docking port is the van whose name the register currently carries,
so two vans are never on the port together.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A registration is never left standing with nobody on the port; whenever the
register carries a name that no van has driven on against, it is eventually cleared.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

vars == <<register, onPort, reading, brokeDown>>

    /\ onPort \in [Vans -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reading \in [Vans -> {"free", "busy", NoRead}]
    /\ brokeDown \subseteq Vans

Running(v) == v \notin brokeDown

    /\ register = Free
    /\ onPort = [v \in Vans |-> FALSE]
    /\ reading = [v \in Vans |-> NoRead]
    /\ brokeDown = {}

\* The read reserves nothing; it only records what the register said.
Look(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ ~onPort[v]
    /\ reading[v] = NoRead
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![v] = IF register = Free THEN "free" ELSE "busy"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, onPort, brokeDown>>

\* The write lands only while the register still reads free.
WriteIn(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ reading[v] = "free"
    /\ register = Free
    /\ register' = v
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![v] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onPort, brokeDown>>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling system works its line with a fixed number of movement authorities. An authority
is the thing that lets a train move over a block, and the line neither prints new ones nor destroys
old ones during service, so at every moment every authority is in exactly one of three places: held
at the control centre, out on one of the line's blocks, or riding on the signalling bus between the
two.

Authorities go out to a block on a lease. The control centre takes a batch out of its own holding
and puts it on the bus addressed to a block; the batch leaves the centre's holding the moment it is
sent and only arrives on the block when the message is delivered. Delivery also starts that block's
lease running at full.

The bus carries several messages at once and delivers them in whatever order it happens to, not the
order they were sent, so a message can sit on the bus while the rest of the line moves on. Lease
timers run on the line's clock, which counts every running lease down together, a tick at a time.
When a block's lease has run out, whatever authorities it is holding are put back on the bus
addressed to the control centre and leave the block at that moment; they only rejoin the centre's
holding when that message is delivered.

The full set of actions is: the control centre takes a batch out of its holding and puts it on a
free place on the bus addressed to a block; a message addressed to a block is delivered, adding its
batch to that block and starting that block's lease at full; the line clock ticks, counting every
running lease down by one; a block whose lease has run out puts everything it is holding onto a
free place on the bus addressed to the control centre, giving it up at that moment; and a message
addressed to the control centre is delivered, adding its batch back to the centre's holding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The authorities held at the control centre, plus those out on the line's blocks,
plus those riding on the signalling bus, always add up to exactly the fixed number the line runs
with.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

ASSUME Centre \notin Blocks

Message == [to : Blocks \cup {Centre}, batch : 1..Authorities]

VARIABLES holding, onBlock, bus, lease

vars == <<holding, onBlock, bus, lease>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ holding \in 0..Authorities
    /\ onBlock \in [Blocks -> 0..Authorities]
    /\ bus \in [Wires -> Message \cup {Empty}]
    /\ lease \in [Blocks -> 0..LeaseTicks]

RECURSIVE OutOnLine(_)
OutOnLine(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN onBlock[b] + OutOnLine(S \ {b})

RECURSIVE OnBus(_)
OnBus(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET w == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN
         (IF bus[w] = Empty THEN 0 ELSE bus[w].batch) + OnBus(S \ {w})

Init ==
    /\ holding = Authorities
    /\ onBlock = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ bus = [w \in Wires |-> Empty]
    /\ lease = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]

\* The batch leaves the centre the moment it is sent, not when it lands.
SendOut(b, k, w) ==
    /\ bus[w] = Empty
    /\ holding >= k
    /\ holding' = holding - k
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![w] = [to |-> b, batch |-> k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBlock, lease>>

\* Any outstanding message may land; the bus does not preserve order.
LandOnBlock(w) ==
    /\ bus[w] # Empty
    /\ bus[w].to # Centre
    /\ onBlock' = [onBlock EXCEPT ![bus[w].to] = @ + bus[w].batch]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![bus[w].to] = LeaseTicks]
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![w] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED holding

\* One clock counts every running lease down together.
Tick ==
    /\ \E b \in Blocks : lease[b] > 0
    /\ lease' = [b \in Blocks |-> IF lease[b] > 0 THEN lease[b] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, onBlock, bus>>

GiveUp(b, w) ==
    /\ lease[b] = 0
    /\ onBlock[b] > 0
    /\ bus[w] = Empty
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![w] = [to |-> Centre, batch |-> onBlock[b]]]
    /\ onBlock' = [onBlock EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holding, lease>>

LandAtCentre(w) ==
    /\ bus[w] # Empty
    /\ bus[w].to = Centre
    /\ holding' = holding + bus[w].batch
    /\ bus' = [bus EXCEPT ![w] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onBlock, lease>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E w \in Wires : LandOnBlock(w) \/ LandAtCentre(w)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks, w \in Wires :
         GiveUp(b, w) \/ \E k \in 1..Authorities : SendOut(b, k, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AuthoritiesConserved ==
    holding + OutOnLine(Blocks) + OnBus(Wires) = Authorities

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A multiplayer game runs one ranked-match server, and only one lobby may be running matches on it at
a time. Which lobby has it is settled by agreement between the region gateways rather than by any
one of them.

Lobbies that want the server put themselves on the asking list. The matchmaker opens a round naming
one lobby off that list, taking it off the list as it does so, and it will only open a round while
the server is unheld. Each gateway then records a yes or a no on the round. If every gateway records a yes the
round commits and the named lobby becomes the holder of the server; if any gateway records a no the
round is abandoned and the server stays unheld. Either way the round closes.

Holding the server is not the same as using it. A lobby that holds the server starts running
matches on it as a separate step, and when it has finished it stops, which also gives the server
back so that it is unheld again.

The operations team holds a privileged override and can pull the server for maintenance at any
moment: doing so stops whatever is running, leaves the server unheld and closes any round that was
open.

The full set of actions is: a lobby puts itself on the asking list; the matchmaker opens a round
naming a lobby off the asking list, taking it off the list, which it may only do while the server
is unheld and no round is open; a gateway records a yes on the open round; a gateway
records a no on the open round; the round commits when every gateway has recorded a yes, making the
named lobby the holder and closing the round; the round is abandoned once a gateway has recorded a
no, closing it with the server still unheld; the holder starts running matches on the server; the
lobby running matches stops and gives the server back; and the operations team pulls the server,
stopping whatever is running, leaving it unheld and closing any open round.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any lobby running matches on the ranked server is the lobby that currently holds
it, and no round is ever open while the server is held, so two lobbies never run matches on it at
once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A lobby that has been made holder of the server never sits on it without using
it; it eventually either starts running matches or stops being the holder.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

    /\ running \in Lobbies \cup {Nobody}
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ ballot \in [Gateways -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ candidate \in Lobbies \cup {Nobody}
    /\ queued \subseteq Lobbies

AllYes == \A g \in Gateways : ballot[g] = "yes"

    /\ running = Nobody
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ ballot = [g \in Gateways |-> "none"]
    /\ candidate = Nobody

OpenRound(l) ==

    /\ holder = Nobody
    /\ l \in queued
    /\ candidate' = l
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ ballot' = [g \in Gateways |-> "none"]

    /\ phase' = "idle"

A skyscraper has two elevator banks that run independently but draw their emergency brake
cartridges from one shared magazine. A cartridge is a one-shot item: firing it is irreversible, and
a cartridge that has been fired is spent for good. The cartridges in the magazine are numbered, and
the building's incident log records, in order, the number of every cartridge that has been fired.

The magazine is worked from the front. There is one shared pointer saying which cartridge number is
next up, and nothing reserves it. A bank whose own alarm is raised reads the pointer and remembers
the number it saw. When it goes to fire, the fire only goes through if the pointer still reads

A blood bank moves donations around in numbered transport boxes. A filled box waits on the intake
queue, is taken into the airlock, and from the airlock it goes onto the cold-store shelves. When
the contents are issued to a ward the box comes back empty to the loading dock and can be filled
again.

The cold store has a fixed number of shelf positions. What matters is not just the boxes actually
on the shelves but also the boxes already taken into the airlock on their way there, because a
position is spoken for from the moment a box is taken in. The bank therefore counts the boxes on
the shelves together with the boxes in the airlock against the cold store's positions, and it will
not take another box into the airlock unless that combined count is below the number of positions.

The intake queue is deliberately short. It has a fixed depth, and while it is at that depth no
further box can be filled and queued; that backpressure is what stops the donation floor from
running ahead of the cold store.

Boxes do not go from the airlock to the shelves on their own. The airlock sends a shelving
confirmation over the bank's internal link, which carries several confirmations at once and
delivers them in whatever order it happens to, not the order they were sent. A confirmation is
applied only if the box it names is still sitting in the airlock; one that has been overtaken is
discarded.

The full set of actions is: an empty box at the loading dock is filled and joins the intake queue,
provided the queue is below its depth; the box at the front of the intake queue is taken into the
airlock, provided the shelves and airlock together are below the cold store's positions; the
airlock sends a shelving confirmation for a box it holds onto a free place on the link; a
confirmation is delivered off the link and moves its box onto the shelves, but only if that box is
still in the airlock; and a box on the shelves has its contents issued and returns empty to the
loading dock.

never exceed the cold store's number of shelf positions.

shared pool. Sending a carrier out onto the yard is done on a shift ticket: the movement is booked

sent out can be brought back in at any time, and a carrier claim is given back only once that
carrier is back in.

The port changes shift as the day goes on. A shift change moves the shift number on and brings every
carrier on the yard back in at the same moment, because a movement booked under the shift that has
just ended is exactly the kind of out-of-date working the port will not allow.

every carrier it had out and gives back every carrier claim it held, so the pool is left completely
free for the other terminal.

the pool claim takes a claim on a free carrier; a terminal sends out a carrier it has claimed,
booking the movement against itself and the current shift; a carrier out on the yard is brought
back in; a terminal gives back a carrier claim, only with that carrier back in; the port changes
shift, moving the shift number on and bringing every carrier back in; and a terminal gives the pool
claim back, bringing in every carrier it had out and dropping every carrier claim it held.

running right now and against the terminal that currently holds that carrier's claim, so no
out-of-date movement and no unclaimed terminal ever has a carrier running.

holding the token.

put back into service afterwards, so the set of drawers actually usable is not fixed. A unit is only
ever put away into a drawer that is in service. Taking a drawer out of service while there is a
unit in it turns that unit out: the drawer's card is cleared and the unit's label is cleared at the
same moment, because a card without a matching label, or a label without a matching card, is
exactly how a drawer ends up looking free while something is still in it.

the station holding the token puts a drawer back into service; the station holding the token lets
it go onto the link to the next station round; and a token travelling on a link arrives at the
station it was sent to.

every card names a unit whose label names that drawer, and every label names a drawer whose card
names that unit -- so no drawer is ever given out to two units.

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od10m7p4t2`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A metropolitan subway runs two line controllers -- one for the north line, one for the south line -- that schedule train movements completely independently of one another. Both draw traction current for the track blocks they energise from a single shared substation pool, and that pool can energise at most PoolCap blocks at any instant. There is no lock between the controllers; their only shared state is a compare-and-swap register holding the number of blocks currently energised.

A controller admits a train into a block in two steps. First it latches: it reads the register into its own private snapshot and records which block it intends to energise, which is only allowed if that block is not already energised by anybody. Then it swaps: it decides from its latched snapshot whether the pool still has headroom, and commits only if the register is still equal to that snapshot. If the register has moved since the read, the swap fails, and the controller discards its snapshot and its claim so it can start over. If the snapshot is current but already sits at the pool limit, the controller instead marks itself as refused and abandons the attempt. Independently of all that, a controller may de-energise any block it currently holds, which decrements the register and clears that controller's own refused mark.

The crucial detail is that the headroom decision is made against the latched snapshot rather than against the live register. Only the compare-and-swap step stops two controllers from both concluding there is room for one more train and both drawing current for it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The two line controllers together never hold more than PoolCap energised blocks at the same time.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Blocks, PoolCap, NoBlock, NoRead

ASSUME NoBlock \notin Blocks

VARIABLES reg, snap, claim, powered, refused

Vars == <<reg, snap, claim, powered, refused>>

\* The substation pool can energise at most PoolCap track blocks at once.
\* The two line controllers share nothing but the register `reg`.
Energised == UNION {powered[c] : c \in Controllers}

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in 0..Cardinality(Blocks)
    /\ snap \in [Controllers -> {NoRead} \union (0..Cardinality(Blocks))]
    /\ claim \in [Controllers -> {NoBlock} \union Blocks]
    /\ powered \in [Controllers -> SUBSET Blocks]
    /\ refused \subseteq Controllers

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Controllers |-> NoRead]
    /\ claim = [c \in Controllers |-> NoBlock]
    /\ powered = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]
    /\ refused = {}

\* A controller latches the register value it saw together with the block
\* it wants; that pair is its compare-and-swap expectation.
Latch(c, b) ==
    /\ snap[c] = NoRead
    /\ b \notin Energised
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = reg]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered, refused>>

\* Headroom is judged from the latched snapshot, so the swap must also
\* confirm that nothing moved the register since the read.
Swap(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] < PoolCap
    /\ snap[c] = reg
    /\ claim[c] \notin Energised
    /\ reg' = reg + 1
    /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![c] = @ \union {claim[c]}]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED refused

\* Stale expectation: some other controller advanced the register first.
SwapFails(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] # reg
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered, refused>>

Refuse(c) ==
    /\ snap[c] # NoRead
    /\ snap[c] >= PoolCap
    /\ snap[c] = reg
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = NoRead]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = NoBlock]
    /\ refused' = refused \union {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, powered>>

Deenergise(c, b) ==
    /\ b \in powered[c]
    /\ powered' = [powered EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {b}]
    /\ reg' = reg - 1
    /\ refused' = refused \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, claim>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : Latch(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Swap(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : SwapFails(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Refuse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, b \in Blocks : Deenergise(c, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars

\* Bounded capacity: the pool is never over-drawn, however the two
\* independent controllers interleave their latch/swap attempts.
PoolNeverOverdrawn == Cardinality(Energised) <= PoolCap
====
```
```cfg
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {northline, southline}
    Blocks = {bkA, bkB, bkC}
    PoolCap = 2
    NoBlock = nb
    NoRead = nr

INVARIANT PoolNeverOverdrawn
```
PROPERTY_INVARIANT: PoolNeverOverdrawn<|return|>

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od7m7p5t2`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container-ship crane yard runs two independent instances of its planning service, yardA and yardB, brought up as a pair so that neither is a single point of failure. They do not talk to each other. Both operate on one shared pool of berth registers, one register per ship, and each register holds the ship's phase together with a version stamp that is advanced by every write to that register.

A ship starts in the stowing phase with an empty hold. A crane may stow one more container onto a stowing ship as long as its hold is not yet full. Once a stowing ship's hold is exactly full, the yard clears it for sea, which moves it to the cleared phase and advances its stamp. Issuing the sailing order is the irreversible step: once a ship has sailed, its entry is on the port's departure manifest permanently and there is no way to recall it or amend the manifest.

A planner issues a sailing order in two stages. First it latches: in one indivisible peek it records the identity of a cleared ship together with the stamp it read from that ship's register. Later it commits: it writes the sailed phase, advances the stamp again, and appends the ship to the departure manifest, but only if the stamp it latched still matches the stamp in the register. If the stamp no longer matches, the other planner got there first, so the latch is stale and the planner simply drops it and moves on. Note that the commit stage never re-reads the phase; the stamp comparison is the only thing that tells a planner its latched view of the ship is still current.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No ship is ever appended to the departure manifest more than once, even when both planner instances latch the same cleared ship.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ship that reaches the cleared phase eventually sails rather than being left indefinitely at the berth.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section.
