===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A wildfire surveillance swarm keeps one common situation sheet listing the observations the swarm has confirmed. Each drone contributes its own report to that sheet, but the mesh radio between the drones has no ordering guarantee at all: reports that were prepared in one order reach the sheet in whatever order the mesh happens to deliver them.

A drone contributes by first reading the sheet -- taking a copy of its contents and the revision number it carried -- and then staging its report against that read. The staging area is deliberately small: while it is full no further report can be staged, and the drones holding reports simply have to wait, which is the backpressure the mesh needs to stop the observers running ahead of the sheet.

A staged report writes back the whole sheet it read plus its own observation. Because the write-back is a whole-sheet write, it may only land while the revision the drone read is still the standing revision; landing bumps the revision. A staged report whose read has gone out of date is bounced instead of written back, since putting its copy back would carry away whatever landed in the meantime. A bounced drone re-reads the sheet and stages afresh. Once every report has been merged the swarm rests.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every report that has been merged is still on the common situation sheet, so no later write-back ever carries away an observation that landed before it.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

vars == <<sheet, rev, stance, basis, snapshot>>

Typing ==

    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ stance \in [Reports -> {"held", "staged", "merged", "bounced"}]
    /\ basis \in [Reports -> 0..MaxRev]
    /\ snapshot \in [Reports -> SUBSET Reports]

Staged == {r \in Reports : stance[r] = "staged"}

Init ==
    /\ sheet = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ stance = [r \in Reports |-> "held"]
    /\ basis = [r \in Reports |-> 0]
    /\ snapshot = [r \in Reports |-> {}]

\* An observer reads the common sheet and stages its report against the
\* revision it read.  The staging area is small, and when it is full no
\* further report can be staged -- that is the backpressure on the observers.
Stage(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "held"
    /\ Cardinality(Staged) < StageCap
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "staged"]
    /\ basis' = [basis EXCEPT ![r] = rev]
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = sheet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev>>

\* Staged reports reach the sheet in whatever order the mesh delivers them,
\* not the order they were staged in.  A report writes back the whole sheet it
\* read plus itself, so it may only land while the revision it read is still
\* the standing one.
Merge(r) ==
    /\ stance[r] = "staged"
    /\ basis[r] = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ sheet' = snapshot[r] \cup {r}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "merged"]

\* A report whose read is out of date is bounced rather than written back,

\* in the meantime.
Bounce(r) ==

    /\ basis[r] # rev
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "bounced"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev, basis, snapshot>>

Reread(r) ==

    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![r] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sheet, rev, basis, snapshot>>

Rest ==

    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Reports : Stage(r) \/ Merge(r) \/ Bounce(r) \/ Reread(r)
    \/ Rest

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostObservation == {r \in Reports : stance[r] = "merged"} \subseteq sheet

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network spreads its decisions across several hubs. No single hub may carry out an unlock request on its own: a request is carried out only when a strict majority of the hubs have attested to it.

The household's access policy rolls forward from time to time -- a resident is added, a lost key is revoked -- and each roll gives the policy a newer number. Attestations written under an older policy are not erased when the policy rolls; they simply become stale. A hub attests to an open request under the policy it currently reads, and a hub whose attestation was written under an older policy re-attests under the new one.

The rule that keeps a revoked resident from getting through is that a request is carried out only on a majority of attestations written under the policy standing at that moment. Attestations left over from a superseded policy do not count towards that majority, so a hub that has not caught up with the roll cannot contribute to letting anybody in. When a request is carried out, the network records which policy it was carried out under.

Hubs on a home mesh are not reliable. A single hub may drop off without announcing it and then attests to nothing further, while the remaining hubs carry on; because a majority of three is two, the network can still reach decisions with one hub gone. Once every request has been settled the network is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Nothing is ever carried out on the strength of a superseded hub -- every granted request is backed by a majority of hubs that attested under the policy the grant was made against, or under a newer one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every open unlock request is eventually granted.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od18m5p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Hubs, Requests, MaxPolicy

Policies == 1..MaxPolicy
Quorums == {Q \in SUBSET Hubs : 2 * Cardinality(Q) > Cardinality(Hubs)}

VARIABLES policy, attest, verdict, mute

vars == <<policy, attest, verdict, mute>>

Typing ==
    /\ policy \in 0..MaxPolicy
    /\ attest \in [Requests -> [Hubs -> 0..MaxPolicy]]
    /\ verdict \in [Requests -> [state : {"open", "granted"}, under : 0..MaxPolicy]]
    /\ mute \subseteq Hubs

Backers(q, e) == {h \in Hubs : attest[q][h] >= e}

Init ==
    /\ policy = 1
    /\ attest = [q \in Requests |-> [h \in Hubs |-> 0]]
    /\ verdict = [q \in Requests |-> [state |-> "open", under |-> 0]]
    /\ mute = {}

\* The household rolls its access policy forward, for instance when a resident
\* is added or a key is revoked.  Attestations written under the old policy
\* are thereby made stale rather than being erased.
Rekey(e) ==
    /\ e > policy
    /\ policy' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attest, verdict, mute>>

\* A hub attests to a request under the policy it currently reads.  A hub that
\* has already attested under an older policy re-attests under the new one.
Attest(h, q) ==
    /\ h \notin mute
    /\ verdict[q].state = "open"
    /\ attest[q][h] < policy
    /\ attest' = [attest EXCEPT ![q][h] = policy]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, verdict, mute>>

\* A request is carried out only on a quorum of attestations written under the
\* policy standing right now; attestations left over from a superseded policy
\* are not counted towards it.
Grant(q) ==
    /\ verdict[q].state = "open"
    /\ {h \in Hubs : attest[q][h] = policy} \in Quorums
    /\ verdict' = [verdict EXCEPT ![q] = [state |-> "granted", under |-> policy]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, attest, mute>>

\* A single hub may drop off the mesh without announcing it.
GoMute(h) ==
    /\ mute = {}
    /\ mute' = {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<policy, attest, verdict>>

Settled ==
    /\ \A q \in Requests : verdict[q].state = "granted"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Policies : Rekey(e)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs, q \in Requests : Attest(h, q)
    \/ \E q \in Requests : Grant(q)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : GoMute(h)
    \/ Settled

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Hubs, q \in Requests : Attest(h, q))
    /\ WF_vars(\E q \in Requests : Grant(q))

\* Nothing is ever carried out on the strength of a superseded hub: every
\* granted request is backed by a quorum that attested under the policy the
\* grant was made against, or a newer one.
NoStaleAuthority ==
    \A q \in Requests :
        (verdict[q].state = "granted") => (Backers(q, verdict[q].under) \in Quorums)

EveryRequestEventuallySettled ==
    \A q \in Requests : (verdict[q].state = "open") ~> (verdict[q].state = "granted")

====

A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over its distribution feeders. Each feeder arrives at the start of the event with a fixed number of demand blocks on its books, and every one of those blocks must always be accounted for in exactly one of three states: energised, curtailed, or not yet placed.

The control room works by republishing a shedding plan. Each republication carries a strictly newer epoch number and sets the quota each feeder is allowed to draw. A plan only changes quotas; it never invents demand and never writes demand off the books.

A feeder energises an unplaced block whenever doing so keeps it inside its standing quota. A block that would take the feeder past its quota is curtailed instead -- curtailment moves the block out of the unplaced pile and into the curtailed pile, so the block is still carried, not discarded. When a newer plan raises a feeder's quota, the feeder picks curtailed blocks back up one at a time and energises them. Feeders here are slow but never fail: a feeder can lag a long way behind the plan the control room has published, and blocks can sit unplaced or curtailed for an arbitrarily long time, but no feeder ever stops responding altogether. Once every feeder has placed all its blocks and is drawing at least its quota, the grid is steady.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The energised, curtailed and unplaced blocks across all feeders always add up to exactly the demand the event started with, through any number of republished plans.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Feeders, Load, MaxEpoch

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES epoch, quota, served, curtailed, unplaced

vars == <<epoch, quota, served, curtailed, unplaced>>

Typing ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ quota \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ served \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ curtailed \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]
    /\ unplaced \in [Feeders -> 0..Load]

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ quota = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ served = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ curtailed = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
    /\ unplaced = [f \in Feeders |-> Load]

\* The control room publishes a new shedding plan under a strictly newer epoch
\* number.  The plan only changes how much each feeder is allowed to draw; it
\* never invents or destroys demand.
Republish(e, q) ==
    /\ e > epoch
    /\ epoch' = e
    /\ quota' = [f \in Feeders |-> q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<served, curtailed, unplaced>>

\* A block of demand is energised, but only within the feeder's standing quota.
Energise(f) ==
    /\ unplaced[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] < quota[f]
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![f] = served[f] + 1]
    /\ unplaced' = [unplaced EXCEPT ![f] = unplaced[f] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, curtailed>>

\* Demand beyond the quota is curtailed rather than dropped from the books.
Curtail(f) ==
    /\ unplaced[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] >= quota[f]
    /\ curtailed' = [curtailed EXCEPT ![f] = curtailed[f] + 1]
    /\ unplaced' = [unplaced EXCEPT ![f] = unplaced[f] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, served>>

\* When a newer plan raises a feeder's quota, curtailed blocks are picked back
\* up one at a time.  Feeders are slow, so this can lag the plan by a long way.
Restore(f) ==
    /\ curtailed[f] > 0
    /\ served[f] < quota[f]
    /\ curtailed' = [curtailed EXCEPT ![f] = curtailed[f] - 1]
    /\ served' = [served EXCEPT ![f] = served[f] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, quota, unplaced>>

Steady ==
    /\ \A f \in Feeders : unplaced[f] = 0 /\ served[f] >= quota[f]
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in 1..MaxEpoch, q \in 0..Load : Republish(e, q)
    \/ \E f \in Feeders : Energise(f) \/ Curtail(f) \/ Restore(f)
    \/ Steady

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every block of demand on the books is in exactly one of the three states,
\* through any number of republished plans: the grid neither invents load nor
\* loses track of load it has already curtailed.
DemandConserved ==
    Tally(served, Feeders) + Tally(curtailed, Feeders) + Tally(unplaced, Feeders)
        = Cardinality(Feeders) * Load

A case can only be listed into a theatre slot if the anaesthetics registry and the nursing registry both agree they can staff it, so the scheduler runs the listing as a two-phase agreement rather than writing the booking straight into the diary.

The scheduler opens a poll for an unlisted case against a theatre slot that is not already booked and that no other case is currently polling for. Opening the poll clears every registry's answer for that case. Each registry then answers for its own resources, yes or no. Registries here are slow but never fail: an answer can take arbitrarily long to come back, but it always comes back in the end.

The case is listed only once every registry has answered yes, and listing marks the slot as booked. A single refusal is enough to take the whole listing down: the case is dropped and gives up its claim on the slot, so the slot is available to be polled for again. A dropped case can be put back on the unlisted pile and tried once more, and once only, so the diary cannot churn for ever. Once every case has either been listed or dropped the diary is quiet.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every case that has gone to poll eventually settles, either listed or dropped.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cases, Slots, Registries, NoSlot

ASSUME NoSlot \notin Slots

VARIABLES stage, ballot, wanted, booked, retried

vars == <<stage, ballot, wanted, booked, retried>>

Typing ==
    /\ stage \in [Cases -> {"unlisted", "polling", "listed", "dropped"}]
    /\ ballot \in [Cases -> [Registries -> {"silent", "yes", "no"}]]
    /\ wanted \in [Cases -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ booked \in [Slots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ retried \subseteq Cases

Init ==
    /\ stage = [c \in Cases |-> "unlisted"]
    /\ ballot = [c \in Cases |-> [r \in Registries |-> "silent"]]
    /\ wanted = [c \in Cases |-> NoSlot]
    /\ booked = [k \in Slots |-> FALSE]
    /\ retried = {}

\* The scheduler opens a poll for a case against a theatre slot that is not
\* already booked and that no other case is currently polling for.
OpenPoll(c, k) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "unlisted"
    /\ ~booked[k]
    /\ \A d \in Cases : ~(stage[d] = "polling" /\ wanted[d] = k)
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "polling"]
    /\ wanted' = [wanted EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = [r \in Registries |-> "silent"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, retried>>

\* Each registry -- anaesthetics, nursing, theatre stores -- answers for its
\* own resources.  Registries here are slow but never fail, so an answer can
\* take arbitrarily long to arrive but always arrives in the end.
Answer(r, c, v) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "polling"
    /\ ballot[c][r] = "silent"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c][r] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, wanted, booked, retried>>

Commit(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "polling"

An airport baggage router keeps its bag manifest on a pool of manifest nodes rather than in one place. Two independent router instances run side by side over that same pool -- one driving the north pier, one the south -- and either of them may raise an amendment to the shared manifest, such as a reroute or a priority change. Raising an amendment records which router raised it and puts the amendment on offer.

An amendment on offer spreads across the pool one node at a time. The pool confirms it back to the router that raised it only once a strict majority of the manifest nodes are holding it. Confirmation is what a router treats as the amendment having taken effect: it will report the bag as rerouted on that basis and will never raise the amendment again, so a confirmed amendment that later vanished from the pool would be an update silently lost.

Manifest nodes are small and the two routers' traffic competes for the same memory. A node can come under pressure, and a node under pressure makes room by dropping one amendment it is holding; each node has a small budget of such drops. A node will only drop an amendment the pool has not yet confirmed. Once every amendment has been confirmed the pool is idle.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every amendment the pool has confirmed to a router is still held by a majority of the manifest nodes, so a confirmed change to the shared manifest is never squeezed back out under the other router's traffic.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Amendments, Routers, ShedBudget, NoRouter

ASSUME NoRouter \notin Routers

VARIABLES entry, kept, strain, sheds

vars == <<entry, kept, strain, sheds>>

Typing ==
    /\ entry \in [Amendments -> [state : {"draft", "offered", "confirmed"},
                                 by : Routers \cup {NoRouter}]]
    /\ kept \in [Nodes -> SUBSET Amendments]
    /\ strain \subseteq Nodes
    /\ sheds \in [Nodes -> 0..ShedBudget]

Init ==
    /\ entry = [a \in Amendments |-> [state |-> "draft", by |-> NoRouter]]
    /\ kept = [n \in Nodes |-> {}]
    /\ strain = {}
    /\ sheds = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]

\* Two routers run side by side over one pool of manifest nodes; either may
\* raise an amendment, and the amendment carries the router that raised it.
Raise(i, a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state = "draft"
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![a] = [state |-> "offered", by |-> i]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<kept, strain, sheds>>

Spread(n, a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state # "draft"
    /\ a \notin kept[n]
    /\ kept' = [kept EXCEPT ![n] = kept[n] \cup {a}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, strain, sheds>>

\* The pool confirms an amendment back to the router that raised it only once
\* a strict majority of the manifest nodes are holding it.
Confirm(a) ==
    /\ entry[a].state = "offered"
    /\ 2 * Cardinality({n \in Nodes : a \in kept[n]}) > Cardinality(Nodes)
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![a].state = "confirmed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<kept, strain, sheds>>

Squeeze(n) ==
    /\ n \notin strain
    /\ strain' = strain \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, kept, sheds>>

\* A node under memory pressure makes room for the other router's traffic, but
\* it will only drop an amendment the pool has not yet confirmed.
Shed(n, a) ==
    /\ n \in strain
    /\ sheds[n] < ShedBudget
    /\ a \in kept[n]
    /\ entry[a].state # "confirmed"
    /\ kept' = [kept EXCEPT ![n] = kept[n] \ {a}]
    /\ sheds' = [sheds EXCEPT ![n] = sheds[n] + 1]
    /\ strain' = strain \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED entry

Idle ==
    /\ \A a \in Amendments : entry[a].state = "confirmed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Routers, a \in Amendments : Raise(i, a)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, a \in Amendments : Spread(n, a) \/ Shed(n, a)
    \/ \E a \in Amendments : Confirm(a)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Squeeze(n)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* An amendment the pool has confirmed to a router is still held by a majority
\* of the manifest nodes, so a confirmed change is never squeezed back out.
NoLostAmendment ==
    \A a \in Amendments :
        (entry[a].state = "confirmed") =>
            (2 * Cardinality({n \in Nodes : a \in kept[n]}) > Cardinality(Nodes))

A university runs course registration across several registrar nodes, each of which keeps its own roll. No registrar can see any other registrar's roll, and no single registrar can enrol anybody on its own.

Enrolment needs a strict majority of the registrars to have pencilled the same student into the same place. Because any two majorities of the registrars share at least one member, and no registrar ever writes two names on one line, two students can never both collect a majority for the same place.

Registrar nodes on a campus network are not reliable. A single registrar may drop off the network without saying so and pencils nothing further, while the rest carry on; a majority of three is two, so registration still completes with one registrar gone.     /\ pencil \in [Registrars -> [Places -> Students \cup {NoStudent}]]
    /\ offline \subseteq Registrars
    /\ slip \in [Students -> {"none", "issued", "spent"}]

    /\ pencil = [r \in Registrars |-> [k \in Places |-> NoStudent]]

    /\ slip[s] = "issued"

The baton is handed on to any other drone still in the rotation, but never while its holder has the relay open. Only the drone holding the baton may open the relay, and only if it is in the rotation and waiting for its turn; when it is done it closes the relay and goes back to waiting.     /\ baton \in Drones \cup {NoDrone}
    /\ ring \subseteq Drones
    /\ churn \in 0..ChurnBudget

Init ==
    /\ stance = [d \in Drones |-> "aloft"]
    /\ baton = NoDrone
    /\ ring = {}
    /\ churn = 0

\* The ring is not a fixed shape: drones join and drop out of the relay
\* rotation as the fire front moves, so its size changes while it is running.
\* The first drone to join is handed the baton.
Join(d) ==
    /\ d \notin ring
    /\ churn < ChurnBudget
    /\ ring' = ring \cup {d}
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "waiting"]
    /\ baton' = IF ring = {} THEN d ELSE baton

\* A drone may only leave while it is not mid-burst and is not the one holding
\* the baton, so the baton is never carried out of the rotation.
Drop(d) ==

    /\ stance[d] # "burst"
    /\ baton # d
    /\ ring' = ring \ {d}
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "aloft"]

\* while its holder has the relay open.
Pass(e) ==
    /\ baton \in ring
    /\ stance[baton] # "burst"
    /\ e \in ring
    /\ e # baton
    /\ baton' = e
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stance, ring, churn>>

    /\ d \in ring
    /\ stance[d] = "waiting"
    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "burst"]

    /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![d] = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, ring, churn>>

Hover ==
    /\ churn = ChurnBudget
    /\ ring = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Join(d) \/ Drop(d) \/ OpenRelay(d) \/ CloseRelay(d)
    \/ \E e \in Drones : Pass(e)
    \/ Hover

An airport allocates departure windows from the tower. A flight held on the ground asks for a window and goes onto the paper strip board. The board holds only so many strips at once: while it is full nothing further can be requested and the holding stacks simply wait, which is the backpressure that stops the tower taking on more sequencing than it can work.

Issuing a clearance against a window is the irreversible step. The clearance goes out over the air and into the departure sequencer downstream, so once a window has been issued it can never be issued again -- not to another flight, and not a second time to the same flight.     /\ lead' = [lead EXCEPT ![m] = e]

\* Either desk may order any ship in the shared pool.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital pharmacy dispenses from a floor of robot bays. Prescriptions arrive on the queue and have to be allocated to a bay before the robot can pick and label them.

The floor is driven by whichever control station currently holds it. A station takes the floor by claiming an epoch number strictly newer than any epoch yet claimed by any station, and then taking the floor under that claim. Claiming and taking are separate steps, so a failover leaves the floor briefly unheld, and only a station that actually holds the floor allocates work.

The floor's capacity changes while it is running. Robot bays are taken out of service for cartridge changes and brought back afterwards; a bay is only taken out while it is standing free, the floor never drops below one bay in service, and the number of such changes in a session is limited.

Allocation writes both sides at once: the script records the bay it has been given and the bay records the script it is carrying, so the two halves of the allocation cannot come apart. A bay must be in service and standing free to be allocated. When the robot finishes, the script is dispensed and the bay goes back to free. Once every script has been dispensed the floor is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A script that has been allocated is held by exactly one robot bay, so no bay is ever carrying two prescriptions at once however the floor is re-sized underneath it.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every prescription that arrives on the queue is eventually dispensed.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Scripts, Bays, Stations, MaxEpoch, ChurnCap, NoBay, NoScript, NoStation

ASSUME NoBay \notin Bays /\ NoScript \notin Scripts /\ NoStation \notin Stations

Epochs == 1..MaxEpoch

VARIABLES script, bay, chief, claim, churn

vars == <<script, bay, chief, claim, churn>>

Typing ==
    /\ script \in [Scripts -> [state : {"received", "assigned", "dispensed"},
                               bay : Bays \cup {NoBay}]]
    /\ bay \in [Bays -> [state : {"offline", "free", "busy"},
                         holder : Scripts \cup {NoScript}]]
    /\ chief \in [ctl : Stations \cup {NoStation}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ claim \in [Stations -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ churn \in 0..ChurnCap

InService == {k \in Bays : bay[k].state # "offline"}

Init ==
    /\ script = [s \in Scripts |-> [state |-> "received", bay |-> NoBay]]
    /\ bay = [k \in Bays |-> [state |-> "free", holder |-> NoScript]]
    /\ chief = [ctl |-> NoStation, ep |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [c \in Stations |-> 0]
    /\ churn = 0

\* The dispensing floor is driven by whichever control station currently holds
\* the floor.  A station claims an epoch newer than any yet claimed; taking the
\* floor is a separate step, so a failover leaves the floor briefly unheld.
Claim(c, e) ==
    /\ \A d \in Stations : e > claim[d]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![c] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, bay, chief, churn>>

TakeFloor(c) ==
    /\ claim[c] > chief.ep
    /\ chief' = [ctl |-> c, ep |-> claim[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, bay, claim, churn>>

\* Robot bays are taken out of service for cartridge changes and brought back,
\* so the floor's capacity changes while it is running.  A bay is only taken
\* out while it is free, and the floor never drops below one bay in service.
CloseBay(k) ==
    /\ bay[k].state = "free"
    /\ Cardinality(InService) > 1
    /\ churn < ChurnCap
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k].state = "offline"]
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, chief, claim>>

OpenBay(k) ==
    /\ bay[k].state = "offline"
    /\ churn < ChurnCap
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k].state = "free"]
    /\ churn' = churn + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<script, chief, claim>>

\* Only the station holding the floor allocates work, and only into a bay that
\* is in service and standing free.  The bay and the script are written in the
\* same movement, so the two sides of the allocation cannot come apart.
Allocate(s, k) ==
    /\ chief.ctl # NoStation
    /\ script[s].state = "received"
    /\ bay[k].state = "free"
    /\ script' = [script EXCEPT ![s] = [state |-> "assigned", bay |-> k]]
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![k] = [state |-> "busy", holder |-> s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, claim, churn>>

Dispense(s) ==
    /\ script[s].state = "assigned"
    /\ script' = [script EXCEPT ![s].state = "dispensed"]
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![script[s].bay] = [state |-> "free", holder |-> NoScript]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, claim, churn>>

Closed ==
    /\ \A s \in Scripts : script[s].state = "dispensed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Stations, e \in Epochs : Claim(c, e)
    \/ \E c \in Stations : TakeFloor(c)
    \/ \E k \in Bays : CloseBay(k) \/ OpenBay(k)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts, k \in Bays : Allocate(s, k)
    \/ \E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s)
    \/ Closed

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Stations, e \in Epochs : Claim(c, e))
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Stations : TakeFloor(c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Scripts, k \in Bays : Allocate(s, k))
    /\ WF_vars(\E s \in Scripts : Dispense(s))

\* is ever carrying two prescriptions at once however the floor is re-sized.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Scripts :
        (script[s].state = "assigned") =>
            (Cardinality({k \in Bays : bay[k].holder = s}) = 1)

EveryScriptEventuallyDispensed ==
    \A s \in Scripts : (script[s].state = "received") ~> (script[s].state = "dispensed")

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container-ship crane yard plans its moves against a shared yard ledger, one ledger per stack, recording which crane orders have been booked against that stack.

Planners lodge moves onto a short crane order queue. The queue is deliberately short: while it is full nothing further can be lodged and the planners simply have to wait, which is the backpressure that stops the plan running ahead of what the cranes can work. Lodging a move stamps it with the yard revision the planner read at that moment.

A move is posted against a stack only while the revision its planner read is still the standing yard revision, and posting bumps that revision. Posting adds the move to the stack's ledger rather than rewriting the ledger wholesale, so nothing already booked there is displaced by it. A move whose planner read a revision that has since moved on is bounced rather than posted, and a bounced move can be lodged again.

There is a privileged override: the yard superintendent may push a stale move through anyway when the ship is on the tide. The override still only adds to the stack's ledger, and there are only so many overrides in a shift. Separately, ledgers are trimmed from time to time of orders that never went anywhere.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every move that has been posted still stands in exactly one stack ledger, so no posted crane order is ever carried away by a later posting, an override, or a trim.

VARIABLES move, ledger, yardRev, forced

vars == <<move, ledger, yardRev, forced>>

Typing ==
    /\ move \in [Moves -> [state : {"waiting", "queued", "posted", "bounced"},
                           base : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ ledger \in [Stacks -> SUBSET Moves]
    /\ yardRev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ forced \in 0..ForceCap

Queued == {m \in Moves : move[m].state = "queued"}

Init ==
    /\ move = [m \in Moves |-> [state |-> "waiting", base |-> 0]]
    /\ ledger = [t \in Stacks |-> {}]
    /\ yardRev = 0
    /\ forced = 0

\* The crane order queue is short: while it is full the planners cannot lodge
\* another move and simply have to wait, which is the backpressure that stops
\* the plan running ahead of the cranes.  Lodging stamps the yard revision the
\* planner read.
Lodge(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "waiting"
    /\ Cardinality(Queued) < QueueCap
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m] = [state |-> "queued", base |-> yardRev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

\* A move is posted against a stack only while the revision its planner read is
\* still the standing yard revision.  Posting adds to the stack's ledger; it
\* never rewrites the ledger wholesale, so nothing already there is displaced.
Post(m, t) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base = yardRev
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = ledger[t] \cup {m}]
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "posted"]
    /\ yardRev' = yardRev + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED forced

Bounce(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base # yardRev
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "bounced"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

\* The privileged override: the yard superintendent may push a stale move
\* through anyway.  It still only adds to the stack's ledger, and there are
\* only so many overrides in a shift.
Force(m, t) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "queued"
    /\ move[m].base # yardRev
    /\ forced < ForceCap
    /\ yardRev < MaxRev
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = ledger[t] \cup {m}]
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "posted"]
    /\ yardRev' = yardRev + 1
    /\ forced' = forced + 1

\* Ledgers are trimmed of orders that never went anywhere.
Compact(t) ==
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![t] = {m \in ledger[t] : move[m].state = "posted"}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<move, yardRev, forced>>

Relodge(m) ==
    /\ move[m].state = "bounced"
    /\ move' = [move EXCEPT ![m].state = "waiting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, yardRev, forced>>

Idle ==
    /\ yardRev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Moves : Lodge(m) \/ Bounce(m) \/ Relodge(m)
    \/ \E m \in Moves, t \in Stacks : Post(m, t) \/ Force(m, t)
    \/ \E t \in Stacks : Compact(t)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every move that has been posted still stands in exactly one stack ledger, so
\* no posted crane order is ever carried away by a later posting or a trim.
NoLostMove ==
    \A m \in Moves :
        (move[m].state = "posted") =>
            (Cardinality({t \in Stacks : m \in ledger[t]}) = 1)

    /\ lease[k].holder = NoBatch
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b] = [state |-> "held", bin |-> k]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> b, until |-> Clip(clock + LeaseLen)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

Store(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "held"
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "stored"]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![batch[b].bin] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, lease, revokes>>

\* A lease that has run out is reclaimed and its batch goes back to pending.
\* Both sides are cleared together, so the bin is never left holding a batch
\* that no longer thinks it has one.
Expire(k) ==
    /\ lease[k].holder # NoBatch
    /\ lease[k].until < clock
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![lease[k].holder] = [state |-> "pending", bin |-> NoBin]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, revokes>>

\* The privileged override: the duty pharmacist may pull a lease back early to
\* free a cold bin for an urgent line.  There are only so many in a shift.
Revoke(k) ==
    /\ lease[k].holder # NoBatch
    /\ revokes < RevokeCap
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![lease[k].holder] = [state |-> "pending", bin |-> NoBin]]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![k] = [holder |-> NoBatch, until |-> 0]]
    /\ revokes' = revokes + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Shut ==
    /\ \A b \in Batches : batch[b].state = "stored"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Batches, k \in Bins : Grant(b, k)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Store(b)
    \/ \E k \in Bins : Expire(k) \/ Revoke(k)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Shut

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches, k \in Bins : Grant(b, k))
    /\ WF_vars(\E b \in Batches : Store(b))

\* A batch that is holding a cold bin holds exactly one, so a bin is never
\* leased to two batches at once across an expiry or an early revocation.
NoDoubleLease ==
    \A b \in Batches :

EveryBatchEventuallyStored ==
    \A b \in Batches : (batch[b].state = "pending") ~> (batch[b].state = "stored")

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A warehouse robot fleet draws its charging allowances for the day from a single shared pool. Two fleet controllers -- the day scheduler and the night scheduler -- run as independent instances but work the same floor and draw from that one pool, so they are constantly racing each other for the same allowances.

The pool is kept in a register carrying a revision stamp. A controller reads the register and the revision on it, then goes away to decide which robot to top up. The write back is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the controller read is still the one on the register. If the other controller has moved the pool in the meantime, the revision has changed, the write is abandoned, and the controller starts again from a fresh read. A landing write takes one allowance out of the pool and puts it on the chosen robot in the same movement, and bumps the revision.

A robot spends an allowance it is carrying by running a shift on it, which burns the allowance. A robot can also hand an allowance back to the pool unspent when its work is cancelled. Nothing else moves allowances around, and no controller can conjure one. The register carries only so many revision stamps in a day; once the last one has been used the floor is parked.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Fleets, Total, MaxRev, NoRobot

ASSUME NoRobot \notin Robots

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tally(f, S \ {x})

VARIABLES pool, rev, drawn, burnt, bid

vars == <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt, bid>>

Typing ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ drawn \in [Robots -> 0..Total]
    /\ burnt \in 0..Total
    /\ bid \in [Fleets -> [state : {"idle", "reading"}, base : 0..MaxRev,
                           robot : Robots \cup {NoRobot}]]

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ drawn = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ burnt = 0
    /\ bid = [f \in Fleets |-> [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]

\* Two fleet controllers work the same floor out of one pool of charge
\* allowances.  A controller reads the pool register and the revision stamped
\* on it, then goes away to decide which robot to top up.
Read(f, r) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "idle"
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev, robot |-> r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt>>

\* The write back is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the
\* controller read is still the one on the register, so the other controller
\* cannot have moved the pool underneath it.  An allowance leaves the pool and
\* arrives on a robot in the same movement.
Commit(f) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "reading"
    /\ bid[f].base = rev
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![bid[f].robot] = drawn[bid[f].robot] + 1]
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]
    /\ UNCHANGED burnt

\* A controller whose read has gone stale abandons the write and starts again.
Retry(f) ==
    /\ bid[f].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ bid[f].base # rev
       \/ pool = 0
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![f] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, robot |-> NoRobot]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, drawn, burnt>>

Spend(r) ==
    /\ drawn[r] > 0
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![r] = drawn[r] - 1]
    /\ burnt' = burnt + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, rev, bid>>

HandBack(r) ==
    /\ drawn[r] > 0
    /\ drawn' = [drawn EXCEPT ![r] = drawn[r] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rev, burnt, bid>>

\* Once the register has been stamped for the last time the floor is parked.
Parked ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Fleets, r \in Robots : Read(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Fleets : Commit(f) \/ Retry(f)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Spend(r) \/ HandBack(r)
    \/ Parked

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Charge allowances are never created or destroyed by the two controllers
\* racing each other: what is left in the pool, what the robots are carrying
\* and what has been burnt always add back up to the day's total.
ChargeConserved == pool + Tally(drawn, Robots) + burnt = Total

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever anything is standing in the controlled-drugs cupboard, the cupboard is holding no more than it is licensed for, however many porters raced each other to put a delivery away.

    /\ onShelf \subseteq Deliveries
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ tries \in [Deliveries -> 0..MaxRev]

    /\ delivery = [d \in Deliveries |-> [state |-> "waiting", base |-> 0]]
    /\ onShelf = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ tries = [d \in Deliveries |-> 0]

\* A porter reads how full the controlled-drugs cupboard is, together with the
\* revision stamped on the count, and then walks the delivery over.  Porters
\* are slow but never give up: that walk can take arbitrarily long.
Read(d) ==

    /\ tries[d] < MaxRev
    /\ delivery' = [delivery EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev]]

\* has used up their attempts -- is turned away to the ward safe instead.
TurnAway(d) ==

    /\ WF_vars(\E d \in Deliveries : TurnAway(d))

\* is holding no more than it is licensed for, however many porters raced each
\* other to put a delivery away.
CapacityRespected ==

    \A d \in Deliveries :

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od17m1p6t1`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router splits its sorting across a ring of sorter nodes. The right to commit routing decisions moves round that ring as a numbered grant: at any moment only the node currently holding a grant may commit decisions, because two nodes committing at once would send the same bag down two chutes.

Grants travel over the baggage network, which gives no ordering guarantee whatsoever. A grant sits on an unordered wire, and a sorter can be handed an old grant after a newer one has already reached it. A sorter therefore takes a grant only if its round number is newer than the round the sorter has already moved to, and it records which grant it acted on.

A grant that arrives behind one the sorter has already moved past is stale: the sorter drops it rather than acting on it, because acting on it would mean committing decisions on authority the ring has already taken away. A grant that finds a sorter already busy is dropped for the same reason.

When a sorter has committed the routing decisions for its round it hands the ring back and goes idle. Once the last round has been issued, the wire is clear and every sorter is idle, the ring is quiet.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A sorter that is committing routing decisions is doing so under a grant it actually took, at exactly the round it took it, so nothing is ever committed on the strength of a grant the ring has already moved past.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A sorter that has taken the ring always eventually hands it back.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Sorters, MaxRound

Grants == [to : Sorters, rnd : 1..MaxRound]

VARIABLES sorter, wire, taken, issued

vars == <<sorter, wire, taken, issued>>

Typing ==
    /\ sorter \in [Sorters -> [state : {"idle", "working"}, rnd : 0..MaxRound]]
    /\ wire \subseteq Grants
    /\ taken \subseteq Grants
    /\ issued \in 0..MaxRound

Init ==
    /\ sorter = [n \in Sorters |-> [state |-> "idle", rnd |-> 0]]
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ taken = {}
    /\ issued = 0

\* The right to commit routing decisions moves round the ring as a numbered
\* grant.  Grants sit on an unordered wire, so a sorter can be handed an old
\* grant after a newer one has already reached it.
PassOn(n) ==
    /\ issued < MaxRound
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ wire' = wire \cup {[to |-> n, rnd |-> issued + 1]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sorter, taken>>

\* A sorter takes a grant only if its round is newer than the round the sorter
\* has already moved to, and it records the grant it acted on.
Take(g) ==
    /\ g \in wire
    /\ sorter[g.to].state = "idle"
    /\ g.rnd > sorter[g.to].rnd
    /\ sorter' = [sorter EXCEPT ![g.to] = [state |-> "working", rnd |-> g.rnd]]
    /\ taken' = taken \cup {g}
    /\ wire' = wire \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED issued

\* A grant that arrives behind one the sorter has already moved past is stale
\* and is dropped rather than acted on; so is one that finds the sorter busy.
Drop(g) ==
    /\ g \in wire
    /\ \/ g.rnd <= sorter[g.to].rnd
       \/ sorter[g.to].state = "working"
    /\ wire' = wire \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sorter, taken, issued>>

\* Committing the routing decisions of a round hands the ring back.
Release(n) ==
    /\ sorter[n].state = "working"
    /\ sorter' = [sorter EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<wire, taken, issued>>

Quiet ==
    /\ issued = MaxRound
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ \A n \in Sorters : sorter[n].state = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Sorters : PassOn(n) \/ Release(n)
    \/ \E g \in Grants : Take(g) \/ Drop(g)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Sorters : Release(n))
    /\ WF_vars(\E g \in Grants : Drop(g))

\* A sorter that is committing routing decisions is doing so under a grant it
\* actually took, at exactly the round it took: nothing is ever committed on
\* the strength of a grant the ring has moved past.
NoStaleAuthority ==
    \A n \in Sorters :
        (sorter[n].state = "working") =>
            (Cardinality({g \in taken : g.to = n /\ g.rnd = sorter[n].rnd}) = 1)

EveryHolderEventuallyHandsBack ==
    \A n \in Sorters : (sorter[n].state = "working") ~> (sorter[n].state = "idle")

====

\* epoch newer than any yet claimed by anybody.

The write into the book is a compare-and-swap against the revision the batch was drawn on, and landing bumps that revision -- so a batch that was drawn twice, because it was put back and drawn again, cannot be written into the book twice.

A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- because the book has moved on since it was drawn, or because there are not enough benches manned to witness it -- goes back into the safe intact and can be restocked and drawn again later. Entries == [btc : Batches, rev : 1..MaxRev]

vars == <<batch, book, rev, manned>>

    /\ book \subseteq Entries
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ manned \subseteq Benches

Init ==

    /\ book = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ manned = Benches

\* Witness benches are manned and stood down through the shift, so the number
\* of witnesses available to a destruction changes while the round is running.
StandDown(w) ==
    /\ w \in manned
    /\ manned' = manned \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

ManUp(w) ==
    /\ w \notin manned
    /\ manned' = manned \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<batch, book, rev>>

\* A batch is drawn from the safe against the revision the destruction book
\* currently carries.
Draw(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "stored"
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b] = [state |-> "drawn", base |-> rev]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

\* entry can never be unwritten.  The write into the book is a compare-and-swap
\* against the revision the batch was drawn on, so a batch drawn twice cannot
\* be written twice; enough benches must also be manned to witness it.
Destroy(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ batch[b].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(manned) >= MinWitness
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ book' = book \cup {[btc |-> b, rev |-> rev + 1]}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "destroyed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED manned

\* A batch that cannot be destroyed on this pass -- the book has moved on, or
\* there are not enough witnesses -- goes back into the safe intact.
Return(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "drawn"
    /\ \/ batch[b].base # rev
       \/ Cardinality(manned) < MinWitness
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "returned"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Restock(b) ==
    /\ batch[b].state = "returned"
    /\ batch' = [batch EXCEPT ![b].state = "stored"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, rev, manned>>

Shut ==
    /\ rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Benches : StandDown(w) \/ ManUp(w)
    \/ \E b \in Batches : Draw(b) \/ Destroy(b) \/ Return(b) \/ Restock(b)

    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QueueCap

    /\ slip[n].state = "filed"
    /\ owner[n] \in working
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![n].state = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, working, epoch>>

\* Re-sectorising under a strictly newer epoch.  Handing a band over carries
\* every slip filed against it to a band that stays worked, in the same
\* movement as the handover, so nothing is stranded in a band nobody has.
HandOver(b, c) ==
    /\ b \in working
    /\ c \in working
    /\ b # c
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ working' = working \ {b}
    /\ owner' = [n \in Notes |-> IF owner[n] = b THEN c ELSE owner[n]]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED slip

\* Splitting a band back out puts it back on a controller's desk.
SplitOut(b) ==
    /\ b \notin working
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ working' = working \cup {b}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, owner>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A n \in Notes : slip[n].state = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Notes, b \in Bands : File(n, b)
    \/ \E n \in Notes : Commit(n)
    \/ \E b, c \in Bands : HandOver(b, c)
    \/ \E b \in Bands : SplitOut(b)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Notes, b \in Bands : File(n, b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E n \in Notes : Commit(n))

\* Every committed coordination slip still belongs to a band a controller is
\* actually working, so no committed slip is stranded by a re-sectorisation.
NoStrandedSlip ==
    \A n \in Notes :
        (slip[n].state = "committed") =>
            (Cardinality({b \in Bands : owner[n] = b /\ b \in working}) = 1)

EverySlipEventuallyCommitted ==
    \A n \in Notes : (slip[n].state = "raised") ~> (slip[n].state = "committed")

====

A bank settles its interbank batches over a small pool of posting rails, one rail per currency. A rail is a critical resource: while one desk is standing on it walking a batch through, no other desk may touch it, because the rail rewrites the same reserve balances leg by leg and two batches interleaved would post against balances the other has already moved.

Two settlement instances run side by side over that one pool -- a day instance and a night instance, each with its own operators and its own batches -- so both are constantly reaching for the same rails. The rails are not held under a lock; each carries a revision stamp instead.

A desk reads the rail it wants together with the revision stamped on it, then goes away to assemble its batch. Taking the rail is a compare-and-swap: it lands only while the revision the desk read is still the one on the rail and nobody is standing on it, and taking it bumps that revision. That is exactly what stops the other instance walking onto the same rail behind this desk's read. A desk whose read has gone stale -- the revision has moved, or somebody is on the rail, or the rail has been stamped for the last time in the window -- drops its batch and starts again from a fresh read.

A desk standing on a rail posts its batch one leg at a time and steps off only when the whole batch is through, leaving the rail free for the next desk and adding one to that rail's tally of batches cleared in the window.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Desks, Rails, MaxRev, Legs, MaxCleared, NoDesk, NoRail

ASSUME NoDesk \notin Desks /\ NoRail \notin Rails

VARIABLES desk, rail, posted, cleared

vars == <<desk, rail, posted, cleared>>

Typing ==
    /\ desk \in [Desks -> [state : {"idle", "reading", "posting"},
                           base : 0..MaxRev, want : Rails \cup {NoRail}]]
    /\ rail \in [Rails -> [holder : Desks \cup {NoDesk}, rev : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ posted \in [Desks -> 0..Legs]
    /\ cleared \in [Rails -> 0..MaxCleared]

Init ==
    /\ desk = [d \in Desks |-> [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ rail = [r \in Rails |-> [holder |-> NoDesk, rev |-> 0]]
    /\ posted = [d \in Desks |-> 0]
    /\ cleared = [r \in Rails |-> 0]

\* Two settlement instances run side by side over one pool of posting rails.
\* A desk reads the rail it wants and the revision stamped on it, then goes
\* away to assemble its batch.
Read(d, r) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "idle"
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rail[r].rev,
                                    want |-> r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rail, posted, cleared>>

\* Taking the rail is a compare-and-swap: it only lands while the revision the
\* desk read is still on the rail and nobody is standing on it.  That is what
\* stops the other instance walking onto the same rail behind this one's read.
Take(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "reading"
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].rev = desk[d].base
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].holder = NoDesk
    /\ rail[desk[d].want].rev < MaxRev
    /\ rail' = [rail EXCEPT ![desk[d].want] = [holder |-> d,
                                               rev |-> rail[desk[d].want].rev + 1]]
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d].state = "posting"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<posted, cleared>>

\* A desk whose read has gone stale drops its batch and starts again.
Retry(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ rail[desk[d].want].rev # desk[d].base
       \/ rail[desk[d].want].holder # NoDesk
       \/ rail[desk[d].want].rev = MaxRev
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rail, posted, cleared>>

PostLeg(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "posting"
    /\ posted[d] < Legs
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = posted[d] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<desk, rail, cleared>>

StepOff(d) ==
    /\ desk[d].state = "posting"
    /\ posted[d] = Legs
    /\ rail' = [rail EXCEPT ![desk[d].want].holder = NoDesk]
    /\ desk' = [desk EXCEPT ![d] = [state |-> "idle", base |-> 0, want |-> NoRail]]
    /\ posted' = [posted EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![desk[d].want] =
                      IF cleared[desk[d].want] < MaxCleared
                      THEN cleared[desk[d].want] + 1 ELSE MaxCleared]

Closed ==
    /\ \A r \in Rails : rail[r].rev = MaxRev
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, r \in Rails : Read(d, r)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : Take(d) \/ Retry(d) \/ PostLeg(d) \/ StepOff(d)
    \/ Closed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A desk that is posting is standing on exactly one rail, so the two
\* settlement instances never work the same rail at the same time.
RailExclusion ==
    \A d \in Desks :
        (desk[d].state = "posting") =>
            (Cardinality({r \in Rails : rail[r].holder = d}) = 1)

A library consortium deaccessions titles from its shared catalogue. Each branch keeps its own catalogue register carrying a revision number, and a branch marks a title for deaccession against the revision its register currently shows.

Withdrawing a title is the irreversible step. The remaining copies are pulped and the shelf mark is retired, so the title can never be withdrawn a second time and nothing can put it back. The write into the deaccession register is a compare-and-swap against the revision the mark was taken on, and a landing write bumps that revision. That check is what stops a title that was marked twice -- because a mark was dropped and taken again -- being pulped twice.

A mark that has gone stale, because the marking branch's register has moved on since, is dropped and the title simply stays on the shelf to be marked again later.

Branch catalogue nodes are not reliable. One branch's node may drop off the consortium without saying so; it then stops confirming anything, and a mark that was taken by that branch is dropped rather than left hanging. The remaining branches carry on deaccessioning normally.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every title marked for deaccession is eventually resolved, either withdrawn or put back on the shelf.

vars == <<title, branch, register, stock>>

Typing ==

                             base : 0..MaxRev, by : Branches \cup {NoBranch}]]
    /\ branch \in [Branches -> [state : {"up", "dark"}, rev : 0..MaxRev]]
    /\ register \subseteq [ttl : Titles, br : Branches]
    /\ stock \in [Titles -> 0..Copies]

Init ==
    /\ title = [t \in Titles |-> [state |-> "held", base |-> 0, by |-> NoBranch]]
    /\ branch = [b \in Branches |-> [state |-> "up", rev |-> 0]]
    /\ register = {}
    /\ stock = [t \in Titles |-> Copies]

\* A branch marks a title for deaccession against the revision its own
\* catalogue register currently carries.
Mark(t, b) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "held"
    /\ branch[b].state = "up"
    /\ branch[b].rev < MaxRev
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t] = [state |-> "marked", base |-> branch[b].rev,
                                      by |-> b]]

\* Withdrawing a title is irreversible: the copies are pulped and the shelf
\* mark is retired, so it can never be withdrawn again.  The write into the
\* deaccession register is a compare-and-swap against the revision the mark was
\* taken on, which is what stops a title marked twice being pulped twice.
Withdraw(t) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "marked"
    /\ branch[title[t].by].state = "up"
    /\ branch[title[t].by].rev = title[t].base
    /\ register' = register \cup {[ttl |-> t, br |-> title[t].by]}
    /\ branch' = [branch EXCEPT ![title[t].by].rev = title[t].base + 1]
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t].state = "withdrawn"]
    /\ stock' = [stock EXCEPT ![t] = 0]

\* A mark that has gone stale, or whose branch has gone dark, is dropped and
\* the title stays on the shelf.
Unmark(t) ==
    /\ title[t].state = "marked"
    /\ \/ branch[title[t].by].state = "dark"
       \/ branch[title[t].by].rev # title[t].base
    /\ title' = [title EXCEPT ![t] = [state |-> "held", base |-> 0, by |-> NoBranch]]

GoDark(b) ==

    /\ Cardinality(Branches) > 1

    \/ \E b \in Branches : GoDark(b)

    /\ WF_vars(\E t \in Titles : Unmark(t))

\* register, however many branches marked it and however often it was marked.

A university runs course registration from several faculty nodes that all amend the same pair of enrolment ledgers, one for undergraduate places and one for postgraduate. The nodes take turns by passing a baton round a ring. Only the node holding the baton may arm itself to write, and the baton is only handed on while its holder is not mid-write, so a node cannot have the baton taken out from under it in the middle of amending a ledger. The baton makes a limited number of laps in a registration window.

A node that armed itself and then lost its turn before reaching a pen simply stands down again. An armed node that still has the baton picks up a ledger's pen, and only a pen that nobody is holding. Nodes here are slow but never fail: an armed node may take a long time to reach for the pen and a long time over its entries, and the baton stays with it throughout, but it always gets there in the end. The node then makes its amendments one at a time and finally puts the pen down, leaving the ledger free.

Typing ==

                           done : 0..Writes]]
    /\ pen \in [Ledgers -> [holder : Nodes \cup {NoNode}]]
    /\ baton \in Nodes
    /\ laps \in 0..MaxLap

Init ==
    /\ node = [n \in Nodes |-> [state |-> "idle", done |-> 0]]
    /\ pen = [g \in Ledgers |-> [holder |-> NoNode]]

    /\ laps = 0

\* The right to pick up an enrolment pen travels round the ring as a baton.
\* It is only handed on while its holder is not mid-write, so a node cannot
\* lose the baton in the middle of amending a ledger.
Hand(m) ==
    /\ node[baton].state # "writing"
    /\ m # baton
    /\ laps < MaxLap
    /\ baton' = m
    /\ laps' = laps + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<node, pen>>

\* Only the node holding the baton may arm itself to write.
Arm(n) ==
    /\ baton = n
    /\ node[n].state = "idle"
    /\ node[n].done < Writes
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "armed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

\* Picking up a ledger's pen needs the baton and a pen nobody is holding.
\* Nodes here are slow but never fail: an armed node may take a long time to
\* reach for the pen, and the baton stays with it while it does.
PickUp(n, g) ==
    /\ baton = n
    /\ node[n].state = "armed"
    /\ pen[g].holder = NoNode
    /\ pen' = [pen EXCEPT ![g].holder = n]
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "writing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, laps>>

    /\ node[n].done < Writes

    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

Disarm(n) ==
    /\ node[n].state = "armed"
    /\ baton # n
    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pen, baton, laps>>

    /\ pen[g].holder = n

    /\ node' = [node EXCEPT ![n].state = "idle"]

    /\ \A n \in Nodes : node[n].state = "idle"

    \/ \E n \in Nodes, g \in Ledgers : PickUp(n, g) \/ PutDown(n, g)
    \/ Closed

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* are never writing the same enrolment ledger at once however slowly the
\* baton goes round.
PenExclusion ==
    \A n \in Nodes :
        (node[n].state = "writing") =>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network issues temporary guest passes -- for a plumber, a sitter, a cleaner -- and the household has set a hard limit on how many passes may be live at once. Going past that limit is exactly the failure the household bought the system to avoid, so the number of live passes must never exceed it however many hubs are working at the same time.

The count of live passes is kept optimistically rather than under a lock, because it is read far more often than written. A hub reads how many passes are live together with the revision stamped on that count, and then goes away to check the request against the household's rules, which takes a while.

Granting a pass lands only while the revision the hub read is still the one on the count and there is still room under the limit; landing bumps the revision. A request whose read has gone stale, whose hub has dropped off the mesh, that arrives with the household already at its limit, or that arrives after the count has been stamped for the last time in the window, is refused outright rather than retried indefinitely.

A live pass is handed back when the guest leaves, which frees a slot and bumps the count's revision as well. Hubs on a home mesh are not reliable: one hub may drop off without saying so, after which it grants nothing further and any request it was checking is refused; the remaining hubs carry on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a guest pass is live, the household is holding no more live passes than its limit allows, however many hubs raced each other to grant one.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every guest pass request is eventually answered, either granted or refused.

CONSTANTS Passes, Hubs, Cap, MaxRev, NoHub

ASSUME NoHub \notin Hubs

VARIABLES pass, live, rev, dark

vars == <<pass, live, rev, dark>>

Typing ==
    /\ pass \in [Passes -> [state : {"asked", "reading", "granted", "refused",
                                     "expired"},
                            base : 0..MaxRev, hub : Hubs \cup {NoHub}]]
    /\ live \subseteq Passes
    /\ rev \in 0..MaxRev
    /\ dark \subseteq Hubs

Init ==
    /\ pass = [p \in Passes |-> [state |-> "asked", base |-> 0, hub |-> NoHub]]
    /\ live = {}
    /\ rev = 0
    /\ dark = {}

\* A hub reads how many guest passes are live and the revision stamped on that
\* count, then goes away to check the request against the household's rules.
Read(p, h) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "asked"
    /\ h \notin dark
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p] = [state |-> "reading", base |-> rev, hub |-> h]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<live, rev, dark>>

\* Granting a pass only lands while the revision the hub read is still the one
\* on the count, and only while there is room under the household's limit.
Grant(p) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "reading"
    /\ pass[p].hub \notin dark
    /\ pass[p].base = rev
    /\ Cardinality(live) < Cap
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ live' = live \cup {p}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "granted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED dark

\* A request whose read has gone stale, whose hub has dropped off, or that
\* arrives with the household already at its limit, is refused outright.
Refuse(p) ==
    /\ pass[p].state = "reading"
    /\ \/ pass[p].base # rev
       \/ pass[p].hub \in dark
       \/ Cardinality(live) = Cap
       \/ rev = MaxRev
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "refused"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<live, rev, dark>>

\* A live pass is handed back when the guest leaves, freeing a slot.
Expire(p) ==
    /\ p \in live
    /\ rev < MaxRev
    /\ live' = live \ {p}
    /\ rev' = rev + 1
    /\ pass' = [pass EXCEPT ![p].state = "expired"]
    /\ UNCHANGED dark

\* One hub may drop off the home mesh without saying so.
GoDark(h) ==
    /\ dark = {}
    /\ Cardinality(Hubs) > 1
    /\ dark' = {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pass, live, rev>>

Quiet ==
    /\ \A p \in Passes : pass[p].state \in {"granted", "refused", "expired"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Passes, h \in Hubs : Read(p, h)
    \/ \E p \in Passes : Grant(p) \/ Refuse(p) \/ Expire(p)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : GoDark(h)
    \/ Quiet

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes, h \in Hubs : Read(p, h))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes : Grant(p))
    /\ WF_vars(\E p \in Passes : Refuse(p))

\* Whenever a guest pass is live, the household is holding no more live passes
\* than its limit allows, however many hubs raced each other to grant one.
PassCapacityRespected ==
    \A p \in Passes :
        (pass[p].state = "granted") => (Cardinality(live) <= Cap)

EveryRequestEventuallyAnswered ==

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A regional grid's load shedder pushes protection setpoints -- an under-frequency threshold, an overload trip level -- out to its substations. A setpoint that has been applied is written into that station's journal, and the protection relays read their behaviour back from that journal, so a setpoint that quietly vanished from a journal would be an update lost where it matters most.

The shedding scheme is re-run through the watch, and each re-run carries a strictly newer epoch number. A setpoint is drafted against the scheme epoch standing at the time, and is applied at a substation only under that same epoch. A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that nobody has pushed through, is dropped rather than applied, and can be redrafted against the current scheme later.

There is a privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding and there is no time to redraft. The override still writes the setpoint into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many overrides in a shift.

Re-running the scheme carries the station journals across untouched: a new scheme changes what will be applied next, never what the relays are already holding. Station journals are separately tidied of setpoints that were drafted at them but never applied.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every applied setpoint stands in exactly one station journal, so no setpoint the relays are already holding is carried away by a re-scheme, an override, or a tidy-up.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Setpoints, Stations, MaxEpoch, ForceCap

VARIABLES entry, journal, epoch, forced

vars == <<entry, journal, epoch, forced>>

Typing ==
    /\ entry \in [Setpoints -> [state : {"draft", "applied", "dropped"},
                                ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ journal \in [Stations -> SUBSET Setpoints]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ forced \in 0..ForceCap

Init ==
    /\ entry = [p \in Setpoints |-> [state |-> "draft", ep |-> 0]]
    /\ journal = [s \in Stations |-> {}]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ forced = 0

\* A setpoint is applied at a substation only under the scheme epoch it was
\* drafted against; applying writes it into that station's journal, which is
\* what the protection relays read back.
Apply(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep = epoch
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, forced>>

\* The privileged override: the control engineer may push a setpoint drafted
\* under an older scheme through anyway when the grid is close to shedding.
\* It still goes into exactly one station journal, and there are only so many
\* overrides in a shift.
Force(p, s) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ forced < ForceCap
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] = journal[s] \cup {p}]
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "applied"]
    /\ forced' = forced + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A setpoint drafted under a scheme that has since been superseded, and that
\* nobody has forced through, is dropped rather than applied.
Drop(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "draft"
    /\ entry[p].ep # epoch
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p].state = "dropped"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

Redraft(p) ==
    /\ entry[p].state = "dropped"
    /\ entry' = [entry EXCEPT ![p] = [state |-> "draft", ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, epoch, forced>>

\* Re-running the shedding scheme under a strictly newer epoch.  Journals are
\* carried across untouched -- a new scheme changes what will be applied next,
\* never what the relays are already holding.
Rescheme ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, journal, forced>>

\* Station journals are tidied of setpoints that never got applied.
Tidy(s) ==
    /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![s] =
                     {p \in journal[s] : entry[p].state = "applied"}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<entry, epoch, forced>>

Steady ==
    /\ \A p \in Setpoints : entry[p].state = "applied"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints, s \in Stations : Apply(p, s) \/ Force(p, s)
    \/ \E p \in Setpoints : Drop(p) \/ Redraft(p)
    \/ \E s \in Stations : Tidy(s)
    \/ Rescheme
    \/ Steady

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every applied setpoint stands in exactly one station journal, so no setpoint
\* the relays are already holding is carried away by a re-scheme, an override
\* or a tidy-up.
NoLostSetpoint ==
    \A p \in Setpoints :
        (entry[p].state = "applied") =>
            (Cardinality({s \in Stations : p \in journal[s]}) = 1)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A wildfire surveillance swarm runs its airframes through a small set of transit corridors over the burn. A corridor is a critical resource: only one airframe may be flying a corridor at a time, because the corridors are narrow lanes between the drop runs and two aircraft in one lane is a collision.

The swarm elects a lead airframe, and the lead is the only aircraft that hands out corridor clearances. Election is by epoch: an airframe becomes lead by taking an epoch strictly newer than any epoch yet taken, so a lead that is lost or superseded is replaced without any hand-back.

The lead clears an orbiting airframe into a corridor that nobody is flying. A cleared airframe then enters the corridor, provided it is still free when it gets there, flies its run and exits, leaving the corridor free for the next.

There is a privileged override: incident command can seize a corridor for a manned helicopter. Seizing turns any airframe that was cleared for that corridor but has not yet entered it back to orbit, so it will need clearing again. Command never seizes a corridor out from under an airframe already in transit, and there are only so many seizures in a sortie.

SAFETY PROPERTY: An airframe in transit is flying exactly one corridor, so two airframes are never in the same corridor at once, across a change of lead or a seizure by incident command.

    /\ corridor \in [Corridors -> [holder : Ships \cup {NoShip}]]
    /\ lead \in [ep : 0..MaxEpoch, ship : Ships \cup {NoShip}]
    /\ seizures \in 0..OverrideCap

    /\ ship = [s \in Ships |-> [state |-> "orbit", want |-> NoCorridor]]
    /\ corridor = [c \in Corridors |-> [holder |-> NoShip]]

\* lead is the only aircraft that hands out corridor clearances.
Elect(s, e) ==

    /\ lead' = [ep |-> e, ship |-> s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ship, corridor, seizures>>

\* corridor that nobody is flying.
Clear(s, c) ==

    /\ corridor[c].holder = NoShip

    /\ ship' = [ship EXCEPT ![s].state = "transit"]

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router works its belts off a routing plan that carries a revision number. Operators at the sorting consoles work reroutes up against the plan -- a gate swap when an aircraft changes stand, a chute swap when a chute jams -- and push them onto the belts.

The plan is not held under a lock. A console reads the plan's revision and works its reroute up against that revision. Operators here are slow but never fail: working a reroute up can take a long time, and the plan may move on underneath the console while it does.

A reroute goes live only if two things still hold: the revision it was drafted against is still the plan's standing revision, and the console that worked it up is itself still reading that revision. A console that has fallen behind the plan is a stale participant, and a reroute from a stale console is refused rather than pushed onto the belts -- pushing it would route bags on a picture of the pier that the router has already left behind. A refused reroute is voided and can be redrafted later.

Consoles catch up with the plan on their own schedule, each at its own pace. A reroute that goes live bumps the plan's revision and records which console pushed it. The pier settles once every reroute is live, or once the plan has been stamped for the last time in the bank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every live reroute was pushed onto the belts exactly once, by a console that was up to date with the routing plan at the moment it went live, so nothing on the belts came from an operator the plan had already left behind.

CONSTANTS Reroutes, Consoles, MaxRev, NoConsole

ASSUME NoConsole \notin Consoles

VARIABLES order, plan, console, applied

vars == <<order, plan, console, applied>>

Typing ==
    /\ order \in [Reroutes -> [state : {"drafted", "checking", "live", "void"},
                               base : 0..MaxRev, by : Consoles \cup {NoConsole}]]
    /\ plan \in [rev : 0..MaxRev, by : Consoles \cup {NoConsole}]
    /\ console \in [Consoles -> 0..MaxRev]
    /\ applied \subseteq [rte : Reroutes, rev : 1..MaxRev]

Init ==
    /\ order = [r \in Reroutes |-> [state |-> "drafted", base |-> 0,
                                    by |-> NoConsole]]
    /\ plan = [rev |-> 0, by |-> NoConsole]
    /\ console = [c \in Consoles |-> 0]
    /\ applied = {}

\* A console reads the routing plan's revision and works a reroute up against
\* it.  Operators here are slow but never fail: that can take a long time, and
\* the plan may move on underneath them while it does.
Draft(r, c) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "drafted"
    /\ console' = [console EXCEPT ![c] = plan.rev]
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r] = [state |-> "checking", base |-> plan.rev,
                                      by |-> c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, applied>>

\* the revision it drafted against, and that revision is still the plan's.  A
\* console that has fallen behind is a stale participant and its reroute is
\* refused rather than pushed onto the belts.
GoLive(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "checking"
    /\ order[r].base = plan.rev
    /\ console[order[r].by] = plan.rev
    /\ plan.rev < MaxRev
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {[rte |-> r, rev |-> plan.rev + 1]}
    /\ plan' = [rev |-> plan.rev + 1, by |-> order[r].by]
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r].state = "live"]
    /\ UNCHANGED console

Void(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "checking"
    /\ \/ order[r].base # plan.rev
       \/ console[order[r].by] # plan.rev
       \/ plan.rev = MaxRev
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r].state = "void"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, console, applied>>

Redraft(r) ==
    /\ order[r].state = "void"
    /\ order' = [order EXCEPT ![r] = [state |-> "drafted", base |-> 0,
                                      by |-> NoConsole]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, console, applied>>

\* A console catches up with the plan on its own schedule.
Refresh(c) ==
    /\ console[c] # plan.rev
    /\ console' = [console EXCEPT ![c] = plan.rev]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<order, plan, applied>>

\* The pier settles once every reroute is live, or once the plan has been

Quiet ==
    /\ \/ plan.rev = MaxRev

    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E r \in Reroutes : GoLive(r) \/ Void(r) \/ Redraft(r)
    \/ \E c \in Consoles : Refresh(c)
    \/ Quiet

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* was up to date with the routing plan at the moment it went live: nothing on
\* the belts came from an operator the plan had already left behind.
NoStaleReroute ==

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A skyscraper's two lift banks are managed as independent instances -- a low-rise controller and a high-rise controller -- but they share one pool of maintenance panels. Maintenance work has to be booked into an out-of-service window, and a window can only carry one job: two jobs booked into the same window would put two crews in the same shaft.

A controller raises a job against a window that no panel has started marking yet, and puts it to the panels. Each panel keeps its own booking sheet and writes at most one job into each window on it; once a panel has filled a line for a window it never rewrites that line, whichever controller asks. No panel can see any other panel's sheet.

A job holds its window only once a strict majority of the panels have written it into that window on their own sheets. Because any two majorities of the panels share at least one panel, and no panel ever writes two jobs into one window, two jobs can never both collect a majority for the same window -- and that holds across the two controllers just as it does within one.

Each bank also rotates which panel it treats as its point of contact through the week; that changes who it talks to first and nothing about the sheets. A job that holds its window is worked and finished. A job that loses the race for its window -- because another job took a majority for it first -- gives that window up and goes back to be raised against a window nobody has started marking; the number of such retries a job has made is tracked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A job that holds an out-of-service window holds a majority of the panels' sheets for that window, so the same window is never allocated to two jobs, whichever bank raised them.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job put to the panels is eventually worked and finished.
