===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An elevator bank in a skyscraper runs its cars as a versioned dispatch group. The group carries an epoch number, and each car carries a badge stamped with the epoch it last registered under. A car whose badge does not match the live epoch is stale: the dispatcher will not give it a hall call. Building security also holds a fire-service key that can override the group for one car at a time.

A hall call may be pressed for any floor that is not already waiting. The dispatcher may send an idle car to a waiting floor only if that car's badge matches the live epoch and the car is not under the fire key; the call is then taken off the waiting set. A car that is running arrives, becomes idle, and takes no further part until dispatched again. A car that is idle and carries a stale badge may re-register, taking the live epoch onto its badge. A regrouping bumps the epoch, restamps every car except the one being dropped from the group, parks the dropped car in the same step, and puts the dropped car's call back on the waiting set if it had one; a car currently under the fire key is never the one dropped. Security may seize any car with the fire key when the key is free, may send a keyed car to any waiting floor regardless of the car's badge, and may yield the key once the keyed car is idle. Cars are slow but never broken: an idle car that could take a waiting call will take one, a running car always arrives, and a stale idle car always re-registers eventually.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any car that is running a call either carries a badge matching the live epoch or is the car currently held under the fire-service key.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every hall call that is pressed is eventually cleared from the waiting set.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, MaxEpoch, NoCall, NoCar

VARIABLES epoch, badge, running, calls, keyed

vars == <<epoch, badge, running, calls, keyed>>

\* The dispatch group is versioned: every regrouping bumps the epoch and
\* restamps the cars that stay in the group. A car carrying an old badge is
\* stale and the dispatcher must ignore it until it re-registers.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ badge \in [Cars -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ running \in [Cars -> Floors \cup {NoCall}]
  /\ calls \subseteq Floors
  /\ keyed \in Cars \cup {NoCar}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ badge = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ running = [c \in Cars |-> NoCall]
  /\ calls = {}
  /\ keyed = NoCar

Press(f) ==
  /\ f \notin calls
  /\ calls' = calls \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, running, keyed>>

Dispatch(c, f) ==
  /\ badge[c] = epoch
  /\ keyed # c
  /\ running[c] = NoCall
  /\ f \in calls
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = f]
  /\ calls' = calls \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, keyed>>

Arrive(c) ==
  /\ running[c] # NoCall
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = NoCall]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, calls, keyed>>

Register(c) ==
  /\ badge[c] # epoch
  /\ running[c] = NoCall
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, running, calls, keyed>>

\* Regrouping parks the car being dropped in the same step it bumps the
\* epoch, so no car is ever left mid-run holding a badge nobody honours.
Regroup(drop) ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ keyed # drop
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ badge' = [c \in Cars |-> IF c = drop THEN badge[c] ELSE epoch + 1]
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![drop] = NoCall]
  /\ calls' = IF running[drop] # NoCall
                THEN calls \cup {running[drop]}
                ELSE calls
  /\ UNCHANGED keyed

\* Fire service: the building key overrides the group entirely.
Seize(c) ==
  /\ keyed = NoCar
  /\ keyed' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, running, calls>>

KeyRun(c, f) ==
  /\ keyed = c
  /\ running[c] = NoCall
  /\ f \in calls
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![c] = f]
  /\ calls' = calls \ {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, keyed>>

Yield ==
  /\ keyed # NoCar
  /\ running[keyed] = NoCall
  /\ keyed' = NoCar
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, badge, running, calls>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Floors : Press(f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : Dispatch(c, f)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Arrive(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Register(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Regroup(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars : Seize(c)
  \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : KeyRun(c, f)
  \/ Yield

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A c \in Cars : \A f \in Floors : SF_vars(Dispatch(c, f))
  /\ \A c \in Cars : WF_vars(Arrive(c))
  /\ \A c \in Cars : SF_vars(Register(c))

\* Intent: a moving car is either badged for the live epoch or is under the
\* fire key. Nothing else gets to answer a call.
NoStaleCarAnswers ==
  \A c \in Cars :
    running[c] # NoCall => (badge[c] = epoch \/ keyed = c)

EveryCallCleared == \A f \in Floors : (f \in calls) ~> (f \notin calls)

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An interbank settlement batch is driven by a small set of coordinator nodes, exactly one of which is the acting chief for the current term. The member banks each open the batch with the same endowment, and value moves between them as settlement notes that ride a fixed set of addressed wires. The wires are addressed slots rather than a queue, so notes can be settled in any order the chief pleases, and a note sitting on a wire is money that has left one bank and not yet reached another.

Only an acting chief that is up may touch value. It may draw a note: an amount is taken off one bank's balance and placed as a note on a free wire naming a different bank as payee. It may apply any note on any wire, crediting the payee and freeing the wire. It may instead return any note on any wire, crediting the drawer back and freeing the wire; returning is what happens to notes a new chief cannot vouch for, and it is deliberately a credit rather than a discard. Any node that is up may be elected chief for the next term while terms remain. The acting chief may fail, going down and leaving the post empty until someone else is elected. A node that is down may restart and become eligible again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The sum of all bank balances plus the value of every note still riding a wire always equals the total cash the batch opened with.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Banks, Nodes, Wires, Endow, MaxAmt, MaxTerm, NoMsg, NoNode

VARIABLES bal, wire, chief, term, up

vars == <<bal, wire, chief, term, up>>

RECURSIVE Total(_, _)
Total(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Total(f, S \ {x})

Cash == Endow * 2

Note == [frm : Banks, to : Banks, amt : 1..MaxAmt]

Floating == Total([w \in Wires |-> IF wire[w] = NoMsg THEN 0 ELSE wire[w].amt],
                  Wires)

\* Wires are addressed slots, not a queue: the chief may settle them in any
\* order, and a settlement note sitting on a wire still counts as money.

TypeOK ==
  /\ bal \in [Banks -> 0..Cash]
  /\ wire \in [Wires -> Note \cup {NoMsg}]
  /\ chief \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ up \in [Nodes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ bal = [b \in Banks |-> Endow]
  /\ wire = [w \in Wires |-> NoMsg]
  /\ chief = NoNode
  /\ term = 0
  /\ up = [n \in Nodes |-> TRUE]

Led == chief # NoNode /\ up[chief]

Draw(b, c, a, w) ==
  /\ Led
  /\ b # c
  /\ wire[w] = NoMsg
  /\ bal[b] >= a
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![b] = @ - a]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![w] = [frm |-> b, to |-> c, amt |-> a]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, term, up>>

Apply(w) ==
  /\ Led
  /\ wire[w] # NoMsg
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![wire[w].to] = @ + wire[w].amt]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![w] = NoMsg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, term, up>>

\* A note the new chief cannot vouch for is returned to the drawer rather
\* than dropped -- dropping it would quietly burn money.
Return(w) ==
  /\ Led
  /\ wire[w] # NoMsg
  /\ bal' = [bal EXCEPT ![wire[w].frm] = @ + wire[w].amt]
  /\ wire' = [wire EXCEPT ![w] = NoMsg]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<chief, term, up>>

Elect(n) ==
  /\ up[n]
  /\ chief # n
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ chief' = n
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, wire, up>>

Fail(n) ==
  /\ chief = n
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ chief' = NoNode
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, wire, term>>

Restart(n) ==
  /\ ~up[n]
  /\ up' = [up EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bal, wire, chief, term>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b, c \in Banks, a \in 1..MaxAmt, w \in Wires : Draw(b, c, a, w)
  \/ \E w \in Wires : Apply(w)
  \/ \E w \in Wires : Return(w)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : Restart(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Intent: failover must not mint or burn value. Whatever the chief does,
\* balances plus notes still riding the wires add up to the opening cash.
CashConserved == Total(bal, Banks) + Floating = Cash

====

A lease ticks down while it is held. A lease whose time to live has reached zero lapses, giving its headroom straight back without a box being placed. A crane holding a live lease may place a box: the bay's stack grows by one, the lease is given up, and one box comes off the vessel. The supervisor may seal a bay against new leases and may unseal it again. The supervisor's override drops a box straight into any bay, sealed or not and with no lease at all, but only while that bay still has headroom counting outstanding leases. Finally, a box may be lifted back off any non-empty bay and returned to the vessel while the vessel has room for it.

Filling a prescription is a two-phase commit across the same set of parties -- the drug vault and the patient chart -- and each fill carries a ballot number. A station in prepare that holds every party, with every party's acknowledgement matching its ballot, may commit: one unit comes off the shared shelf and the station moves to ready. A station in prepare may instead abort, dropping back to idle and releasing every party it holds along with their acknowledgements. A station that is ready hands the prescription over, dropping back to idle and likewise releasing its parties. The shelf may be restocked whenever it is below capacity. Neither station stalls forever: a station in prepare eventually aborts if it does not commit, and a ready station always completes the handover.

  /\ feeding \in [Routers -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]
  /\ belt \subseteq Bags
  /\ sorted \subseteq Bags

Init ==
  /\ owner = NoRouter
  /\ life = 0
  /\ feeding = [r \in Routers |-> NoBag]
  /\ belt = {}
  /\ sorted = {}

Arrive(b) ==
  /\ b \notin belt
  /\ b \notin sorted
  /\ \A r \in Routers : feeding[r] # b
  /\ belt' = belt \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, life, feeding, sorted>>

Grant(r) ==
  /\ owner = NoRouter
  /\ owner' = r
  /\ life' = MaxLife
  /\ UNCHANGED <<feeding, belt, sorted>>

Countdown ==
  /\ life > 0
  /\ life' = life - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, feeding, belt, sorted>>

\* The reclaim waits for the chute to run empty; that wait is exactly what
\* keeps a slow holder from being overlapped by the next lease.
Reclaim ==
  /\ owner # NoRouter
  /\ life = 0
  /\ Quiet
  /\ owner' = NoRouter
  /\ UNCHANGED <<life, feeding, belt, sorted>>

Feed(r, b) ==
  /\ owner = r
  /\ life > 0
  /\ feeding[r] = NoBag
  /\ b \in belt
  /\ feeding' = [feeding EXCEPT ![r] = b]
  /\ belt' = belt \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, life, sorted>>

Clear(r) ==
  /\ feeding[r] # NoBag
  /\ sorted' = sorted \cup {feeding[r]}
  /\ feeding' = [feeding EXCEPT ![r] = NoBag]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, life, belt>>

Offload(b) ==
  /\ b \in sorted
  /\ sorted' = sorted \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, life, feeding, belt>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Arrive(b)
  \/ \E r \in Routers : Grant(r)
  \/ Countdown
  \/ Reclaim
  \/ \E r \in Routers, b \in Bags : Feed(r, b)
  \/ \E r \in Routers : Clear(r)
  \/ \E b \in Bags : Offload(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Intent: nobody but the current leaseholder ever has a bag in the chute,
\* so the chute is worked by one router at a time.
ChuteWorkedByOwner ==
  \A r \in Routers : (owner # r) => feeding[r] = NoBag

A hospital operating-room scheduler runs two booking desks that work independently but draw anaesthesia teams from one shared pool. ===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling block system controls which train may stand in which track block. Every block carries a serial number that is bumped whenever the interlocking for that block is reset. A movement authority quotes the block it covers and the serial it was cut against, so an authority issued before a reset is worthless afterwards. The signaller also has hand signalling, a privileged override that puts a train into a block with no authority at all.

Route requests pile into a bounded request book: a train with no authority and no request already in the book may add one while there is room, and a full book is simply refused, which is how the interlocking pushes back on the timetable. The head request is issued when its train still has no authority and the block it names is clear; the authority is cut against that block's current serial and the request leaves the book. The head request may instead be refused outright and dropped. A train may enter the block its authority names, provided the authority's serial still matches the block's serial, the block is clear, and the train is not already standing somewhere. A train may exit its block, which clears the block and tears up its authority. A block that is clear may have its interlocking reset, bumping its serial. The signaller may flag a block for hand signalling, may unflag it only once it is clear, and may hand-signal any train that is not already standing somewhere into a flagged clear block.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every occupied block either is flagged for hand signalling or holds a train whose authority names that block and quotes the serial the block is currently on.

Route == [tr : Trains, blk : Blocks]

\* authority issued before a reset is worthless afterwards.

Somewhere(t) == \E b \in Blocks : occ[b] = t

  /\ auth \in [Trains -> Ticket \cup {NoAuth}]
  /\ occ \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NoTrain}]

  /\ auth = [t \in Trains |-> NoAuth]
  /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> NoTrain]
  /\ manual = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]

\* Route requests pile into a bounded book; a full book is simply refused,
\* which is how the interlocking pushes back on the timetable.
Request(t, b) ==

  /\ auth[t] = NoAuth
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(queue) : queue[i].tr # t

  /\ occ[auth[t].blk] = NoTrain

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od18m2p6t4`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network pushes deadbolt policy changes out from a hub using a two-phase commit across every lock in the house. Each change is polled under a round number. A lock only counts as a voter if it has caught up to the round the hub is polling; a vote left over from a superseded round is a stale voice and must not be on the board. The mesh radio also has a working width -- the number of locks it can hold in the prepare phase at once -- and that width is retuned while the system is running.

When the hub is idle it opens a round: the round number advances, every vote from the previous round is torn down in the same step, and the hub starts polling. A lock whose last sync does not match the current round, and which is not currently a voter, may sync itself up to the round. While the hub is polling, a lock that is synced to the round and not yet a voter may prepare, provided the number of current voters is below the mesh width. When every lock is a voter, the hub commits: the deadbolt state of every lock flips. The hub may instead abort the poll. After a commit or an abort the hub settles back to idle, tearing down the votes. The mesh width may be retuned to any other permitted value at any time. The hub never hangs: a poll that does not commit is always eventually aborted, and a decided round is always eventually settled.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every lock currently on the vote board has a last sync equal to the round the hub is polling, so no vote cast under a superseded round is ever counted.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every round the hub starts polling eventually settles back to idle.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od18m2p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Locks, MaxRound, MaxWidth

VARIABLES round, seen, vote, decision, bolt, width

vars == <<round, seen, vote, decision, bolt, width>>

\* The hub polls every lock before a policy change lands. A lock's vote only
\* counts if the lock has caught up to the round the hub is polling; the mesh
\* radio can only carry so many locks at once, and that width moves at runtime.

Nxt(r) == IF r = MaxRound THEN 1 ELSE r + 1

Voters == {l \in Locks : vote[l]}

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0..MaxRound
  /\ seen \in [Locks -> 0..MaxRound]
  /\ vote \in [Locks -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ decision \in {"idle", "polling", "commit", "abort"}
  /\ bolt \in [Locks -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ width \in 1..MaxWidth

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ seen = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
  /\ vote = [l \in Locks |-> FALSE]
  /\ decision = "idle"
  /\ bolt = [l \in Locks |-> FALSE]
  /\ width = 1

\* Opening a round tears down every vote from the previous one in the same
\* step; otherwise a vote cast under the old round would still be sitting there.
Open ==
  /\ decision = "idle"
  /\ round' = Nxt(round)
  /\ vote' = [l \in Locks |-> FALSE]
  /\ decision' = "polling"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seen, bolt, width>>

Sync(l) ==
  /\ seen[l] # round
  /\ ~vote[l]
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![l] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, vote, decision, bolt, width>>

Prepare(l) ==
  /\ decision = "polling"
  /\ seen[l] = round
  /\ ~vote[l]
  /\ Cardinality(Voters) < width
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![l] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, seen, decision, bolt, width>>

Commit ==
  /\ decision = "polling"
  /\ \A l \in Locks : vote[l]
  /\ decision' = "commit"
  /\ bolt' = [l \in Locks |-> ~bolt[l]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, seen, vote, width>>

Abort ==
  /\ decision = "polling"
  /\ decision' = "abort"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, seen, vote, bolt, width>>

Settle ==
  /\ decision \in {"commit", "abort"}
  /\ decision' = "idle"
  /\ vote' = [l \in Locks |-> FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, seen, bolt, width>>

Retune ==
  /\ width' \in (1..MaxWidth) \ {width}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, seen, vote, decision, bolt>>

Next ==
  \/ Open
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Sync(l)
  \/ \E l \in Locks : Prepare(l)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ Settle
  \/ Retune

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Abort)
  /\ WF_vars(Settle)

\* Intent: a vote on the board was cast by a lock that had caught up to the
\* round being polled. A vote left over from a superseded round would show
\* up here as a voter whose last sync predates the current round.
NoStaleVoteCounted ==
  \A l \in Locks : vote[l] => seen[l] = round

RoundsAlwaysSettle == (decision = "polling") ~> (decision = "idle")

====

  MaxRound = 2
  MaxWidth = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoStaleVoteCounted

PROPERTY RoundsAlwaysSettle

A blood-bank inventory tracker is run by two independent allocation services -- one for the wards, one for the theatres -- that keep separate ledgers over one shared fridge of blood units. Which service may write up a given unit is fixed by an ownership map, and that map is only ever redrawn under a fresh epoch number. Each service carries the epoch its view was drawn from.

A unit may be redrawn to a different service only while no service has that unit written up in its ledger; redrawing advances the epoch until the epoch ceiling is reached, after which the map may still be redrawn but the epoch stands still. A service whose view epoch does not match the live epoch may refresh it. A clinical order that is not already waiting and is not already written up anywhere may be placed onto the waiting list, and a waiting order may be cancelled. A service whose view matches the live epoch may assign a unit it owns, which is not already written up in its own ledger, against a waiting order that is not written up anywhere; the order then leaves the waiting list. A written-up unit may be transfused, which clears that entry from the service's ledger.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For any unit that both services have written up, the two ledgers name the same order, so the same bag of blood is never promised to two different orders.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Services, Units, Orders, MaxEpoch, NoService, NoOrder

VARIABLES epoch, owner, ledger, view, waiting

vars == <<epoch, owner, ledger, view, waiting>>

\* Two allocation services keep their own ledgers over one shared fridge of
\* units. Which service may write a unit is decided by an ownership map that
\* is only ever redrawn under a fresh epoch, and only for an idle unit.

Booked(u) == \E a \in Services : ledger[a][u] # NoOrder

Taken(o) == \E a \in Services : \E u \in Units : ledger[a][u] = o

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ owner \in [Units -> Services \cup {NoService}]
  /\ ledger \in [Services -> [Units -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]]
  /\ view \in [Services -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ owner = [u \in Units |-> NoService]
  /\ ledger = [a \in Services |-> [u \in Units |-> NoOrder]]
  /\ view = [a \in Services |-> 0]
  /\ waiting = {}

\* Redrawing ownership is the only way a unit changes hands, and a unit that
\* is written up in anyone's ledger is off limits to the redraw.
Redraw(u, s) ==
  /\ ~Booked(u)
  /\ owner[u] # s
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![u] = s]
  /\ epoch' = IF epoch = MaxEpoch THEN epoch ELSE epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, view, waiting>>

Refresh(a) ==
  /\ view[a] # epoch
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![a] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, ledger, waiting>>

Order(o) ==
  /\ o \notin waiting
  /\ ~Taken(o)
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, ledger, view>>

Cancel(o) ==
  /\ o \in waiting
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, ledger, view>>

Assign(a, u, o) ==
  /\ view[a] = epoch
  /\ owner[u] = a
  /\ ledger[a][u] = NoOrder
  /\ o \in waiting
  /\ ~Taken(o)
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![a][u] = o]
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, view>>

Transfuse(a, u) ==
  /\ ledger[a][u] # NoOrder
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![a][u] = NoOrder]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, view, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E u \in Units, s \in Services : Redraw(u, s)
  \/ \E a \in Services : Refresh(a)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Order(o)
  \/ \E o \in Orders : Cancel(o)
  \/ \E a \in Services, u \in Units, o \in Orders : Assign(a, u, o)
  \/ \E a \in Services, u \in Units : Transfuse(a, u)

An operator may prepare a machine it holds whose escrow is empty, moving an amount out of that machine's till into that machine's escrow, provided the till holds that much. An operator in the prepare phase may instead abort, which puts each held machine's escrow back into that same machine's till. After committing or aborting the operator closes the round, going idle and releasing every machine it held. Mine(r) == {m \in Machines : claim[m] = r}

\* Two route operators run their own collection rounds against one shared
\* coin vault. A round is two-phase: coin moved into escrow has left the till
\* but not yet reached the vault, and it is counted the whole time.

  /\ escrow \in [Machines -> 0..Purse]
  /\ vault \in 0..Purse

  /\ escrow = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ vault = Purse
  /\ phase = [r \in Routes |-> "idle"]
  /\ claim = [m \in Machines |-> NoRoute]

  /\ phase[r] = "idle"
  /\ Mine(r) = {}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![r] = "prep"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, escrow, vault, claim>>

  /\ claim[m] = NoRoute
  /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![m] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<till, escrow, vault, phase>>

Prepare(r, m, n) ==

  /\ claim[m] = r
  /\ escrow[m] = 0
  /\ till[m] >= n

  /\ escrow' = [escrow EXCEPT ![m] = n]

  /\ Mine(r) # {}

  /\ vault' = vault + Pot([m \in Machines |->

  /\ escrow' = [m \in Machines |-> IF claim[m] = r THEN 0 ELSE escrow[m]]

  \/ \E r \in Routes : Abort(r)
  \/ \E r \in Routes : Close(r)

An airport baggage router assigns bags to aircraft load cans. Each bag has a routing card carrying a version number, and routers work optimistically: a router reads a bag's card, and later writes only if that card's version has not moved underneath it. The duty manager also has a privileged override.

A router with no card in hand may read the card of any bag that is not yet on any load bill. A router holding a card may load its bag onto any flight, but only if the bag's live version still equals the version on the card it is holding; loading writes the bag onto that flight's bill, bumps the bag's version, and hands the card back. A router holding a card whose version no longer matches the live version must retry, throwing the card away so it can read again. A bag that is not yet on a bill may be retagged, which bumps its version and invalidates any card read against it. A drive-through car-wash site runs two conveyor lines, line A and line B, side by side. Both lines pull vehicles out of the same shared arrival pool, so a chassis waiting in the pool can be picked up by either line. After the seal has been applied the chassis is discharged from the line and its ticket is torn up; a discharged chassis never re-enters the arrival pool.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and a central interlocking hands out timed occupancy leases for those blocks to trains. Time is kept by a shared wall clock that ticks forward. When the interlocking leases a block to a train it stamps the lease with the current clock reading as the start and a fixed lease duration as the expiry, files the lease as a numbered row in its allocation ledger, and radios a grant to the train. The interlocking will only issue a fresh lease for a block if that block has no lease on file or the lease on file has already expired according to the clock.

Radio traffic between the interlocking and the trains is not ordered: grants and hand-backs sit in a common in-flight pool and can be picked up in any order, so an old message can surface long after the lease it refers to is history. Every message carries the ledger row number of the lease it belongs to. A train that picks up a grant moves into the block only if that row number is still the block's current lease and the clock has not passed the expiry; it remembers the row number it entered under. When a train leaves a block it radios a hand-back quoting that remembered row number. The interlocking honours a hand-back only when the quoted row number is still the block's current lease; it then closes out that ledger row by writing the current clock reading as the row's real end and marks the block free. Any message whose row number is no longer the block's current lease is thrown away by whoever picks it up.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A multiplayer game matchmaker seats waiting parties into lobbies. Several matchmaker agents run at once, and to keep them from tangling they always take locks in the same order: first the coarse lock on the whole lobby region, then the fine lock on the one lobby they intend to seat into. An agent starts idle, then names the lobby it wants and joins the queue for the region lock. Once it holds the region lock it waits for that lobby's own lock; because only the region-lock holder ever reaches for a lobby lock, the agents cannot end up waiting on each other in a cycle.

Holding the lobby lock, the agent reads the lobby's current seat count and remembers it. If the remembered count is below the lobby's seat limit, the agent seats its party by writing back the remembered count plus one; the read and the write-back are only safe because the lobby lock is held throughout. If the remembered count is already at the limit the agent bounces the party instead. Either way it then drops both locks in one go and returns to idle.

Any agent can die silently at any moment, without dropping whatever locks it holds. The region watchdog notices the missing heartbeat and reclaims every lock that the dead agent was holding, after which the agent is retired for good and never acts again.

The full action set is: an idle agent names a target lobby and queues, an agent takes the coarse region lock, an agent takes the fine lock on its target lobby and reads the seat count, an agent seats its party by writing back the incremented count, an agent bounces because its target is full, an agent drops both locks and goes idle, an agent dies silently, and the watchdog reclaims a dead agent's locks and retires it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No lobby's seat count ever rises above its seat limit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the coarse region lock is held it is eventually free again.

  /\ aim = [a \in Agents |-> NoAim]
  /\ roster = [l \in Lobbies |-> 0]

NameTarget(a, l) ==

  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]

TakeRegion(a) ==
  /\ step[a] = "queued"
  /\ region = FREE
  /\ region' = a
  /\ step' = [step EXCEPT ![a] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyLock, aim, roster>>

\* Coarse before fine: only the region holder ever reaches for a lobby lock,
\* so the two lock levels can never be grabbed in opposite orders.
TakeLobby(a) ==

AnySeat == \E a \in Agents : Seat(a)
AnyBounce == \E a \in Agents : Bounce(a)
AnyDrop == \E a \in Agents : DropLocks(a)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
The wash bays along a car-wash conveyor all feed off one high-pressure water main, and the main can supply exactly one bay at a time without losing pressure. Access is arbitrated by a token that travels round the bays in a fixed ring order. The token carries a serial number. When a bay receives the token it writes the token's serial onto its own badge; a bay may open its valve onto the main only while it is the bay the token sits at and its badge still matches the serial of the token in circulation.

Passing the token means handing it to the next bay round the ring that is still running: dead bays are skipped over, and the first running bay clockwise from the current holder takes it. A bay must have closed its valve before it can pass the token on.

A bay can lose power without warning. When that happens it stops running, and its valve interlock slams the valve shut on the way down, so a dead bay is never left drawing from the main. But the token it was holding goes down with it. The ring supervisor watches for this: when the bay the token sits at is no longer running, the supervisor mints a replacement token with the next serial number up and places it at some running bay, which badges itself with the new serial. The old serial is thereby fenced off, so nothing that still believed in the old token could act on it.

The full action set is: pass the token clockwise to the next running bay, open a valve onto the main, close a valve, lose power silently with the valve interlock tripping shut, and mint a replacement token at a running bay when the current holder is dead.

  /\ running \in [Bays -> BOOLEAN]

A swarm of surveillance drones circles a wildfire and works from a shared hotspot table held at the incident base. Each hotspot row carries a revision number. A drone that wants to work a hotspot reads the row and copies the revision number into its onboard plan; nothing is locked at that moment, the plan is simply a bet that the row will not have moved on by the time the drone is overhead. Every drone launches with a fixed number of sorties in it, and taking a plan burns one, so no drone can keep cycling through plans forever.

The irreversible act is the retardant release: once a hotspot has been doused the canister is gone and the ground chemistry cannot be undone, and each release is written into the mission log. A drone releases only if the revision it copied still matches the row's revision and the row is not flagged for a ground crew. A successful release marks the row spent and steps the revision number up, which is exactly what fences off any other drone still flying on the old revision. A drone whose bet has gone stale, or whose target got flagged for a ground crew, tears up its plan and goes back to loitering.

The incident commander has an override that does not play by the optimistic rules. The commander can recall a hotspot, stepping its revision number up by hand purely to invalidate every plan in the air against it; can flag a hotspot for a ground crew so no drone will douse it; and can clear that flag again later. Drones only pick up plans against hotspots that are unspent and unflagged.

The full action set is: a loitering drone with sorties left reads a hotspot row and takes a plan, a drone releases retardant when its revision still matches and the row is unflagged, a drone tears up a stale or flagged plan, the commander recalls a hotspot by stepping its revision, the commander flags a hotspot for a ground crew, and the commander clears that flag.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every plan a drone takes is eventually resolved, either by releasing retardant or by being torn up.

A regional blood bank tracks its inventory across several storage sites. Each site keeps one reserved slot in its cold room that a cross-site order can claim. An order that needs blood from every site is settled by a two-phase commit run by the dispatch desk.

The desk opens an order by sending a prepare notice to all sites; the notices travel over a slow internal courier network, so a site may sit for a long while before its notice reaches it. When a prepare notice finally lands, the site looks at its reserved slot. If the slot is unclaimed the site claims it for that order and answers yes; if the slot is already claimed by some other order the site answers no.

The desk commits an order only when every site has answered yes, and on commit it writes that order's name into the allocation register of every site. If any site answers no, the desk aborts the order and tells the sites to drop the claims that this order and only this order was holding; claims belonging to other orders are left alone. A committed order keeps its claims permanently, because the blood has left the cold room.

The full action set is: the desk opens an order and sends prepare notices, a prepare notice is delivered to a site after an arbitrary delay, a site claims its free slot and votes yes, a site votes no because its slot is already claimed, the desk commits an order whose sites all voted yes and writes the allocation register, and the desk aborts an order that got a no and releases only that order's claims.

  /\ ballot \in [Orders -> [Sites -> {"silent", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ claim \in [Sites -> Orders \cup {FreeSlot}]
  /\ landed \in [Orders -> SUBSET Sites]
  /\ register \in [Sites -> Orders \cup {"empty"}]

  /\ ballot = [o \in Orders |-> [s \in Sites |-> "silent"]]
  /\ claim = [s \in Sites |-> FreeSlot]
  /\ landed = [o \in Orders |-> {}]

  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![o] = "preparing"]

\* arbitrary delay -- there is no timeout path anywhere in this protocol.
DeliverNotice(o, s) ==

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A car-wash site runs two conveyor lanes that were installed independently but were plumbed into one shared pool of service modules -- the chemical pump and the air blower serve both lanes. A wash cycle on a lane can only run once every module in the pool has committed to that cycle, so each lane's controller runs the cycle as a two-phase commit over the pool.

Opening a cycle draws the next ticket number from the site's single ticket book, and the lane stamps its cycle with that ticket. A module enrols in a lane's cycle by writing down the lane and the ticket it saw; a module will only accept a new enrolment if the enrolment it is currently carrying has gone dead, meaning the lane named on it has moved on to a different ticket or is no longer running that cycle. Enrolments are never actively torn up when a cycle ends, they are simply left to go dead and get overwritten later, so stale slips are a normal sight around the site.

A lane commits its cycle once every module in the pool is carrying a live enrolment for that lane at that lane's current ticket. A lane aborts instead if some module is carrying a live enrolment belonging to the other lane. Once a lane's cycle is committed, a module may begin its dose run, and it may end that dose run afterwards. A decided cycle -- committed or aborted -- is closed out and the lane goes back to idle, but only when no module is still in the middle of a dose run for it.

The full action set is: open a cycle and draw a ticket, enrol a module whose current slip has gone dead, commit a cycle whose whole pool is live-enrolled, abort a cycle blocked by a live enrolment belonging to the other lane, begin a module's dose run, end a module's dose run, and close out a decided cycle when nothing is mid-run.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A module in the middle of a dose run is always carrying an enrolment naming the very lane it is dosing for, stamped with that lane's current ticket, and that lane's cycle is committed -- so no stale or unenrolled module ever gets to act.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every cycle that reaches the prepare stage eventually reaches a decision, either committed or aborted.

DeadSlip == [lane |-> "none", tkt |-> 0]

VARIABLES cycle, stamp, slip, dosing, book
vars == <<cycle, stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

\* A slip is live only while the lane it names is still on that same ticket.
LiveSlip(m) ==
  /\ slip[m].lane \in Lanes
  /\ slip[m].tkt = stamp[slip[m].lane]
  /\ cycle[slip[m].lane] \in {"preparing", "committed"}

Init ==
  /\ cycle = [l \in Lanes |-> "idle"]
  /\ stamp = [l \in Lanes |-> 0]
  /\ slip = [m \in Modules |-> DeadSlip]
  /\ dosing = [m \in Modules |-> "none"]
  /\ book = 1

OpenCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "idle"
  /\ book <= MaxTicket
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "preparing"]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![l] = book]
  /\ book' = book + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slip, dosing>>

\* Enrolment overwrites whatever dead slip the module was carrying.
Enrol(m, l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ ~LiveSlip(m)
  /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![m] = [lane |-> l, tkt |-> stamp[l]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, dosing, book>>

CommitCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ \A m \in Modules : LiveSlip(m) /\ slip[m].lane = l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "committed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

AbortCycle(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] = "preparing"
  /\ \E m \in Modules : LiveSlip(m) /\ slip[m].lane # l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "aborted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

BeginDose(m) ==
  /\ dosing[m] = "none"
  /\ LiveSlip(m)
  /\ cycle[slip[m].lane] = "committed"
  /\ dosing' = [dosing EXCEPT ![m] = slip[m].lane]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, slip, book>>

EndDose(m) ==
  /\ dosing[m] \in Lanes
  /\ dosing' = [dosing EXCEPT ![m] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cycle, stamp, slip, book>>

CloseOut(l) ==
  /\ cycle[l] \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ \A m \in Modules : dosing[m] # l
  /\ cycle' = [cycle EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, slip, dosing, book>>

DecideStep ==
  \/ \E m \in Modules, l \in Lanes : Enrol(m, l)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : CommitCycle(l)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : AbortCycle(l)

Next ==
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : OpenCycle(l)
  \/ DecideStep
  \/ \E m \in Modules : BeginDose(m)
  \/ \E m \in Modules : EndDose(m)
  \/ \E l \in Lanes : CloseOut(l)

  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(DecideStep)

\* Nobody doses on a dead slip or on somebody else's cycle.
NoStaleDoser ==
  \A m \in Modules :
    dosing[m] \in Lanes =>
      /\ slip[m].lane = dosing[m]
      /\ slip[m].tkt = stamp[dosing[m]]
      /\ cycle[dosing[m]] = "committed"

EveryCycleDecided ==
  \A l \in Lanes :
    (cycle[l] = "preparing") ~> (cycle[l] \in {"committed", "aborted"})

Name the module `W4Od16m0p0t1`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital pharmacy has one controlled-substance counting tray, and only one technician may be at that tray at any moment. There is no real lock on the tray; instead the tray controller keeps a single record holding the tray's current occupant (or the word free) and a stamp number that goes up by one every time the record changes. Technicians work optimistically against that record.

A technician who wants the tray reads the record, remembers the stamp it saw, and posts a claim carrying that stamp. All traffic between technicians and the controller sits in one message pool and is picked up in arbitrary order, so a claim, a grant, a refusal or a hand-back can be processed long after it was posted and well out of the order it was posted in.

When the controller picks up a claim it does a compare-and-set: only if the record currently reads free and its stamp is exactly the stamp on the claim does it write the claimant into the record, bump the stamp, and post a grant carrying the new stamp. Otherwise it posts a refusal. A technician steps up to the tray when it picks up a grant whose stamp is exactly one past the stamp it remembered; on picking up a refusal it goes back to reading the record and tries again. A technician waiting on an answer may also lose patience and go back to reading, leaving its old claim floating in the pool.

When a technician steps away from the tray it posts a hand-back carrying the stamp it entered under. The controller frees the record and bumps the stamp only if the record still names that technician at that same stamp. Any grant or hand-back that no longer applies is simply thrown away by whoever picks it up.

The full action set is: read the record and post a claim, compare-and-set a claim into a grant, refuse a claim that fails the compare-and-set, step up to the tray on a matching grant, go back and retry on a refusal, lose patience while waiting, step away and post a hand-back, apply a hand-back that still matches the record, and discard a message that no longer applies.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Two technicians are never at the counting tray at the same time.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m0p0t1 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, MaxStamp

FreeRec == [holder |-> "free", stamp |-> 0]

VARIABLES record, mode, seen, pool
vars == <<record, mode, seen, pool>>

Modes == {"away", "waiting", "attray"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ record \in [holder : Techs \cup {"free"}, stamp : 0 .. MaxStamp]
  /\ mode \in [Techs -> Modes]
  /\ seen \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxStamp]
  /\ pool \subseteq [kind : {"claim", "grant", "refuse", "handback"},
                     who : Techs, stamp : 0 .. MaxStamp]

Init ==
  /\ record = FreeRec
  /\ mode = [t \in Techs |-> "away"]
  /\ seen = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ pool = {}

ReadAndClaim(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "away"
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![t] = record.stamp]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "waiting"]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {[kind |-> "claim", who |-> t, stamp |-> record.stamp]}
  /\ UNCHANGED record

\* The compare-and-set: the record must still read free at exactly the stamp
\* the claimant copied, otherwise the claim lost its race and is refused.
GrantClaim(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "claim"
  /\ record.holder = "free"
  /\ record.stamp = m.stamp
  /\ record.stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ record' = [holder |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]
  /\ pool' = (pool \ {m})
       \cup {[kind |-> "grant", who |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, seen>>

RefuseClaim(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "claim"
  /\ \/ record.holder # "free"
     \/ record.stamp # m.stamp
  /\ pool' = (pool \ {m})
       \cup {[kind |-> "refuse", who |-> m.who, stamp |-> m.stamp]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mode, seen>>

StepUp(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "grant"
  /\ mode[m.who] = "waiting"
  /\ m.stamp = seen[m.who] + 1
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m.who] = "attray"]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

RetryAfterRefusal(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "refuse"
  /\ mode[m.who] = "waiting"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m.who] = "away"]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

LosePatience(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "waiting"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "away"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen, pool>>

StepAway(t) ==
  /\ mode[t] = "attray"
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![t] = "away"]
  /\ pool' = pool \cup
       {[kind |-> "handback", who |-> t, stamp |-> seen[t] + 1]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, seen>>

\* A hand-back only counts if the record still names that tech at that stamp.
ApplyHandback(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "handback"
  /\ record.holder = m.who
  /\ record.stamp = m.stamp
  /\ record.stamp < MaxStamp
  /\ record' = [holder |-> "free", stamp |-> m.stamp + 1]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, seen>>

DiscardDead(m) ==
  /\ m.kind \in {"grant", "handback"}
  /\ \/ m.kind = "grant" /\ (mode[m.who] # "waiting" \/ m.stamp # seen[m.who] + 1)
     \/ m.kind = "handback" /\ (record.holder # m.who \/ record.stamp # m.stamp)
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, mode, seen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs : ReadAndClaim(t) \/ LosePatience(t) \/ StepAway(t)
  \/ \E m \in pool :
       \/ GrantClaim(m) \/ RefuseClaim(m) \/ StepUp(m)
       \/ RetryAfterRefusal(m) \/ ApplyHandback(m) \/ DiscardDead(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOneAtTray ==
  \A t1, t2 \in Techs : (mode[t1] = "attray" /\ mode[t2] = "attray") => t1 = t2
================================================================================

Before the bell, an exchange runs an opening auction in which a panel of designated market makers files indications of interest with the auction desk. The panel is not fixed: the exchange re-seats it during the session, and the number of indication slots the desk will accept for a session also changes when it re-seats. Every re-seating is stamped with a new epoch number, and the desk keeps the seated panel and the slot count for each epoch on file.

When the desk re-seats the panel it moves to the next epoch, files the new panel roster and the new slot count under that epoch, and goes into a settling state. In the settling state each newly seated market maker picks up its new badge, which is simply the epoch number it now believes it is trading under. Once every seated market maker is badged for the current epoch, the desk declares the auction open again.

A market maker may file an indication only while the desk is open, only if it is on the roster for the current epoch, and only if its own badge already reads the current epoch; a maker still carrying an old badge is stale and cannot file. Each accepted indication is filed stamped with the epoch it was accepted under. The desk refuses a filing if the number of indications already on the book for the current epoch has reached that epoch's slot count -- and because that count can be lowered at a re-seating, a book that was legal under the old configuration may leave no room at all under the new one. A market maker may also pull one of its own indications back off the book.

The full action set is: re-seat the panel with a new roster and a new slot count, badge a seated market maker for the current epoch, declare the auction open once everyone seated is badged, file an indication from a badged and seated maker while a slot is free, and pull an indication back off the book.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every indication sitting on the book was filed by a market maker who was on the roster for the very epoch that indication is stamped with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the desk goes into settling after a re-seating, it eventually declares the auction open again.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Makers, MaxEpoch, MaxSlots, StartSlots

Epochs == 0 .. MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, roster, slots, badge, book, desk
vars == <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, book, desk>>

OnBook(e) == {q \in book : q.ep = e}

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ roster \in [Epochs -> SUBSET Makers]
  /\ slots \in [Epochs -> 1 .. MaxSlots]
  /\ badge \in [Makers -> Epochs]
  /\ desk \in {"open", "settling"}

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ roster = [e \in Epochs |-> IF e = 0 THEN Makers ELSE {}]
  /\ slots = [e \in Epochs |-> StartSlots]
  /\ badge = [m \in Makers |-> 0]
  /\ book = {}
  /\ desk = "open"

\* Re-seating files a fresh roster and a fresh slot count under a new epoch;
\* the slot count may well come down, squeezing a book that was legal before.
ReSeat(p, c) ==
  /\ desk = "open"
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ p # {}
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = p]
  /\ slots' = [slots EXCEPT ![epoch + 1] = c]
  /\ desk' = "settling"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, book>>

PickUpBadge(m) ==
  /\ desk = "settling"
  /\ m \in roster[epoch]
  /\ badge[m] # epoch
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![m] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, book, desk>>

DeclareOpen ==
  /\ desk = "settling"
  /\ \A m \in roster[epoch] : badge[m] = epoch
  /\ desk' = "open"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, book>>

FileIndication(m) ==
  /\ desk = "open"
  /\ m \in roster[epoch]
  /\ badge[m] = epoch
  /\ Cardinality(OnBook(epoch)) < slots[epoch]
  /\ [who |-> m, ep |-> epoch] \notin book
  /\ book' = book \cup {[who |-> m, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, desk>>

PullIndication(q) ==
  /\ q \in book
  /\ book' = book \ {q}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, slots, badge, desk>>

Settle ==
  \/ \E m \in Makers : PickUpBadge(m)
  \/ DeclareOpen

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in SUBSET Makers, c \in 1 .. MaxSlots : ReSeat(p, c)
  \/ Settle
  \/ \E m \in Makers : FileIndication(m)
  \/ \E q \in book : PullIndication(q)

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Settle)

\* Each filing traces back to the roster of the epoch it was stamped with.
OnlySeatedMakersOnBook ==

If any no vote is on the wire the depot aborts, clears that run's votes off the wire, and puts an undo decision to each machine. A machine acts on a decision only while it still has room booked for that run: on do-it it moves the batch onto the shelf and gives back the booking, on undo it just gives back the booking. Either way that run's slot at that machine is marked settled, so a decision that turns up again later finds nothing booked and is thrown away.

A house is wired with a small cluster of smart-home hubs that jointly control the door locks. Throwing a bolt open is not something any single hub may do: an unlock has to be backed by a majority of the hubs. The reason the hubs care is electrical, not social. Each lock's latch solenoid draws current the whole time the door stands open, the garage lock draws twice what the interior locks draw, and the low-voltage supply feeding the latches has a fixed current budget. Doors that are open together share that budget.

A door that wants to open is put up for backing, and the house never has more than a couple of unlock requests up for backing at any one time. A hub backs at most one door at a time, and its backing stays attached to that door until the request is settled; that is what keeps two doors from being cleared at the same moment, since their backer sets would have to overlap. Once a door has a majority of backers, the cluster checks whether the latch current already being drawn by the doors standing open, plus this door's own draw, would stay inside the budget. If it fits, the door is cleared; if it does not, the request is refused and the backings are handed back. A cleared door is then thrown open, at which point its backings are handed back too, and an open door is shut again later.

One hub at a time can drift behind the rest of the cluster. A hub that has drifted is not dead and is never written off: it simply cannot cast a backing until it catches up, and it always does catch up eventually.

The full action set is: put a shut door up for backing, let one hub drift behind, have the drifted hub catch up, have a hub back a door that is up for backing, clear a door that has a majority and fits in the current budget, refuse a door that has a majority but does not fit, throw a cleared door open, and shut an open door again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total latch current drawn by all the doors standing open never exceeds the low-voltage supply's budget.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every door put up for backing is eventually settled, one way or the other.

A car-wash conveyor line keeps one shared tally board recording which wash tickets have had their undercarriage flush logged. Only the bay controller currently acting as line master is allowed to write to that board, and which controller holds that role is decided by failover: at any point the site can anoint a different bay as master under a higher term number. The bay being replaced is not told anything, so it may well still have work in the air.

To log a ticket, the master reads the tally board, takes the board's revision number and its set of logged tickets, and posts a write carrying that revision as its base, the read set plus the new ticket, and the term the master was serving under. Posted writes and the receipts that come back sit on a shared wire and are picked up in any order at all, so a write from a superseded master can turn up long after a newer write has already landed.

The board takes a write only when two things hold: the base revision on the write is still the board's current revision, meaning nothing has moved underneath the reader, and the write's term is not older than the term of the write the board last took. When it takes a write the board bumps its revision, replaces its logged set with the one carried on the write, and puts a receipt on the wire. A write failing either test is bounced off the wire and has no effect. When the site picks up a receipt it confirms that ticket to the crew, and the crew treats a confirmed ticket as done with.

The full action set is: fail over to a different bay under a higher term, the master posts a write built from a fresh read of the board, the board lands a write whose base revision and term both still check out, the board bounces a write that fails either check, and the site picks up a receipt and confirms the ticket to the crew.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every wash ticket the site has already confirmed to the crew is still present in the tally board's logged set, so no confirmed update is ever written away.

CONSTANTS Bays, Tickets, MaxWrites, MaxTerms

VARIABLES board, wire, confirmed, term, master
vars == <<board, wire, confirmed, term, master>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ board \in [rev : 0 .. MaxWrites, logged : SUBSET Tickets, term : 0 .. MaxTerms]
  /\ confirmed \subseteq Tickets
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerms
  /\ master \in Bays

Init ==
  /\ board = [rev |-> 0, logged |-> {}, term |-> 0]
  /\ wire = {}
  /\ confirmed = {}
  /\ term = 0
  /\ master = CHOOSE b \in Bays : TRUE

\* Failover simply anoints a new master at a higher term; the old master is not
\* told, and whatever it already put on the wire is still coming.
Failover(b) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerms
  /\ b # master
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ master' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, wire, confirmed>>

\* The master reads the tally board and posts a whole new logged set built from
\* what it just read, tagged with the revision that reading came from.
PostWrite(b, t) ==
  /\ master = b
  /\ t \notin board.logged
  /\ t \notin confirmed
  /\ ~ \E m \in wire : m.kind = "write" /\ m.tkt = t /\ m.term = term
  /\ wire' = wire \cup {[kind |-> "write", tkt |-> t, base |-> board.rev,
                         logged |-> board.logged \cup {t}, term |-> term]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, confirmed, term, master>>

\* The board takes a write only if nothing has changed under it since the read
\* and the writer is not from a superseded term.
LandWrite(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "write"
  /\ m.base = board.rev
  /\ m.term >= board.term
  /\ board.rev < MaxWrites
  /\ board' = [rev |-> board.rev + 1, logged |-> m.logged, term |-> m.term]
  /\ wire' = (wire \ {m}) \cup {[kind |-> "done", tkt |-> m.tkt]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<confirmed, term, master>>

BounceWrite(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "write"
  /\ \/ m.base # board.rev
     \/ m.term < board.term
  /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, confirmed, term, master>>

TakeReceipt(m) ==
  /\ m.kind = "done"
  /\ confirmed' = confirmed \cup {m.tkt}
  /\ wire' = wire \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, term, master>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Bays : Failover(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bays, t \in Tickets : PostWrite(b, t)
  \/ \E m \in wire : LandWrite(m) \/ BounceWrite(m) \/ TakeReceipt(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing the site has already confirmed to the crew may fall off the board.
NoLostUpdate == confirmed \subseteq board.logged
================================================================================

A surveillance drone swarm works a wildfire perimeter divided into sectors. Ground crews want defensive backburns lit in some sectors, and lighting a backburn is a one-way door: once a sector's backburn is alight the fuel there is gone and the sector can never be lit again.

The base grants a drone a timed lease over a sector. The lease is stamped with an expiry read off the incident clock, and the base only grants a lease it can be sure will run out before the incident clock reaches the end of the operational window. A lease is live while it names a drone and the clock has not yet reached its expiry; once the clock passes the expiry the lease is simply dead, no message required. The base will only grant a lease over a sector that is still unlit and has no live lease on it.

A drone holding a live lease over an unlit sector may light the backburn there. Lighting it marks the sector alight and gives the lease straight back, so the sector ends up alight with nothing leased on it. A drone that decides not to light may also hand the lease back early. The incident clock ticks forward through the operational window.

Drones can fail silently: one may simply go dark mid-flight, without handing anything back and without telling anyone. A dark drone never acts again, so a sector it was holding stays leased to a ghost until the clock walks past the lease expiry, at which point the lease is dead and the base is free to grant the sector to somebody else.

The full action set is: tick the incident clock, grant a lease over an unlit sector with no live lease, light the backburn under a live lease and hand the lease back, hand a live lease back without lighting anything, and go dark.

A print shop spools its jobs on a shared board, one entry per job. Presses help themselves to work off that board, and nothing on the board is ever locked. A press with nothing on its rollers reads an entry and copies down the entry's stamp number, which is simply the shop's way of noticing that an entry has moved on since somebody last looked at it.

To actually take the job, the press does a single combined step: it checks that the entry's stamp is still the one it copied and that the entry is still unassigned, and if both hold it writes itself into the entry as the assigned press, bumps the stamp, and puts the job on its own rollers. Doing the spool side and the press side together in one step is the only reason the two views of who is running what can be trusted to agree. If the stamp has moved or somebody else got there first, the press throws away what it copied and can start over from a fresh read.

A press that finishes a run clears the entry back to unassigned and comes off the job. A press can also lose power without warning, mid-run, telling nobody: its rollers stop, so it is no longer running anything, but the spool board still shows the job assigned to it. The shop's spool keeper reclaims a job whose assigned press has lost power, clearing the entry back to unassigned so another press can read it. The spool keeper only ever reclaims from a press that has actually lost power; it never pulls a job out from under a press that is still turning.

A house runs a small cluster of smart-home hubs over its door locks. At any moment one hub is the chair of the cluster, serving under a term number, and only the chair may order a lock rekeyed. When the cluster fails over it moves to a higher term and a different hub takes the chair.

Rekeying a lock is a one-way step. It blows a physical fuse inside the lock, wiping the old pairing material for good; the fuse can only ever be blown once, and the lock stamps the term of the chair that blew it into the fuse record. The blow and the announcement to the hubs happen in the same breath: the lock cannot be rekeyed without word of that exact rekey going out, and word cannot go out ahead of the blow. Sending word first and blowing afterwards is precisely the ordering that would let a failover slip a second, differently stamped rekey in between.

Announcements sit on the house bus until a hub picks one up. A hub that picks up word of a rekey it has no record of writes down the term carried in that word. A hub that missed the word altogether can instead read the blown fuse straight off the lock and write down what it finds there. Once a hub has a record for a lock it keeps it.

Hubs can also fail silently: a hub simply stops responding, without saying so and without giving up the chair if it had it. A dead hub never picks up word, never polls a lock, and never takes the chair again, and if it was the chair the cluster has to fail over to a live hub before any more rekeying can happen.

The full action set is: fail over to a live hub under a higher term, blow a lock's fuse and announce that rekey in one step, pick word up off the bus and record it, poll a lock directly and record its blown fuse, and fail silently.

\* A machine reserves its slot for whichever desk asks first; a desk that finds
\* a slot already taken by the other desk is out of luck for that order.
Reserve(m, d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ slot[m][o] = "free"
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![m][o] = d]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, settled, chute>>

\* The vend is the irreversible bit: the can drops and the card is captured.
\* Unanimous reservations are not enough on their own -- the order must also
\* not already be on the settled list, because slots are freed after a vend.
Vend(d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ \A m \in Machines : slot[m][o] = d
  /\ o \notin settled
  /\ chute' = chute \cup {[ord |-> o, desk |-> d]}
  /\ settled' = settled \cup {o}
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d][o] = "closed"]
  /\ slot' = [m \in Machines |-> [slot[m] EXCEPT ![o] = "free"]]

WalkAway(d, o) ==
  /\ stage[d][o] = "asking"
  /\ \/ \E m \in Machines : slot[m][o] \notin {"free", d}
     \/ o \in settled
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![d][o] = "closed"]
  /\ slot' = [m \in Machines |-> [slot[m] EXCEPT ![o] =
                 IF slot[m][o] = d THEN "free" ELSE slot[m][o]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<settled, chute>>

ClearSlot(m, o) ==
  /\ slot[m][o] \in Desks
  /\ stage[slot[m][o]][o] = "closed"
  /\ slot' = [slot EXCEPT ![m][o] = "free"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, settled, chute>>

Turn ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines, d \in Desks, o \in Orders : Reserve(m, d, o)
  \/ \E d \in Desks, o \in Orders : Vend(d, o) \/ WalkAway(d, o)

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Desks, o \in Orders : OpenSettlement(d, o)
  \/ Turn
  \/ \E m \in Machines, o \in Orders : ClearSlot(m, o)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Turn)

\* One drop per order, no matter which desk got there.
NothingVendedTwice ==
  \A v1, v2 \in chute : v1.ord = v2.ord => v1 = v2

EverySettlementCloses ==
  \A d \in Desks :
    \A o \in Orders :
      (stage[d][o] = "asking") ~> (stage[d][o] = "closed")
================================================================================

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A blood bank tracks its fridge inventory through a small board of registrars, and no unit leaves the fridge on one person's say-so: issuing a unit needs a majority of the registrars to have signed for it. The board works in numbered rounds, and the bank opens a new round whenever it needs to.

A registrar pledges itself to the round that is currently open, and once pledged it will not sign anything for an older round. But pledging does not retract anything: every slip that registrar already signed in earlier rounds is still lying on the bench. A pledged registrar signs a slip for a unit that is still in the fridge; the slip carries the registrar's name, the round it was signed in, and the unit it is for.

Slips are picked up off the bench in no particular order at all, and a slip signed two rounds ago looks exactly like one signed a minute ago. That is why the round written on a slip has to be read every single time slips are counted: a unit is only issued when a majority of the registrars have slips for that unit signed in the round that is currently open. Issuing takes the unit out of the fridge and writes the issue into the record with the round it went out under. A unit that was issued and not used can be put back into the fridge, and it can then be signed for and issued again in some later round.

The full action set is: open a new round, pledge a registrar to the open round, have a pledged registrar sign a slip for a unit in the fridge, issue a unit that has a majority of slips signed in the open round, and return an issued unit to the fridge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every issue in the record is backed by a majority of slips signed for that very unit in that very round, so slips from a stale round or for another unit can never authorise a release.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Registrars, Units, MaxRound

VARIABLES round, pledge, slips, issued, fridge
vars == <<round, pledge, slips, issued, fridge>>

SlipsFor(b, u) == {s \in slips : s.rnd = b /\ s.unit = u}
Quorum(b, u) == 2 * Cardinality(SlipsFor(b, u)) > Cardinality(Registrars)

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 0 .. MaxRound
  /\ pledge \in [Registrars -> 0 .. MaxRound]
  /\ slips \subseteq [reg : Registrars, rnd : 1 .. MaxRound, unit : Units]
  /\ issued \subseteq [rnd : 1 .. MaxRound, unit : Units]
  /\ fridge \subseteq Units

Init ==
  /\ round = 0
  /\ pledge = [r \in Registrars |-> 0]
  /\ slips = {}
  /\ issued = {}
  /\ fridge = Units

OpenRound ==
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pledge, slips, issued, fridge>>

\* A registrar that pledges to the open round will not sign for an older one,
\* but the slips it already signed are still lying around on the bench.
Pledge(r) ==
  /\ pledge[r] < round
  /\ pledge' = [pledge EXCEPT ![r] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, slips, issued, fridge>>

SignSlip(r, u) ==
  /\ pledge[r] = round
  /\ round > 0
  /\ u \in fridge
  /\ slips' = slips \cup {[reg |-> r, rnd |-> round, unit |-> u]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, issued, fridge>>

\* Slips are picked up off the bench in no particular order and old slips look
\* just like new ones, so the round on the slip has to be read every time.
IssueUnit(u) ==
  /\ round > 0
  /\ u \in fridge
  /\ Quorum(round, u)
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {[rnd |-> round, unit |-> u]}
  /\ fridge' = fridge \ {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, slips>>

ReturnUnit(u) ==
  /\ u \notin fridge
  /\ fridge' = fridge \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pledge, slips, issued>>

Next ==
  \/ OpenRound
  \/ \E r \in Registrars : Pledge(r)
  \/ \E r \in Registrars, u \in Units : SignSlip(r, u)
  \/ \E u \in Units : IssueUnit(u) \/ ReturnUnit(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every issue on the record is backed by a majority of slips signed in that
\* very round for that very unit -- slips from other rounds do not count.
NoIssueWithoutFreshQuorum ==

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A vending operator lets field technicians service its kiosks, and who is servicing which kiosk is settled by a single compare-and-swap tag on each kiosk. The tag holds the name of the technician currently on the box, or nothing if the box is free, along with a generation number that goes up by one every time the box is taken.

A technician reads a box's tag and remembers what it said. To actually take the box the technician swaps the tag: this only goes through if the tag still reads exactly what was read, namely free and at the same generation. If the tag has moved on, or somebody else got there first, or the dispatcher's service window has no room, the technician simply tears up the read and can go and read again.

The dispatcher sets how many boxes may be under service at once, and changes that number while the day runs; narrowing it can leave a read with nowhere to go, and it gets torn up like any other failed swap.

A technician on a box queues up a price sheet stamped with the generation the tag showed when it was queued. Sheets travel over the fleet network and can turn up at the box long after their author has handed the tag back and somebody else has taken the box. That is why the box only writes a sheet into its journal if the sheet's generation beats the generation of the last sheet it wrote; a sheet that does not beat it is binned. A technician hands a box back by clearing its name off the tag, leaving the generation where it is.

The full action set is: read a box's tag, swap the tag to take the box when the read still holds and the window has room, tear up a read that can no longer be swapped, queue a price sheet stamped with the current generation, land a sheet whose generation beats the box's last, bin a sheet that does not, hand a box back, and resize the service window.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Each kiosk's journal records price sheets in strictly rising generation order, so a sheet written under a superseded tag never lands on top of a newer one.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every kiosk that is taken under service is eventually handed back.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p6t4 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Boxes, Techs, MaxGen, MaxWindow, MaxFlight

NoRead == [box |-> "none", gen |-> 0]

VARIABLES tag, readout, journal, outbox, window
vars == <<tag, readout, journal, outbox, window>>

InService == {b \in Boxes : tag[b].who # "none"}
LastGen(b) == IF journal[b] = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE journal[b][Len(journal[b])].gen

TypeOK ==
  /\ tag \in [Boxes -> [who : Techs \cup {"none"}, gen : 0 .. MaxGen]]
  /\ readout \in [Techs -> [box : Boxes \cup {"none"}, gen : 0 .. MaxGen]]
  /\ window \in 0 .. MaxWindow

\* Held down so the model stays small: only a couple of price sheets are ever
\* in flight across the fleet at once.
BoundedFlight == Cardinality(outbox) <= MaxFlight

Init ==
  /\ tag = [b \in Boxes |-> [who |-> "none", gen |-> 0]]
  /\ readout = [t \in Techs |-> NoRead]
  /\ journal = [b \in Boxes |-> <<>>]
  /\ outbox = {}
  /\ window = MaxWindow

ReadTag(t, b) ==
  /\ readout[t].box = "none"
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = [box |-> b, gen |-> tag[b].gen]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, journal, outbox, window>>

\* The swap only goes through if the tag still reads exactly what the tech saw:
\* free, and at the same generation. Anything else and the read is torn up.
Swap(t) ==
  /\ readout[t].box \in Boxes
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].who = "none"
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].gen = readout[t].gen
  /\ tag[readout[t].box].gen < MaxGen
  /\ Cardinality(InService) < window
  /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![readout[t].box] =
        [who |-> t, gen |-> readout[t].gen + 1]]
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, outbox, window>>

TearUpRead(t) ==
  /\ readout[t].box \in Boxes
  /\ \/ tag[readout[t].box].who # "none"
     \/ tag[readout[t].box].gen # readout[t].gen
     \/ Cardinality(InService) >= window
  /\ readout' = [readout EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, journal, outbox, window>>

QueuePush(t, b) ==
  /\ tag[b].who = t
  /\ outbox' = outbox \cup {[box |-> b, gen |-> tag[b].gen, who |-> t]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, window>>

\* A pushed price sheet can turn up at the box long after its author lost the
\* tag, so the box only writes it down if its generation beats the last one in.
LandPush(p) ==
  /\ p.gen > LastGen(p.box)
  /\ journal' = [journal EXCEPT ![p.box] =
        Append(journal[p.box], [gen |-> p.gen, who |-> p.who])]
  /\ outbox' = outbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, window>>

BinPush(p) ==
  /\ p.gen <= LastGen(p.box)
  /\ outbox' = outbox \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, window>>

HandBack(t, b) ==
  /\ tag[b].who = t
  /\ tag' = [tag EXCEPT ![b].who = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<readout, journal, outbox, window>>

\* The dispatcher widens or narrows the service window while the day runs.
Resize(c) ==
  /\ c # window
  /\ window' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tag, readout, journal, outbox>>

AnyHandBack == \E t \in Techs, b \in Boxes : HandBack(t, b)

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs, b \in Boxes : ReadTag(t, b) \/ QueuePush(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Techs : Swap(t) \/ TearUpRead(t)
  \/ \E p \in outbox : LandPush(p) \/ BinPush(p)
  \/ AnyHandBack
  \/ \E c \in 0 .. MaxWindow : Resize(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(AnyHandBack)

\* Price sheets are written into a box's journal in strictly rising generation
\* order, so nothing signed under a superseded tag ever lands on top.
JournalStrictlyRises ==
  \A b \in Boxes :
    \A i \in 1 .. (Len(journal[b]) - 1) :
      journal[b][i].gen < journal[b][i + 1].gen

EveryServiceEnds ==
  \A b \in Boxes : (tag[b].who # "none") ~> (tag[b].who = "none")
================================================================================

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

Name the module `W4Od10m4p5t0`.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks, and each block has a one-shot emergency latch that cuts traction power to it. Firing that latch is irreversible for the shift: resetting it needs a maintenance crew on site with a key, so once a block is latched out it stays latched out.

Trip orders are handled through a work queue with a hard length limit. A controller raises a trip order for a block only when that block has nothing outstanding anywhere -- nothing parked at the desk, nothing sitting in the queue, nothing in a crew's hand -- and only when the block has not already been latched out. A raised order parks at the desk. Orders move from the desk onto the work queue when the queue has room; when the queue is full they simply stay parked, which is the whole of the backpressure story here.

A crew on duty with empty hands takes the order at the front of the queue. Firing the latch and closing out the order happen as one indivisible step: the block latches and the order leaves the crew's hand together. That indivisibility is what stops a crew from dying in between and having the same order handed out to somebody else afterwards.

A crew can go silent at any moment without warning and without saying what it was holding. The desk eventually notices a silent crew still holding an order and puts that order back on the desk to be queued again -- which is safe precisely because a crew that had already fired its latch would not still be holding anything.

The full action set is: raise a trip order for a block with nothing outstanding and no latch fired, admit a parked order onto the queue when there is room, take the front order off the queue, fire the latch and close the order in one step, go silent, and recover an order still held by a silent crew back onto the desk.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A block whose latch has been fired has nothing outstanding anywhere in the system -- not parked, not queued, not in any crew's hand -- so its latch can never be fired a second time.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m4p5t0 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Blocks, Crews, QueueCap

VARIABLES queue, hand, latched, onDuty, parked
vars == <<queue, hand, latched, onDuty, parked>>

Queued(b) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i] = b
InSystem(b) == Queued(b) \/ b \in parked \/ \E c \in Crews : hand[c] = b

TypeOK ==
  /\ hand \in [Crews -> Blocks \cup {"none"}]
  /\ latched \in [Blocks -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ onDuty \in [Crews -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ parked \subseteq Blocks

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ hand = [c \in Crews |-> "none"]
  /\ latched = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]
  /\ onDuty = [c \in Crews |-> TRUE]
  /\ parked = {}

\* A trip order is only raised for a block that has nothing outstanding and has
\* not already been latched out.
RaiseOrder(b) ==
  /\ ~latched[b]
  /\ ~InSystem(b)
  /\ parked' = parked \cup {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, latched, onDuty>>

\* Backpressure: orders sit parked at the desk while the work queue is full.
Admit(b) ==
  /\ b \in parked
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
  /\ parked' = parked \ {b}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hand, latched, onDuty>>

TakeOrder(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] = "none"
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = Head(queue)]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<latched, onDuty, parked>>

\* Firing the latch and closing the order are one indivisible step; that is what
\* stops a crew from dying in between and having the order handed out again.
FireLatch(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] \in Blocks
  /\ ~latched[hand[c]]
  /\ latched' = [latched EXCEPT ![hand[c]] = TRUE]
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, onDuty, parked>>

GoSilent(c) ==
  /\ onDuty[c]
  /\ onDuty' = [onDuty EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, latched, parked>>

Recover(c) ==
  /\ ~onDuty[c]
  /\ hand[c] \in Blocks
  /\ parked' = parked \cup {hand[c]}
  /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, latched, onDuty>>

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Blocks : RaiseOrder(b) \/ Admit(b)
  \/ \E c \in Crews : TakeOrder(c) \/ FireLatch(c) \/ GoSilent(c) \/ Recover(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A latched block has nothing left anywhere in the system -- not parked at the
\* desk, not in the queue, not in anybody's hand -- so it cannot be fired twice.
LatchedBlockHasNothingOutstanding ==
  \A b \in Blocks : latched[b] => ~InSystem(b)
================================================================================

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.
