Holders(s) == {d \in Drones : sector[d] = s}

Init ==
  /\ sector = [d \in Drones |-> NoSector]
  /\ cell = [d \in Drones |-> NoCell]
  /\ flying = {}
  /\ acked = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]
  /\ closed = {}

\* Coarse rung: the sector ration is charged the moment the clearance is issued,
\* not when the drone gets round to using it.
Clear(d, s) ==
  /\ sector[d] = NoSector
  /\ s \notin closed
  /\ Cardinality(Holders(s)) < SectorCap
  /\ sector' = [sector EXCEPT ![d] = s]
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cell, flying, closed>>

\* Slow but not failed: the drone always still has the ability to confirm.
Confirm(d) ==
  /\ sector[d] # NoSector
  /\ ~acked[d]
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, cell, flying, closed>>

\* Fine rung: an orbit cell inside the drone's own cleared sector, taken only
\* after the clearance has been confirmed.
ClaimCell(d, c) ==
  /\ acked[d]
  /\ sector[d] = SectorOf(c)
  /\ cell[d] = NoCell
  /\ \A e \in Drones \ {d} : cell[e] # c
  /\ cell' = [cell EXCEPT ![d] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, flying, acked, closed>>

Launch(d) ==
  /\ cell[d] # NoCell
  /\ d \notin flying
  /\ Cardinality(flying) < AirCap
  /\ flying' = flying \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, cell, acked, closed>>

Land(d) ==
  /\ d \in flying
  /\ flying' = flying \ {d}
  /\ cell' = [cell EXCEPT ![d] = NoCell]
  /\ sector' = [sector EXCEPT ![d] = NoSector]
  /\ acked' = [acked EXCEPT ![d] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED closed

CloseSector(s) ==
  /\ s \notin closed
  /\ Holders(s) = {}
  /\ closed' = closed \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, cell, flying, acked>>

OpenSector(s) ==
  /\ s \in closed
  /\ closed' = closed \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, cell, flying, acked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E d \in Drones : \E s \in Sectors : Clear(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : \E c \in Cells : ClaimCell(d, c)
  \/ \E d \in Drones : Confirm(d) \/ Launch(d) \/ Land(d)
  \/ \E s \in Sectors : CloseSector(s) \/ OpenSector(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bounded capacity at both rungs: per-sector clearance ration and the swarm's
\* overall airborne ceiling.
CapacityRespected ==
  /\ \A s \in Sectors : Cardinality(Holders(s)) =< SectorCap
  /\ Cardinality(flying) =< AirCap
====

A route of networked vending machines shares one settlement line to the payment
processor, and access to that line is granted by a single token passed round the
machines in a fixed ring order. The irreversible step in this system is the
dispense-and-charge: when a machine dispenses an item it draws the customer's
money in the same motion, and that draw can never be undone, so an order must
never be dispensed a second time. Each order is placed against one machine and
sits ready; only the machine currently holding the token may dispense a ready
order it owns, and only while the machine has stock on hand. Dispensing takes the
order off the ready list, decrements stock, and writes the order into the sealed
book, which is the permanent record of orders whose money has been drawn. Orders
can also jam - a ready order may fail, and a failed order can be put back on the
ready list for another try, but the sealed book is consulted first and an order
already in it is never re-offered. The bay capacity is not fixed: a route driver
may reset the machine's bay capacity at any time while on site, and restocking is
allowed only while stock is below the capacity currently in force. The token keeps
moving round the ring regardless of what else is happening. The full action set
is: place an order against a machine, dispense and charge a ready order under the
token, jam a ready order, re-offer a jammed order, pass the token to the next
machine in the ring, restock a unit, and reset the bay capacity.

sitting on the ready list, so the irreversible dispense-and-charge can happen at
most once per order.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The token keeps circulating, so from any point every machine
in the ring eventually holds it again.

  /\ state \in [Orders -> {"new", "ready", "jammed", "drawn"}]
  /\ sealed \in SUBSET Orders
  /\ owner \in [Orders -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]
  /\ stock \in 0 .. MaxCap
  /\ cap \in 1 .. MaxCap

  /\ state = [o \in Orders |-> "new"]
  /\ sealed = {}
  /\ owner = [o \in Orders |-> NoMachine]

\* in the same instant, and only the token holder may do it.
Draw(o) ==

  /\ owner[o] = token
  /\ o \notin sealed
  /\ stock > 0
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![o] = "drawn"]

  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, sealed, owner, stock, cap>>

Restock ==

SetCap(c) ==

  \/ PassToken
  \/ Restock
  \/ \E c \in 1 .. MaxCap : SetCap(c)

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(PassToken)

A hospital pharmacy runs a bank of automated prescription dispensers under a

dispenses it - but only while the stamp still matches the live term. After a
failover the new coordinator's term no longer matches any claim stamped by the
old one, so those stale claims are put back on the queue instead of being acted

paperwork reprint, but it can never be claimed for dispensing again. The
canister's per-shift quota is not fixed: the duty pharmacist resets it while the
bank is running, and a prescription may only be claimed while the number of
entries already in the dispense ledger is below the quota currently in force.

coordinator go down, claim a queued prescription under the live term, dispense a
freshly claimed prescription, put a stale claim back on the queue, re-queue a
ledgered prescription for reprint, and reset the shift quota.

ever carrying a live claim stamp or sitting in the claimed state, so the
irreversible dispense can happen at most once per prescription.

dispensed or put back on the queue - so no claim is left hanging across a
failover.

groups, or running a trip for exactly one of the two groups - never in two of
those situations at once and never in none of them. A group with calls waiting
reserves a car out of the shared pool; it then sends a reserved car off on a
trip, which consumes one call from that group's queue; when the trip finishes the
car returns to the shared idle pool. A group may also give a reserved car back to
the pool without using it, which is how the two groups end up competing for the
same cars. The full action set is: accept a hall call onto a group's queue,
apply backpressure and drop a hall call from a full queue, reserve an idle car
for a group, send a reserved car on a trip, return a finished car to the idle
pool, and yield an unused reserved car back to the pool.

instant - idle pool, reserved by one group, or running a trip for one group - so
no car is ever conjured up or lost as the two groups pass cars through the shared

  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held, riding, dropped>>

\* Backpressure: a full queue turns the call away rather than growing.
Drop(g) ==

  /\ dropped[g] < DropBound

  /\ UNCHANGED <<free, held, riding, queue>>

advances the version. The full action set is: a desk reads a snapshot and picks a
room, a desk commits its booking, a desk retries after a failed attempt, and a
finished case is released from a room.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A stock exchange runs its opening auction against a membership configuration that
is versioned by an epoch number. Each reconfiguration advances the epoch, and
every member firm's trading credential is stamped with the epoch it was issued
for, so a reconfiguration silently turns every outstanding credential stale. A
firm renews its credential for the live epoch only if it was carrying a
credential for the immediately preceding epoch - membership is meant to be
continuous - and each renewal is written into the exchange's admissions book for
that epoch. The exchange's market-operations officer holds a privileged override
and may grant a firm a credential for the live epoch with no continuity
requirement at all, which is how a firm that lapsed gets back in; such a grant is
written into the very same admissions book, so the override is privileged but
never invisible. A firm may put an order in at any time; the auction accepts the
order into that epoch's accepted-orders record only if the firm's credential is
stamped for the live epoch, and turns it away otherwise. The full action set is:
reconfigure into the next epoch, renew a credential under the continuity rule,
grant a credential by market-operations override, put in an order, accept an
order from a currently credentialed firm, and turn away an order from a firm
whose credential has gone stale.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every epoch, the firms recorded as having orders accepted in
that epoch are all listed in that epoch's admissions book, and no epoch beyond the
live one has any accepted orders at all, so no uncredentialed firm and no firm
acting on a stale credential ever gets an order into the auction.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that is put in is eventually resolved, either
accepted into the auction or turned away as stale.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Firms, EpochBound

Epochs == 0 .. EpochBound
NoCred == EpochBound + 1

VARIABLES epoch, cred, admissions, accepted, pending

vars == <<epoch, cred, admissions, accepted, pending>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in Epochs
  /\ cred \in [Firms -> Epochs \cup {NoCred}]
  /\ admissions \in [Epochs -> SUBSET Firms]
  /\ accepted \in [Epochs -> SUBSET Firms]
  /\ pending \in [Firms -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ cred = [f \in Firms |-> 0]
  /\ admissions = [e \in Epochs |-> IF e = 0 THEN Firms ELSE {}]
  /\ accepted = [e \in Epochs |-> {}]
  /\ pending = [f \in Firms |-> FALSE]

\* Reconfiguration advances the epoch and thereby stales every credential.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < EpochBound
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, admissions, accepted, pending>>

\* Ordinary renewal requires unbroken membership across the epoch boundary.
Renew(f) ==
  /\ cred[f] # epoch
  /\ epoch > 0
  /\ cred[f] = epoch - 1
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![f] = epoch]
  /\ admissions' = [admissions EXCEPT ![epoch] = admissions[epoch] \cup {f}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted, pending>>

\* The market-operations override: no continuity needed, but still booked.
OfficerGrant(f) ==
  /\ cred[f] # epoch
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![f] = epoch]
  /\ admissions' = [admissions EXCEPT ![epoch] = admissions[epoch] \cup {f}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, accepted, pending>>

PutIn(f) ==
  /\ ~pending[f]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![f] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cred, admissions, accepted>>

Accept(f) ==
  /\ pending[f]
  /\ cred[f] = epoch
  /\ accepted' = [accepted EXCEPT ![epoch] = accepted[epoch] \cup {f}]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cred, admissions>>

TurnAway(f) ==
  /\ pending[f]
  /\ cred[f] # epoch
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![f] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cred, admissions, accepted>>

Resolve(f) == Accept(f) \/ TurnAway(f)

Next ==

  /\ \A f \in Firms : WF_vars(Resolve(f))

\* Every accepted order in an epoch belongs to a firm booked into that epoch's
\* admissions, and no epoch past the live one has accepted anything.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling system protects each track block with a version counter that
the interlocking keeps: an even version means the block is free, an odd version
means it is held, and the interlocking also records which train holds it. Trains
work optimistically instead of waiting on anything. A train reads a block's
version and posts a claim carrying that version into the signalling network. The
network does not preserve order - claims sit in an unordered pool and the
interlocking may pick up any waiting claim before any other, so a claim posted
earlier can easily be examined after one posted later. The interlocking grants a
claim only if the version it carries still matches the block's live version, that
version is even, and the claiming train is neither already granted a block nor
already inside one; granting advances the block's version to odd and records the
claimant as the holder. Any other claim is denied and the train simply reads
again and posts a new claim, which is the retry. A train with a grant rolls into
the block. Leaving the block advances the version back to even and clears the
recorded holder. The full action set is: read a block's version and post a claim,
grant a matching claim, deny a claim that no longer matches, roll into a granted
block, and leave a block.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A train is inside a track block only when the interlocking's
record names that same train as the holder of that block, and since a block has
exactly one recorded holder, two trains can never be inside the same block at
once.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, VerBound

NoTrain == "notrain"
NoBlock == "noblock"

Claims == [t : Trains, b : Blocks, v : 0 .. (VerBound - 1)]

VARIABLES ver, holder, inBlock, grant, pool

vars == <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant, pool>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [Blocks -> 0 .. (VerBound - 1)]
  /\ holder \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NoTrain}]
  /\ inBlock \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ grant \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ pool \in SUBSET Claims

Init ==
  /\ ver = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ holder = [b \in Blocks |-> NoTrain]
  /\ inBlock = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ grant = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ pool = {}

Idle(t) == grant[t] = NoBlock /\ inBlock[t] = NoBlock

\* Optimistic read: the claim carries the version the train saw, nothing is held.
PostClaim(t, b) ==
  /\ Idle(t)
  /\ \A m \in pool : m.t # t
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {[t |-> t, b |-> b, v |-> ver[b]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant>>

Matches(m) ==
  /\ ver[m.b] = m.v
  /\ ver[m.b] % 2 = 0
  /\ Idle(m.t)

\* The pool is a set, so claims are examined in whatever order the network likes.
GrantClaim(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ Matches(m)
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![m.b] = (ver[m.b] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m.b] = m.t]
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![m.t] = m.b]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED inBlock

DenyClaim(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ ~Matches(m)
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant>>

RollIn(t) ==
  /\ grant[t] # NoBlock
  /\ inBlock[t] = NoBlock
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = grant[t]]
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, pool>>

\* Leaving flips the version back to even, which is what makes any claim taken
\* against the odd version fail on retry.
LeaveBlock(t) ==
  /\ inBlock[t] # NoBlock
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![inBlock[t]] = (ver[inBlock[t]] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![inBlock[t]] = NoTrain]
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, pool>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : \E b \in Blocks : PostClaim(t, b)
  \/ \E m \in Claims : GrantClaim(m) \/ DenyClaim(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : RollIn(t) \/ LeaveBlock(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A train on the track is the recorded holder of the block it is in; since a
\* block records one holder, no two trains share a block.
OccupantIsHolder ==
  \A t \in Trains : inBlock[t] # NoBlock => holder[inBlock[t]] = t
====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A container terminal works its yard with cranes that must climb a two-level lock
ladder before touching a stack. The coarse level is the bay: a crane takes the
bay lock for one bay at a time. The fine level is the individual stack slot
inside that bay, and a crane may only take a slot lock for a slot in the bay it
already holds. A crane is allowed to begin lifting at a slot - the critical
operation, since two machines over one stack would collide - only while it holds
both the slot's lock and the enclosing bay's lock. Completing a lift takes one
container off the slot's pile and stands the crane down from the slot; a crane
may also release its locks and step away entirely. Any crane can fail silently:
it stops dead, with no signal, while still holding whatever locks it had. The
yard watchdog is the only thing that can prise locks out of a dead crane's hands,
and it will only do so for a crane recorded as failed; a failed crane may not be
brought back into service until the watchdog has stripped it of every lock it was
holding. The full action set is: take a bay lock, take a slot lock inside a held
bay, begin a lift holding both locks, complete a lift, release held locks, fail a
crane silently, reclaim a failed crane's locks, and return a stripped crane to
service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A crane is lifting at a slot only while the yard's lock records
name that same crane as the holder of that slot's lock and of the enclosing bay's
lock, and since each lock names a single holder, two cranes can never be lifting
at the same slot.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Locks left in the hands of a crane that has failed are always
eventually reclaimed by the watchdog, so a silent failure never wedges a bay or a
slot forever.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

BayOf(s) == s[1]

NoCrane == "nocrane"
NoSlot == <<"noslot", 0>>

VARIABLES coarse, fine, lifting, pile, failed

vars == <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile, failed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in [Bays -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
  /\ fine \in [Slots -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
  /\ lifting \in [Cranes -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ pile \in [Slots -> 0 .. PileHeight]
  /\ failed \in SUBSET Cranes

Holds(c) == (\E b \in Bays : coarse[b] = c) \/ (\E s \in Slots : fine[s] = c)

Init ==
  /\ coarse = [b \in Bays |-> NoCrane]
  /\ fine = [s \in Slots |-> NoCrane]
  /\ lifting = [c \in Cranes |-> NoSlot]
  /\ pile = [s \in Slots |-> PileHeight]
  /\ failed = {}

\* Coarse rung: one bay per crane.
TakeBay(c, b) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ coarse[b] = NoCrane
  /\ \A y \in Bays : coarse[y] # c
  /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, lifting, pile, failed>>

\* Fine rung: only inside the bay the crane already holds.
TakeSlot(c, s) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ coarse[BayOf(s)] = c
  /\ fine[s] = NoCrane
  /\ \A u \in Slots : fine[u] # c
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, lifting, pile, failed>>

BeginLift(c, s) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ fine[s] = c
  /\ coarse[BayOf(s)] = c
  /\ lifting[c] = NoSlot
  /\ pile[s] > 0
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, pile, failed>>

FinishLift(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ lifting[c] # NoSlot
  /\ pile[lifting[c]] > 0
  /\ pile' = [pile EXCEPT ![lifting[c]] = pile[lifting[c]] - 1]
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, failed>>

Release(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ lifting[c] = NoSlot
  /\ Holds(c)
  /\ coarse' = [b \in Bays |-> IF coarse[b] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE coarse[b]]
  /\ fine' = [s \in Slots |-> IF fine[s] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE fine[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lifting, pile, failed>>

\* Silent failure: the crane stops without letting go of anything.
Fail(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ failed' = failed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile>>

\* Only the watchdog can strip a failed crane, and it strips the lift too.
Reclaim(c) ==
  /\ c \in failed
  /\ Holds(c)
  /\ coarse' = [b \in Bays |-> IF coarse[b] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE coarse[b]]
  /\ fine' = [s \in Slots |-> IF fine[s] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE fine[s]]
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pile, failed>>

Restore(c) ==
  /\ c \in failed
  /\ ~Holds(c)
  /\ failed' = failed \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : \E b \in Bays : TakeBay(c, b)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : \E s \in Slots : TakeSlot(c, s) \/ BeginLift(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : FinishLift(c) \/ Release(c) \/ Fail(c) \/ Reclaim(c) \/ Restore(c)

  /\ \A c \in Cranes : WF_vars(Reclaim(c))

LiftingCraneOwnsBothRungs ==

FailedLocksReclaimed ==
  \A c \in Cranes : (c \in failed /\ Holds(c)) ~> ~Holds(c)

acknowledged the epoch it may not enter any new order, though its existing

pull a resting order at any time, and the auction may execute a resting order,
which takes it out of the book and into the fill tape. The full action set is:
reconfigure into the next epoch with new allowances and trim any over-allowance
firm, acknowledge the current epoch, enter a new order, pull a resting order, and
execute a resting order into the fill tape.

exceeds the book's hard depth, and no firm ever has more orders resting than the

instances - the operator's back office and a contracted field servicer - and both
work over the same shared pool of machines. Each machine carries a service
authorization naming at most one instance at a time, which is what stops the two

snapshot still matches the machine's live version, the instance still holds that

the instance clears down and reads again, which is the retry. An outstanding
change is signed off by the route inspector, which clears the recorded author.

authorization may only be revoked while no change is outstanding on it. The full
action set is: grant a machine's service authorization, revoke a quiet machine's
authorization, read a snapshot and target a machine, commit a change, reject a
failed attempt, clear down after an answer, and sign off an outstanding change.

author exactly the instance that currently holds that machine's service
authorization, so no unauthorized instance and no instance whose authorization has
moved on is ever left standing as the author of a change.

either committed or rejected, so no instance is left waiting on a machine.

A container-ship crane yard keeps a landing apron between the quay cranes and the
stacking blocks, and that apron physically holds only a fixed number of boxes at once.

yard's current shift controller, and the controllers run a leader-election protocol among
themselves: exactly one controller is the acting leader, the leadership is stamped with a
monotone epoch number, and if the acting leader drops off the radio net the remaining
controllers elect a replacement under a fresh epoch. Yard management also keeps a
privileged override: a dispatcher at the terminal operations centre may push a chosen
controller into the leader seat directly, without waiting for the incumbent to fail, and
that override also advances the epoch.

Because authorisations are epoch-stamped, an authorisation issued by a controller that has
since been replaced is void, and the crane holding it must throw it away rather than act
on it. The acting leader hands out an authorisation only when the boxes already sitting on
the apron plus the authorisations that are still live under the current epoch leave room
for one more; when there is no room, the leader turns the request down and the crane must
ask again later. Boxes are eventually hauled off the apron into the stacks, which frees
space back up.

leader stamps that crane with an authorisation carrying the current epoch, but only while

into the stacks), Elect (a controller takes the vacant leader seat under a new epoch),
LeaderFail (the acting leader drops off the net, vacating the seat), and AdminInstall (the
terminal operations dispatcher overrides the election and installs a chosen controller
under a new epoch).

The reefer plugs at a container-ship crane yard are a single shared pool: a fixed number
of powered sockets on the quay, and no more. Two independent yard-planning instances --
one driving the import stacks, one driving the export stacks -- both draw from that same
socket pool, and neither is aware of the other's bookings except through the pool total.
Each instance books sockets for a batch of reefer boxes using a two-phase commit across
its own participants: the yard planner acts as coordinator, opens a round by provisionally
setting aside a batch of sockets, and then collects a vote from each participant (the quay
crane, the stack crane, the reefer technician). Only if every participant votes yes does
the round commit and the set-aside sockets become genuinely energised; a single no vote
aborts the round and hands the set-aside sockets straight back.

The crucial accounting rule is that sockets which are merely set aside for a round that is
still voting are just as unavailable as sockets already energised, and this holds across
both instances at once. A coordinator may therefore only open a new round when the sockets
already energised, plus every socket set aside by either instance's in-flight round, still
leave room for the whole batch. Energised sockets are freed one at a time as reefer boxes
are collected by their consignees.

The full action set is: BeginRound (an instance's coordinator opens a two-phase round and
provisionally sets aside a batch of sockets, only if the shared pool has room for the
batch on top of everything already energised or set aside), VoteYes (a participant of an
in-flight round votes to commit), VoteNo (a participant of an in-flight round votes to
abort), CommitRound (a round whose participants have all voted yes turns its set-aside
sockets into energised sockets), AbortRound (a round with at least one no vote returns its
set-aside sockets to the pool untouched), and FreeSocket (an energised socket is released
when its reefer box is collected).
SAFETY PROPERTY: across both yard-planning instances together, the sockets already energised plus the sockets provisionally set aside by in-flight two-phase rounds never exceed the size of the shared socket pool.

The elevator bank in a skyscraper shares one hoist power feeder, and that feeder can
sustain only a limited number of amp-units of acceleration at any instant. Each car, when
it takes on a run, draws a known number of amp-units for the whole duration of that run,
and heavy cars draw more than light ones. To keep the total draw inside the feeder's
rating, the bank uses a dispatch token that circulates around the cars in a fixed ring:
car 1 hands it to car 2, car 2 to car 3, and the last car hands it back to car 1. Only the
car currently holding the token is allowed to commit itself to a run, and it may do so
only if its own draw fits in whatever headroom the feeder has left after the cars already
running. A car that wants a run but finds no headroom simply keeps the token and waits for
running cars to finish, which is why the token is not passed on while its holder still has
an unstarted run pending.

The building engineer holds a privileged override: with the fire-service key, the token
can be pulled out of the ring and handed straight to a nominated car, skipping the normal
rotation. The override is deliberately restricted to a small number of uses per
service period so that the ordinary rotation is not defeated.

The full action set is: RequestRun (a car registers that it wants a run and fixes the
amp-units it will draw), StartRun (the token holder with a pending request commits to its
run, provided its draw fits in the feeder's remaining headroom), FinishRun (a running car
completes and gives its amp-units back to the feeder), PassToken (a token holder with no
pending request hands the token to the next car in the ring), and AdminHandToken (the
building engineer uses the fire-service key to move the token directly to a nominated car,
consuming one of the limited overrides).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total amp-units drawn by all cars currently running never exceeds the hoist feeder's rating.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every car that registers a request for a run eventually gets that run started.

A warehouse robot fleet picks from bin slots that are grouped into aisles. To stop two
robots from ever being handed the same bin slot, the fleet controller uses a two-level
locking discipline: a robot must first take the coarse lock on a whole aisle, and only
then may it be allocated individual fine-grained slots inside that aisle. An aisle lock is
exclusive, so if the discipline is respected the slots inside an aisle can only ever be
allocated to the robot that currently owns the aisle.

The complication is the radio link. When a robot asks for a slot, the controller's
allocation message goes into the fleet's mesh network, and the mesh delivers messages in
whatever order it likes -- an allocation posted early can arrive after an aisle lock has
already been given up and re-taken by somebody else. The discipline therefore re-checks
the coarse lock at the moment of delivery rather than trusting the message: an allocation
that arrives when the addressee no longer owns the relevant aisle is thrown away instead
of being honoured. A robot is also forbidden from releasing an aisle lock while it still
holds slots inside that aisle, so an aisle can never change hands underneath an
outstanding allocation.

The full action set is: PickTask (an idle robot chooses a bin slot it wants to work on),
TakeAisle (a robot with a chosen slot takes the free coarse lock on that slot's aisle),
PostRequest (a robot that owns the aisle puts an allocation request for its chosen slot
onto the mesh, where it will be delivered in an arbitrary order), DeliverGrant (a mesh
message arrives and, because the addressee still owns the aisle and the slot is
unallocated, the slot is allocated to it), DropStale (a mesh message arrives to a robot
that no longer owns the aisle and is discarded), ReleaseSlot (a robot gives up one of its
allocated slots), and ReleaseAisle (a robot with no remaining slots in an aisle gives up
the coarse lock).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bin slot allocated to a robot lies in an aisle whose coarse lock is currently held by that same robot, so no slot can be allocated to two robots at once.

Slots == Aisles \X (1..NumBays)

Free == "free"

VARIABLES aisleOwner, holdSlot, mesh, task

vars == <<aisleOwner, holdSlot, mesh, task>>

TypeOK ==

  /\ holdSlot \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ mesh \subseteq (Robots \X Slots)
  /\ task \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
  /\ aisleOwner = [a \in Aisles |-> Free]
  /\ holdSlot = [r \in Robots |-> NoSlot]

  /\ task = [r \in Robots |-> NoSlot]

Idle(r) ==
  /\ task[r] = NoSlot
  /\ holdSlot[r] = NoSlot

PickTask(r, s) ==

TakeAisle(r) ==

crew must first take the cabinet lock, which is exclusive. The fine level is the
individual column: only once a crew owns the cabinet may it be assigned columns inside it,

spiral, a product line discontinued, a chiller compartment shut down -- and brought back
into service later, so the set of usable columns in a cabinet changes while crews are
working. The discipline is that a column may only be withdrawn from service when no crew
currently holds an assignment for it, because a withdrawn column must never leave a live

an assignment on any column of that cabinet, so a cabinet cannot change hands underneath

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
The machines in a vending machine network each keep a coin float so they can give change,
and those floats are drawn from one regional cash reserve of fixed size. The depot cannot
put more cash on the street than the reserve holds, counting both the floats already
sitting inside machines and the top-ups it has authorised but not yet handed over to a
driver. Authorisation is governed by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the depot's route
plan carries an epoch number, and every top-up authorisation is stamped with the epoch
current when it was granted. When the route plan is reconfigured the epoch advances, and
any authorisation still stamped with an older epoch stops counting against the reserve and
can no longer be collected.

One machine in the network can go dark without warning: its modem dies, it stops reporting,
and it will never collect the top-up it was promised. The depot cannot tell a silent
machine from a merely slow one, so it does not try. Instead it may time out any
outstanding authorisation, stale or not, writing it off and taking that money straight
back into the reserve. A machine that has gone dark still dispenses product and still pays
out change from the float it already holds; what it can no longer do is talk to the depot,
so it never collects anything more.

The full action set is: RequestTopUp (a machine that is short of change asks the depot for
a float top-up of some amount), Authorise (the depot grants a machine a top-up stamped
with the current epoch, but only if the floats already held plus every authorisation still
valid under the current epoch leave that much of the reserve free), Collect (a machine
that has not gone dark takes up an authorisation still stamped with the current epoch and
adds it to its float), Timeout (the depot writes off an outstanding authorisation and
returns that money to the reserve), SpendFloat (a machine, dark or not, pays out change
and its float falls by one), Reconfigure (the depot revises the route plan and advances
the epoch, invalidating every authorisation stamped with an older epoch), and GoDark (the
one machine that can fail silently loses its modem).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the coin floats held by all machines plus every top-up authorisation still stamped with the current epoch never exceed the regional cash reserve.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every outstanding top-up authorisation is eventually settled, either collected by its machine or timed out by the depot.

A car-wash conveyor line has a ring of numbered line controllers that drive its treatment

round number can lag behind reality. Worse, the bus is a mesh that reorders traffic: a
command a controller puts on the bus can sit there while several handovers go by and only
then reach the bay. So two bad things can reach a bay. One is a command from a controller
that was never entitled in the first place -- a desynchronised unit that wrongly believes
it is the current holder. The other is a command from a controller that genuinely was
entitled, but whose command has aged past the end of its round. The bay's defence is to
check, at the moment the command lands, that the round it is entitled to act in right now

step around the ring and the round number advances).

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A car-wash conveyor line can carry only so many vehicles between the entry gate and the
blower at the far end; past that number the cars touch and the line has to be stopped.
Vehicles are let on by gate attendants, and because the line is long the attendants work
optimistically rather than holding a gate lock. An attendant reads the line console, which
shows a version counter together with how many vehicles are on the line and how many have
been cleared onto the ramp but have not yet rolled on. It writes that pair down and then
walks back to its gate. Any change to the line -- a vehicle being cleared, a vehicle
rolling on, a vehicle leaving under the blower -- bumps the version counter.

An attendant can be slow. It is never removed from its post and it never abandons the
line, but an arbitrary amount of time can pass between reading the console and acting on
what it read, during which the line may have filled up behind its back. That is exactly
what the version counter is for: when the attendant finally tries to clear a vehicle, the
commit only goes through if the version it wrote down is still the live version, which
guarantees the occupancy figure it wrote down is still accurate and there is genuinely
room. If the version has moved, or the snapshot said there was no room, or the console has
run out of version numbers for this shift, the attendant tears up its snapshot and starts
over.

The full action set is: TakeSnapshot (an attendant records the current version together
with the occupancy it saw), CommitClear (an attendant whose snapshot version is still live
and whose snapshot showed headroom clears one vehicle onto the ramp and bumps the
version), Retry (an attendant whose snapshot is stale, showed no headroom, or cannot be
committed because the version counter is exhausted throws the snapshot away), RollOn (a
cleared vehicle actually rolls onto the line and bumps the version), and Exit (a vehicle
leaves the line under the blower and bumps the version).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the vehicles on the conveyor line plus the vehicles cleared onto the ramp but not yet rolled on never exceed the line's carrying capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every snapshot an attendant takes is eventually disposed of, either by committing a clearance or by being torn up and retried.

  /\ onLine \in 0..LineCap

  /\ cleared = 0

A blood-bank inventory tracker guards the issue fridge. Technicians do not lock the
inventory record while they work; they read it optimistically. A technician glances at the

goes off to do something else. Any change to the inventory -- a unit signed out, a unit
returned, a donation added -- advances the version number, so when the technician finally
comes back to sign a unit out, the fridge only lets the sign-out through if the version it
noted is still the live one. That is what proves the reading it is acting on has not gone
stale. Otherwise the technician tears up the note and reads again.

Fridge capacity is not a constant. Shelves are taken out and brought back into use as
chillers are serviced, so the number of units the fridge may hold is reconfigured while
the tracker is running, and reconfiguration is only permitted when nothing is signed out,
so that the count on the floor always reconciles. Reconfiguration is also the moment
credentials are re-issued: a technician's badge records the fridge configuration it was
issued against. A technician who has never been badged is simply unauthorised, and a
technician still carrying a badge from the previous configuration is stale; neither is
permitted to sign a unit out, and both must present themselves for a fresh badge first.

signed-out unit back, which advances the version), AcceptDonation (a new unit is added
while the fridge is under its configured capacity, which advances the version), and
Reconfigure (the fridge's capacity is changed while nothing is signed out, which
invalidates every badge issued against the previous configuration).

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler feeds one imagesetter, and the imagesetter is the critical
resource: it exposes one plate at a time and nothing else may drive it while a plate is on
it. The workstations that submit jobs are arranged in a ring, and a single dispatch token
travels around that ring in fixed order. A workstation may only put a plate on the
imagesetter while the token is sitting with it.

Job submissions do not travel with the token. A workstation announces a job by dropping a
request card into the shop's pigeonhole rack, and the rack is emptied in whatever order
the spooler clerk happens to pick cards out, so a card dropped earlier can easily be
picked up later than one dropped afterwards. The spooler will not start a plate for a
workstation until that workstation's card has actually been picked up, so a workstation
whose card is still sitting in the rack simply keeps hold of the token and waits. That is
also why the token is never handed on while its holder still has an outstanding job: the
turn belongs to that workstation until its plate has been exposed.

The full action set is: SubmitJob (a workstation takes on a job and drops its request card
into the pigeonhole rack), PickUpCard (the clerk picks some card out of the rack, in no
particular order, and registers that job with the spooler), StartPlate (the workstation
that holds the token, and whose card has been picked up, puts its plate on the
imagesetter), FinishPlate (the plate is exposed, the imagesetter is released and the job is
done), and PassToken (a workstation with no outstanding job hands the dispatch token to
the next workstation around the ring).
SAFETY PROPERTY: a workstation has a plate on the imagesetter only while it is the one holding the dispatch token, so two workstations can never be driving the imagesetter at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every workstation that takes on a job eventually gets its plate onto the imagesetter.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

  /\ pending \subseteq Stations
  /\ carded \subseteq Stations
  /\ driving \subseteq Stations
  /\ rack \subseteq Stations

  /\ carded = {}
  /\ driving = {}
  /\ rack = {}

A pharmacy prescription dispenser takes work through a bounded spool. Prescriptions queue
up in the order they are lodged, the spool holds only a set number of them, and when it is
full the counter simply refuses new work -- backpressure, so the robot is never asked to
hold more than it can track. Every queued item is lodged on behalf of a named pharmacist.

Who may lodge work is governed by the formulary revision in force. A pharmacist's
dispensing credential is stamped with the revision it was granted under. When the
formulary is revised, every credential stamped with the old revision becomes stale, and a
pharmacist carrying a stale credential is as barred from lodging or dispensing work as one
who was never credentialed at all; they must be re-credentialed against the new revision
first. Because a revision would strand any work already lodged under the old rules, the
formulary is only revised when the spool has been drained empty. In the same spirit, a
credential is only withdrawn from a pharmacist who has no work sitting in the spool.

The superintendent pharmacist has one privilege the others do not: an emergency lodgement
that goes into a reserved slot beyond the ordinary spool limit, so a genuinely urgent
prescription is not turned away by backpressure. The privilege buys a way past the
backpressure only -- the superintendent still needs a credential stamped with the current
revision like everyone else.

formulary revision now in force), Withdraw (a credential is taken away from a pharmacist
who has nothing in the spool), Lodge (a currently credentialed pharmacist adds a
prescription to the back of the spool, provided the spool is below its ordinary limit),

using the reserved slot beyond the ordinary limit), Dispense (the robot takes the
prescription at the head of the spool and makes it up onto the collection shelf), Collect
(a patient takes a made-up prescription off the collection shelf), and Revise (the formulary
revision is advanced while the spool is empty, retiring every credential stamped with the
previous revision).

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm divides the fire perimeter into a fixed set of survey
sectors. There are exactly as many sector cards as there are sectors, and the swarm's
whole point is that a card is never duplicated and never mislaid: at any instant every
card is either sitting unassigned in the ground station's pool, or booked out to a drone
and awaiting handover, or actually flown by a drone. Nothing else can happen to a card.

Drones take work optimistically instead of holding the assignment board. A drone reads the
board, noting its version number and how many cards were in the pool, and then flies on.
Any movement of a card advances the board's version, so when the drone finally tries to
book a card out, the ground station lets it through only if the version the drone noted is
still the live one -- proof that the pool count it read is still true. Otherwise the drone
discards its reading and reads the board again later.

Any one drone in the swarm may go silent without warning: the radio fails and it stops
answering, though the ground station has no way to distinguish that from a drone that is
simply busy. So the ground station will not wait indefinitely for an outstanding reading
to be acted on; it may abandon any reading it is still waiting on, which returns the drone
to a clean slate without moving any card.

BookOut (a drone whose noted version is still live and who saw a card in the pool moves one
card from the pool into its own booking, advancing the version), Discard (a drone whose
reading is stale, who saw an empty pool, or who finds the board's version counter used up
tears up its reading), Abandon (the ground station gives up on an outstanding reading it is
still waiting on), TakeUp (a drone that is still answering converts its booking into a card
it is actually flying), HandBack (a drone that is still answering returns a card it was
flying to the pool, advancing the version), and GoSilent (the one drone that can fail
silently loses its radio).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the cards in the ground station's pool, the cards booked out to drones and the cards being flown always add up to exactly the number of sector cards the swarm started with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every reading a drone takes off the board is eventually cleared, whether by booking a card out, by the drone tearing it up, or by the ground station abandoning it.

An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared record of the departure order: an
append-only strip board, where each strip in turn names the runway a departure has been

When a strip is accepted the controller is given a receipt: the position its strip landed
at and the runway written on it. A receipt is a promise about the shared record, and the
allocator must honour it.

crosswind and reopened later, so the set of usable runways changes underneath a board that
already has strips on it. The allocator deals with that in two ways. It may rewrite a
strip that names a runway which has since closed, moving that departure to a runway that

become unflyable. Both are only permitted on strips that no controller has been given a
receipt for -- a receipted strip may be neither rewritten nor cut away.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler hands out press slots -- the numbered windows in the day's press
schedule. The shop keeps one slot board on the wall, and operators do not lock it while
they think. An operator glances at the board, memorises which slots are showing free,
walks back to its press, and only then tries to take one. The take is accepted only if the
board still shows exactly the free slots the operator memorised; if anything on the board
has moved in the meantime, the memorised picture is worthless and the operator has to look
again. Because the board itself is what records who has which slot, and because the take
is only accepted against an unchanged board, the same slot cannot end up written against
two operators.

Taking a slot on the board and writing it into your own press docket are separate steps,
and there is a gap between them. That gap is where the shop manager's privilege bites. The
manager may override the board and force a slot across to a different operator, and the
rule is that the override must strike the slot out of the previous holder's docket in the
same movement: an entry in a docket that the board no longer backs would send two presses
after the same window. The manager's privilege is rationed to a handful of uses per shift,
so it cannot be used to keep a slot in play forever.

The full action set is: ReadTheBoard (an operator memorises the set of slots currently
showing free), TakeSlot (an operator whose memorised picture still matches the board takes
one of the slots it saw free, and the board is written up in that operator's name),
LookAgain (an operator whose memorised picture no longer matches the board, or who saw
nothing free, throws the picture away), WriteDocket (an operator whose name is on the board
against a slot copies that slot into its own press docket), ReleaseSlot (an operator
finishes with a slot and clears it from both the board and its docket), and
ManagerOverride (the shop manager forces a slot across to a nominated operator, striking
it out of the previous holder's docket as part of the same movement, and using up one of
the shift's rationed overrides).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every slot written in an operator's press docket is a slot the wall board currently records against that same operator, so no slot is ever allocated to two operators at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every slot that gets written up on the board is eventually cleared from it again.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital operating-room scheduler protects one shared booking register. The register
holds, for every theatre, how many sessions of the day have already been committed to it,
and no theatre may be committed beyond the number of sessions its staff can actually
cover. That number is not the same everywhere: the theatres that share the recovery bay
run one session fewer than the rest. Planners update the register with a compare-and-swap: a planner takes a complete
copy of the register, works out from that copy whether the theatre it has a patient for
still has a session spare, and then swaps its decision in. The swap is accepted only if
the register is still, in every entry, identical to the copy the planner took. If anything
has moved, the copy the planner reasoned from was out of date and the whole attempt is
thrown away and started again.

Planners can be slow. A planner is never taken off the rota and never abandons a patient,
but an arbitrary amount of time may pass between taking its copy of the register and
trying to swap its decision in -- a ward round, a delayed transfer, a conversation with a
surgeon. During that gap other planners commit sessions, which is exactly why the
comparison covers the whole register and not just the entry being changed: a decision
reasoned from a stale copy must never be allowed through.

time), CopyRegister (a planner with a patient takes a complete copy of the booking
register), CommitSession (a planner whose copy still matches the register in every entry,

that theatre), StartOver (a planner whose copy no longer matches the register, or whose
copy showed no theatre with a session to spare, throws the copy away), and CloseCase (a
committed session is completed and released back to its theatre).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no theatre is ever committed to more sessions than its staff can cover.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling block system does not let any single interlocking node hand a train
movement authority for a block. Authority is granted only when a quorum of the nodes on
the current signalling roster votes for it, and voting happens in numbered ballots. Every
vote a node casts is stamped with the ballot it was cast in, so a vote left over from an
earlier ballot carries no weight in the current one; and a node that is not on the roster
has no standing to vote at all. Between them those two rules mean that neither a node
whose authorisation has been taken away nor a node still repeating an old ballot's answer
can move a train.

Exactly one node in the system may fail silently. Its radio simply stops and it casts no
more votes, but nobody can tell whether it has failed or is merely busy, so it is left on
the roster and the quorum is sized so that the remaining nodes can still reach a decision
without it. Roster changes are a separate, deliberate matter: a node may be taken off the
roster only when doing so would still leave any outstanding grant backed by a quorum of
rostered nodes, and it can be put back on later.

The full action set is: OpenBallot (the system opens a new numbered ballot for a block,
which can only happen when no grant is outstanding), CastVote (a rostered node that has
not gone silent casts its vote, stamped with the current ballot), Grant (a quorum of
rostered nodes has voted in the current ballot, so movement authority is granted and the
voters who backed it are recorded), Abandon (too few rostered nodes are still answering to
reach a quorum, so the ballot is dropped), Release (the train clears the block and the
grant is given up), Decommission (a node is taken off the roster, permitted only when any
outstanding grant would still hold a quorum without it), Recommission (a node is put back
on the roster), and GoSilent (the one node that can fail silently loses its radio).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever movement authority is outstanding, the nodes recorded as having voted for it still include a quorum of nodes on the current roster.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every ballot that is opened eventually reaches a decision, either granting movement authority or being abandoned.

  /\ backers = {}
  /\ silent = NoNode

OpenBallot ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ backers = {}
  /\ ballot < MaxBallot
  /\ ballot' = ballot + 1
  /\ phase' = "voting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, roster, backers, silent>>

CastVote(n) ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ n \in roster
  /\ n # silent
  /\ vote[n] # ballot
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![n] = ballot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, roster, backers, silent>>

Grant ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ Cardinality(LiveVoters) >= Quorum
  /\ backers' = LiveVoters
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, vote, roster, silent>>

Abandon ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ Cardinality(Answering) < Quorum
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, vote, roster, backers, silent>>

Release ==
  /\ backers # {}
  /\ backers' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, roster, silent>>

\* Taking a node off the roster may not undermine an outstanding grant.
Decommission(n) ==
  /\ n \in roster
  /\ Cardinality(backers \cap (roster \ {n})) >= Quorum \/ backers = {}
  /\ roster' = roster \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, backers, silent>>

Recommission(n) ==
  /\ n \notin roster
  /\ roster' = roster \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, backers, silent>>

GoSilent(n) ==
  /\ silent = NoNode
  /\ silent' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, roster, backers>>

Next ==
  \/ OpenBallot \/ Grant \/ Abandon \/ Release
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : CastVote(n) \/ Decommission(n) \/ Recommission(n) \/ GoSilent(n)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : SF_vars(CastVote(n))
  /\ SF_vars(Grant \/ Abandon)

GrantsKeepAQuorum ==
  backers # {} => Cardinality(backers \cap roster) >= Quorum

BallotsDecide ==
  (phase = "voting") ~> (phase = "idle")

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A car-wash conveyor line takes its work from a bounded spool. Attendant terminals lodge
wash tickets into the spool, the spool holds only so many tickets, and when it is full the
terminals are simply refused -- backpressure, so nothing is accepted that the tunnel
cannot track. Each ticket records which terminal lodged it and which revision of the wash
programme was in force at the moment of lodging.

Two things disqualify a ticket from actually driving the tunnel. A terminal may have been
decommissioned since it lodged its ticket -- taken out of the till system, no longer a
party to anything -- in which case it has no standing to start a wash. Or the wash
programme may have been revised since the ticket was lodged, in which case the ticket
describes a wash the tunnel no longer offers and is stale. The tunnel therefore re-checks
both facts as it takes each ticket off the front of the spool, and throws away any ticket
that fails either check rather than running it. Two matching rules keep the running wash
honest: a terminal cannot be decommissioned while its ticket is the one the tunnel is
actually running, and the wash programme is only revised between washes, never while the
tunnel is mid-cycle.

One terminal in the shop can fail silently: its till link dies and it stops lodging
anything more, but nobody notices and it is left commissioned, so tickets it lodged before
the failure sit in the spool and remain perfectly valid work.

The full action set is: LodgeTicket (a commissioned terminal that has not failed lodges a
ticket stamped with the current programme revision, provided the spool is below its
limit), StartWash (the tunnel takes the ticket at the front of the spool and begins the
wash, having re-checked that its terminal is still commissioned and its revision is still
current), DropTicket (the tunnel takes a ticket off the front and discards it because its
terminal has been decommissioned or its revision has been superseded), FinishWash (the
wash completes and the tunnel goes idle), ReviseProgramme (the wash programme revision is
advanced while the tunnel is idle), Commission (a terminal is brought into the till
system), Decommission (a terminal is taken out of the till system, which is not permitted
while its ticket is the running wash), and GoSilent (the one terminal that can fail
silently loses its till link).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the tunnel is running a wash, that wash belongs to a terminal that is still commissioned and carries the wash programme revision currently in force.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router feeds bags onto a sorting loop. The loop is divided into
numbered carrier slots, and a bag can only ride the loop if it is sitting in a slot that is
actually in service. Slots go out of service and come back during the day -- a carrier
plate cracks, a section is isolated for a belt splice, an engineer releases it again -- so
the loop's real capacity moves around underneath the traffic. A slot may only be taken out
of service when nothing is riding in it and nothing has been promised it.

Injection is not decided by the handlers. One routing controller acts as leader and issues
injection permits, and each permit names a slot and carries the epoch of the leadership
that issued it. If the leader drops out, a replacement takes over under a fresh epoch, and
every permit stamped with the old epoch is thereby void: a handler holding one must
discard it rather than inject against it, because the slot it names may since have been
isolated or promised to somebody else. The leader will only issue a permit for a slot that
is in service, unoccupied, and not already promised to another handler, and the handler
re-checks all of that at the moment it injects.

The full action set is: GrantPermit (the acting leader promises a handler a slot that is in
service, empty and unpromised, stamping the permit with the current epoch), Inject (a
handler with a current-epoch permit puts a bag into the named slot, the slot still being in
service and empty), ExpirePermit (a handler discards a permit whose epoch has been
superseded), Unload (a bag rides round to its chute and leaves its slot), TakeOutOfService
(a slot with nothing in it and nothing promised on it is isolated, shrinking the loop's
capacity), ReturnToService (an isolated slot is brought back), Elect (a controller takes
the vacant leader seat under a new epoch), and LeaderDrop (the acting leader falls off the
control network, vacating the seat).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bag riding the sorting loop is in a carrier slot that is currently in service, so the loop never carries more bags than it has serviceable slots.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag that gets onto the sorting loop eventually leaves its slot at its chute.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Handlers, NumSlots, MaxEpoch

Slots == 1..NumSlots
NoLeader == "vacant"
NoPermit == <<0, 0>>

VARIABLES leader, epoch, permit, occupied, inService

vars == <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied, inService>>

\* A permit is only worth anything while its epoch is the leadership now in force.
Promised(s) == \E h \in Handlers : permit[h] = <<s, epoch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Handlers \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ permit \in [Handlers -> (Slots \X (1..MaxEpoch)) \cup {NoPermit}]
  /\ occupied \subseteq Slots
  /\ inService \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ permit = [h \in Handlers |-> NoPermit]
  /\ occupied = {}
  /\ inService = Slots

GrantPermit(h, s) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ permit[h] = NoPermit
  /\ s \in inService
  /\ s \notin occupied
  /\ ~Promised(s)
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = <<s, epoch>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, occupied, inService>>

Inject(h) ==
  /\ permit[h] # NoPermit
  /\ permit[h][2] = epoch
  /\ permit[h][1] \in inService
  /\ permit[h][1] \notin occupied
  /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {permit[h][1]}
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = NoPermit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, inService>>

ExpirePermit(h) ==
  /\ permit[h] # NoPermit
  /\ permit[h][2] # epoch
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = NoPermit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, occupied, inService>>

Unload(s) ==
  /\ s \in occupied
  /\ occupied' = occupied \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, inService>>

\* Capacity shrinks only where nothing is riding and nothing has been promised.
TakeOutOfService(s) ==
  /\ s \in inService
  /\ s \notin occupied
  /\ ~Promised(s)
  /\ inService' = inService \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied>>

ReturnToService(s) ==

  /\ inService' = inService \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied>>

Elect(h) ==

  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch

  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1

  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(Unload(s))

LoopRidesOnlyServiceableSlots == occupied \subseteq inService

BagsLeaveTheLoop ==
  \A s \in Slots : (s \in occupied) ~> (s \notin occupied)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
The elevator bank in a skyscraper has an express shaft zone that only a limited number of
cars may occupy at once -- the zone shares one ventilation and rescue corridor, and beyond
that number the corridor cannot be cleared in time. Which cars are in the zone is held in a
single compare-and-swap register on the group controller: the register holds the whole set
of cars currently inside.

Two dispatch instances share that one register. The low-rise dispatcher owns the lower
cars and the high-rise dispatcher owns the upper ones, and neither knows anything about
what the other is about to do; the register is their only point of contact. A dispatcher
that wants to send one of its cars into the zone first takes a copy of the register, checks
against that copy that the zone has room and that its car is not already inside, and then
swaps the enlarged set in. The swap is accepted only if the register still holds exactly
the set the dispatcher copied. If the other dispatcher got there first the copy is stale,
the swap is rejected, and the dispatcher takes a fresh copy and tries again.

The full action set is: CallCar (a car is called and starts waiting for the express zone),
CopyRegister (a dispatcher takes a copy of the register's current set of cars in the zone),
Admit (a dispatcher whose copy still matches the register, and whose copy showed both room
in the zone and its own waiting car outside it, swaps that car into the register), Retry (a
dispatcher whose copy no longer matches the register, or whose copy showed the zone
already full, throws the copy away), and LeaveZone (a car finishes its express run and is
taken out of the register).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars in the express shaft zone never exceeds the number the rescue corridor can clear.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumCars, ZoneLimit, MaxTrips

Cars == 1..NumCars
Dispatchers == 1..2
NoCopy == {0}

\* The lower half of the bank belongs to one dispatcher, the upper half to the other.
Owner(c) == IF 2 * c <= NumCars THEN 1 ELSE 2

VARIABLES zone, copy, waiting, trips

vars == <<zone, copy, waiting, trips>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ zone \subseteq Cars
  /\ copy \in [Dispatchers -> SUBSET (0..NumCars)]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Cars
  /\ trips \in 0..MaxTrips

Init ==
  /\ zone = {}
  /\ copy = [d \in Dispatchers |-> NoCopy]
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ trips = 0

CallCar(c) ==
  /\ c \notin waiting
  /\ c \notin zone
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, copy, trips>>

CopyRegister(d) ==
  /\ copy[d] = NoCopy
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = zone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, waiting, trips>>

\* The swap goes in only against a register still identical to the copy taken, which
\* is what stops the two dispatchers filling the zone twice over.
Admit(d, c) ==
  /\ copy[d] # NoCopy
  /\ copy[d] = zone
  /\ Owner(c) = d
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ c \notin copy[d]
  /\ Cardinality(copy[d]) < ZoneLimit
  /\ zone' = zone \cup {c}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = NoCopy]
  /\ UNCHANGED trips

Retry(d) ==
  /\ copy[d] # NoCopy
  /\ \/ copy[d] # zone
     \/ Cardinality(copy[d]) >= ZoneLimit
     \/ ~\E c \in waiting : Owner(c) = d /\ c \notin copy[d]
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = NoCopy]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, waiting, trips>>

LeaveZone(c) ==
  /\ c \in zone
  /\ trips < MaxTrips
  /\ zone' = zone \ {c}
  /\ trips' = trips + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : CallCar(c) \/ LeaveZone(c)
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers : CopyRegister(d) \/ Retry(d)
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers, c \in Cars : Admit(d, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ZoneWithinRescueLimit == Cardinality(zone) <= ZoneLimit

====

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler has one raster image processor, and the RIP is the critical
resource: it can only be rendering for one operator at a time. Access is handed out as a
lease rather than a lock. When the RIP is free an operator that has asked for it is given
a lease with a deadline measured on the shop clock, and the lease is only good until that
deadline passes. An operator may only put work on the RIP while it holds a lease whose
deadline has not yet been reached; the moment the lease expires it grants nothing at all,
which is what stops a forgotten holder blocking the machine forever. Correspondingly the
shop clock is only allowed to advance past a job that is actually rendering if the deadline
is still ahead of it -- a job must be sized to finish inside its lease.

The shop manager has a privilege on top of this: the manager can revoke a lease outright
without waiting for its deadline, pulling any running job off the RIP at the same moment.
That privilege is rationed to a small number of uses, so it cannot be leaned on as a
substitute for the ordinary lease cycle.

The full action set is: RequestRIP (an operator asks for the RIP), GrantLease (the RIP is
free, so a waiting operator is given a lease with a deadline on the shop clock), StartJob
(an operator whose lease has not yet expired puts a job on the RIP), StopJob (an operator
takes its job off the RIP), Tick (the shop clock advances, which is only permitted if
nothing is rendering or the deadline is still ahead), ExpireLease (a lease whose deadline
has been reached, with nothing rendering under it, is given up), and ManagerRevoke (the
shop manager tears up the current lease and pulls any running job off the RIP, using one of
the rationed revocations).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the only operator ever rendering on the RIP is the holder of a lease whose deadline has not yet been reached.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every lease that is handed out is eventually given up again, so the RIP always comes back free.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Operators == 1..NumOperators
NoHolder == 0

VARIABLES clock, holder, deadline, rendering, asked, revokes

vars == <<clock, holder, deadline, rendering, asked, revokes>>

\* An expired lease confers nothing, so the set of operators entitled to the RIP is
\* empty as soon as the clock reaches the deadline.
Entitled == IF holder # NoHolder /\ clock < deadline THEN {holder} ELSE {}

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ holder \in Operators \cup {NoHolder}
  /\ deadline \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ rendering \subseteq Operators
  /\ asked \subseteq Operators
  /\ revokes \in 0..MaxRevokes

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ deadline = 0
  /\ rendering = {}
  /\ asked = {}
  /\ revokes = 0

RequestRIP(o) ==
  /\ o \notin asked
  /\ asked' = asked \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, rendering, revokes>>

GrantLease(o, d) ==
  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ o \in asked
  /\ holder' = o
  /\ clock' = 0
  /\ deadline' = d
  /\ asked' = asked \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rendering, revokes>>

StartJob(o) ==

  /\ clock < deadline
  /\ o \notin rendering
  /\ rendering' = rendering \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, asked, revokes>>

StopJob(o) ==

  /\ rendering' = rendering \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, asked, revokes>>

\* A job must fit inside its lease: the clock cannot run past a live rendering.

  /\ clock' = clock + 1

  /\ clock >= deadline

  /\ holder' = NoHolder
  /\ deadline' = 0

\* The privileged revocation cuts the lease and the running job in one movement.
ManagerRevoke ==

  /\ holder # NoHolder
  /\ holder' = NoHolder
  /\ deadline' = 0
  /\ rendering' = {}
  /\ revokes' = revokes + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, asked>>

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A print shop job spooler allocates press slots -- the numbered windows in the day's press
schedule -- and a slot must never end up allocated to two jobs. The spooler keeps a wall
ledger saying which job, if any, owns each slot. Allocations are not applied on the spot:
the spooler writes a promise into a bounded spool of allocation notes and the notes are
carried down to the press floor by runners. The spool holds only so many notes at once,
and when it is full the spooler refuses to take on further work -- backpressure -- rather
than promising more than it can carry.

The runners do not keep order. A note written first can easily reach the press floor after

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps one master ledger of donor-unit movements, written as
an append-only run of entries, and each collection site keeps its own copy of that ledger
so it can work when the line to head office is quiet. The whole point of the arrangement is
that no movement a site has written is ever lost or overwritten: every site's copy must be
an exact leading run of the master ledger, never a divergent one.

The right to write to the master is passed around the sites as a token, in a fixed ring.
A site that has a movement to record stages it locally and then waits for the token to
come round; it does not hand the token on while it still has something staged, so its turn
is not skipped. When the token arrives, the site may only write into the master if its own
copy has already been brought fully up to date with everything written before it -- writing
from behind is exactly how a movement gets overwritten.

Sites can be slow. None of them ever fails or drops out of the ring, but a site can be
several entries behind, and it pulls entries down one at a time until it is level. Because
the master run has a finite length, there is also an end-of-day archive: once every site's
copy is level with the master, the master run and all the copies are archived together and
the ledger starts empty again.

The full action set is: StageMovement (a site takes down a donor-unit movement and holds it
locally), CommitMovement (the site holding the token, whose copy is fully level with the
master, appends its staged movement to the master ledger and to its own copy at the same
moment), PullEntry (a site that is behind pulls the next entry of the master ledger into
its copy), PassToken (a site with nothing staged hands the token to the next site in the
ring), and Archive (with every copy level with the master, the run is archived and the
ledger starts empty again).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every site's copy of the ledger is exactly a leading run of the master ledger, so no recorded movement is ever lost or overwritten.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every movement a site stages is eventually written into the master ledger.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A smart-home door lock network can only hold a limited number of live guest credentials at
once: the locks share one credential table, and beyond that many entries the table cannot
be pushed out to the hardware. Two independent apps share that one table. The residents'
app issues credentials for their own visitors, and the property manager's app issues them
for contractors and cleaners; neither app knows what the other is doing, and the only thing
they have in common is the table itself.

Neither app locks the table. An app reads it optimistically: it notes the table's revision
number together with how many credentials were live at that moment, and then goes off to
work out who to admit. Every change to the table -- a credential issued, a credential
revoked -- moves the revision number on. When the app finally comes to issue, the write is
accepted only if the revision it noted is still current, which is what proves the count it
noted is still true and there really is a free entry. If the revision has moved, the app's
whole reading is worthless and it starts again; if the reading showed the table already
full, the app turns the request away instead.

The full action set is: ReadTable (an app notes the current revision number and the number
of live credentials), IssueCredential (an app whose noted revision is still current, and
whose noted count showed a free entry, adds a credential for a guest who does not yet have
one, moving the revision on), RefuseGuest (an app whose noted count showed the table
already full turns the request away and records a refusal), StartOver (an app whose noted
revision is no longer current, or which finds no candidate guest or the revision counter
used up for the day, throws its reading away), and RevokeCredential (a live credential is
taken back, moving the revision on).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of live guest credentials in the shared table never exceeds the number of entries the locks can hold.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands out theatre slots, and a slot must never be
given to two surgical teams. Slots are booked on the theatre wall board, which is the
physical record of who has what. The board is not written directly by the schedulers: one
coordinator acts as lead, and the lead keeps its own commitment list of the slots it has
already given away, only ever committing a slot that is not on that list, not already on
the wall board, and does not already have a booking slip travelling towards the board.

Booking slips go to the theatre floor through the hospital's paging system, which does not
preserve order -- a slip written first can reach the board minutes after one written later.
Each slip carries the number of the leadership under which it was written. If the lead
coordinator drops out, another takes over under a new leadership number and rebuilds its
commitment list from what is actually on the wall board, which necessarily leaves out
anything still travelling. That is why a slip is only honoured when its leadership number
is the one currently in force: a slip from a superseded lead names a slot the new lead has
never committed to, and honouring it would put a booking on the board that nobody is
tracking, ready to be given away a second time.

The full action set is: Commit (the acting lead gives a waiting team a slot that is not on
its commitment list, not on the wall board and not already travelling, and sends a booking
slip through the paging system), Deliver (a slip reaches the board while its leadership
number is the one in force and the slot is still empty, so the booking goes up),
DiscardSlip (a slip reaches the board carrying a superseded leadership number or naming a
slot already taken, and is thrown away), FreeSlot (a case finishes and the slot comes off
both the wall board and the lead's commitment list), TakeLead (a coordinator takes the
vacant lead role under a new leadership number and rebuilds its commitment list from the
wall board), and LeadDropsOut (the acting lead is called away and the lead role falls
vacant).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every booking on the theatre wall board is a slot the acting lead has on its commitment list, so no slot is ever given away a second time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every booking slip put into the paging system is eventually resolved, either going up on the wall board or being thrown away.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Vacant == 0
Empty == 0

  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, leadNo, wall>>

\* The leadership number on the slip is what makes an out-of-order delivery safe.
Deliver(s, t, n) ==

  /\ status \in [Jobs -> {"queued", "leased", "done"}]
  /\ owner \in [Jobs -> Printers \cup {NoPrinter}]
  /\ expiry \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxTime]
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxCap

\* named-printer owner -- never a stale (expired) or unauthorized holder.

  /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NoPrinter]

Claim(p, j) ==

Only the printer currently holding the exclusive access token may pull a job off the shared spool and physically print it, and physically printing a job is irreversible -- ink hits paper and it can never be undone or repeated for that same job. Before a job can be printed it must first be released from the shop's backlog into the live spool, and the shop's admin has a privileged override that can seize the token for any printer out of the normal ring order, or void a job outright before it prints, cancelling it permanently. lapsed is evicted and their slot freed; and Tick, where the shared clock

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An elevator bank keeps one shared dispatch record describing which car
currently holds the active claim, tagged with a version number. Elevator
controllers do not write to this record blindly: each controller must first
cache a snapshot of the record's current version, and its later
compare-and-swap write only takes effect if the record's version still
matches what it cached -- if the record moved on in the meantime, the
controller's write attempt is simply not accepted, and it must cache a
fresh snapshot before trying again. A controller can be arbitrarily slow
between caching its snapshot and attempting its write -- it is never taken
out of service, so it can always re-cache and retry as many times as it
needs. Separately, the central dispatcher can claim the record directly
(for example, to force an emergency recall), bypassing the compare-and-swap
path entirely, and can also clear the record's current owner once a claim
has been served. The full action set is: ReadSnapshot, where a controller
refreshes its cached copy of the record's version; CAS, where a controller
attempts its compare-and-swap write, which lands only if its cached version
still matches the record's actual current version; DispatcherOverride,
where the dispatcher advances the record's version and claims it directly;
and ClearOwner, where the dispatcher resets the record's owner once a claim
is done.

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the dispatch record shows a live owner, that
owner's own record of the version it last successfully wrote always agrees
with the record's actual current version, so no controller is ever left
believing it holds an update that was actually lost.

\* controller must re-read the record before every write attempt, and its
\* write only takes effect if nothing else changed the record meanwhile.

\* attempt, but it is never removed -- it can always re-read and retry.
