===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
In a stock exchange's opening auction the order book is the critical resource: only one trading desk may be inside it amending orders at any instant. The desks sit in a ring, and the right to amend travels around that ring as a single baton, handed from each desk to the next one downstream. A desk that has amendments to make keeps the baton until it has worked through all of them. These desks are slow but never absent: one can take an arbitrarily long time inside the book, and the ring simply waits, but it always finishes and always lets go.

The full action set is: Wake -- a quiet desk decides it has some number of amendments to make and joins the queue for the book. Grab -- a queued desk that is holding the baton goes inside the order book and starts amending. Edit -- a desk inside the book makes one amendment, which moves the book's revision on by one and leaves it one fewer to do. Yield -- a desk inside the book that has no amendments left comes out and is finished for the session. Hand -- a desk holding the baton hands it to the next desk downstream on the ring; the baton leaves the one desk in the very same step it arrives at the next, and a desk that is queued or amending will not hand it on.

The whole exclusion argument rests on the baton being singular. It is handed on, never copied and never duplicated: at every instant exactly one desk in the ring has it. Because being inside the book requires holding it, two desks can never be inside the book at once -- there is simply not enough baton to go around.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every instant exactly one desk in the ring holds the baton, and any desk that is inside the order book amending is a desk holding it, so two desks can never be amending the order book at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every desk eventually gets the baton, makes all of its amendments and finishes for the session.

  /\ phase \in [Desks -> {"quiet", "queued", "amending", "done"}]
  /\ todo \in [Desks -> 0 .. MaxEdit]

  /\ todo = [d \in Desks |-> 0]

  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "queued"]
  /\ todo' = [todo EXCEPT ![d] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, rev>>

  /\ baton[d]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![d] = "amending"]

  /\ todo[d] > 0
  /\ rev < MaxRev

  /\ todo[d] = 0

  /\ phase[d] \in {"quiet", "done"}

  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, todo, rev>>

GrabStep  == \E d \in Desks : Grab(d)
EditStep  == \E d \in Desks : Edit(d)

  /\ \A d \in Desks : phase[d] = "amending" => baton[d]

A power-grid load shedder never drops a feeder on one person's say-so. A shed order has to be countersigned by a majority of the substation wardens before it stands, and only a standing order is ever acted on. The wardens are not reliable: one can stop answering at any moment, silently, with no announcement and no chance to hand anything over. From the instant a warden stops answering its countersignature is worth nothing, and the shedder is built to pull orders that were resting on it rather than leave them standing on authority that no longer exists.

The full action set is: Sign -- a warden that is still answering countersigns an order that is not yet standing and not yet spent. Unsign -- a warden that is still answering takes its countersignature back off an order that has not yet been raised. Raise -- an order is raised to standing, which requires that every countersignature on it belongs to a warden answering right now and that those signatures make up a strict majority of the whole warden board. GoQuiet -- a warden stops answering without warning; every standing order carrying its countersignature is pulled down and marked spent in the same motion. Shed -- a standing order is acted on, the feeder is dropped, and the order is marked spent.

The hazard is the shedder acting on authority nobody is behind any more. A silent failure is invisible by construction: the warden simply stops, and its signature sits there on the paperwork looking exactly like a live one. If a standing order were allowed to keep resting on signatures from wardens that had gone quiet, the shedder would be dropping load on the word of participants that are no longer part of the board at all -- and a bare majority is precisely the margin where losing one warden matters.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every shed order that is standing is countersigned only by wardens that are answering at that moment, and by a strict majority of the whole warden board, so no order ever rests on a silent or withdrawn signature.

A blood-bank inventory tracker runs as two separate desks: a ward-side desk and a depot-side desk. They are independent programs that cannot see each other's work, but they track one shared pool of units and both amend one shared count sheet. The sheet is not patched in place: a requisition reads the whole sheet, keeps that reading, and writes the sheet back as exactly that reading plus itself. Because of that, every requisition runs as a two-phase commit across the fridges: it must be holding every fridge in the bank before it is allowed to take its reading, and it still has to be holding them all when it writes.

The full action set is: Open -- a fresh requisition from either desk starts gathering fridges. Prepare -- a gathering requisition takes hold of one fridge that is currently free. Take -- a gathering requisition that is holding every fridge in the bank takes its reading of the whole count sheet and is readied. Post -- a readied requisition that is still holding every fridge writes the sheet back as its reading plus itself, is recorded as posted, and lets all its fridges go. Tear -- a gathering requisition that finds some fridge already held by a different requisition tears itself up and lets go of whatever fridges it had taken.

The hazard is a lost update, and the two independent desks make it easy to reach. A reading is a snapshot of the whole sheet and a write replaces the whole sheet, so if a requisition could take its reading before it had every fridge, the other desk's requisition could post in between and the first one's write would silently erase it. Unanimous holding across the fridges is the only thing that makes the reading and the write behave as one indivisible step.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared count sheet carries exactly the requisitions the desks have been told were posted, no more and no fewer, so no posted requisition is ever erased from the sheet by a write built on an older reading.

  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ expiry = 0
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ active = NoOne
  /\ msgs = {}

\* ownership and any active status riding on it, closing the staleness
\* window at the instant expiry actually occurs.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ IF owner # NoOne /\ clock + 1 >= expiry
       THEN /\ owner' = NoOne
            /\ active' = NoOne
       ELSE /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, active>>
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, expiry, msgs>>

  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ owner' = s
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1

  \/ \E s \in Students : Grant(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : Renew(s)

the train read; otherwise the write is rejected because someone else has
already moved the record forward. A train may become slow -- it can dawdle
for an arbitrary number of steps between reading the version and attempting
its compare-and-swap -- but it never fails outright, so it always eventually
attempts the swap. Because the swap is guarded by the version check, a slow
train's stale attempt is cleanly rejected instead of silently clobbering a
newer update, so no accepted update is ever lost even though the record has

\* "slow" is a lifecycle state that delays a train's CAS attempt but never
\* removes it from progress -- fairness still forces it to act eventually.

  /\ owner \in Trains \cup {NoOwner}
  /\ snapshot \in [Trains -> 0..6]

  /\ applied \in [Trains -> BOOLEAN]

In a hospital operating-room scheduler, participants submit requests to book
the shared OR schedule. The schedule carries a version stamp, `epoch`, and a
writer may only commit its request if the epoch it cached when it read the
schedule still matches the live epoch (optimistic locking). If another
writer committed in the meantime, the pending writer's stamp goes stale, so
it must retry: re-read the current epoch and attempt the commit again. One
participant (the crash-prone one) may go permanently and silently unresponsive
at any point, leaving any request it had outstanding forever pending, while a
reliable participant keeps competing for the schedule via request/retry/commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The participant recorded as owning the current epoch's OR
booking is never a stale writer (its cached stamp always matches the live
epoch) and never a participant that has silently crashed.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the reliable, non-crash-prone participant has a
pending scheduling request, that request is eventually committed.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, CrashProne, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, owner, localEpoch, crashed, pending

\* The OR schedule is versioned by `epoch`. A writer may only commit if its
\* cached epoch still matches the current one (optimistic locking). A stale
\* writer must retry: re-read the epoch, then attempt the commit again.

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 0..(MaxEpoch-1)
  /\ owner \in Participants \cup {"none"}
  /\ localEpoch \in [Participants -> 0..(MaxEpoch-1)]
  /\ crashed \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ pending \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ owner = "none"
  /\ localEpoch = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]
  /\ pending = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]

\* A non-crashed, idle participant submits a scheduling request, stamping it
\* with the epoch it currently observes.
Request(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~pending[p]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, crashed>>

\* Commit only succeeds if the writer's stamp still matches: this is the
\* optimistic-locking check that rejects stale or unauthorized writers.
Commit(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ pending[p]
  /\ localEpoch[p] = epoch
  /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % MaxEpoch
  /\ owner' = p
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = (epoch + 1) % MaxEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A stale writer (its stamp lost the race) discovers the mismatch and
\* refreshes its view of the epoch before it may retry the commit.
RetryStale(p) ==
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ pending[p]
  /\ localEpoch[p] # epoch
  /\ localEpoch' = [localEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, pending, crashed>>

\* The twist: the crash-prone participant may go silent at any time,
\* permanently, without ever releasing or completing its pending request.
CrashSilently ==
  /\ ~crashed[CrashProne]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![CrashProne] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, localEpoch, pending>>

Next ==
  \/ (\E p \in Participants: Request(p) \/ Commit(p) \/ RetryStale(p))
  \/ CrashSilently

\* SAFETY: the participant recorded as owning the current epoch must never
\* be a stale writer: its cached stamp must always match the live epoch
\* (a crashed writer can never reach this state at all, since Commit's
\* guard already excludes crashed participants from acting).
OwnerNotStale ==
  owner # "none" => localEpoch[owner] = epoch

Reliable == CHOOSE p \in Participants : p # CrashProne

\* LIVENESS: a non-crash-prone participant's pending request is always
\* eventually committed, despite races with a stale/crashing peer.
EventualCommit == pending[Reliable] ~> ~pending[Reliable]

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Request(Reliable))
  /\ WF_vars(RetryStale(Reliable))
  /\ SF_vars(Commit(Reliable))

  /\ nextSeq = 1
  /\ log = <<>>

\* as long as the bounded queue still has room.

  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
  /\ \E p \in Players :

  /\ network = {}

  /\ reconfiguring' = TRUE

\* Reconfiguration completes: epoch advances, prior holds are invalidated

  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holds' = {}
  /\ reconfiguring' = FALSE

  \/ FinishReconfigure

  \/ \E m \in network : Deliver(m)

VARIABLES occA, occB, verA, verB, ver

\* occA/occB: robots currently holding a dock slot claimed by fleet instance A / B
\* verA/verB: the shared pool version each instance last read when starting a reservation attempt
\* ver: shared version counter, bumped on every successful commit or release (the CAS token)

TypeOK ==
    /\ occA \in 0..Cap
    /\ occB \in 0..Cap
    /\ verA \in ({-1} \cup 0..VMax)
    /\ verB \in ({-1} \cup 0..VMax)
    /\ ver \in 0..VMax

Init ==
    /\ occA = 0
    /\ occB = 0
    /\ verA = -1
    /\ verB = -1
    /\ ver = 0

StartA ==
    /\ verA = -1
    /\ occA + occB < Cap
    /\ verA' = ver
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, occB, verB, ver>>

\* CommitA succeeds only if the pool version is unchanged since StartA's read (optimistic check);
\* otherwise it aborts and clears verA so instance A retries with a fresh read next time
CommitA ==
    /\ verA # -1
    /\ IF verA = ver /\ ver < VMax
       THEN /\ occA' = occA + 1
            /\ ver' = ver + 1
            /\ verA' = -1
       ELSE /\ verA' = -1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, ver>>
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, verB>>

ReleaseA ==

    /\ ver < VMax
    /\ occA' = occA - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, verA, verB>>

    /\ occA + occB < Cap
    /\ verB' = ver

            /\ verB' = -1
       ELSE /\ verB' = -1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<occB, ver>>
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, verA>>

ReleaseB ==
    /\ occB > 0
    /\ ver < VMax
    /\ occB' = occB - 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occA, verA, verB>>

Next == StartA \/ CommitA \/ ReleaseA \/ StartB \/ CommitB \/ ReleaseB

twist, at most one of the two passengers may crash silently at any point while it holds

block the other passenger's boarding cycle.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every non-crashed passenger's pending floor-call request is eventually served (boarded), unless it is abandoned by a silent crash.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Capacity

\* Two boarding candidates share one cabin of the given Capacity.
Passengers == {"p1", "p2"}

VARIABLES status, crashed, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock

vars == <<status, crashed, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ status \in [Passengers -> {"idle", "called", "waiting", "boarding", "boarded"}]
  /\ crashed \in [Passengers -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ occupancy \in 0..Capacity
  /\ coarseLock \in BOOLEAN
  /\ fineLock \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ status = [p \in Passengers |-> "idle"]
  /\ crashed = [p \in Passengers |-> FALSE]
  /\ occupancy = 0
  /\ coarseLock = FALSE
  /\ fineLock = FALSE

\* Coarse lock: only one passenger may register a floor call at a time.
CallFloor(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "idle"
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~coarseLock
  /\ coarseLock' = TRUE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "called"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, fineLock>>

ReleaseCoarse(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "called"
  /\ coarseLock' = FALSE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, fineLock>>

\* Fine lock: the finer-grained gate that actually admits a passenger into
\* the cabin, rechecking capacity right at the point of boarding.
AcquireFine(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "waiting"
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ ~fineLock
  /\ occupancy < Capacity
  /\ fineLock' = TRUE
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "boarding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, occupancy, coarseLock>>

ReleaseFine(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "boarding"
  /\ fineLock' = FALSE
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "boarded"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, coarseLock>>

ExitCabin(p) ==
  /\ status[p] = "boarded"
  /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, coarseLock, fineLock>>

\* Twist: at most one passenger ever crashes silently, and only while it
\* holds no lock, so its stall cannot wedge the other passenger's progress.
Crash(p) ==
  /\ status[p] \in {"idle", "waiting"}
  /\ ~crashed[p]
  /\ \A q \in Passengers : ~crashed[q]
  /\ crashed' = [crashed EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<status, occupancy, coarseLock, fineLock>>

    \/ CallFloor(p)
    \/ ReleaseCoarse(p)
    \/ AcquireFine(p)
    \/ ReleaseFine(p)
    \/ ExitCabin(p)
    \/ Crash(p)

\* the uncontended release/exit steps only need weak fairness.

  /\ [][Next]_vars

  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("p1")) /\ WF_vars(ReleaseCoarse("p2"))
  /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine("p1"))   /\ SF_vars(AcquireFine("p2"))
  /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("p1"))   /\ WF_vars(ReleaseFine("p2"))
  /\ WF_vars(ExitCabin("p1"))     /\ WF_vars(ExitCabin("p2"))

\* SAFETY: cabin occupancy is exactly the count of boarded passengers and
\* never exceeds the cabin's fixed capacity.

  LET boarded == {p \in Passengers : status[p] = "boarded"} IN
    /\ occupancy = Cardinality(boarded)
    /\ Cardinality(boarded) <= Capacity

Served(p) == status[p] = "boarded"

\* boarded (or explicitly abandoned by a silent crash).
RequestsEventuallyServed ==

    /\ s \notin submitted

    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {s}

\* remain unaware (stale) of the change until they explicitly resync belief.
Failover ==

    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leaderLog' = [leaderLog EXCEPT ![term + 1] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<believed, status, committedBy, capacity>>

SyncBelief(p) ==

  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lockHolder, adminHolds>>

Vote(t, p) ==

  /\ p \notin votes[t]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = @ \union {p}]

  /\ lockHolder = {}
  /\ ~adminHolds

  /\ lockHolder' = {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, adminHolds>>

  /\ adminHolds' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, lockHolder>>

\* processed at any later point, modeling arbitrary network reordering.
Send(c) ==

  /\ ~ \E m \in inflight : m.ctrl = c
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[ctrl |-> c, expVer |-> ver]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, pending, applied, acked>>

SendAny == \E c \in Controllers : Send(c)

\* The CAS succeeds only when the message's expected version still matches

Apply(m) ==

  /\ ver' = ver + 1

  /\ droneSlot[d] = NoSlot
  /\ pendingSlot[d] = NoSlot

\* this check is the sole guard against two drones claiming one slot.

  /\ inflight \subseteq 1..MaxId
  /\ acked \subseteq 1..MaxId

  /\ acked = {}

  /\ Len(queue) + Cardinality(inflight) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextId)
  /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, acked>>
  /\ backpressure' = (Len(queue') + Cardinality(inflight') >= Capacity)

how many containers have been placed at each crane slot. Before a crane

the fine-grained crane-slot lock underneath it. Once both locks are held,
the process reads the manifest, computes the incremented value, and hands
it off as an asynchronous update message to the yard's manifest service
rather than writing it in place immediately. These update messages travel
over an unordered channel, so they can be delivered out of send order --
a message from one crane can be applied before or after a message from
another, and delivery for different slots can interleave arbitrarily. The
hierarchical locking discipline keeps this safe: a process does not
release its section and slot locks until its own update message has
actually been delivered and applied, so no other process can slip in a
conflicting read/write on the same slot while an update is still in
flight, even though reordering across slots and processes is otherwise
unconstrained.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every in-flight (undelivered) manifest-update message is
always still exactly one greater than the manifest's current value for
its slot, so no concurrently interleaved or reordered update can silently
overwrite -- lose -- another process's completed update.

\* Coarse (yard-section) and fine (crane-slot) locks must be acquired in
\* that order before a process may compute and ship a manifest update.
Init ==
  /\ sectionLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoneVal]
  /\ slotLock    = [s \in Slots |-> NoneVal]
  /\ manifest    = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ pending     = {}
  /\ phase       = [p \in Procs |-> "idle"]
  /\ workSlot    = [p \in Procs |-> NoneVal]

AcquireSection(p, s) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "idle"
  /\ sectionLock[s] = NoneVal
  /\ sectionLock' = [sectionLock EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ workSlot'    = [workSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]
  /\ phase'       = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "section"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, manifest, pending>>

AcquireSlot(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "section"
  /\ LET s == workSlot[p] IN
       /\ sectionLock[s] = p
       /\ slotLock[s] = NoneVal
       /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "slot"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sectionLock, manifest, pending, workSlot>>

\* off as an asynchronous message; the locks are NOT released yet.
SendUpdate(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "slot"
  /\ LET s == workSlot[p] IN
       /\ slotLock[s] = p
       /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<p, s, manifest[s] + 1>>}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sectionLock, slotLock, manifest, workSlot>>

\* Messages sit in an unordered set, so delivery order across processes
\* and slots is arbitrary -- this is where reordering happens. Locks are
\* only released once the matching message is actually applied.
DeliverUpdate(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "waiting"
  /\ LET s   == workSlot[p]
         msg == CHOOSE m \in pending : m[1] = p /\ m[2] = s
     IN
       /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![s] = msg[3]]
       /\ pending'  = pending \ {msg}
       /\ slotLock'    = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneVal]
       /\ sectionLock' = [sectionLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneVal]

  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]

  \/ \E p \in Procs : AcquireSlot(p)

  /\ inCS \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]

  /\ ticksLeft = 0
  /\ status = [p \in Participants |-> "alive"]
  /\ inCS = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]

\* A live participant grabs the free match-commit lease and enters the critical section
Acquire(p) ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ status[p] = "alive"
  /\ holder' = p
  /\ ticksLeft' = LeaseLen
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED status

\* The holder commits the match and voluntarily releases the lease
Release(p) ==
  /\ holder = p
  /\ inCS[p]
  /\ status[p] = "alive"
  /\ holder' = NoOne
  /\ ticksLeft' = 0
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]

A bank runs two independent settlement-processing instances that draw on one
shared pool holding the lease for a single interbank settlement batch. Before
either instance may act on the batch it must acquire a time-bounded lease from
the shared pool: the lease carries an expiry countdown (a "ttl") and each
newly granted lease is stamped with a fresh epoch number. Only the instance
currently recorded as the lease holder may begin settling the batch, and it
may only begin while its lease has not yet expired (ttl > 0). Because the pool
is shared between the two instances, once a lease genuinely expires (ttl
reaches 0) either instance may reclaim it, which bumps the epoch and hands the
batch to whichever instance next acquires it. An in-flight settlement attempt
records the epoch it observed when it began; if the lease is reclaimed under a
new epoch while that attempt is still outstanding, the attempt is now stale
and can never be credited -- it must instead be discarded so a fresh attempt
by the batch's current lease holder can proceed. The full action set is:
Acquire1 and Acquire2 (instance 1 or instance 2 takes an expired, unsettled
batch's lease from the pool and starts a new epoch), Begin1 and Begin2 (the
current, unexpired lease holder stamps a new in-flight settlement attempt with
the epoch it currently observes), CompleteSettle (an in-flight attempt is
credited to its instance only if the epoch it observed still equals the
batch's current epoch), AbortStale (an in-flight attempt whose observed epoch
no longer matches the current epoch is discarded, freeing the batch for a
fresh attempt), and Tick (the lease countdown decrements toward expiry, or
idles once already expired). SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the batch is credited
as settled to some instance, that instance is still the batch's recorded
lease holder at that moment and remains so forever after, so settlement
credit can never be given to an unauthorized instance or to one whose claim
has gone stale under a reclaimed lease. LIVENESS PROPERTY: the batch is
eventually settled.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
In a container-ship crane yard, cranes admit containers into a storage area
of bounded capacity. Admission of each container is coordinated by a
two-phase commit protocol across the yard's participants -- the crane
operator, the yard controller, and the ship's manifest system: the
coordinator opens a preparing phase and asks every participant to cast a
vote, and only commits the admission once every participant has voted yes.
If any participant votes no, the admission aborts instead. A privileged yard
administrator may invoke an override that forces a commit without waiting
for unanimous consent from the participants, bypassing the normal voting
requirement entirely -- but the override still respects the yard's physical
capacity limit, so a container is only ever moved in when there is room,
whether the commit came from ordinary consensus or from the override. Once a
transaction is settled (committed or aborted), the yard resets to idle and
is ready for the next admission attempt. Containers already resting in the
yard may also depart, freeing capacity for future admissions. If every
participant has voted yes but the yard is already at capacity by the time
voting completes, the coordinator aborts instead of stalling, so a
resolution always exists once voting finishes. The admin override is itself
rate-limited, so only a bounded number of overrides can occur over the
yard's lifetime, preventing uncontrolled bypass of the normal protocol. The
full action set is: starting a new admission round, a participant casting
its vote, committing on unanimous consent, aborting on any dissenting vote,
aborting because the yard has no room left despite unanimous consent, the
admin's override commit, resetting after a settled transaction, and a
container departing the yard.

force an admission through without unanimous participant consent, the
number of containers physically present in the crane yard never exceeds its
bounded capacity.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A small wildfire drone surveillance swarm patrols a burn perimeter and shares a common pool of battery/fuel reserve units so that no drone runs dry while another is over-provisioned. When a drone needs more reserve, it proposes an optimistic-locking transfer: it reads the source drone's current version stamp, computes the amount to move, and submits the request tagged with that stamp. Independently, any drone may log a local patrol update, which bumps its own version stamp (this is bounded so the system stays finite). When the in-flight transfer request is finally checked against the source drone's version, two things can happen. If the version still matches what the requester read, the optimistic lock succeeds: the transfer commits, the requested amount moves from source to destination, and the source's version stamp advances. If the version has since changed because of an intervening patrol update, the lock check fails; rather than aborting, the requester retries by re-reading the source's current version and resubmitting the same request. A drone whose transfer keeps losing the race can be slow to converge -- it may need several retries before its request finally commits -- but it is never treated as failed and its request is never dropped: the retry loop keeps making progress until the lock check succeeds. Only one transfer request is in flight across the swarm at a time. The full action set is: Propose (create a new transfer request when none is in flight), Patrol (a drone bumps its own version stamp, up to a small cap), CommitTransfer (the lock check matches, so the request applies and clears), and RetryTransfer (the lock check fails, so the request re-reads the version and tries again).

SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state the sum of all drones' reserve units equals the swarm's initial total, since a transfer only moves reserve between two drones and never creates or destroys it, even while retries are outstanding or a drone's convergence is slow.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every transfer request that becomes active is eventually cleared (committed), so a slow-but-not-failed drone's request is never left pending forever.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

A library's online reservation system lets patrons claim a pickup slot for a
requested book using optimistic locking with retry instead of a blocking

to commit the reservation with a compare-and-swap that only succeeds if

begins an attempt by picking a slot and snapshotting its version. If the
compare-and-swap finds the slot still free and unchanged, the attempt
commits and the patron becomes the recorded owner of that slot. If the
compare-and-swap loses the race (the slot was already taken or its version
moved), the patron retries with a fresh snapshot as long as a small retry
budget remains; once the budget is exhausted and the race is still lost, the
patron abandons the attempt instead of retrying forever. One designated
patron's client can crash silently at any point while idle or mid-attempt,
after which it never acts again -- it does not release anything and does not
notify anyone. The system must ensure that a patron who believes it holds a
slot really does hold it, so the same pickup slot is never handed out to two
different reservations even though several patrons may be racing the same
compare-and-swap and one of them may vanish mid-race. The actions are:
starting an attempt (reading a slot's version), committing via a successful
compare-and-swap, retrying after a lost race while budget remains,
abandoning after the retry budget is exhausted, and the designated patron's
silent crash. SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a patron's reservation attempt is
recorded as done, that patron is truly the slot's recorded owner, so no
pickup slot is ever double-allocated to two patrons.

has its reservation attempt resolved -- either committed or abandoned --
even if the crash-prone patron goes silent forever.

    /\ readVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]

    /\ retries = [p \in Participants |-> 0]

compete to allocate access slots on shared door hardware. Each slot is

allocation record claiming the slot. A controller releases a slot by
clearing the allocation record together with both locks in one step. The
twist is that a controller can crash silently at any time -- it simply stops
acting while still holding whatever locks and allocation record it had, with
no notification to the rest of the network. To keep the network from
wedging permanently on a crashed controller's slot, any other live
controller may run a reclaim step on a slot whose coarse or fine lock is
held by a crashed controller: the reclaim step hands both locks to the
reclaiming controller and clears any stale allocation record for that slot
in the same step, so a fresh allocation must be written from scratch before
the slot counts as allocated again. The full action set is: acquiring the
coarse lock, acquiring the fine lock, writing the allocation record,
releasing a slot, a controller crashing silently, and reclaiming a slot from
a crashed controller.

slot's allocation record is only ever valid while it is corroborated by that
same controller currently holding both the coarse and fine locks for the
slot, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two controllers at once.

  /\ fineOwner \in [Slots -> Participants \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ alloc \in [Slots -> Participants \cup {NoOne}]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Participants

  /\ fineOwner = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
  /\ alloc = [s \in Slots |-> NoOne]
  /\ crashed = {}

\* Outer tier of the hierarchical lock: reserve the hub before touching the slot.
AcquireCoarseLock(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ coarseOwner[s] = NoOne
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, alloc, crashed>>

\* Inner tier: only the current coarse-lock holder may confirm the fine lock.
AcquireFineLock(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ coarseOwner[s] = p
  /\ fineOwner[s] = NoOne
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, alloc, crashed>>

  /\ fineOwner[s] = p
  /\ alloc[s] = NoOne

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a fixed number of runway-capacity
tokens, one per takeoff slot the runway can support at a time. Aircraft draw
a token from the shared pool as a lease, which grants the right to use the
runway. Because coordination between the tower and an aircraft is
asynchronous, every granted lease carries an expiry timer: if the aircraft
has not yet moved onto the runway before the timer lapses, the lease is
flagged expired rather than revoked outright. Expiry is only a staleness
flag, not a failure verdict -- a slow aircraft (delayed by taxi congestion
or a stuck handoff) is not the same as one that has failed, so an expired
aircraft still holds its token and may either renew the lease, proving it is
merely slow and still active, or proceed straight onto the runway using the
expired lease. Once an aircraft is on the runway it eventually completes its
takeoff and departs, returning its token to the pool for reuse. The full
action set is: RequestLease (an aircraft draws a free token from the pool
and becomes leased), ExpireLease (a leased aircraft's timer lapses and its
token moves to the expired bucket without being lost), RenewLease (an
expired aircraft proves it is only slow and its token moves back to
leased), EnterRunway (a leased or expired aircraft moves onto the runway,
its token following it), and Depart (an aircraft on the runway finishes and
returns its token to the pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, each of the runway-capacity
tokens is accounted for in exactly one of the pool, the leased aircraft, the
expired-but-not-evicted aircraft, or the aircraft currently on the runway,
so the total is conserved even while a lease sits expired because its
holder is merely slow rather than failed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every aircraft that holds a token -- whether its lease is
currently active or merely expired -- eventually reaches the runway and
departs, handing its token back to the pool.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m6p2t3 -------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS a1, a2, Capacity

Aircraft == {a1, a2}

VARIABLES pool, leased, expired, onRunway

vars == <<pool, leased, expired, onRunway>>

\* Every runway-capacity token issued from the pool always sits in exactly
\* one of the four buckets below. A lease's expiry timer is only a staleness
\* flag: a slow aircraft keeps its token in "expired" instead of losing it,
\* so it can still renew the lease or head straight to the runway.

Init ==
    /\ pool = Capacity
    /\ leased = {}
    /\ expired = {}
    /\ onRunway = {}

RequestLease(c) ==
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ c \notin leased \cup expired \cup onRunway
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ leased' = leased \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<expired, onRunway>>

ExpireLease(c) ==
    /\ c \in leased
    /\ leased' = leased \ {c}
    /\ expired' = expired \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, onRunway>>

RenewLease(c) ==
    /\ c \in expired
    /\ expired' = expired \ {c}
    /\ leased' = leased \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, onRunway>>

EnterRunway(c) ==
    /\ \/ c \in leased
       \/ c \in expired
    /\ leased' = leased \ {c}
    /\ expired' = expired \ {c}
    /\ onRunway' = onRunway \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED pool

Depart(c) ==
    /\ c \in onRunway
    /\ onRunway' = onRunway \ {c}
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leased, expired>>

Next ==
    \E c \in Aircraft :
        \/ RequestLease(c)
        \/ ExpireLease(c)
        \/ RenewLease(c)
        \/ EnterRunway(c)
        \/ Depart(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(EnterRunway(a1) \/ Depart(a1))
    /\ WF_vars(EnterRunway(a2) \/ Depart(a2))

\* Conservation of the runway-capacity quantity: nothing is ever created
\* or destroyed, it only moves between the pool and the three bucket sets.
TokenConservation ==
    pool + Cardinality(leased) + Cardinality(expired) + Cardinality(onRunway) = Capacity

\* Every aircraft holding a token (active or merely stale/slow) eventually
\* reaches the runway and departs, handing the token back to the pool.
RunwayReturns ==
    \A c \in Aircraft :
        (c \in leased \/ c \in expired \/ c \in onRunway)
            ~> (c \notin leased /\ c \notin expired /\ c \notin onRunway)

=============================================================================

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A car-wash conveyor line has a single wash bay that only one car may occupy
at a time. A car gains the right to enter the bay by acquiring a lease on
it: the lease is granted only while the bay is free, and it binds the car
to the bay until the car either finishes and releases the lease explicitly,
or the lease's expiry deadline (set at grant time, a fixed lease length
ahead of the shared discrete clock) is reached and the system reclaims it.
The twist is that a car's onboard controller can crash silently while it
holds the lease: the crash does not run any release logic, so the car's
status simply flips to crashed while the lease record still shows it as
the bay's owner, and the bay stays unusable by anyone else until the
system's reclaim action later notices the lease has expired and clears it.
The shared clock advances independently, one tick at a time, up to a
bounded horizon, and is the only thing that can make a lease eligible for
reclamation. The full action set is: Acquire (a car with no lease takes the
bay's lease if it is currently unowned, setting itself as owner, marking
its status as washing, and recording an expiry deadline as the current
clock plus a fixed lease length), Release (the owning car voluntarily gives
up the lease while it is washing, clearing ownership and returning its
status to idle), Crash (the owning car's controller silently fails while
washing, flipping its status to crashed without clearing ownership or the
lease record), Tick (the shared clock advances by one, bounded by a
maximum horizon), and Reclaim (once the clock has reached or passed the
current lease's expiry deadline, the system clears the ownership record and
resets the former owner's status to idle, regardless of whether that owner
had crashed or was still legitimately finishing up).
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the set of cars whose status is
washing is always a subset of the single recorded lease owner, so the bay
is never occupied by a car that isn't the current lease holder and never
by more than one car at once, even across a silent crash and the eventual
reclaim of that crashed car's expired lease.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od4m6p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, MaxClock, LeaseLen, NoOwner

VARIABLES owner, expiry, clock, status

vars == <<owner, expiry, clock, status>>

\* owner is the single lease holder (or NoOwner); expiry is its deadline.

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Cars \union {NoOwner}
    /\ expiry \in 0..(MaxClock + LeaseLen)
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ status \in [Cars -> {"idle", "washing", "crashed"}]

Init ==
    /\ owner = NoOwner
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ status = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]

\* Expiry is capped at MaxClock so every lease is reclaimable in-bound.
Acquire(c) ==
    /\ owner = NoOwner
    /\ status[c] = "idle"
    /\ owner' = c
    /\ expiry' = IF clock + LeaseLen > MaxClock THEN MaxClock ELSE clock + LeaseLen
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "washing"]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Release(c) ==
    /\ owner = c
    /\ status[c] = "washing"
    /\ owner' = NoOwner
    /\ expiry' = 0
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

\* The twist: the owning car's controller dies without releasing the lease.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ owner = c
    /\ status[c] = "washing"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, clock>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, expiry, status>>

Reclaim ==
    /\ owner # NoOwner
    /\ clock >= expiry
    /\ owner' = NoOwner
    /\ expiry' = 0
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![owner] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED clock

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Acquire(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Release(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Crash(c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ Reclaim

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: whoever is washing must be the sole recorded owner.
MutualExclusion == {c \in Cars : status[c] = "washing"} \subseteq {owner}

====
```

    LeaseLen = 2

INVARIANT MutualExclusion

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares one record of the fire's current
perimeter. The swarm is kept coherent through epoch-numbered reconfiguration:
whenever the swarm reorganizes -- a relay drone drops off the mesh, a new
drone joins, or the flight plan changes -- the coordinator stamps a fresh
epoch number, and every drone is expected to resubmit its most recent
perimeter reading tagged with that new epoch. A drone that is merely
experiencing radio delay or is temporarily out of line-of-sight is never
treated as failed and is never dropped from the swarm's membership; the
protocol does not wait for it, but it keeps the right to resubmit its latest
reading, tagged with whatever epoch is current when it finally can
communicate again. The coordinator folds a drone's submitted reading into
the shared record only when that reading is at least as fresh (same epoch
or newer) as what the record already reflects, and it then acknowledges
that drone up through the epoch it just committed. This prevents a merely
slow drone's late-arriving reading from ever silently overwriting the
record with stale data once a newer epoch's readings have already landed,
and it also means the slow drone's contribution is never permanently
discarded -- it is simply folded in whenever it catches up. The swarm
supports four actions: reconfiguring to advance the shared epoch number, a
drone submitting its latest perimeter reading tagged with the current
epoch, the coordinator committing a submitted reading that is fresh enough
into the shared record and acknowledging that drone, and marking a drone as
currently slow for observability only -- this marking never blocks,
excludes, or otherwise changes what any drone or the coordinator is allowed
to do. SAFETY PROPERTY: no drone is ever acknowledged for an epoch newer
than the epoch the shared record actually reflects at that moment, so a
slow drone's earlier acknowledged contribution can never be silently lost
behind a stale overwrite. LIVENESS PROPERTY: once reconfiguration settles
at its final epoch, every drone's reading -- including a reading from a
drone that was slow -- is eventually committed into the shared record and
acknowledged.
===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxEpoch

ASSUME Drones # {}
ASSUME MaxEpoch \in Nat /\ MaxEpoch > 1
ASSUME "none" \notin Drones

VARIABLES epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow

vars == <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the coordinator stamps a fresh epoch and
\* drones resubmit readings tagged with it; a merely slow drone keeps its
\* right to resubmit later instead of being dropped from the swarm.

NoDrone == "none"

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ recordEpoch = 0
  /\ recordDrone = NoDrone
  /\ submittedEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ ackedEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ slow = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch, slow>>

SubmitStep(d) ==
  /\ submittedEpoch[d] < epoch
  /\ submittedEpoch' = [submittedEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, ackedEpoch, slow>>

Submit == \E d \in Drones : SubmitStep(d)

CommitStep(d) ==
  /\ submittedEpoch[d] >= recordEpoch
  /\ recordEpoch' = submittedEpoch[d]
  /\ recordDrone' = d
  /\ ackedEpoch' = [ackedEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = submittedEpoch[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, submittedEpoch, slow>>

Commit == \E d \in Drones : CommitStep(d)

MarkSlowStep(d) ==
  /\ slow' = [slow EXCEPT ![d] = ~slow[d]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, recordEpoch, recordDrone, submittedEpoch, ackedEpoch>>

MarkSlow == \E d \in Drones : MarkSlowStep(d)

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ Submit
  \/ Commit
  \/ MarkSlow

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Reconfigure)
  /\ WF_vars(Submit)
  /\ WF_vars(Commit)

\* SAFETY: an acknowledgment can never outrun what the record actually shows.
NoLostUpdates == \A d \in Drones : ackedEpoch[d] <= recordEpoch

\* LIVENESS: once the epoch settles, every drone -- slow or not -- catches up.
AllAcked == <>(epoch = MaxEpoch /\ (\A d \in Drones : ackedEpoch[d] = MaxEpoch))

====
```

  MaxEpoch = 3

INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY AllAcked

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
This system models a library book reservation service shared by two independent
branch instances, Branch A and Branch B, that both draw reservations from a
single shared pool of book titles bounded by a fixed physical capacity. Rather
than committing a change unilaterally, each branch first proposes an action and
must collect a strict majority of votes from a fixed committee of voting
members -- quorum voting -- before the pool's state actually changes. A branch
proposes to reserve a title that is not currently held by either branch, or to
propose releasing a title that it currently holds; committee members then cast
votes for the single pending proposal; once more than half the committee has
voted, the proposal commits, applying the reservation or release to whichever
branch initiated it and clearing the vote tally; a pending proposal may instead
be aborted (withdrawn) before it commits, which likewise clears the vote tally
so a new proposal can be raised. Because both branches draw from the same
shared pool, a title reserved through Branch A must never also be held by
Branch B, and the combined number of titles reserved across both branches must
never exceed the pool's capacity. The full action set is: ProposeReserve,
ProposeRelease, CastVote, Commit, and Abort.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A title reserved through Branch A is never simultaneously
reserved through Branch B, and the combined number of titles reserved across
both branches never exceeds the shared pool's capacity.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od19m5p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Books, Voters, Capacity

VARIABLES reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook, votes

vars == <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook, votes>>

\* Branches A and B share one Books pool; every reserve/release needs quorum.

Init ==
  /\ reservedA = {}
  /\ reservedB = {}
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ proposalInst = "A"
  /\ proposalBook = CHOOSE b \in Books : TRUE
  /\ votes = {}

ProposeReserve(inst, book) ==
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ book \notin (reservedA \cup reservedB)
  /\ proposalType' = "reserve"
  /\ proposalInst' = inst
  /\ proposalBook' = book
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB>>

ProposeRelease(inst, book) ==
  /\ proposalType = "none"
  /\ book \in (IF inst = "A" THEN reservedA ELSE reservedB)
  /\ proposalType' = "release"
  /\ proposalInst' = inst
  /\ proposalBook' = book
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB>>

CastVote(v) ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ v \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {v}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalType, proposalInst, proposalBook>>

\* Commit fires only once a majority backs the proposal; reserving may not
\* push the shared pool over Capacity.
Commit ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(Voters)
  /\ IF proposalType = "reserve"
       THEN /\ Cardinality(reservedA \cup reservedB) < Capacity
            /\ IF proposalInst = "A"
                 THEN reservedA' = reservedA \cup {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedA' = reservedA
            /\ IF proposalInst = "B"
                 THEN reservedB' = reservedB \cup {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedB' = reservedB
       ELSE /\ IF proposalInst = "A"
                 THEN reservedA' = reservedA \ {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedA' = reservedA
            /\ IF proposalInst = "B"
                 THEN reservedB' = reservedB \ {proposalBook}
                 ELSE reservedB' = reservedB
  /\ proposalType' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<proposalInst, proposalBook>>

Abort ==
  /\ proposalType # "none"
  /\ proposalType' = "none"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reservedA, reservedB, proposalInst, proposalBook>>

Next ==
  \/ \E inst \in {"A", "B"}, book \in Books : ProposeReserve(inst, book)
  \/ \E inst \in {"A", "B"}, book \in Books : ProposeRelease(inst, book)
  \/ \E v \in Voters : CastVote(v)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the instances never overlap on a title, and combined reservations
\* across both never exceed the shared pool Capacity.
PoolCapacityCoherence ==
  /\ reservedA \cap reservedB = {}
  /\ Cardinality(reservedA \cup reservedB) <= Capacity

====

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A network of vending machines shares one authoritative record -- the running
tally of a shared inventory ledger -- that must stay consistent even though
only one machine is allowed to write it at a time. The machines use leader
election with failover: whenever there is no leader, any machine in the
network may become the new leader. The current leader can fail at any
moment (a coin jam, a power blip, a lost heartbeat), which drops it back to
no-leader and lets another machine take over. While it holds leadership, a
machine submits update messages for the shared record; each update it
originates is stamped with the next unused sequence number, and sequence
numbers are never reused or reset across a failover, so two different
leaders can never stamp two different updates with the same number. Once
submitted, an update becomes a message travelling across the network to the
shared record, and the network can reorder these messages in flight -- an
update stamped later can be delivered and observed before one stamped
earlier. To cope with that reordering, the shared record only accepts an
incoming update if its sequence number is strictly greater than the
sequence number of the update it currently holds; an update that arrives
after a newer one has already been applied is recognized as stale and is
discarded rather than being allowed to clobber the newer value. The full
action set is: Elect (an available machine becomes leader when there is
none), Fail (the current leader drops leadership at any time), Submit (the
leader stamps and sends the next update), and Deliver (a message in transit
is delivered to the shared record, applied only if it is newer than what is
already recorded, otherwise dropped as stale).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record's visible value always matches the
sequence number of the highest-numbered update that has actually been
applied to it, so a reordered, lower-numbered message can never overwrite a
value that a higher-numbered update already established -- no update, once
applied, is ever lost to a late-arriving stale message.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite leader failover and message reordering, every
update that gets submitted is eventually delivered and applied to the
shared record, so the record's sequence number eventually reaches the
highest sequence number any leader ever submitted.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxSeq

ASSUME Nodes # {}
ASSUME MaxSeq \in Nat /\ MaxSeq > 0

VARIABLES leader, nextSeq, msgs, version, record

vars == <<leader, nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

NoLeader == "none"

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ nextSeq = 1
  /\ msgs = {}
  /\ version = 0
  /\ record = 0

\* A leaderless network elects any available machine.
Elect ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ \E n \in Nodes : leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

\* Failover: the current leader can drop out at any time.
Fail ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, msgs, version, record>>

\* The leader stamps and sends the next update. Sequence numbers are never
\* reused or reset across a failover, so two leaders never collide.
Submit ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ nextSeq <= MaxSeq
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {nextSeq}
  /\ nextSeq' = nextSeq + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, version, record>>

\* Delivery is order-agnostic (msgs is a set, so the network may reorder
\* in-flight updates). A message only commits if it is newer than the
\* update already applied; a stale, reordered message is simply dropped,
\* which is what prevents lost updates under reordering.
Deliver ==
  /\ \E s \in msgs :
       /\ s > version
       /\ version' = s
       /\ record' = s
       /\ msgs' = msgs \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, nextSeq>>

Next == Elect \/ Fail \/ Submit \/ Deliver

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Elect) /\ WF_vars(Deliver) /\ SF_vars(Submit)

\* SAFETY: the visible record always matches the highest-numbered update
\* actually applied -- no applied update can ever be clobbered by a
\* later-arriving, lower-numbered (stale) message.
RecordCoherent == record = version

\* LIVENESS: every submitted update is eventually delivered and applied,
\* so the record eventually reaches the highest number ever submitted.
AllSubmittedEventuallyApplied == <>(version = MaxSeq)

====

CONSTANTS
  Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
  MaxSeq = 3
INVARIANT RecordCoherent
PROPERTY AllSubmittedEventuallyApplied

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A library operates a book reservation system over a fixed catalog of physical
copies. Time is organized into numbered epochs; each epoch carries its own
soft reservation capacity, and the library periodically reconfigures to the

A pharmacy operates a small cluster of dispenser stations that fill

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router coordinates several handling stations (conveyor
junctions, scanners, and gate-transfer arms) that must jointly agree before
the shared baggage-routing record -- which flight a given bag is currently
assigned to -- is updated. The router itself acts as a two-phase-commit
coordinator: for each proposed reassignment it opens a preparing round with a
fresh transaction id and asks every station to vote yes or no on whether it
can safely apply the change. Only once every station has voted yes does the
coordinator commit, writing that round's transaction id into the shared
record. If any station votes no, the coordinator aborts the round and the
record keeps its previous value. The twist is that a station can crash
silently while a round is preparing: instead of voting no, it simply stops
responding and joins the round's crashed set. The coordinator must treat a
silent crash the same way it treats an explicit no vote -- it detects the
missing response and aborts the round rather than committing, because
committing while a station is silently down would apply an update that
station never actually agreed to, effectively losing that station's implicit
veto and corrupting the shared record. After a round finishes, whether
committed or aborted, every station's vote and crash status is cleared and
the coordinator returns to idle so the next reassignment can be proposed.
The system supports six actions: Propose (the idle coordinator opens a new
preparing round with the next transaction id, bounded by a fixed maximum
number of rounds), Vote (a station that has not crashed and has not yet
voted in the current round casts yes or no), CrashSilently (a station that
has not crashed and has not yet voted in the current round instead stops
responding and is added to the round's crashed set), Commit (the coordinator
applies the round's transaction id to the shared record once every station
has voted yes and none has crashed), Abort (the coordinator abandons the
round, leaving the shared record unchanged, once some station has voted no
or some station has crashed), and ResetRound (once a round has committed or
aborted, all votes and crash markers are cleared and the coordinator returns
to idle).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the coordinator reaches the committed phase, the
shared record equals that round's transaction id and every station had
actually voted yes with none having crashed silently, so a station's missing
response can never be silently treated as an agreed update.

that elect one of themselves as leader. Only the current leader is allowed

an operator can force-admit a queued player straight into the lobby even
while no leader is present, skipping the leader gate entirely for

same lobby capacity as an ordinary admission -- it can bypass the leader

joins the bounded wait queue if it has room), ElectLeader (when no leader
is present, one of the matchmaker nodes is chosen as the new leader),
LeaderFail (the current leader crashes and the lobby becomes leaderless),
LeaderAdmit (the leader dequeues one waiting player and seats them if the
lobby is under capacity), AdminOverrideAdmit (the admin force-admits one
waiting player into the lobby if it is under capacity, regardless of

counter), and PlayerLeave (a seated player departs, freeing one seat).

by the elected leader or forced by the privileged admin override.

a new leader is eventually elected, so failover never leaves the
matchmaker permanently without a leader.

A car-wash conveyor line moves cars through a single wash bay, the critical
resource that only one car may occupy while being washed. Access to the wash
bay is coordinated by optimistic locking with retry: instead of taking a lock
up front, a waiting car first reads the wash bay's current version number as
a snapshot. It then attempts to claim the bay by comparing its saved snapshot
against the bay's live version and checking that the bay currently has no
holder. If the version still matches and the bay is free, the claim
succeeds: the car enters the wash bay, becomes the bay's recorded holder, and
the version number is bumped so that any other car holding a now-stale
snapshot -- including one who read while the bay was occupied -- will detect
the conflict on its own next attempt. If the version has moved on, the car
does not force its way in and is not removed from consideration; it simply
re-reads the live version and waits to try its claim again. A car in this waiting-to-retry state can be arbitrarily slow -- it may
re-read and retry as many times as it likes -- but the line has no
failure-detection or eviction mechanism, so a slow car is never treated as
failed or dropped from the queue, only left to retry patiently. Once a car
finishes washing it exits the bay and clears itself as holder, freeing the
bay for the next successful claim. The full action set is: a car reading the
bay's current version to take a snapshot, a car's claim succeeding because
its snapshot still matches the live version and the bay is free (entering the
bay, becoming its holder, and bumping the version), a car's claim failing
because the version has moved on (re-reading and retrying without being
evicted), and a car exiting the bay once it finishes washing.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the wash bay is never occupied by more than one car at a

processed into its local batch but not yet published are simply stranded

which vacates the leader slot, and a fresh election then promotes a new,

empty local batch rather than any memory of the old leader's unpublished

shrink it. A controller that has been marked crashed can no longer process
requests, publish, or acknowledge anything. The system proceeds through six
kinds of steps: (1) a non-crashed controller may be elected leader whenever
no leader is currently active; (2) the active leader may crash silently at
any time; (3) a crashed leader's failure may later be detected, vacating the
leader slot; (4) the active, non-crashed leader may locally process an
unprocessed floor-call request into its own batch; (5) the active,
non-crashed leader may publish its locally processed batch into the shared
dispatch record; (6) a floor-call request already present in the shared
dispatch record may be acknowledged as durably serviced.

across silent leader crashes and subsequent failovers.

  /\ localLog = [c \in Controllers |-> {}]

A university course-registration system lets a fixed set of participants
(students) compete for the single critical resource that finalizes an
enrollment write: the shared "commit" slot on the registrar's record. The
system uses optimistic locking with retry: a participant who wants to

taking any lock (Request). If a participant's remembered snapshot no
longer matches the live version -- because someone else already
committed and bumped it -- the participant simply re-reads the version and
keeps waiting (Retry), instead of blocking. A participant may attempt to
acquire the critical resource only when its snapshot still matches the
live version and the resource is currently free (Acquire); this is the one
moment where exclusive access is required, because writing the enrollment
record must not interleave with another participant's write. Holding the
resource, the participant may finish normally, writing its enrollment and
bumping the version so the resource becomes free again (Release). The
twist: one designated participant can crash silently while it holds the
resource, after having acquired it but before releasing it (CrashWhileCommitting)
-- it simply stops taking steps and never calls Release. Because the
registration system cannot tell a crashed holder from a slow one, it runs a
recovery action that reclaims the resource from that specific crashed
participant once it has been marked crashed, freeing it for the remaining
participants (Recover). The full action set is: Request, Retry, Acquire,
Release, CrashWhileCommitting, and Recover.

participant's phase -- whoever the pointer names is either actively
committing or has crashed while holding it, and no participant other than
the one the pointer names is ever in the committing phase, so the critical
resource is never held by two participants at once even accounting for the
silent crash.

participant, it is eventually released -- either the holder finishes
normally and releases it, or, if that holder is the one that crashed
silently, the recovery action eventually reclaims it -- so the resource
never stays stuck forever.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A subway signalling block system divides a stretch of track into a fixed
sequence of numbered blocks. Each block guards its own occupancy count with
a compare-and-swap register: before a train may enter a block, or advance
from one block into the next, the controller compares the block's current
occupancy against the block's fixed capacity and only then swaps the
register to the incremented value together with a version counter, so
concurrent entry attempts never both succeed against a stale reading. A
train starts idle in the yard, enters the first block when that block's
register admits it, advances block by block along the line, and finally
exits back to the yard once it clears the last block, decrementing the
register it leaves behind. The twist is that a train can crash silently
while it is sitting inside a block: it simply stops taking any further
action (it can never advance or exit again) without ever running the
release swap on that block's register, so the unit of capacity it was
holding stays permanently pinned even though the train is gone. The full
action set is: CasEnter (a yard-idle train enters block 1 if its register
has spare capacity), Advance (a train in block b moves into block b+1 if
that block's register has spare capacity), ExitTrack (a train in the last
block leaves to the yard, freeing its block's register), and CrashSilently
(a non-crashed train currently in some block is marked crashed, leaving all
registers untouched forever after). SAFETY PROPERTY: no signalling block's
compare-and-swap register ever records more trains occupying it than the
block's declared capacity, whether or not a train has silently crashed
inside it.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, Capacity, VersionBound

ASSUME NumBlocks \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Capacity \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME VersionBound \in Nat \ {0}

Blocks == 1..NumBlocks

VARIABLES trainLoc, occ, version, crashed

vars == <<trainLoc, occ, version, crashed>>

(* occ/version is a compare-and-swap register pair per signalling block:
   an action first compares occ[b] against Capacity, then swaps both
   fields together. The version tag has fixed width (wraps mod
   VersionBound), matching a real bounded ABA counter. trainLoc[t] = 0
   means train t is idle in the yard. *)

Init ==
  /\ trainLoc = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ version = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = {}

CasEnter(t) ==
  LET b == 1 IN
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = 0
  /\ occ[b] < Capacity
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Advance(t, b) ==
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = b
  /\ b < NumBlocks
  /\ occ[b + 1] < Capacity
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = b + 1]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1, ![b + 1] = @ + 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound,
                                 ![b + 1] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

ExitTrack(t, b) ==
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = b
  /\ b = NumBlocks
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

CrashSilently(t) ==
  (* The twist: a train can die inside a block without ever releasing the
     CAS register, permanently pinning that unit of occupancy forever. *)
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] # 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trainLoc, occ, version>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CasEnter(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Advance(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ExitTrack(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CrashSilently(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected ==
  (* Literal safety property: no block's CAS register ever records more
     trains than its declared capacity, whether or not a crash occurred. *)
  \A b \in Blocks : occ[b] <= Capacity

====

work a job an operator must acquire a time-bounded lease naming it the

is rejected, so a job already printed by a faster operator can never be
printed again by the operator that fell behind. The full action set is:
AcquireLease (an operator takes an unheld or expired, not-yet-printed job at
the current clock, bumps its epoch, and records that new epoch for itself),
ReleaseLease (the current holder voluntarily gives up an unprinted job),
Print (an operator whose recorded epoch for a job still equals the job's
live epoch commits the irreversible print), Tick (the shop's clock
advances, which is what lets a lease's expiry actually pass), and

idles). SAFETY

attributable to an operator whose recorded lease epoch had not yet been
superseded at the moment it fired, even when the operator that eventually
prints it was merely slow rather than failed. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job
is eventually printed, since a slow operator's stale attempt being fenced
off never stalls the job forever -- the lease keeps moving until some
operator with a live epoch actually prints it.

\* Mechanism: each job's lease carries a fencing epoch bumped on every
\* hand-off. A worker only remembers the epoch it captured when it took
\* the lease. Print (the irreversible action) commits only if that
\* remembered epoch still matches the job's live epoch, so a slow
\* worker whose lease has since been reassigned gets fenced off instead
\* of double-printing a job someone faster already finished.

    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ holder \in [Jobs -> Workers \cup {NoWorker}]
    /\ epoch \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ expiry \in [Jobs -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDuration)]
    /\ printed \in [Jobs -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ heldEpoch \in [Workers -> [Jobs -> 0..MaxEpoch]]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = [j \in Jobs |-> NoWorker]
    /\ epoch = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ expiry = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ printed = [j \in Jobs |-> FALSE]
    /\ heldEpoch = [w \in Workers |-> [j \in Jobs |-> 0]]

\* Take an unheld or expired job, bump its epoch, and remember that epoch.
AcquireLease(w, j) ==
    /\ ~printed[j]
    /\ epoch[j] < MaxEpoch
    /\ \/ holder[j] = NoWorker
       \/ clock >= expiry[j]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![j] = w]
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![j] = epoch[j] + 1]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![j] = clock + LeaseDuration]
    /\ heldEpoch' = [heldEpoch EXCEPT ![w] = [@ EXCEPT ![j] = epoch[j] + 1]]

    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch>>

    /\ printed' = [printed EXCEPT ![j] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, epoch, expiry, heldEpoch>>

Tick ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch>>

Quiescent ==

AnyRelease == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : ReleaseLease(w, j)
AnyPrint == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : Print(w, j)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which several participants
(brokers) submit orders during the pre-open phase before the market opens.
Access to the shared auction book is coordinated through optimistic locking
with retry: each participant caches a version number for the book, and to
commit an order it must present a cached version that still matches the
book's current version. If the version has since moved on -- because
another participant committed an order first, or because the exchange
revoked someone's access -- the stale participant's submission is rejected
and it must resynchronize by re-reading the current version before it can
retry. The exchange may also revoke a participant's authorization outright,
for instance after detecting abusive or erroneous order flow, immediately
barring that participant from any further action. As a twist, exactly one
designated participant may crash silently at any point: from that moment on
it simply stops being able to interact with the auction book, exactly as
though it had been deauthorized, but without generating any explicit
notification event that other participants could observe. The model's full
action set is: Sync (a participant refreshes its cached version to the
book's current version), SubmitOrder (a participant commits an order using
its cached version as an optimistic-locking token, which only succeeds if
that token still matches the book's current version, and which advances the
book's version on success), RevokeAuth (the exchange deauthorizes a
participant, recording the book version at which the deauthorization took
effect), and Crash (the one designated participant silently drops out,
treated exactly like a deauthorization for bookkeeping purposes). SAFETY
PROPERTY: every order ever committed to the auction book either still
belongs to a currently authorized participant, or -- if that participant
was later deauthorized or crashed -- the order was made strictly before
that deauthorization/crash event, so that no unauthorized, revoked, or
silently-crashed participant's action is ever recorded as legitimate.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

CONSTANTS Participants, CrashParticipant, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, authorized, crashed, partVersion, orders, authVersion

vars == <<version, authorized, crashed, partVersion, orders, authVersion>>

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ authorized = Participants
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ partVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ authVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ orders = {}

\* Sync is the read half of optimistic locking: a participant refreshes its
\* cached version so a later SubmitOrder's compare-and-swap can succeed.
Sync(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ partVersion[p] < version
  /\ partVersion' = [partVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, crashed, orders, authVersion>>

\* SubmitOrder is the CAS-style commit: it only succeeds while the cached
\* version still matches the book's current version, else the caller is
\* stale and must Sync and retry.
SubmitOrder(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ partVersion[p] = version
  /\ orders' = orders \cup {[part |-> p, ver |-> version]}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ partVersion' = [partVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version']
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, crashed, authVersion>>

\* RevokeAuth deauthorizes a participant and stamps the book version at
\* which authorization ended, so past orders can be checked against it.
RevokeAuth(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ authVersion' = [authVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, partVersion, orders>>

\* Crash is the twist: exactly one designated participant may silently drop
\* out, handled identically to RevokeAuth for staleness bookkeeping.
Crash(p) ==
  /\ p = CrashParticipant
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ authVersion' = [authVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<partVersion, orders>>

Next ==
  \E p \in Participants :
    \/ Sync(p)
    \/ SubmitOrder(p)
    \/ RevokeAuth(p)
    \/ Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateConstraint == version <= MaxVersion

\* NoStaleAction: an order in the log either still belongs to a currently
\* authorized participant, or -- if that participant was later deauthorized
\* or crashed -- the order predates that event, so no unauthorized, revoked,
\* or silently-crashed participant's action is ever recorded as legitimate.
NoStaleAction ==

                     \/ o.ver < authVersion[o.part]

  /\ votes = {}

A clearing utility coordinates a bank's interbank settlement batch using hierarchical locking: a coarse batch lock admits one participant bank at a time as the batch coordinator, and only the current coordinator may then take a fine-grained lock on the settlement ledger to post transfers. The twist is that the participant currently holding the coarse lock can crash silently while it still nominally holds both locks, without releasing anything itself. The action set is: AcquireBatchLock (a bank takes the free coarse lock, bumping the epoch and stamping its own credential with the new epoch), CrashHolder (the current coordinator crashes silently, leaving both locks nominally held), RecoverBatchLock (the coordinator's crash is detected and both locks are forced back to free), AcquireFineLock (the coordinator takes the free fine-grained ledger lock, but only while its stamped credential epoch still equals the live epoch), Settle (the fine-lock holder posts one settlement, releasing the fine lock, but only while its credential epoch is still current), and ReleaseBatchLock (the coordinator voluntarily gives up the coarse lock once the fine lock is free).

A print shop job spooler assigns queued print jobs to worker printers under an

that increments each time the printer roster is reconfigured; a new

outstanding, and the shop only reconfigures up to a fixed number of rounds

resync -- fetch and adopt the new epoch number -- before it is authorized to
touch a job again. A worker may only claim a queued job, or mark its currently
held job complete, while its locally recorded epoch exactly matches the
shop's current global epoch; a worker whose recorded epoch is stale is
unauthorized and cannot act. The number of jobs any worker may hold at once
across the whole shop is bounded by the spooler's current capacity, and that
capacity is itself raised or lowered at runtime as printers are brought
online or taken offline, though it never drops to zero. Actions: the shop
reconfigures and bumps the epoch once every worker is caught up, a worker
resyncs its recorded epoch to the current one, an authorized idle worker
claims an available queued job within the current capacity, an authorized
worker completes the job it holds, and an operator adjusts the current
capacity within its declared bounds.

moment it completed the job always matches the shop's global epoch recorded
at that same moment, so no stale or unauthorized worker's completion is ever
recorded as valid.

how reconfigurations, resyncs, and capacity adjustments interleave.

  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ workerEpoch = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
  /\ claimed = [w \in Workers |-> NoJob]
  /\ completed = {}
  /\ capacity = MaxCapacity
  /\ completionRecord = [j \in Jobs |-> [claimant |-> 0, ground |-> 0]]

  /\ \A w \in Workers : workerEpoch[w] = epoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1

A stock exchange runs a pre-market opening auction. Orders for the auctioned symbol
start out unsubmitted, waiting off to the side. To be considered in the auction an
order must be admitted into a bounded work queue; when the queue is already at its
current capacity the exchange applies backpressure and the order simply keeps
waiting unsubmitted. An admitted order is either matched by the opening-auction

unsubmitted, and counted as cancelled). Unlike a fixed-size venue, this exchange's
operator can raise or lower the queue's capacity at runtime -- to widen or throttle
intake as the opening approaches -- and lowering capacity never evicts orders that
are already sitting in the queue, it only blocks new admissions until the queue
drains back under the new limit. No order is ever silently created or destroyed by
any of this: every order that starts unsubmitted ends up, at any point in time, in
exactly one of the four pools -- unsubmitted, queued, matched, or cancelled.

current capacity; a queued order is matched by the opening auction; a queued order
is cancelled by its owner; an unsubmitted order is withdrawn before ever being
queued; the exchange operator adjusts the queue's capacity up or down.

orders plus cancelled orders always equals the fixed total number of orders for the
symbol.

\* wrapping never weakens the safety mechanism, only the version bookkeeping.

    /\ version \in [Slots -> 1..MaxVersion]
    /\ holderRel \subseteq (Slots \X Workstations)
    /\ readVersion \in [Workstations -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ pending \in [Workstations -> {0} \cup Slots]

    /\ holderRel = {}
    /\ readVersion = [w \in Workstations |-> 0]
    /\ pending = [w \in Workstations |-> 0]

    /\ pending[w] = 0
    /\ ~ \E q \in Workstations : <<s, q>> \in holderRel

    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = version[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holderRel>>

\* Commit only succeeds if nothing changed since the read (compare-and-swap).
CommitClaim(w) ==

    /\ version[pending[w]] = readVersion[w]
    /\ ~ \E q \in Workstations : <<pending[w], q>> \in holderRel
    /\ holderRel' = holderRel \cup {<<pending[w], w>>}

    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = 0]

\* A workstation may be arbitrarily slow to notice this, but never fails.
