    /\ readVersion' = [readVersion EXCEPT ![w] = 0]

        \/ RetryConflict(w)

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
An airport baggage router moves cases between conveyor branches using a
two-phase commit protocol run by a coordinator over a fixed set of station
controllers. Every routing decision is stamped with an epoch number, and each
station controller keeps its own record of the last epoch it has synced to.
Before the router starts a new transaction it advances the epoch, so any
controller that has not yet synced to the new epoch is, by definition, stale
for that transaction. A stale controller must first sync, which is when it
learns the current epoch, before it is authorized to cast a prepare vote; a
vote cast by a controller that has not synced to the current epoch is simply
not accepted, so a stale controller's opinion can never influence whether a
transaction commits. Once every station controller that is still functioning
has cast an authorized vote, the coordinator commits the transaction and
routes the bag. One station controller can crash silently at any time: once
crashed it stops syncing and stops voting, and the coordinator no longer waits
for it, so the remaining live controllers can still authorize the commit on
their own. The full action set is: StartTxn (the coordinator advances the
epoch and opens a new prepare phase), Sync (a live controller that is behind
learns the current epoch), Vote (a live controller that is already synced to
the current epoch casts its prepare vote), Commit (once every still-live
controller has voted, the coordinator commits the transaction), Crash (the
one designated station controller fails silently and is dropped from the set
the coordinator waits on), and Reset (after a commit, the router returns to
idle so the next bag's transaction can start).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A prepare vote is only ever counted from a controller that
has synced to the transaction's current epoch, so no unauthorized or stale
controller's vote ever contributes to a commit decision.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every transaction the coordinator opens is eventually
committed, even if one station controller has crashed silently.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od17m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, CrashableController, MaxEpoch

\* phase: coordinator state. epoch: current transaction epoch (bounded by MaxEpoch).
\* votes: controllers who have cast an authorized prepare vote this epoch.
\* partEpoch: each controller's last-synced epoch. crashed: TRUE once the one
\* designated controller has failed silently.
VARIABLES phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed

vars == <<phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

\* A controller can act unless it is the one that has crashed.
CanAct(p) == crashed = FALSE \/ p # CrashableController

LiveControllers == IF crashed THEN Controllers \ {CrashableController} ELSE Controllers

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ partEpoch = [p \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = FALSE

\* Epochs wrap within a bounded range so the transaction count stays finite
\* without ever permanently disabling the coordinator.
StartTxn ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ epoch' = (epoch % MaxEpoch) + 1
    /\ phase' = "prepare"
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<partEpoch, crashed>>

Sync(p) ==
    /\ CanAct(p)
    /\ partEpoch[p] # epoch
    /\ partEpoch' = [partEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, votes, crashed>>

SyncAny == \E p \in Controllers : Sync(p)

\* Only a controller synced to the current epoch may vote: no stale votes count.
Vote(p) ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ CanAct(p)
    /\ partEpoch[p] = epoch
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, partEpoch, crashed>>

VoteAny == \E p \in Controllers : Vote(p)

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "prepare"
    /\ LiveControllers \subseteq votes
    /\ phase' = "commit"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = FALSE
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, epoch, votes, partEpoch>>

Reset ==
    /\ phase = "commit"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, votes, partEpoch, crashed>>

Next == StartTxn \/ SyncAny \/ VoteAny \/ Commit \/ Crash \/ Reset

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(SyncAny) /\ WF_vars(VoteAny)
             /\ WF_vars(Commit) /\ WF_vars(Reset)

VotesAreAuthorized == \A p \in votes : partEpoch[p] = epoch

TxnEventuallyCommits == (phase = "prepare") ~> (phase = "commit")
====

    CrashableController = ctl1

and controllers along the conveyor network take turns owning the right to
update it. Ownership is granted as a time-bounded lease: a controller must
hold the current lease before it may stage a change, and it must confirm
that change while its lease term is still the live one. If a controller
goes quiet, its lease silently expires and reverts to unassigned, bumping
the term so any change staged under the old term can never be confirmed
later. A privileged operations-desk admin can seize the lease at any
moment, even preempting a controller that currently holds it, which is how
the router forces through an emergency re-route. A staged change whose
captured term has fallen behind the live term is discarded rather than
applied, so a controller that was already superseded can never sneak its
update into the record after the fact.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A staged update is only ever eligible to commit while its
captured lease term still equals the record's live term and the controller
that staged it still equals the current lease holder, so no lost update to
the shared routing record can be produced by a controller acting on a
superseded lease.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every staged update is eventually resolved -- either
committed to the shared record or discarded once its lease term goes
stale -- so no staged update is left pending forever.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

---- MODULE W4Od17m6p1t5 ----
(* Airport baggage router: a shared routing record protected by a
   time-bounded lease. Controllers stage an update while they believe
   they hold the lease, then commit only if their captured term is still
   the live term -- this is what prevents a lost update from a
   controller that was silently superseded. A privileged admin can seize
   the lease at any time, bumping the term and staling out any pending
   staged update. *)
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Admin, NullOwner, MaxTerm, MaxVersion

VARIABLES leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm

Vars == <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

Owners == Controllers \cup {Admin}

TypeOK == /\ leaseOwner \in Owners \cup {NullOwner}
          /\ leaseTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
          /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
          /\ pendingWriter \in Owners \cup {NullOwner}
          /\ pendingTerm \in 0..MaxTerm

Init == /\ leaseOwner = NullOwner
        /\ leaseTerm = 0
        /\ version = 0
        /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
        /\ pendingTerm = 0

\* A controller claims the free lease; claiming always advances the term.
AcquireLease == \E c \in Controllers :
                   /\ leaseOwner = NullOwner
                   /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
                   /\ leaseOwner' = c
                   /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
                   /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The lease can silently expire, releasing ownership to nobody.
ExpireLease == /\ leaseOwner # NullOwner
               /\ leaseOwner # Admin
               /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
               /\ leaseOwner' = NullOwner
               /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
               /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The current holder stages an update, capturing the term it believes live.
PrepareWrite == \E c \in Controllers :
                    /\ c = leaseOwner
                    /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
                    /\ pendingWriter' = c
                    /\ pendingTerm' = leaseTerm
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version>>

\* A staged update commits only if its captured term is still the live term.
CommitWrite == /\ pendingWriter # NullOwner
               /\ pendingTerm = leaseTerm
               /\ leaseOwner = pendingWriter
               /\ version' = IF version < MaxVersion THEN version + 1 ELSE version
               /\ pendingWriter' = NullOwner
               /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, pendingTerm>>

\* A staged update whose term has gone stale is discarded, never applied.
InvalidateWrite == /\ pendingWriter # NullOwner
                    /\ pendingTerm # leaseTerm
                    /\ pendingWriter' = NullOwner
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, leaseTerm, version, pendingTerm>>

\* The admin's privileged override seizes the lease at any moment.
AdminOverride == /\ leaseTerm < MaxTerm
                  /\ leaseOwner' = Admin
                  /\ leaseTerm' = leaseTerm + 1
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

\* The term counter recycles once exhausted, but only while nothing is
\* staged, so there is never a live pending write left to mis-invalidate.
ResetEpoch == /\ leaseTerm = MaxTerm
              /\ pendingWriter = NullOwner
              /\ leaseTerm' = 0
              /\ UNCHANGED <<leaseOwner, version, pendingWriter, pendingTerm>>

Next == \/ AcquireLease
        \/ ExpireLease
        \/ PrepareWrite
        \/ CommitWrite
        \/ InvalidateWrite
        \/ AdminOverride
        \/ ResetEpoch

\* No lost update: a staged write is only ever poised to commit while its
\* captured term and staging controller still match the live lease state.
NoLostUpdates == (pendingWriter # NullOwner /\ pendingTerm = leaseTerm)
                    => leaseOwner = pendingWriter

\* Every staged update is eventually resolved, one way or the other.
EventuallyResolved == pendingWriter # NullOwner ~> pendingWriter = NullOwner

====

(* queued + in-flight + completed must equal total issued at all times.    *)

vars == <<queue, assigned, progress, completed, nextId>>

\* Nat sentinel avoids ever comparing an integer to a non-integer value.
TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(1..MaxCommands)
    /\ assigned \in [Devices -> 0..MaxCommands]
    /\ progress \in [Devices -> 0..Threshold]
    /\ completed \subseteq 1..MaxCommands
    /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxCommands + 1)

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ assigned = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
    /\ progress = [d \in Devices |-> 0]
    /\ completed = {}
    /\ nextId = 1

    /\ nextId <= MaxCommands
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextId)
    /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, progress, completed>>

    /\ assigned[d] = 0
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![d] = Head(queue)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ progress' = [progress EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<completed, nextId>>

    /\ progress[d] < Threshold

    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![d] = 0]

    \/ \E d \in Devices : Assign(d) \/ Work(d) \/ Finish(d)

A clearinghouse runs an interbank settlement batch for three member banks (bA, bB,
bC) using hierarchical locking: a coarse lock on the whole batch, and a nested fine
lock on the individual leg being posted inside it. A bank may seize the coarse lock

coarse lock, which settles the batch and advances the clearinghouse to the next
epoch. Compliance may revoke or restore a bank's authorization to settle, but never
while that bank is currently holding either lock. A bank can be slow -- lagging on
syncing its epoch, or taking its time between acquiring and releasing the fine lock
-- but it never crashes or drops out of the batch entirely, so whatever it starts it
eventually finishes.
Actions: a bank syncs its local epoch to the current one; a bank acquires the coarse
batch lock; a bank acquires the nested fine leg lock; a bank releases the fine lock;
a bank releases the coarse lock, advancing the epoch; compliance toggles a bank's
authorization when that bank holds neither lock.

no unauthorized or stale bank ever holds a lock.

it, so the batch is never stuck indefinitely in one bank's hands.

fill a prescription, one station takes out a lease on a batch of pills

ticks. If the lease is used before it expires, the held pills are recorded
as dispensed to a patient; if it expires unrenewed, the held pills are
reclaimed back into free stock instead of vanishing. Only one lease can be
outstanding at a time, so every pill in the system is at every moment
accounted for as exactly one of: free stock, held under the current
lease, or already dispensed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, free stock plus the amount held
under the current lease plus the running dispensed total equals the
current capacity -- the pill count is fully conserved across restocks,
write-offs, leases, dispenses, and expirations.

system eventually resolves it -- either by dispensing the held pills to a
patient or by reclaiming them back into free stock after expiry -- so no

(* changes at runtime (restock / write-off) are the only source or sink,   *)
(* so the three buckets always sum back to the current capacity.          *)

CONSTANTS Stations, NoStation, MaxCapacity, LeaseTTL, MaxDispensed

VARIABLES capacity, stock, holder, heldAmt, age, dispensedTotal

vars == <<capacity, stock, holder, heldAmt, age, dispensedTotal>>

Init ==
  /\ capacity = 0
  /\ stock = 0
  /\ holder = NoStation
  /\ heldAmt = 0
  /\ age = 0
  /\ dispensedTotal = 0

Restock(amt) ==
  /\ amt > 0 /\ capacity + amt <= MaxCapacity
  /\ capacity' = capacity + amt
  /\ stock' = stock + amt
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, heldAmt, age, dispensedTotal>>

Writedown(amt) ==
  /\ amt > 0 /\ amt <= stock
  /\ capacity' = capacity - amt
  /\ stock' = stock - amt
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, heldAmt, age, dispensedTotal>>

GrantLease(station, amt) ==
  /\ holder = NoStation
  /\ amt \in 1..stock
  /\ holder' = station
  /\ heldAmt' = amt
  /\ stock' = stock - amt
  /\ age' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, dispensedTotal>>

Tick ==
  /\ holder # NoStation
  /\ age < LeaseTTL
  /\ age' = age + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, stock, holder, heldAmt, dispensedTotal>>

Dispense ==
  /\ holder # NoStation
  /\ age < LeaseTTL
  /\ dispensedTotal' = dispensedTotal + heldAmt
  /\ dispensedTotal + heldAmt <= MaxDispensed
  /\ holder' = NoStation
  /\ heldAmt' = 0
  /\ age' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, stock>>

  /\ age >= LeaseTTL
  /\ stock' = stock + heldAmt
  /\ holder' = NoStation
  /\ heldAmt' = 0
  /\ age' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, dispensedTotal>>

\* pipeline has drained, so idle here instead of reporting a deadlock.
Done == /\ holder = NoStation

        /\ capacity = MaxCapacity

  \/ \E amt \in 1..MaxCapacity : Writedown(amt)
  \/ \E station \in Stations, amt \in 1..MaxCapacity : GrantLease(station, amt)
  \/ Tick
  \/ ResolveStep
  \/ Terminating

Conservation == stock + heldAmt + dispensedTotal = capacity

unreliable inter-library network, vote messages travel independently and can be

coordinator has already moved on to a newer round. The coordinator only counts a vote

vote of theirs that was previously counted is withdrawn. The coordinator commits the

    /\ held = [p \in Participants |-> 0]

(* Warehouse robot fleet: a CAS ownership register gates task claims.     *)
(* One robot may crash silently; a live robot fences the register to a   *)
(* fresh epoch so the crashed owner's stale token can never claim again. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Tasks, InitOwner, MaxEpoch, MaxCrashes

VARIABLES epoch, owner, robotEpoch, crashed, claimed

vars == <<epoch, owner, robotEpoch, crashed, claimed>>

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ owner = InitOwner
  /\ robotEpoch = [r \in Robots |-> IF r = InitOwner THEN 1 ELSE 0]
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ claimed = {}

Crash(r) ==
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ Cardinality(crashed) < MaxCrashes
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, robotEpoch, claimed>>

Fence(r) ==
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ owner \in crashed
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ owner' = r
  /\ robotEpoch' = [robotEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, claimed>>

Sync(r) ==
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ robotEpoch' = [robotEpoch EXCEPT ![r] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, crashed, claimed>>

ClaimTask(r, t) ==
  /\ r \notin crashed
  /\ r = owner
  /\ robotEpoch[r] = epoch
  /\ t \notin claimed
  /\ claimed' = claimed \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, robotEpoch, crashed>>

ProgressStep ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Fence(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in Tasks : ClaimTask(r, t)

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Crash(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Fence(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : Sync(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, t \in Tasks : ClaimTask(r, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(ProgressStep)

\* claim can never come from an unauthorized or stale participant.
NoStaleClaim == (owner \notin crashed) => (robotEpoch[owner] = epoch)

\* Liveness: despite one silent crash, every task is eventually claimed.
LivenessProp == <>(claimed = Tasks)

A multiplayer game lobby fills its open slots with a compare-and-swap register per
slot. A player who wants a slot first reads the slot's register (a witness of what it
currently holds) and then performs the actual compare-and-swap: the swap only takes
effect if the register still matches what the player witnessed, otherwise the attempt
silently loses the race and the player is free to try again. The lobby's capacity
changes at runtime: an operator can open an additional slot at any time, and can also
shrink capacity, which evicts whichever player currently sits in the top slot back
into a waiting pool so they can attempt to rejoin once capacity allows. A player only
ever has one outstanding compare-and-swap attempt at a time, and a player who already
holds a slot cannot start a new attempt until they release it.

Actions: a player who currently holds no slot and has no outstanding attempt
witnesses an open slot's register as currently empty and records an attempt; a
player's outstanding attempt resolves -- the compare-and-swap succeeds and
claims the slot if it is still empty, otherwise it fails and the attempt is simply
dropped; a player already holding a slot releases it; the operator grows capacity by
one slot; the operator shrinks capacity by one, evicting the top slot's occupant into
the waiting pool; an evicted player leaves the waiting pool so they can try again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: no slot is ever claimed by more than one player at once, and no
player ever ends up holding two slots at once, so the compare-and-swap never
double-allocates a slot.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever a player has an outstanding compare-and-swap attempt on a
slot, that attempt is eventually resolved, one way or the other, so no player is left
waiting on a claim forever.

\* <<player, slot>> pairs for the read half of a compare-and-swap; Resolve
\* performs the actual compare-and-set against what was witnessed, so a

    /\ capacity = 1
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
    /\ witnessed = {}
    /\ waiting = {}

    /\ p \notin waiting
    /\ s <= capacity
    /\ owner[s] = {}

    /\ witnessed' = witnessed \ {<<p, s>>}

\* The ring has made its last hand-off, the final round is already sent,
\* and nothing is left in transit: idle here instead of a false deadlock.

        /\ round \in sentRounds
        /\ inflight = {}

Terminating == Done /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ AdvanceToken
  \/ \E v \in Values : SendUpdate(v)
  \/ \E r \in 1..MaxRound, v \in Values : ApplyUpdate(r, v)
  \/ \E r \in 1..MaxRound, v \in Values : DropStale(r, v)
  \/ Terminating

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: every sent round is either folded into (or superseded by) the
\* record's current version, or still pending -- no update ever vanishes.
NoLostUpdate ==
  \A r \in sentRounds : r <= recordVersion \/ (\E v \in Values : <<r, v>> \in inflight)

A university course-registration system processes seat requests for a single
capped section through a bounded work queue: students submit registration
requests, but the queue only holds a fixed number of pending requests at a
time, and once it is full, new arrivals are turned away by backpressure
instead of being queued. Accepted requests are dequeued and routed toward a
candidate seat as an allocation-offer message. Because the network between
the queue processor and the seat ledger can reorder messages, offers may be
delivered and resolved in an order different from the order they were sent,
and a stale or duplicate offer that arrives for a seat or a student that has
already been finalized is discarded rather than acted on. A seat is
finalized for a student only if that seat has not already been committed to
someone else and that student does not already hold a finalized seat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: for every pair of finalized allocation records in the
commit log, if the two records name the same seat, they also name the same
student -- no seat slot is ever finalized (double allocated) to two
different students, regardless of the order in which offer messages were
reordered and resolved.

---- MODULE W4Od8m4p3t1 ----
(* University course registration: a bounded work queue with backpressure  *)
(* feeds allocation-offer messages that a reordering network may resolve   *)
(* out of order.  A stale offer for an already-finalized seat or student   *)
(* is discarded, so the commit log stays a well-formed seat-to-student map.*)
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Seats, MaxQueue

VARIABLES queue, requested, inflight, committed, rejected

vars == <<queue, requested, inflight, committed, rejected>>

SeatTaken(seat) == \E s \in Students : <<seat, s>> \in committed
HasSeat(s) == \E seat \in Seats : <<seat, s>> \in committed

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ requested = {}
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ committed = {}
  /\ rejected = {}

Submit(s) ==
  /\ s \notin requested
  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, s)
  /\ requested' = requested \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, committed, rejected>>

RejectFull(s) ==
  /\ s \notin requested
  /\ Len(queue) = MaxQueue
  /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {s}
  /\ requested' = requested \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inflight, committed>>

Dequeue ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ \E seat \in Seats : inflight' = inflight \cup {<<Head(queue), seat>>}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, committed, rejected>>

Commit(s, seat) ==
  /\ <<s, seat>> \in inflight
  /\ ~SeatTaken(seat)
  /\ ~HasSeat(s)
  /\ committed' = committed \cup {<<seat, s>>}
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<s, seat>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, requested, rejected>>

DropOffer(s, seat) ==
  /\ <<s, seat>> \in inflight
  /\ (SeatTaken(seat) \/ HasSeat(s))
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<s, seat>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, requested, committed, rejected>>

\* Every student has been submitted or turned away, and the pipeline has
\* drained; the model idles here instead of reporting a spurious deadlock.
Done == /\ requested = Students
        /\ queue = <<>>
        /\ inflight = {}

Terminating == Done /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : Submit(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : RejectFull(s)
  \/ Dequeue
  \/ \E s \in Students, seat \in Seats : Commit(s, seat)
  \/ \E s \in Students, seat \in Seats : DropOffer(s, seat)
  \/ Terminating

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the commit log, read as a relation, is functional on seats -- a
\* seat never appears in two records naming different students.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A x, y \in committed : x[1] = y[1] => x[2] = y[2]

====

  Seats = {seat1, seat2}

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A university course-registration system grants a contested seat through a
lease: a student who claims the seat holds it only for a bounded countdown of
registration ticks, may renew that lease exactly once before it lapses, and
loses the claim automatically once the countdown reaches zero without a
renewal. Any one of the other competing students' registration clients can
crash silently, going dark without releasing its lease early, but a dark
client's lease still counts down and lapses on schedule like any other. Once a
seat's lease has lapsed or been released it is open for the next student to
claim, and a claim always replaces any lapsed lease outright rather than
letting two students ever hold the same seat. SAFETY PROPERTY: no course seat
is ever held by two different students at the same time. LIVENESS PROPERTY: one
designated waiting student is never starved out by the other, faster-cycling
students -- it always eventually claims a seat.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od8m6p3t0 ----
(* University course-registration lease. A claim on a seat counts down from
   LeaseLen and may be renewed exactly once before it must lapse; a lapsed or
   released seat is open to the next claim, which always replaces any lapsed
   record rather than coexisting with it. One competing student's client may
   crash silently, but its lease still counts down and lapses normally. A
   designated waiting student must never be starved out of a seat. *)
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Slots, WaitingStudent, LeaseLen
ASSUME /\ LeaseLen \in Nat /\ LeaseLen >= 1
       /\ WaitingStudent \in Students
       /\ Slots # {}

VARIABLES allocated, ticksLeft, renewedOnce, crashed

vars == <<allocated, ticksLeft, renewedOnce, crashed>>

TypeOK == /\ allocated \subseteq (Students \X Slots)
          /\ ticksLeft \in [Slots -> 0..LeaseLen]
          /\ renewedOnce \subseteq Slots
          /\ crashed \subseteq (Students \ {WaitingStudent})

Init == /\ allocated = {}
        /\ ticksLeft = [sl \in Slots |-> 0]
        /\ renewedOnce = {}
        /\ crashed = {}

Free(sl) == ~(\E s \in Students : <<s, sl>> \in allocated) \/ ticksLeft[sl] = 0

\* The waiting student claims any free-or-lapsed seat.
AcquireWaiting == \E sl \in Slots :
                     /\ Free(sl)
                     /\ allocated' = (allocated \ {p \in allocated : p[2] = sl}) \cup {<<WaitingStudent, sl>>}
                     /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![sl] = LeaseLen]
                     /\ renewedOnce' = renewedOnce \ {sl}
                     /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* Any other student claims any free-or-lapsed seat.
AcquireOther == \E s \in Students \ {WaitingStudent}, sl \in Slots :
                     /\ s \notin crashed
                     /\ Free(sl)
                     /\ allocated' = (allocated \ {p \in allocated : p[2] = sl}) \cup {<<s, sl>>}
                     /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![sl] = LeaseLen]
                     /\ renewedOnce' = renewedOnce \ {sl}
                     /\ UNCHANGED crashed

RenewLease == \E s \in Students, sl \in Slots :
                     /\ <<s, sl>> \in allocated
                     /\ s \notin crashed
                     /\ sl \notin renewedOnce
                     /\ ticksLeft[sl] > 0
                     /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![sl] = LeaseLen]
                     /\ renewedOnce' = renewedOnce \cup {sl}
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, crashed>>

ReleaseLease == \E s \in Students, sl \in Slots :
                     /\ <<s, sl>> \in allocated
                     /\ allocated' = allocated \ {<<s, sl>>}
                     /\ ticksLeft' = [ticksLeft EXCEPT ![sl] = 0]
                     /\ renewedOnce' = renewedOnce \ {sl}
                     /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* The countdown ticks down every active lease together.
Tick == /\ \E sl \in Slots : ticksLeft[sl] > 0
        /\ ticksLeft' = [sl \in Slots |-> IF ticksLeft[sl] > 0 THEN ticksLeft[sl] - 1 ELSE 0]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, renewedOnce, crashed>>

\* One of the other students' clients can crash silently.
Crash == /\ crashed = {}
         /\ \E s \in Students \ {WaitingStudent} : crashed' = {s}
         /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, ticksLeft, renewedOnce>>

Next == AcquireWaiting \/ AcquireOther \/ RenewLease \/ ReleaseLease \/ Tick \/ Crash

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Tick) /\ SF_vars(AcquireWaiting)

\* Literal property: no seat is ever simultaneously claimed by two students.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A sl \in Slots : Cardinality({s \in Students : <<s, sl>> \in allocated}) <= 1

\* Liveness: the waiting student is never starved out of a seat.
WaitingGetsSlot == <>(\E sl \in Slots : <<WaitingStudent, sl>> \in allocated)
====
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS
    Students = {ws, o1}
    Slots = {c1}
    WaitingStudent = ws
    LeaseLen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY WaitingGetsSlot
```

<|start|>user<|message|>Write a TLA+ specification that implements EXACTLY the system described below, and a TLC .cfg to model-check it. The system's safety property described in the NL text must be captured as a real, non-trivial INVARIANT (not `Inv == TRUE`) in the .cfg.

===BEGIN NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===
A regional power grid runs an automated load shedder over a set of feeder
circuits. To shed or restore load on a feeder, a controller first acquires a
coarse region lock covering the whole zone, then a fine per-feeder lock on
the feeder itself; only after holding both may it change that feeder's
committed load, and it releases both locks together the moment the change is
committed. Restoring load onto a feeder is only permitted up to the grid
operator's current emergency capacity ceiling, and the operator may raise or
lower that ceiling at runtime as conditions change -- a sudden drop can leave
total committed load momentarily above the new ceiling. Regardless of how the
ceiling moves, total committed load must never exceed the grid's fixed
physical capacity limit. Whenever a ceiling drop (or any other change) leaves
total committed load above the current ceiling, the shedder must keep working
the coarse-then-fine lock sequence until enough feeders have been shed back
down.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the sum of committed load across
all feeders does not exceed the grid's fixed physical capacity limit.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever total committed load exceeds the current
emergency capacity ceiling, the shedder eventually sheds load back down to at
most that ceiling.

===END NATURAL LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION===

Reply with exactly one TLA+ module in a ```tla fenced block and exactly one .cfg in a ```cfg fenced block. After the two blocks, add exactly one line of the form `PROPERTY_INVARIANT: <Name>` naming the invariant in your module that implements THE safety property stated in the description's SAFETY PROPERTY section. That name must be defined in the module, listed as an INVARIANT in the .cfg, and must be a semantic safety invariant (not a TypeOK-style type-correctness check).<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>```tla
---- MODULE W4Od9m8p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, HardCap

VARIABLES load, ceiling, coarseHeld, fineHeld

Vars == <<load, ceiling, coarseHeld, fineHeld>>

NoFeeder == "none"

\* Sum committed load across all feeders (recursive fold over a finite set).
RECURSIVE SumLoad(_)
SumLoad(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
              ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                   IN load[f] + SumLoad(S \ {f})
TotalLoad == SumLoad(Feeders)

TypeOK ==
  /\ load \in [Feeders -> 0..HardCap]
  /\ ceiling \in 0..HardCap
  /\ coarseHeld \in BOOLEAN
  /\ fineHeld \in Feeders \cup {NoFeeder}

Init ==
  /\ load = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
  /\ ceiling = HardCap
  /\ coarseHeld = FALSE
  /\ fineHeld = NoFeeder

\* Coarse region lock must be taken before any fine per-feeder lock, and only
\* when some feeder actually has something to shed or room to restore into.
AcquireCoarse ==
  /\ ~coarseHeld
  /\ fineHeld = NoFeeder
  /\ \E f \in Feeders : load[f] > 0 \/ TotalLoad + 1 <= ceiling
  /\ coarseHeld' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ceiling, fineHeld>>

\* Only take the fine lock on a feeder that can actually be acted on next
\* (something to shed, or headroom under the ceiling to restore into) --
\* otherwise a badly-chosen feeder could wedge the lock chain forever.
AcquireFine(f) ==
  /\ coarseHeld
  /\ fineHeld = NoFeeder
  /\ load[f] > 0 \/ TotalLoad + 1 <= ceiling
  /\ fineHeld' = f
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ceiling, coarseHeld>>

\* Committing a shed and releasing both locks happen in one atomic step.
ShedRelease(f) ==
  /\ fineHeld = f
  /\ load[f] > 0
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![f] = load[f] - 1]
  /\ coarseHeld' = FALSE
  /\ fineHeld' = NoFeeder
  /\ UNCHANGED ceiling

\* Restoring load is bounded by the CURRENT ceiling, not the hard limit --
\* so a fresh ceiling drop can never be worsened by a concurrent restore.
RestoreRelease(f) ==
  /\ fineHeld = f
  /\ TotalLoad + 1 <= ceiling
  /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![f] = load[f] + 1]
  /\ coarseHeld' = FALSE
  /\ fineHeld' = NoFeeder
  /\ UNCHANGED ceiling

\* The operator can only move the ceiling between lock-chains, not mid-commit,
\* so an in-flight fine-lock decision is never invalidated out from under it.
RaiseCeiling ==
  /\ ~coarseHeld
  /\ ceiling < HardCap
  /\ ceiling' = ceiling + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, coarseHeld, fineHeld>>

LowerCeiling ==
  /\ ~coarseHeld
  /\ ceiling > 0
  /\ ceiling' = ceiling - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<load, coarseHeld, fineHeld>>

AnyAcquireFine == \E f \in Feeders : AcquireFine(f)
AnyShedRelease == \E f \in Feeders : ShedRelease(f)

Next ==
  \/ AcquireCoarse
  \/ AnyAcquireFine
  \/ AnyShedRelease
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : RestoreRelease(f)
  \/ RaiseCeiling
  \/ LowerCeiling

\* Fairness on the lock-and-shed chain drives the shedder to make progress
\* whenever it stays enabled, without forcing quantified per-feeder clauses.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_Vars
             /\ WF_Vars(AcquireCoarse)
             /\ WF_Vars(AnyAcquireFine)
             /\ WF_Vars(AnyShedRelease)

\* The grid's fixed physical capacity limit is never exceeded.
CapacityBound == TotalLoad <= HardCap

\* Whenever load exceeds the operator's current ceiling, it is eventually shed back.
CeilingRecovers == (TotalLoad > ceiling) ~> (TotalLoad <= ceiling)
====
```
```cfg
CONSTANTS
Feeders = {f1, f2}
HardCap = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityBound
PROPERTY CeilingRecovers
```
